text.ar: وَالتَّقْصِيرُ الْوَاقِعُ مِنَ الْخَلْقِ يَقْتَضِي الْعُقُوبَاتِ الْمُتَنَوِّعَةَ، وَلَكِنَّ عَفْوَ اللَّهِ وَمَغْفِرَتَهُ تَدْفَعُ هَذِهِ الْمُوجِبَاتِ وَالْعُقُوبَاتِ ﴿وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُواْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهۡرِهَا مِن دَآبَّةٖ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٖ مُّسَمّٗىۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ بَصِيرَۢا﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٤٥]، وَهَذَا مِنْ كَمَالِ عَفْوِهِ، فَلَوْلَا كَمَالُ عَفْوِهِ وَحِلْمِهِ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَى ظَهْرِ الْأَرْضِ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ، وَمِثْلُهَا قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلۡمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيۡهَا مِن دَآبَّةٖ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٖ مُّسَمّٗىۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَـٔۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةٗ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ٦١].
text.en: The shortcomings that occur from creation call for various punishments, but Allah’s pardon and forgiveness ward off these causes and punishments: ﴾And if Allah were to seize the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its surface a single creature. But He defers them until a specified term. And when their term comes, then indeed Allah is ever All-Seeing of His servants﴿ [Fatir 35:45]. This is from the perfection of His pardon; were it not for the perfection of His pardon and forbearance, He would not have left a single creature upon the face of the earth. Similar to it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴾And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it a single creature. But He defers them until a specified term. And when their term comes, they will not delay it for an hour, nor will they bring it forward﴿ [an-Nahl 16:61].

text.ar: وَمِنْ هَذَا الْبَابِ مَا وَرَدَ فِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[1] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ ـ أَوْ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ ـ أَصْبَرَ عَلَى أَذًى سَمِعَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّهُمْ لَيَدْعُونَ لَهُ وَلَداً، وَإِنَّهُ لَيُعَافِيهِمْ وَيَرْزُقُهُمْ».
text.en: Of this kind is what is reported in the *Two Sahihs*[1] from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no one — or: nothing — more patient over harm he hears than Allah. They claim that He has a son, yet He grants them well-being and provides for them.”

text.ar: وَعَفْوُهُ تَعَالَى نَوْعَانِ:
text.en: His pardon, the Exalted, is of two kinds:

text.ar: النَّوْعُ الْأَوَّلُ: عَفْوُهُ الْعَامُّ عَنْ جَمِيعِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ، بِدَفْعِ الْعُقُوبَاتِ الْمُنْعَقِدَةِ أَسْبَابُهَا، وَالْمُقْتَضِيَةِ لِقَطْعِ النِّعَمِ عَنْهُمْ، فَهُمْ يُؤْذُونَهُ بِالسَّبِّ وَالشِّرْكِ وَغَيْرِهَا مِنْ أَصْنَافِ الْمُخَالَفَاتِ، وَهُوَ يُعَافِيهِمْ وَيَرْزُقُهُمْ وَيُدِرُّ عَلَيْهِمُ النِّعَمَ الظَّاهِرَةَ وَالْبَاطِنَةَ، وَيَبْسُطُ لَهُمُ الدُّنْيَا، وَيُعْطِيهِمْ مِنْ نَعِيمِهَا وَمَنَافِعِهَا وَيُمْهِلُهُمْ وَلَا يُهْمِلُهُمْ بِعَفْوِهِ وَحِلْمِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ.
text.en: The first kind: His general pardon of all wrongdoers, disbelievers and others, by warding off the punishments whose causes have been established and which call for His blessings to be cut off from them. They harm Him with abuse, with shirk and with other kinds of disobedience, yet He grants them well-being, provides for them and pours upon them blessings outward and inward. He spreads out the world for them and gives them of its delights and benefits, and He gives them respite without neglecting them, out of His pardon and forbearance, Glorified is He.

text.ar: وَالنَّوْعُ الثَّانِي: عَفْوُهُ الْخَاصُّ، وَمَغْفِرَتُهُ الْخَاصَّةُ لِلتَّائِبِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ وَالدَّاعِينَ وَالْعَابِدِينَ، وَالْمُصَابِينَ بِالْمَصَائِبِ الْمُحْتَسِبِينَ، فَكُلُّ مَنْ تَابَ إِلَيْهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحاً ـ وَهِيَ الْخَالِصَةُ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ الْعَامَّةُ الشَّامِلَةُ الَّتِي لَا يَصْحَبُهَا تَرَدُّدٌ وَلَا إِصْرَارٌ ـ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ لَهُ مِنْ أَيِّ ذَنْبٍ كَانَ، مِنْ كُفْرٍ وَفُسُوقٍ وَعِصْيَانٍ، وَكُلُّهَا دَاخِلَةٌ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ٥٣].
text.en: The second kind: His special pardon and His special forgiveness for those who repent, those who seek forgiveness, those who supplicate, those who worship, and those afflicted with calamities who hope for the reward. Everyone who turns to Him in sincere repentance — that is, repentance done purely for the Face of Allah, general and comprehensive, accompanied by no hesitation and no persistence — Allah forgives him, whatever the sin was, whether disbelief, wickedness or disobedience. All of this falls under His saying, the Exalted: ﴾Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴿ [az-Zumar 39:53].

text.ar: وَقَدْ تَوَاتَرَتْ النُّصُوصُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ فِي قَبُولِ اللَّهِ التَّوْبَةَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ مِنْ أَيِّ ذَنْبٍ كَانَ، وَكَذَلِكَ الِاسْتِغْفَارُ الْمُجَرَّدُ يَحْصُلُ بِهِ مِنْ مَغْفِرَةِ الذُّنُوبِ وَالسَّيِّئَاتِ بِحَسَبِهِ، وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ الْقُدْسِيِّ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: «يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ إِنَّكَ مَا دَعَوْتَنِي وَرَجَوْتَنِي غَفَرْتُ لَكَ مَا كَانَ فِيكَ وَلَا أُبَالِي، يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ لَوْ بَلَغَتْ ذُنُوبُكَ عَنَانَ السَّمَاءِ، ثُمَّ اسْتَغْفَرْتَنِي غَفَرْتُ لَكَ وَلَا أُبَالِي، يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ لَوْ أَتَيْتَنِي بِقُرَابِ الْأَرْضِ خَطَايَا ثُمَّ لَقِيتَنِي لَا تُشْرِكُ بِي شَيْئاً لَأَتَيْتُكَ بِقُرَابِهَا مَغْفِرَةً». رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ[2].
text.en: The texts of the Book and the Sunnah have come in great abundance about Allah’s acceptance of repentance from His servants, whatever the sin was. Likewise, seeking forgiveness on its own brings about forgiveness of sins and evil deeds in proportion to it. In the hadith qudsi, Allah the Exalted said: “O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you whatever you have done, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, if your sins were to reach the clouds of the sky and then you sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you, and I do not mind. O son of Adam, if you were to come to Me with nearly an earthful of sins and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I would come to you with nearly an earthful of forgiveness.” Reported by at-Tirmidhi[2].

text.ar: وَكَذَلِكَ مِنْ عَفْوِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ وَالْأَعْمَالَ الصَّالِحَةَ تُكَفِّرُ السَّيِّئَاتِ وَالْخَطَايَا، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلۡحَسَنَٰتِ يُذۡهِبۡنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ﴾ [هُودٍ: ١١٤]، وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: «وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا» رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ وَالتِّرْمِذِيُّ وَالْحَاكِمُ وَغَيْرُهُمْ[3].
text.en: Likewise, part of His pardon, Glorified is He, is that good deeds and righteous actions expiate evil deeds and sins. The Exalted said: ﴾Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴿ [Hud 11:114]. And in the hadith: “And follow up a bad deed with a good deed; it will wipe it out.” Reported by Ahmad, at-Tirmidhi, al-Hakim and others[3].

text.ar: وَكَذَلِكَ مِنْ عَفْوِهِ أَنَّ الْمَصَائِبَ الَّتِي تُصِيبُ الْعَبْدَ فِي نَفْسِهِ أَوْ وَلَدِهِ أَوْ مَالِهِ تُكَفِّرُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ، خُصُوصاً إِذَا احْتَسَبَ ثَوَابَهَا وَقَامَ بِوَظِيفَةِ الصَّبْرِ أَوِ الرِّضَى.
text.en: Likewise, part of His pardon is that the calamities that befall the servant in himself, his children or his wealth expiate his evil deeds, especially if he seeks their reward from Allah and fulfils the duty of patience or contentment.

text.ar: وَمِنْ عَظِيمِ عَفْوِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنَّ الْعَبْدَ يُبَارِزُ رَبَّهُ بِالْعَظَائِمِ وَالْجَرَائِمِ فَيَلْطُفُ بِهِ رَبُّهُ، وَيُحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَفْوَهُ، فَيَشْرَحُ صَدْرَهُ لِلتَّوْبَةِ، وَيَتَقَبَّلُ مِنْهُ مَتَابَهُ، بَلْ إِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ يَفْرَحُ بِتَوْبَةِ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا تَابَ مَعَ أَنَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ، لَا تَنْفَعُهُ طَاعَةُ مَنْ أَطَاعَ، وَلَا تَضُرُّهُ مَعْصِيَةُ مَنْ عَصَى.
text.en: And part of the greatness of His pardon, Glorified is He, is that the servant openly confronts his Lord with enormities and crimes, yet his Lord is kind to him and lets His pardon descend upon him; He opens his heart to repentance and accepts his turning back. Indeed, He, Glorified is He, rejoices at His servant’s repentance when he repents, even though He is Free of all need, Praiseworthy: the obedience of whoever obeys does not benefit Him, and the disobedience of whoever disobeys does not harm Him.

text.ar: رَوَى مُسْلِمٌ فِي «صَحِيحِهِ»[4] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَلَّهُ أَشَدُّ فَرَحاً بِتَوْبَةِ عَبْدِهِ حِينَ يَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ أَحَدِكُمْ كَانَ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ بِأَرْضِ فَلَاةٍ، فَانْفَلَتَتْ مِنْهُ، وَعَلَيْهَا طَعَامُهُ وَشَرَابُهُ، فَأَيِسَ مِنْهَا، فَأَتَى شَجَرَةً فَاضْطَجَعَ فِي ظِلِّهَا قَدْ أَيِسَ مِنْ رَاحِلَتِهِ، فَبَيْنَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ هُوَ بِهَا قَائِمَةً عِنْدَهُ، فَأَخَذَ بِخِطَامِهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ ـ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْفَرَحِ ـ: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ عَبْدِي وَأَنَا رَبُّكَ، أَخْطَأَ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْفَرَحِ».
text.en: Muslim reported in his *Sahih*[4] from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him in repentance than one of you who was on his riding camel in a barren desert, and it escaped from him, carrying his food and drink. He despaired of it, so he came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having lost hope of his camel. While he was in that state, suddenly there it was, standing beside him. He took hold of its halter and then said, out of intense joy: ‘O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord.’ He made the mistake out of intense joy.”

text.ar: وَيَنْبَغِي هُنَا أَنْ يُعْلَمَ أَنَّ عِلْمَ الْعَبْدِ بِهَذِهِ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْعَظِيمَةِ بَابٌ عَظِيمٌ لِنَيْلِ عَالِي الْمَقَامَاتِ، وَلَا سِيَّمَا مَعَ مُجَاهَدَةِ النَّفْسِ عَلَى تَحْقِيقِ مُقْتَضَيَاتِهَا، مِنْ لُزُومِ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ، وَطَلَبِ الْعَفْوِ، وَدَوَامِ التَّوْبَةِ، وَرَجَاءِ الْمَغْفِرَةِ، وَالْبُعْدِ عَنِ الْقُنُوطِ وَتَعَاظُمِ غُفْرَانِ الذُّنُوبِ، فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ عَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ لَا يَتَعَاظَمُهُ ذَنْبٌ أَنْ يَغْفِرَهُ مَهْمَا بَلَغَ الذَّنْبُ وَعَظُمَ الْجُرْمُ، وَالْعَبْدُ عَلَى خَيْرٍ عَظِيمٍ مَا دَامَ طَالِباً عَفْوَ رَبِّهِ، رَاجِياً غُفْرَانَهُ.
text.en: It should be known here that the servant’s knowledge of these great names is a mighty door to attaining lofty stations, especially when joined with striving against the soul to fulfil what they require: persisting in seeking forgiveness, asking for pardon, constant repentance, hoping for forgiveness, and keeping far from despair and from thinking the forgiveness of sins too great. For He, Glorified is He, is Pardoning, Forgiving; no sin is too great for Him to forgive, however far the sin goes and however great the crime. And the servant is upon tremendous good as long as he keeps seeking his Lord’s pardon and hoping for His forgiveness.

text.ar: وَتَأَمَّلْ فِي هَذَا الْمَقَامِ مَا رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ وَمُسْلِمٌ فِي «صَحِيحَيْهِمَا»[5] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِيمَا يَحْكِيهِ عَنْ رَبِّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ قَالَ: «أَذْنَبَ عَبْدٌ ذَنْباً، فَقَالَ:
text.en: Reflect, in this regard, on what al-Bukhari and Muslim reported in their *Sahihs*[5] from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who said: “A servant committed a sin and said:

text.ar: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي، فَقَالَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: أَذْنَبَ عَبْدِي ذَنْباً، فَعَلِمَ أَنَّ لَهُ رَبًّا يَغْفِرُ الذَّنْبَ، وَيَأْخُذُ بِالذَّنْبِ. ثُمَّ عَادَ فَأَذْنَبَ، فَقَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي، فَقَالَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: عَبْدِي أَذْنَبَ ذَنْباً فَعَلِمَ أَنَّ لَهُ رَبًّا يَغْفِرُ الذَّنْبَ وَيَأْخُذُ بِالذَّنْبِ. ثُمَّ عَادَ فَأَذْنَبَ فَقَالَ: أَيْ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي، فَقَالَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: أَذْنَبَ عَبْدِي ذَنْباً فَعَلِمَ أَنَّ لَهُ رَبًّا يَغْفِرُ الذَّنْبَ وَيَأْخُذُ بِالذَّنْبِ، اعْمَلْ مَا شِئْتَ فَقَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَكَ» أَيْ مَا دُمْتَ تَائِباً أَوَّاهاً مُنِيبًا.
text.en: ‘O Allah, forgive me my sin.’ So He, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ‘My servant committed a sin, then knew that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes to account for sin.’ Then he went back and sinned again, and said: ‘My Lord, forgive me my sin.’ So He, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ‘My servant committed a sin, then knew that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes to account for sin.’ Then he went back and sinned again, and said: ‘My Lord, forgive me my sin.’ So He, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ‘My servant committed a sin, then knew that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes to account for sin. Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.’” That is, as long as you remain repentant, humbly beseeching, and turning back to Him.

text.ar: وَأَبْوَابُ عَفْوِهِ وَغُفْرَانِهِ مَفْتُوحَةٌ، وَلَمْ يَزَلْ وَلَا يَزَالُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا، وَقَدْ وَعَدَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ وَالْعَفْوِ لِمَنْ أَتَى بِأَسْبَابِهَا، كَمَا قَالَ سُبْحَانَهُ: ﴿وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٞ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحٗا ثُمَّ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ﴾ [طه: ٨٢].
text.en: The doors of His pardon and forgiveness are open; He has always been and will always be Pardoning, Forgiving. He has promised forgiveness and pardon to whoever brings about their causes, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴾And indeed, I am the Ever-Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteous deeds and then remains guided﴿ [Ta Ha 20:82].

text.ar: اللَّهُمَّ مُنَّ عَلَيْنَا بِعَفْوِكَ وَأَكْرِمْنَا بِغُفْرَانِكَ، وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ.
text.en: O Allah, bless us with Your pardon, honour us with Your forgiveness, and turn to us in mercy; indeed You are at-Tawwab, ar-Rahim (the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful).
*Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 6099) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 2804).

text.ar: فِي «جَامِعِهِ» (رَقْمُ: ٣٥٤٠) مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَنَسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، وَقَالَ: «غَرِيبٌ» وَفِي بَعْضِ النُّسَخِ: «حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ» وَفِي إِسْنَادِهِ جَهَالَةٌ، وَلَكِنْ لَهُ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ؛ وَلِذَلِكَ حَسَّنَهُ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي «السِّلْسِلَةِ الصَّحِيحَةِ» (رَقْمُ: ١٢٧).
text.en: In his *Jami‘* (no. 3540) from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: “Gharib (unusual)”, and in some copies: “Hasan gharib (sound but unusual)”. Its chain contains an unknown narrator, but it has a supporting narration from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him); that is why al-Albani (may Allah have mercy on him) graded it hasan (sound) in *as-Silsilah as-Sahihah* (no. 127).

text.ar: «الْمُسْنَدُ» (٥/ ١٥٣)، وَ«جَامِعُ التِّرْمِذِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ١٩٨٧)، وَ«مُسْتَدْرَكُ الْحَاكِمِ» (١/ ٥٤) وَهُوَ طَرَفٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، وَصَحَّحَهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ وَالْحَاكِمُ.
text.en: *al-Musnad* (5/153), *Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi* (no. 1987) and *Mustadrak al-Hakim* (1/54). It is part of the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), and at-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim graded it authentic.

text.ar: «صَحِيحُ الْبُخَارِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٧٥٠٧)، وَ«صَحِيحُ مُسْلِمٍ» (رَقْمُ: ٢٧٥٨) وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ.
text.en: *Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 7507) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 2758), and the wording is his.

title.en: al-‘Aliyy, al-A‘la, al-Muta‘al (the Most High, the Most Exalted, the Supremely Exalted)

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٥٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ٦٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَبِّحِ ٱسۡمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَى﴾ [الْأَعْلَى: ١]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِلَّا ٱبۡتِغَآءَ وَجۡهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ﴾ [اللَّيْلِ: ٢٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ ٱلۡمُتَعَالِ﴾ [الرَّعْدِ: ٩][1].
text.en: The Exalted said: ﴾And He is the Most High, the Magnificent﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:255]. And the Exalted said: ﴾And that Allah is the Most High, the Most Great﴿ [al-Hajj 22:62]. And the Exalted said: ﴾Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Exalted﴿ [al-A‘la 87:1]. And the Exalted said: ﴾But only seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most Exalted﴿ [al-Layl 92:20]. And the Exalted said: ﴾Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Supremely Exalted﴿ [ar-Ra‘d 13:9][1].

text.ar: وَهَذِهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ تَدُلُّ عَلَى عُلُوِّهِ الْمُطْلَقِ بِجَمِيعِ الْوُجُوهِ وَالِاعْتِبَارَاتِ:
text.en: These names indicate His absolute highness in every respect and from every angle:

text.ar: فَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ عُلُوَّ ذَاتٍ، قَدِ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ، وَعَلَا عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْكَائِنَاتِ، وَبَايَنَهَا، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ﴾ [طه: ٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى فِي سِتِّ آيَاتٍ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِ﴾ [الْأَعْرَافِ: ٥٤]، أَيْ: عَلَا وَارْتَفَعَ عَلَيْهِ عُلُوّاً يَلِيقُ بِجَلَالِهِ وَكَمَالِهِ وَعَظَمَتِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ.
text.en: He is al-‘Aliyy (the Most High) in the highness of His Essence: He has risen over the Throne, is above all created beings and is separate and distinct from them. The Exalted said: ﴾The Most Merciful rose over the Throne﴿ [Ta Ha 20:5]. And the Exalted said in six verses of the Qur’an: ﴾Then He rose over the Throne﴿ [al-A‘raf 7:54], meaning: He ascended and rose above it in a manner befitting His majesty, perfection and greatness, Glorified is He.

text.ar: وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ عُلُوَّ قَدْرٍ، وَهُوَ عُلُوُّ صِفَاتِهِ وَعَظَمَتِهَا، فَإِنَّ صِفَاتِهِ عَظِيمَةٌ لَا يُمَاثِلُهَا وَلَا يُقَارِبُهَا صِفَةُ أَحَدٍ، بَلْ لَا يُطِيقُ الْعِبَادُ أَنْ يُحِيطُوا بِصِفَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْ صِفَاتِهِ.
text.en: And He is the Most High in the highness of His standing, which is the highness of His attributes and their greatness; for His attributes are mighty, and no one’s attribute resembles them or even comes near them. Indeed, the servants are incapable of comprehending even a single one of His attributes.

text.ar: وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ عُلُوَّ قَهْرٍ، حَيْثُ قَهَرَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ، وَدَانَتْ لَهُ الْكَائِنَاتُ بِأَسْرِهَا، فَجَمِيعُ الْخَلْقِ نَوَاصِيهِمْ بِيَدِهِ، فَلَا يَتَحَرَّكُ مِنْهُمْ مُتَحَرِّكٌ، وَلَا يَسْكُنُ سَاكِنٌ إِلاّ بِإِذْنِهِ، وَمَا شَاءَ كَانَ وَمَا لَمْ يَشَأْ لَمْ يَكُنْ.
text.en: And He is the Most High in the highness of His dominance, for He has subdued everything, and all beings without exception submit to Him. The forelocks of all creation are in His hand; none of them moves and none is still except by His permission. Whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen.

text.ar: هَذَا وَقَدْ تَنَوَّعَتِ الدَّلَائِلُ، وَتَكَاثَرَتِ الْبَرَاهِينُ، وَتَعَدَّدَتِ الشَّوَاهِدُ عَلَى عُلُوِّ اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى عَلَى خَلْقِهِ، حَتَّى إِنَّ الْقُرْآنَ الْكَرِيمَ فِيهِ أَزْيَدُ مِنْ أَلْفِ دَلِيلٍ عَلَى عُلُوِّ اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ، وَهِيَ مُنْدَرِجَةٌ تَحْتَ أَنْوَاعٍ عَدِيدَةٍ، بَيَانُهَا فِيمَا يَلِي:
text.en: The proofs are varied, the evidences numerous and the testimonies many for the highness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, above His creation — so much so that the Noble Qur’an contains more than a thousand proofs of the highness of Allah, Glorified is He. They fall under many types, which are explained as follows:

text.ar: الْأَوَّلُ: التَّصْرِيحُ بِالْفَوْقِيَّةِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦ﴾ [الْأَنْعَامِ: ١٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُم مِّن فَوۡقِهِمۡ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ٥٠].
text.en: The first: explicit mention of His being above. The Exalted said: ﴾And He is the Subduer above His servants﴿ [al-An‘am 6:18]. And the Exalted said: ﴾They fear their Lord above them﴿ [an-Nahl 16:50].

text.ar: وَعَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: «أَنَّ سَعْداً حَكَمَ عَلَى بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ أَنْ يُقْتَلَ مِنْهُمْ كُلُّ مَنْ جَرَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْمُوسَى، وَأَنْ تُسْبَى ذَرَارِيُّهُمْ، وَأَنْ تُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ، فَذُكِرَ ذَلِكَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَقَالَ: «لَقَدْ حَكَمْتَ فِيهِمْ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي حَكَمَ بِهِ فَوْقَ سَبْعِ سَمَوَاتٍ» رَوَاهُ النَّسَائِيُّ فِي «الْكُبْرَى» وَالْبَزَّارُ وَالْحَاكِمُ وَغَيْرُهُمْ[2].
text.en: From Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him): “Sa‘d judged concerning Banu Qurayzah that every one of them on whom the razor had passed should be killed, that their offspring be taken captive and that their wealth be divided. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: ‘You have judged among them with the judgement of Allah, which He passed above seven heavens.’” Reported by an-Nasa’i in *al-Kubra*, al-Bazzar, al-Hakim and others[2].

text.ar: الثَّانِي: التَّصْرِيحُ بِالْعُرُوجِ إِلَيْهِ سُبْحَانَهُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ يَعۡرُجُ إِلَيۡهِ﴾ [السَّجْدَةِ: ٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذِي ٱلۡمَعَارِجِ تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ﴾ [الْمَعَارِجِ: ٣ ـ ٤].
text.en: The second: explicit mention of ascending to Him, Glorified is He. Allah the Exalted said: ﴾He arranges every matter from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him﴿ [as-Sajdah 32:5]. And the Exalted said: ﴾From Allah, Owner of the ways of ascent. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him﴿ [al-Ma‘arij 70:3–4].

text.ar: الثَّالِثُ: التَّصْرِيحُ بِالصُّعُودِ إِلَيْهِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِلَيۡهِ يَصۡعَدُ ٱلۡكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلۡعَمَلُ ٱلصَّٰلِحُ يَرۡفَعُهُۥ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ١٠].
text.en: The third: explicit mention of rising up to Him. The Exalted said: ﴾To Him rises the good word, and righteous deeds raise it up﴿ [Fatir 35:10].

text.ar: وَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[3] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «مَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِعَدْلِ تَمْرَةٍ مِنْ كَسْبٍ طَيِّبٍ، وَلَا يَصْعَدُ إِلَى اللَّهِ إِلاّ الطَّيِّبُ؛ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَتَقَبَّلُهَا بِيَمِينِهِ، ثُمَّ يُرَبِّيهَا لِصَاحِبِهَا كَمَا يُرَبِّي أَحَدُكُمْ فَلُوَّهُ حَتَّى تَكُونَ مِثْلَ الْجَبَلِ».
text.en: In the *Two Sahihs*[3] from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from good earnings — and nothing rises up to Allah except what is good — Allah accepts it with His right hand, then nurtures it for its owner as one of you nurtures his foal, until it becomes like a mountain.”

text.ar: الرَّابِعُ: التَّصْرِيحُ بِرَفْعِ بَعْضِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ إِلَيْهِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡهِ﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١٥٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ﴾ [آلِ عِمْرَانَ: ٥٥].
text.en: The fourth: explicit mention of some created beings being raised to Him. The Exalted said: ﴾Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself﴿ [an-Nisa’ 4:158]. And the Exalted said: ﴾I will take you and raise you up to Myself﴿ [Al ‘Imran 3:55].

text.ar: الْخَامِسُ: التَّصْرِيحُ بِتَنْزِيلِ الْكِتَابِ مِنْهُ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ١]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [السَّجْدَةِ: ٢].
text.en: The fifth: explicit mention of the Book being sent down from Him. The Exalted said: ﴾The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴿ [az-Zumar 39:1]. And the Exalted said: ﴾The revelation of the Book, in which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds﴿ [as-Sajdah 32:2].

text.ar: السَّادِسُ: التَّصْرِيحُ بِأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي السَّمَاءِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ أَمۡ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبٗاۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ كَيۡفَ نَذِيرِ﴾ [الْمُلْكِ: ١٦ ـ ١٧].
text.en: The sixth: explicit mention that He, the Exalted, is in the heaven. The Exalted said: ﴾Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up, when suddenly it quakes? Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how My warning was﴿ [al-Mulk 67:16–17].

text.ar: وَفِي «صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ»[4] مِنْ حَدِيثِ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ لِلْجَارِيَةِ: «أَيْنَ اللَّهُ؟ قَالَتْ: فِي السَّمَاءِ. قَالَ: مَنْ أَنَا؟ قَالَتْ: أَنْتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ. قَالَ: أَعْتِقْهَا فَإِنَّهَا مُؤْمِنَةٌ».
text.en: In *Sahih Muslim*[4], from the hadith of Mu‘awiyah ibn al-Hakam (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet ﷺ said to the slave girl: “Where is Allah?” She said: “In the heaven.” He said: “Who am I?” She said: “You are the Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Free her, for she is a believer.”

text.ar: وَفِي التِّرْمِذِيِّ[5]، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْكُمْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ».
text.en: In at-Tirmidhi[5], from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Those who show mercy are shown mercy by ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful). Show mercy to those on the earth, and the One who is in the heaven will show mercy to you.”

text.ar: السَّابِعُ: التَّصْرِيحُ بِرَفْعِ الْأَيْدِي إِلَيْهِ، رَوَى التِّرْمِذِيُّ[6] عَنْ سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ يَسْتَحْيِي إِذَا رَفَعَ الرَّجُلُ إِلَيْهِ يَدَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْراً خَائِبَتَيْنِ».
text.en: The seventh: explicit mention of raising the hands to Him. At-Tirmidhi[6] reported from Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, Allah is Modest and Generous; when a man raises his hands to Him, He is too shy to send them back empty and disappointed.”

text.ar: الثَّامِنُ: الْإِشَارَةُ إِلَيْهِ حِسّاً إِلَى الْعُلُوِّ كَمَا أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ، لَمَّا كَانَ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ وَسَلَامُهُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْمَجْمَعِ الْأَعْظَمِ فِي الْيَوْمِ الْأَعْظَمِ، قَالَ لِلنَّاسِ: «وَأَنْتُمْ تُسْأَلُونَ عَنِّي فَمَا أَنْتُمْ قَائِلُونَ؟ قَالُوا: نَشْهَدُ أَنَّكَ قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ وَأَدَّيْتَ وَنَصَحْتَ. فَقَالَ بِإِصْبَعِهِ السَّبَّابَةِ يَرْفَعُهَا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَيَنْكُتُهَا إِلَى النَّاسِ: اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدْ، اللَّهُمَّ اشْهَدْ ـ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[7].
text.en: The eighth: pointing to Him physically towards what is above, just as the one who knew Him best pointed to Him. When he — Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him — was at the greatest gathering on the greatest day, he said to the people: “And you will be asked about me, so what will you say?” They said: “We bear witness that you have conveyed the message, fulfilled your trust and given sincere counsel.” Then he gestured with his index finger, raising it to the sky and pointing it down towards the people: “O Allah, bear witness; O Allah, bear witness” — three times. Reported by Muslim[7].

text.ar: التَّاسِعُ: إِخْبَارُهُ ﷺ أَنَّهُ تَرَدَّدَ بَيْنَ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَبَيْنَ رَبِّهِ لَيْلَةَ الْمِعْرَاجِ بِسَبَبِ تَخْفِيفِ الصَّلَاةِ، فَيَصْعَدُ إِلَى رَبِّهِ، ثُمَّ يَعُودُ إِلَى مُوسَى عِدَّةَ مِرَارٍ، وَحَدِيثُ الْمِعْرَاجِ مُخَرَّجٌ فِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[8] وَغَيْرِهِمَا.
text.en: The ninth: his ﷺ informing us that, on the night of the Mi‘raj, he went back and forth between Musa (peace be upon him) and his Lord to have the prayer reduced; he would ascend to his Lord, then return to Musa, several times. The hadith of the Mi‘raj is recorded in the *Two Sahihs*[8] and elsewhere.

text.ar: الْعَاشِرُ: إِخْبَارُهُ تَعَالَى عَنْ فِرْعَوْنَ أَنَّهُ رَامَ الصُّعُودَ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ لِيَطَّلِعَ إِلَى إِلَهِ مُوسَى، فَيُكَذِّبَهُ فِيمَا أَخْبَرَهُ مِنْ أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ فَوْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ: ﴿وَقَالَ فِرۡعَوۡنُ يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ ٱبۡنِ لِي صَرۡحٗا لَّعَلِّيٓ أَبۡلُغُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَٰبَ أَسۡبَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُۥ كَٰذِبٗاۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرۡعَوۡنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِۚ وَمَا كَيۡدُ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِلَّا فِي تَبَابٖ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ٣٦ ـ ٣٧]، أَيْ: إِنِّي لَأَظُنُّ مُوسَى كَاذِباً فِيمَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ مِنْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ فِي السَّمَاءِ، فَمَنْ نَفَى عُلُوَّ اللَّهِ فَفِيهِ شَبَهٌ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ، وَمَنْ أَثْبَتَ عُلُوَّ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ عَلَى نَهْجِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَنَهْجِ جَمِيعِ النَّبِيِّينَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ وَسَلَامُهُ.
text.en: The tenth: His informing us, the Exalted, about Pharaoh, that he sought to ascend to the heaven to look at the deity of Musa, so as to belie him in what he had informed of — that He, Glorified is He, is above the heavens: ﴾And Pharaoh said: O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways — the ways into the heavens — and look at the deity of Musa; and indeed, I think he is a liar. And thus the evil of his deed was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was turned away from the path. And the plotting of Pharaoh was nothing but in ruin﴿ [Ghafir 40:36–37], meaning: I think Musa is lying in what he has informed of, that Allah is in the heaven. So whoever denies the highness of Allah has some resemblance to Pharaoh, and whoever affirms the highness of Allah is upon the way of Musa (peace be upon him) and the way of all the prophets, Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them.

text.ar: فَهَذِهِ الْأَدِلَّةُ وَنَظَائِرُهَا كَثِيرٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ؛ تَضَمَّنَتْ إِثْبَاتَ عُلُوِّ اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى، وَأَنَّهُ عَالٍ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَلَا شَيْءَ فَوْقَهُ، بَلْ هُوَ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدِ كَمَا أَخْبَرَ بِذَلِكَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ، وَكَمَا أَخْبَرَ بِذَلِكَ عَنْهُ رَسُولُهُ ﷺ، وَهُوَ أَمْرٌ مُتَقَرِّرٌ مُجْمَعٌ عَلَيْهِ بَيْنَ سَلَفِ الْأُمَّةِ وَأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ.
text.en: These proofs, and the many like them in the Book and the Sunnah, contain the affirmation of the highness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: that He is high over everything and above everything, with nothing above Him; rather, He is above the Glorious Throne, as He has informed about Himself and as His Messenger ﷺ has informed about Him. This is an established matter, agreed upon by consensus among the Salaf of this Ummah and the imams of the Muslims.

text.ar: قَالَ أَبُو نَصْرٍ السِّجْزِيُّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ «الْإِبَانَةِ»: «وَأَئِمَّتُنَا كَسُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيِّ، وَمَالِكِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ، وَسُفْيَانَ بْنِ عُيَيْنَةَ، وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ، وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، وَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ ابْنِ الْمُبَارَكِ، وَفُضَيْلِ بْنِ عِيَاضٍ، وَأَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَنْبَلٍ، وَإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ رَاهَوَيْهِ؛ مُتَّفِقُونَ عَلَى أَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ بِذَاتِهِ فَوْقَ الْعَرْشِ، وَأَنَّ عِلْمَهُ بِكُلِّ مَكَانٍ»[9].
text.en: Abu Nasr as-Sijzi (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his book *al-Ibanah*: “Our imams, such as Sufyan ath-Thawri, Malik ibn Anas, Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, Hammad ibn Salamah, Hammad ibn Zayd, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, are agreed that Allah, Glorified is He, is with His Essence above the Throne, and that His knowledge is in every place.”[9]

text.ar: وَالْإِيمَانُ بِعُلُوِّ اللَّهِ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ يُورِثُ الْعَبْدَ تَعْظِيمًا لِلَّهِ وَذُلاًّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، وَانْكِسَاراً لَهُ، وَتَنْزِيهاً لَهُ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْعُيُوبِ، وَإِخْلَاصاً فِي عِبَادَتِهِ، وَبُعْداً عَنِ اتِّخَاذِ الْأَنْدَادِ وَالشُّرَكَاءِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ هُوَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ٦٢].
text.en: Belief in Allah’s highness above His creation produces in the servant reverence for Allah, humility before Him and brokenness towards Him, declaring Him free of deficiencies and faults, sincerity in worshipping Him, and keeping far from taking rivals and partners besides Him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴾That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Most Great﴿ [al-Hajj 22:62].

text.ar: وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا لَهُمۡ فِيهِمَا مِن شِرۡكٖ وَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡهُم مِّن ظَهِيرٖ وَلَا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا لِمَنۡ أَذِنَ لَهُۥۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَن قُلُوبِهِمۡ قَالُواْ مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ ٱلۡحَقَّۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ﴾ [سَبَأٍ: ٢٢ ـ ٢٣].
text.en: And the Exalted said: ﴾Say: Call upon those you claim besides Allah. They do not possess an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in either, nor does He have any helper among them. And intercession will not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits. Until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they will say: What did your Lord say? They will say: The truth. And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴿ [Saba’ 34:22–23].

text.ar: قَرَأَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ: «الْمُتَعَالِي» بِيَاءٍ فِي الْوَصْلِ وَالْوَقْفِ، وَقَرَأَ الْبَاقُونَ بِحَذْفِهَا فِي الْحَالَيْنِ. انْظُرْ: «الْمِفْتَاحَ فِي اخْتِلَافِ الْقُرَّاءِ السَّبْعِ» لِأَبِي الْقَاسِمِ الْقُرْطُبِيِّ (٢/ ٦٣٩).
text.en: Ibn Kathir recited “al-Muta‘ali” with a ya’ both when continuing and when pausing, while the rest recited it without it in both cases. See: *al-Miftah fi Ikhtilaf al-Qurra’ as-Sab‘ah* by Abu al-Qasim al-Qurtubi (2/639).

text.ar: «السُّنَنُ الْكُبْرَى» (رَقْمُ: ٥٩٠٦) ـ وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ ـ، وَ«مُسْنَدُ الْبَزَّارِ» (رَقْمُ: ١٠٩١)، وَ«مُسْتَدْرَكُ الْحَاكِمِ» (٢/ ١٢٤). وَحَسَّنَهُ الْحَافِظُ ابْنُ حَجَرٍ فِي «مُوَافَقَةِ الْخُبْرِ الْخَبَرَ» (٢/ ٤٣٩)، وَانْظُرْ: «السِّلْسِلَةَ الصَّحِيحَةَ» (رَقْمُ: ٢٧٤٥).
text.en: *as-Sunan al-Kubra* (no. 5906) — the wording is his — *Musnad al-Bazzar* (no. 1091) and *Mustadrak al-Hakim* (2/124). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar graded it hasan (sound) in *Muwafaqat al-Khubr al-Khabar* (2/439). And see: *as-Silsilah as-Sahihah* (no. 2745).

text.ar: «صَحِيحُ الْبُخَارِيِّ» (رَقْمُ:٧٤٣٠) ـ وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ ـ، وَ«صَحِيحُ مُسْلِمٍ» (رَقْمُ: ١٠١٤).
text.en: *Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 7430) — the wording is his — and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 1014).
In his *Jami‘* (no. 1924), and he graded it authentic. It was also reported by Abu Dawud (no. 4941), Ahmad (2/160), al-Hakim (4/159) and others.

In his *Jami‘* (no. 3556), and he graded it authentic. It was also reported by Abu Dawud (no. 1488), Ibn Majah (no. 3865), Ahmad (5/138), Ibn Hibban (nos. 876, 880) and al-Hakim (1/497), who graded it authentic.

text.ar: (رَقْمُ: ١٢١٨) وَهُوَ جُزْءٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ جَابِرٍ الطَّوِيلِ فِي صِفَةِ حَجَّةِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
text.en: (no. 1218). It is part of the long hadith of Jabir describing the Hajj of the Prophet ﷺ.

text.ar: «صَحِيحُ الْبُخَارِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٣٤٢)، وَ«صَحِيحُ مُسْلِمٍ» (رَقْمُ: ١٦٣) مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَنَسِ ابْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ الْغِفَارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: *Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 342) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 163), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him).

text.ar: نَقَلَهُ عَنْهُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ فِي «الْمَجْمُوعِ» (٣/ ٢٦٢).
text.en: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah quoted it from him in *al-Majmu‘* (3/262).

title.en: al-Kabir, al-‘Azim (the Most Great, the Magnificent)

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ﴾ [لُقْمَانَ: ٣٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَٱلۡحُكۡمُ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡعَلِيِّ ٱلۡكَبِيرِ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ١٢]، ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٥٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَسَبِّحۡ بِٱسۡمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ﴾ [الْحَاقَّةِ: ٥٢].
text.en: The Exalted said: ﴾That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Most Great﴿ [Luqman 31:30]. And the Exalted said: ﴾So the judgement belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great﴿ [Ghafir 40:12], ﴾And He is the Most High, the Magnificent﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:255]. And the Exalted said: ﴾So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent﴿ [al-Haqqah 69:52].

text.ar: وَالْكَبِيرُ الْعَظِيمُ أَيْ: الَّذِي لَهُ الْكِبْرِيَاءُ نَعْتاً وَالْعَظَمَةُ وَصْفاً، قَالَ تَعَالَى فِي الْحَدِيثِ الْقُدْسِيِّ: «الْكِبْرِيَاءُ رِدَائِي، وَالْعَظَمَةُ إِزَارِي، فَمَنْ نَازَعَنِي وَاحِداً مِنْهُمَا قَذَفْتُهُ فِي النَّارِ»، رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ وَأَبُو دَاوُدَ[1].
text.en: al-Kabir (the Most Great) and al-‘Azim (the Magnificent) means: the One to whom grandeur belongs as a description and magnificence as an attribute. The Exalted said in the hadith qudsi: “Grandeur is My cloak and magnificence is My lower garment; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will cast him into the Fire.” Reported by Ahmad and Abu Dawud[1].

text.ar: وَمَعَانِي الْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَالْعَظَمَةِ نَوْعَانِ:
text.en: The meanings of grandeur and magnificence are of two kinds:

text.ar: أَحَدُهُمَا: يَرْجِعُ إِلَى صِفَاتِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ، وَأَنَّ لَهُ جَمِيعَ مَعَانِي الْعَظَمَةِ وَالْجَلَالِ، كَالْقُوَّةِ، وَالْعِزَّةِ، وَكَمَالِ الْقُدْرَةِ، وَسَعَةِ الْعِلْمِ، وَكَمَالِ الْمَجْدِ، وَغَيْرِهَا مِنْ أَوْصَافِ الْعَظَمَةِ وَالْكِبْرِيَاءِ، وَمِنْ عَظَمَتِهِ أَنَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعَ وَالْأَرَضِينَ السَّبْعَ فِي يَدِ اللَّهِ كَخَرْدَلَةٍ فِي يَدِ أَحَدِنَا، كَمَا قَالَ ذَلِكَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا.
text.en: The first: it goes back to His attributes, Glorified is He, and that to Him belong all the meanings of magnificence and majesty, such as strength, might, perfect power, vast knowledge, perfect glory and other attributes of magnificence and grandeur. Part of His magnificence is that the seven heavens and the seven earths are in the hand of Allah like a mustard seed in the hand of one of us, as Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said.

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعٗا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ٦٧]، فَلَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى الْكِبْرِيَاءُ وَالْعَظَمَةُ الْوَصْفَانِ اللَّذَانِ لَا يُقَادَرُ قَدْرُهُمَا، وَلَا يَبْلُغُ الْعِبَادُ كُنْهَهُمَا، وَقَدْ صَحَّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَسُجُودِهِ: «سُبْحَانَ ذِي الْجَبَرُوتِ، وَالْمَلَكُوتِ، وَالْكِبْرِيَاءِ، وَالْعَظَمَةِ»، رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ وَأَبُو دَاوُدَ وَالنَّسَائِيُّ[2].
text.en: The Exalted said: ﴾They have not esteemed Allah as He truly deserves, while the whole earth will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴿ [az-Zumar 39:67]. So to Him, Glorified and Exalted is He, belong grandeur and magnificence, the two attributes whose extent cannot be measured and whose true nature the servants cannot reach. It is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he used to say in his bowing and his prostration: “Glory be to the Possessor of might, dominion, grandeur and magnificence.” Reported by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and an-Nasa’i[2].

text.ar: النَّوْعُ الثَّانِي: أَنَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحِقُّ أَحَدٌ التَّعْظِيمَ وَالتَّكْبِيرَ وَالْإِجْلَالَ وَالتَّمْجِيدَ غَيْرُهُ، فَيَسْتَحِقُّ عَلَى الْعِبَادِ أَنْ يُعَظِّمُوهُ بِقُلُوبِهِمْ وَأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَأَعْمَالِهِمْ، وَذَلِكَ بِبَذْلِ الْجُهْدِ فِي مَعْرِفَتِهِ وَمَحَبَّتِهِ وَالذُّلِّ لَهُ وَالْخَوْفِ مِنْهُ، وَمِنْ تَعْظِيمِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنْ يُطَاعَ فَلَا يُعْصَى، وَيُذْكَرَ فَلَا يُنْسَى، وَيُشْكَرَ فَلَا يُكْفَرَ، وَمِنْ تَعْظِيمِهِ وَإِجْلَالِهِ أَنْ يُخْضَعَ لِأَوَامِرِهِ وَشَرْعِهِ وَحُكْمِهِ، وَأَنْ لَا يُعْتَرَضَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ أَوْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْ شَرْعِهِ، وَمِنْ تَعْظِيمِهِ تَعْظِيمُ مَا عَظَّمَهُ وَاحْتَرَمَهُ مِنْ زَمَانٍ وَمَكَانٍ وَأَشْخَاصٍ وَأَعْمَالٍ، وَالْعِبَادَةُ رُوحُهَا تَعْظِيمُ الْبَارِي وَتَكْبِيرُهُ؛ وَلِهَذَا شُرِعَتِ التَّكْبِيرَاتُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ فِي افْتِتَاحِهَا وَتَنَقُّلَاتِهَا لِيَسْتَحْضِرَ الْعَبْدُ مَعْنَى تَعْظِيمِهِ فِي هَذِهِ الْعِبَادَةِ الَّتِي هِيَ أَجَلُّ الْعِبَادَاتِ.
text.en: The second kind: that no one other than Him deserves reverence, being declared great, exaltation and glorification. It is His right over the servants that they revere Him with their hearts, their tongues and their deeds, by exerting effort in knowing Him, loving Him, humbling themselves before Him and fearing Him. Part of revering Him, Glorified is He, is that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, thanked and not met with ingratitude. Part of revering and exalting Him is submitting to His commands, His law and His judgement, and not objecting to anything of His creation or anything of His law. Part of revering Him is revering what He has revered and made sacred of times, places, persons and deeds. The spirit of worship is revering al-Bari’ (the Originator) and declaring His greatness; this is why the takbirs (saying “Allahu akbar”) were legislated in the prayer, at its opening and at its transitions, so that the servant keeps present the meaning of revering Him in this act of worship, which is the most majestic of all acts of worship.

text.ar: بَلْ إِنَّ التَّكْبِيرَ مُصَاحِبٌ لِلْمُسْلِمِ فِي عِبَادَاتٍ عَدِيدَةٍ وَطَاعَاتٍ مُتَنَوِّعَةٍ، فَالْمُسْلِمُ يُكَبِّرُ اللَّهَ عِنْدَمَا يُكْمِلُ عِدَّةَ الصِّيَامِ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ١٨٥]، وَيُكَبِّرُ اللَّهَ فِي الْحَجِّ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ مِنكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمۡ لِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ٣٧].
text.en: Indeed, takbir accompanies the Muslim in many acts of worship and various acts of obedience. The Muslim declares Allah’s greatness when he completes the number of days of fasting, as the Exalted said: ﴾And that you complete the number of days and declare Allah’s greatness for having guided you, and that you may be grateful﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:185]. And he declares Allah’s greatness in Hajj; the Exalted said: ﴾Neither their meat nor their blood reaches Allah, but what reaches Him is the piety from you. Thus has He subjected them to you, that you may declare Allah’s greatness for having guided you; and give glad tidings to those who do good﴿ [al-Hajj 22:37].

text.ar: وَبِهَذَا تَتَبَيَّنُ مَكَانَةُ التَّكْبِيرِ وَجَلَالَةُ قَدْرِهِ، وَعِظَمُ شَأْنِهِ مِنَ الدِّينِ، وَالتَّكْبِيرُ يُرَادُ بِهِ أَنْ يَكُونَ اللَّهُ عِنْدَ الْعَبْدِ أَكْبَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، كَمَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ لِعَدِيِّ بْنِ حَاتِمٍ: «مَا يُفِرُّكَ أَنْ تَقُولَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، فَهَلْ تَعْلَمُ مِنْ إِلَهٍ سِوَى اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ: لَا. قَالَ: ثُمَّ تَكَلَّمَ سَاعَةً، ثُمَّ قَالَ: إِنَّمَا تَفِرُّ أَنْ تَقُولَ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ شَيْئاً أَكْبَرَ مِنَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ: لَا» الْحَدِيثَ. رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ وَالتِّرْمِذِيُّ وَابْنُ حِبَّانَ[3].
text.en: By this the standing of takbir becomes clear, along with the majesty of its rank and the greatness of its place in the religion. What is meant by takbir is that Allah should be, for the servant, greater than everything, as the Prophet ﷺ said to ‘Adi ibn Hatim: “What makes you flee from saying ‘La ilaha illa Allah’ (there is no god but Allah)? Do you know of any god besides Allah?” He said: I said: “No.” He said: Then he spoke for a while, then said: “You only flee from saying ‘Allahu akbar’; do you know of anything greater than Allah?” He said: I said: “No.” — to the end of the hadith. Reported by Ahmad, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Hibban[3].

text.ar: وَبِهِ يَتَبَيَّنُ مَعْنَى (اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ) أَيْ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَلَا شَيْءَ أَكْبَرُ وَلَا أَعْظَمُ مِنْهُ، وَلِهَذَا يُقَالُ: إِنَّ أَبْلَغَ لَفْظَةٍ لِلْعَرَبِ فِي مَعْنَى التَّعْظِيمِ وَالْإِجْلَالِ هِيَ: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، أَيْ صِفْهُ بِأَنَّهُ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَاعْتَقِدْ أَنَّهُ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ.
text.en: Through this, the meaning of (Allahu akbar) becomes clear: that is, greater than everything; nothing is greater or more magnificent than Him. This is why it is said that the most eloquent expression the Arabs have for the meaning of reverence and exaltation is: Allahu akbar — that is, describe Him as greater than everything, and believe that He is greater than everything.

text.ar: وَكَمَا تَقَدَّمَ؛ التَّكْبِيرُ مَعْنَاهُ: التَّعْظِيمُ، لَكِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مُرَادِفاً لَهُ، فَالْكِبْرِيَاءُ أَكْمَلُ مِنَ الْعَظَمَةِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَتَضَمَّنُهَا وَيَزِيدُ عَلَيْهَا فِي الْمَعْنَى، وَلِهَذَا يَقُولُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَفِي قَوْلِهِ «اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ» إِثْبَاتُ عَظَمَتِهِ، فَإِنَّ الْكِبْرِيَاءَ تَتَضَمَّنُ الْعَظَمَةَ، وَلَكِنَّ الْكِبْرِيَاءَ أَكْمَلُ. وَلِهَذَا جَاءَتِ الْأَلْفَاظُ الْمَشْرُوعَةُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَالْأَذَانِ بِقَوْلِ: «اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ»، فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَكْمَلُ مِنْ قَوْلِ: «اللَّهُ أَعْظَمُ»، كَمَا ثَبَتَ فِي «الصَّحِيحِ» عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: الْكِبْرِيَاءُ رِدَائِي، وَالْعَظَمَةُ إِزَارِي، فَمَنْ نَازَعَنِي وَاحِداً مِنْهُمَا عَذَّبْتُهُ»، فَجَعَلَ الْعَظَمَةَ كَالْإِزَارِ، وَالْكِبْرِيَاءَ كَالرِّدَاءِ، وَمَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ الرِّدَاءَ أَشْرَفُ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ التَّكْبِيرُ أَبْلَغَ مِنَ التَّعْظِيمِ صَرَّحَ بِلَفْظِهِ، وَتَضَمَّنَ ذَلِكَ التَّعْظِيمَ»[4] اهـ.
text.en: As has preceded, takbir means reverence, but it is not synonymous with it, for grandeur is more complete than magnificence, because it includes it and adds to it in meaning. This is why Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) says: “In his saying ‘Allahu akbar’ there is an affirmation of His magnificence, for grandeur includes magnificence, but grandeur is more complete. This is why the wording legislated in the prayer and the adhan came as saying ‘Allahu akbar’, for that is more complete than saying ‘Allahu a‘zam (Allah is more magnificent)’, as is established in the *Sahih* from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: ‘Allah the Exalted says: Grandeur is My cloak and magnificence is My lower garment; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will punish him.’ So He made magnificence like the lower garment and grandeur like the cloak, and it is known that the cloak is the nobler. So since takbir is more far-reaching than ta‘zim (declaring magnificence), its wording was stated explicitly, and that included ta‘zim.”[4] End quote.

text.ar: وَهَاهُنَا أَمْرٌ يَنْبَغِي التَّنَبُّهُ لَهُ وَعَدَمُ إِغْفَالِهِ، وَهُوَ أَنَّ الْمُسْلِمَ إِذَا اعْتَقَدَ وَآمَنَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى أَكْبَرُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَأَنَّ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ مَهْمَا كَبُرَ يَصْغُرُ عِنْدَ كِبْرِيَاءِ اللَّهِ وَعَظَمَتِهِ، عَلِمَ مِنْ خِلَالِ ذَلِكَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ أَنَّ كِبْرِيَاءَ الرَّبِّ وَعَظَمَتَهُ وَجَلَالَهُ وَجَمَالَهُ وَسَائِرَ أَوْصَافِهِ وَنُعُوتِهِ أَمْرٌ لَا يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تُحِيطَ بِهِ الْعُقُولُ أَوْ تَتَصَوَّرَهُ الْأَفْهَامُ، أَوْ تُدْرِكَهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَالْأَفْكَارُ، فَاللَّهُ أَعْظَمُ وَأَكْبَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ﴿وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدٗا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٞ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِيّٞ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّۖ وَكَبِّرۡهُ تَكۡبِيرَۢا﴾ [الْإِسْرَاءِ: ١١١].
text.en: There is a matter here that should be noted and not overlooked: when the Muslim believes with conviction that Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, is greater than everything, and that everything, however great, becomes small before Allah’s grandeur and magnificence, he knows from that with certain knowledge that the grandeur of the Lord, His magnificence, majesty, beauty and all His other attributes and descriptions are beyond what minds can encompass, what understanding can conceive, or what eyes and thoughts can grasp. Allah is more magnificent and greater than that: ﴾And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son and has no partner in His dominion and has no protector out of weakness; and declare His greatness with great glorification﴿ [al-Isra’ 17:111].

text.ar: وَأَمْرٌ آخَرُ، أَلَا وَهُوَ أَنَّ مَنْ عَلِمَ مَدْلُولَ هَذَيْنِ الِاسْمَيْنِ ذَلَّ لِرَبِّهِ وَانْكَسَرَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، وَصَرَفَ لَهُ أَنْوَاعَ الْعِبَادَةِ، وَاعْتَقَدَ أَنَّهُ الْمُسْتَحِقُّ لَهَا دُونَ سِوَاهُ، وَعَرَفَ أَنَّ كُلَّ مُشْرِكٍ لَمْ يَقْدُرْ رَبَّهُ الْعَظِيمَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعٗا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ٦٧]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارٗا وَقَدۡ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَطۡوَارًا أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٖ طِبَاقٗا وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورٗا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجٗا وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتٗا ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيهَا وَيُخۡرِجُكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجٗا وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِسَاطٗا لِّتَسۡلُكُواْ مِنۡهَا سُبُلٗا فِجَاجٗا﴾ [نُوحٍ: ١٣ ـ ٢٠].
text.en: Another matter is that whoever knows what these two names indicate humbles himself before his Lord and is broken before Him, directs all kinds of worship to Him, believes that He alone deserves it and none besides Him, and knows that everyone who associates partners with Allah has not esteemed his Magnificent Lord as He truly deserves, as the Exalted said: ﴾They have not esteemed Allah as He truly deserves, while the whole earth will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴿ [az-Zumar 39:67]. And the Exalted said: ﴾What is the matter with you that you do not hope for Allah’s majesty, when He has created you in stages? Do you not see how Allah has created seven heavens one above another, and made the moon a light in them and made the sun a lamp? And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth like plants. Then He will return you into it and bring you out once again. And Allah has made the earth a wide expanse for you, so that you may travel along its spacious paths﴿ [Nuh 71:13–20].

text.ar: وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ! أَيْنَ ذَهَبَتْ عُقُولُ هَؤُلَاءِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ حِينَ صَرَفُوا ذُلَّهُمْ وَخُضُوعَهُمْ وَانْكِسَارَهُمْ وَرَجَاءَهُمْ وَخَوْفَهُمْ وَرَغَبَهُمْ وَرَهَبَهُمْ وَحُبَّهُمْ وَطَمَعَهُمْ إِلَى مَخْلُوقَاتٍ ضَئِيلَةٍ، وَكَائِنَاتٍ ذَلِيلَةٍ، لَا تَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِهَا شَيْئاً مِنَ النَّفْعِ وَالضُّرِّ، فَضْلاً عَنْ أَنْ تَمْلِكَهُ لِغَيْرِهَا، وَتَرَكُوا الْخُضُوعَ وَالذُّلَّ لِلرَّبِّ الْعَظِيمِ وَالْكَبِيرِ الْمُتَعَالِ، وَالْخَالِقِ الْجَلِيلِ تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ، وَهُوَ وَحْدَهُ الْمُسْتَحِقُّ لِلتَّعْظِيمِ وَالْإِجْلَالِ وَالتَّأَلُّهِ وَالْخُضُوعِ وَالذُّلِّ، وَهَذَا خَالِصُ حَقِّهِ، فَمِنْ أَقْبَحِ الظُّلْمِ أَنْ يُعْطَى حَقُّهُ لِغَيْرِهِ، أَوْ يُشْرَكَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ غَيْرِهِ فِيهِ، وَمَنِ اتَّخَذَ الشُّرَكَاءَ وَالْأَنْدَادَ لَهُ مَا قَدَرَ اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ، وَلَا عَظَّمَهُ حَقَّ تَعْظِيمِهِ، سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى الَّذِي عَنَتْ لَهُ الْوُجُوهُ، وَخَشَعَتْ لَهُ الْأَصْوَاتُ، وَوَجِلَتِ الْقُلُوبُ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ، وَذَلَّتْ لَهُ الرِّقَابُ، تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ.
text.en: Glory be to Allah! Where did the minds of these idolaters go when they directed their humility, submission, brokenness, hope, fear, longing, dread, love and eager desire towards puny created things and lowly beings that possess no benefit or harm for themselves, let alone for others, and abandoned submission and humility before the Magnificent Lord, al-Kabir al-Muta‘al (the Most Great, the Most Exalted), the Majestic Creator? Exalted is Allah above what they describe, and glorified is Allah above what they associate with Him! He alone deserves to be magnified, revered, worshipped, submitted to and humbled before. This is purely His right, so it is among the ugliest of wrongs that His right be given to another, or that another be made His partner in it. Whoever takes partners and rivals to Him has not esteemed Allah as He truly deserves to be esteemed, nor magnified Him as He truly deserves to be magnified. Glorified and Exalted is He, before whom faces are humbled, voices are hushed, hearts tremble in awe of Him, and necks are bowed. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

text.ar: «مُسْنَدُ الْإِمَامِ أَحْمَدَ» (٢/ ٢٤٨)، وَ«سُنَنُ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» (رَقْمُ: ٤٠٩٠) وَغَيْرُهُمَا مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، وَإِسْنَادُهُ حَسَنٌ.
text.en: *Musnad al-Imam Ahmad* (2/248), *Sunan Abi Dawud* (no. 4090) and others, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Its chain is good (hasan).

text.ar: «مُسْنَدُ الْإِمَامِ أَحْمَدَ» (٢/ ٢٢٣)، وَ«سُنَنُ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» (رَقْمُ: ٨٧٣)، وَ«سُنَنُ النَّسَائِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ١٠٤٩)، وَغَيْرُهُمْ مِنْ حَدِيثِ عَوْفِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ الْأَشْجَعِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، وَإِسْنَادُهُ صَحِيحٌ.
text.en: *Musnad al-Imam Ahmad* (2/223), *Sunan Abi Dawud* (no. 873), *Sunan an-Nasa'i* (no. 1049) and others, from the hadith of ‘Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja‘i (may Allah be pleased with him). Its chain is authentic.

text.ar: «مُسْنَدُ الْإِمَامِ أَحْمَدَ» (٤/ ٣٧٨)، وَ«جَامِعُ التِّرْمِذِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٢٩٥٣) ـ وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ ـ، وَ«صَحِيحُ ابْنِ حِبَّانَ» (رَقْمُ: ٧٢٠٦) وَغَيْرُهُمْ. وَحَسَّنَهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ.
text.en: *Musnad al-Imam Ahmad* (4/378), *Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi* (no. 2953) — the wording is his — *Sahih Ibn Hibban* (no. 7206) and others. At-Tirmidhi graded it good (hasan).
*Majmu‘ al-Fatawa* (10/253).

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَاءَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ «الْقَوِيُّ» فِي عِدَّةِ مَوَاضِعَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ، مِنْهَا قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱللَّهُ لَطِيفُۢ بِعِبَادِهِۦ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ﴾ [الشُّورَى: ١٩]، وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَغۡلِبَنَّ أَنَا۠ وَرُسُلِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٞ﴾ [الْمُجَادَلَةِ: ٢١]، وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ﴾ [هُودٍ: ٦٦].
text.en: The name of Allah “al-Qawiyy” (the All-Strong) has come in several places in the Noble Qur'an, among them His saying, exalted is He: ﴾Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills. And He is the All-Strong, the Almighty﴿ [ash-Shura 42:19], His saying: ﴾Allah has decreed, “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.” Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, Almighty﴿ [al-Mujadilah 58:21], and His saying: ﴾Indeed, your Lord — He is the All-Strong, the Almighty﴿ [Hud 11:66].

text.ar: وَاسْمُ اللَّهِ «الْمَتِينُ» لَمْ يَرِدْ إِلَّا فِي مَوْضِعٍ وَاحِدٍ مَقْرُونًا بِوَصْفِ اللَّهِ بِأَنَّهُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلۡقُوَّةِ ٱلۡمَتِينُ﴾ [الذَّارِيَاتِ: ٥٨].
text.en: As for the name of Allah “al-Matin” (the Firm), it has come in only one place, joined with Allah's description of Himself as the Possessor of strength. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Indeed, it is Allah who is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴿ [adh-Dhariyat 51:58].

text.ar: وَمَعْنَى «الْمَتِينِ» أَيْ: شَدِيدُ الْقُوَّةِ، وَمَعْنَى «الْقَوِيِّ» أَيْ: الَّذِي لَا يُعْجِزُهُ شَيْءٌ، وَلَا يَغْلِبُهُ غَالِبٌ، وَلَا يَرُدُّ قَضَاءَهُ رَادٌّ، يَنْفُذُ أَمْرُهُ وَيَمْضِي قَضَاؤُهُ فِي خَلْقِهِ، يُعِزُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ، وَيُذِلُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ، وَيَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ، وَيَخْذُلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ، فَالْقُوَّةُ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً، لَا مَنْصُورَ إِلَّا مَنْ نَصَرَهُ، وَلَا عَزِيزَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَعَزَّهُ، وَكَذَلِكَ الْمَخْذُولُ مَنْ خَذَلَهُ اللَّهُ، وَالذَّلِيلُ مَنْ أَذَلَّهُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِن يَنصُرۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَخۡذُلۡكُمۡ فَمَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۗ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ﴾ [آلِ عِمْرَانَ: ١٦٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعٗا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ١٦٥]، وَهِيَ حَقِيقَةٌ سَوْفَ يُدْرِكُهَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ عَذَابَ اللَّهِ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ، فَيَعْلَمُونَ حِينَئِذٍ عِلْماً جَازِماً أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً. وَقَدْ عَمِيَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا عَنْ رُؤْيَةِ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ وَدَلَائِلِ قُدْرَتِهِ فَاتَّخَذُوا الْأَنْدَادَ وَعَبَدُوا الْأَوْثَانَ وَتَعَلَّقَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِمَا لَا يُعْطِي وَلَا يَمْنَعُ وَلَا يَخْفِضُ وَلَا يَرْفَعُ وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِهِ نَفْعاً وَلَا دَفْعاً فَضْلًا عَنْ أَنْ يَمْلِكَ شَيْئاً مِنْ ذَلِكَ لِغَيْرِهِ.
text.en: “Al-Matin” (the Firm) means: the One intense in strength. “Al-Qawiyy” (the All-Strong) means: the One whom nothing can overpower, whom no conqueror can overcome, and whose decree no one can turn back. His command is carried out and His decree takes effect among His creation. He honours whom He wills and humbles whom He wills; He grants victory to whom He wills and forsakes whom He wills. All strength belongs to Allah: none is granted victory except one whom He helps, and none is mighty except one whom He makes mighty; likewise, the forsaken one is he whom Allah forsakes, and the humbled one is he whom He humbles. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴿ [Al ‘Imran 3:160], and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And if only those who did wrong could see, when they see the punishment, that all strength belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:165]. This is a reality the idolaters will come to grasp on the Day of Resurrection, the day they see Allah's punishment with their own eyes; then they will know with certain knowledge that all strength belongs to Allah. Their eyes were blind in this world to the signs of His strength and the proofs of His power, so they took rivals, worshipped idols, and attached their hearts to things that neither give nor withhold, neither lower nor raise, and possess for themselves neither benefit nor any means of warding off harm, let alone possessing any of that for others.

text.ar: هَذَا وَمِنْ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ نَصْرُهُ لِأَنْبِيَائِهِ وَتَأْيِيدُهُ لِأَوْلِيَائِهِ وَفِي قَصَصِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ خَيْرُ شَاهِدٍ عَلَى هَذَا، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا نَجَّيۡنَا صَٰلِحٗا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحۡمَةٖ مِّنَّا وَمِنۡ خِزۡيِ يَوۡمِئِذٍۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ﴾ [هُودٍ: ٦٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ٤٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَغۡلِبَنَّ أَنَا۠ وَرُسُلِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٞ﴾ [الْمُجَادَلَةِ: ٢١]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكَفَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ ٱلۡقِتَالَۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزٗا﴾ [الْأَحْزَابِ: ٢٥].
text.en: Moreover, among the signs of His strength are His granting victory to His prophets and His support of His allies, and the stories of the prophets in the Qur'an are the best witness to this. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord — He is the All-Strong, the Almighty﴿ [Hud 11:66]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And Allah will surely help those who help Him. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, Almighty﴿ [al-Hajj 22:40]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Allah has decreed, “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers.” Indeed, Allah is All-Strong, Almighty﴿ [al-Mujadilah 58:21]; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And Allah spared the believers the fighting, and Allah is ever All-Strong, Almighty﴿ [al-Ahzab 33:25].

text.ar: وَمِنْ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ إِهْلَاكُهُ لِلظَّالِمِينَ وَانْتِقَامُهُ مِنَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ وَإِحْلَالُهُ بِهِمْ أَنْوَاعَ الْعُقُوبَاتِ وَصُنُوفَ الْمَثُلَاتِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿كَدَأۡبِ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيّٞ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ﴾ [الْأَنْفَالِ: ٥٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَوَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَانُواْ هُمۡ أَشَدَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةٗ وَءَاثَارٗا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمۡ وَمَا كَانَ لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن وَاقٖ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانَت تَّأۡتِيهِمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَكَفَرُواْ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّهُۥ قَوِيّٞ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ٢١ ـ ٢٢].
text.en: Among the signs of His strength are His destroying the wrongdoers, His taking retribution from the criminals, and His bringing down upon them every kind of punishment and exemplary chastisement. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is All-Strong and severe in penalty﴿ [al-Anfal 8:52], and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those who were before them? They were greater than them in strength and in the traces they left in the land, but Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah. That was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is All-Strong, severe in penalty﴿ [Ghafir 40:21–22].

text.ar: وَمِنْ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ قِيَامُ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَحِفْظُهُ لَهُمَا وَلِمَا فِيهِمَا بِقُدْرَتِهِ فَلَا يُعْجِزُهُ شَيْءٌ قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٥٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَوَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَكَانُوٓاْ أَشَدَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةٗۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعۡجِزَهُۥ مِن شَيۡءٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَلِيمٗا قَدِيرٗا﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٤٤].
text.en: Among the signs of His strength is that the heavens and the earth stand firm by His command, and that He preserves them and all that is in them by His power, so that nothing is beyond Him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And preserving them does not tire Him. And He is the Most High, the Magnificent﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:255], and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? And they were greater than them in strength. And Allah is not such that anything in the heavens or on the earth could escape Him. Indeed, He is ever All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴿ [Fatir 35:44].

text.ar: وَمِنْ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ أَنَّ الرِّزْقَ بِيَدِهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱللَّهُ لَطِيفُۢ بِعِبَادِهِۦ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ﴾ [الشُّورَى: ١٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلۡقُوَّةِ ٱلۡمَتِينُ﴾ [الذَّارِيَاتِ: ٥٨]، وَلَا حَوْلَ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي جَلْبِ نَفْعٍ أَوْ دَفْعِ ضُرٍّ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ دَخَلۡتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلۡتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِۚ﴾ [الْكَهْفِ: ٣٩].
text.en: Among the signs of His strength is that provision is in His hand; He gives it to whom He wills. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills. And He is the All-Strong, the Almighty﴿ [ash-Shura 42:19], and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Indeed, it is Allah who is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴿ [adh-Dhariyat 51:58]. The servant has no power to bring about benefit or ward off harm, and no strength, except through Allah. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, “What Allah wills! There is no strength except through Allah”?﴿ [al-Kahf 18:39].

text.ar: وَمِنْ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ أَنَّهُ لَا مَفَرَّ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ وَلَا مَلْجَأَ لِلْعَبْدِ وَلَا مَنْجَا مِنْهُ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَا يَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَبَقُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُمۡ لَا يُعۡجِزُونَ﴾ [الْأَنْفَالِ: ٥٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى عَنِ الْجِنِّ: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعۡجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَن نُّعۡجِزَهُۥ هَرَبٗا﴾ [الْجِنِّ: ١٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن لَّا يُجِبۡ دَاعِيَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَيۡسَ بِمُعۡجِزٖ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَيۡسَ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءُۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٍ﴾ [الْأَحْقَافِ: ٣٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَفِرُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرٞ مُّبِينٞ﴾ [الذَّارِيَاتِ: ٥٠].
text.en: Among the signs of His strength is that there is no fleeing except to Him, and the servant has no refuge from Him and no escape from Him except to Him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And let not those who disbelieve think that they have got away. Indeed, they cannot escape Him﴿ [al-Anfal 8:59]; He, the Exalted, says about the jinn: ﴾And we have realised that we can never escape Allah on earth, nor can we escape Him by flight﴿ [al-Jinn 72:12]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah cannot escape Him on earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him. Those are in manifest error﴿ [al-Ahqaf 46:32]; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you a clear warner from Him﴿ [adh-Dhariyat 51:50].

text.ar: وَمِنْ شَوَاهِدِ قُوَّتِهِ أَنَّهُ الْفَعَّالُ لِمَا يُرِيدُ، لَا يَقَعُ شَيْءٌ فِي هَذَا الْعَالَمِ مِنْ حَرَكَةٍ أَوْ سُكُونٍ، أَوْ خَفْضٍ أَوْ رَفْعٍ، أَوْ عِزٍّ أَوْ ذُلٍّ، أَوْ عَطَاءٍ أَوْ مَنْعٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ، يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَلَا يُمَانَعُ وَلَا يُغَالَبُ، بَلْ قَهَرَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ، وَدَانَ لَهُ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [الْأَعْرَافِ: ٥٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿مَّا يَفۡتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحۡمَةٖ فَلَا مُمۡسِكَ لَهَاۖ وَمَا يُمۡسِكۡ فَلَا مُرۡسِلَ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَۖ مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِذۡنِهِۦۚ﴾ [يُونُسَ: ٣].
text.en: Among the signs of His strength is that He does whatever He wills. Nothing happens in this world — no movement or stillness, no lowering or raising, no honour or humiliation, no giving or withholding — except by His permission. He does what He wills; He is neither resisted nor overpowered. Rather, He has subdued everything, and everything has submitted to Him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴿ [al-A‘raf 7:54]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴿ [Fatir 35:2]; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾He directs the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission﴿ [Yunus 10:3].

text.ar: هَذَا وَإِنَّ إِيمَانَ الْعَبْدِ بِهَذَا الِاسْمِ يُثْمِرُ فِيهِ انْكِسَارًا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَخُضُوعًا لِجَانِبِهِ وَخَوْفًا مِنْهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَلُجُوءًا إِلَيْهِ وَحْدَهُ، وَحُسْنَ تَوَكُّلٍ عَلَيْهِ، وَاسْتِسْلَاماً لِعَظَمَتِهِ، وَتَفْوِيضَ الْأُمُورِ كُلِّهَا إِلَيْهِ، وَالتَّبَرُّؤَ مِنَ الْحَوْلِ وَالْقُوَّةِ إِلَّا بِهِ.
text.en: Moreover, the servant's faith in this name yields in him brokenness before Allah, submission to Him, fear of Him (Glorified is He), turning to Him alone for refuge, sound reliance upon Him, surrender to His greatness, entrusting all affairs to Him, and disowning any power or strength except through Him.

text.ar: وَلِهَذَا كَانَتْ كَلِمَةُ «لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ» جَلِيلَةَ الشَّأْنِ، كَبِيرَةَ الْقَدْرِ، عَظِيمَةَ الْأَثَرِ، قَالَ ﷺ لِأَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: «يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ قَيْسٍ، قُلْ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ؛ فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ»، مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ[1].
text.en: This is why the phrase “La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah” (There is no power and no strength except through Allah) is of lofty standing, great worth and immense effect. The Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (may Allah be pleased with him): “O ‘Abdullah ibn Qays, say: There is no power and no strength except through Allah, for it is one of the treasures of Paradise.” Agreed upon.[1]

text.ar: وَرَوَى الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ: «أَمَرَنِي خَلِيلِي ﷺ بِسَبْعٍ، فَذَكَرَهَا، قَالَ: «وَأَمَرَنِي أَنْ أُكْثِرَ مِنْ قَوْلِ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ؛ فَإِنَّهُنَّ مِنْ كَنْزٍ تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ»[2].
text.en: Imam Ahmad narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “My beloved friend ﷺ commanded me with seven things” — and he mentioned them — he said: “and he commanded me to say often: There is no power and no strength except through Allah, for they are from a treasure beneath the Throne.”[2]

text.ar: وَهِيَ كَلِمَةُ إِسْلَامٍ وَاسْتِسْلَامٍ، وَتَفْوِيضٍ وَالْتِجَاءٍ، وَتَبَرُّؤٍ مِنَ الْحَوْلِ وَالْقُوَّةِ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، وَأَنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَا يَمْلِكُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ شَيْئاً، وَلَيْسَ لَهُ حِيلَةٌ فِي دَفْعِ شَرٍّ، وَلَا قُوَّةٌ فِي جَلْبِ خَيْرٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ، وَلَا تَحَوُّلَ لِلْعَبْدِ مِنْ مَعْصِيَةٍ إِلَى طَاعَةٍ، وَلَا مِنْ مَرَضٍ إِلَى صِحَّةٍ، وَلَا مِنْ وَهْنٍ إِلَى قُوَّةٍ، وَلَا مِنْ نَقْصٍ إِلَى زِيَادَةٍ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، وَلَا قُوَّةَ لِلْعَبْدِ عَلَى الْقِيَامِ بِأَيِّ شَأْنٍ مِنْ شُؤُونِهِ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
text.en: It is a phrase of Islam and surrender, of entrusting and seeking refuge, of disowning any power and strength except through Allah, and of acknowledging that the servant possesses nothing of his own affair: he has no means of warding off evil, and no strength to bring about good, except by Allah's permission. The servant cannot move from disobedience to obedience, from sickness to health, from weakness to strength, or from deficiency to increase except through Allah, and the servant has no strength to carry out any of his affairs except through Allah.

text.ar: وَمَنْ قَالَ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةَ مُحَقِّقًا مَا دَلَّتْ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوَكُّلِ وَالتَّفْوِيضِ وَحُسْنِ الِالْتِجَاءِ هُدِيَ وَوُقِيَ وَكُفِيَ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَقْوَى النَّاسِ قَلْبًا وَأَحْسَنِهِمْ حَالاً وَمَآلاً، وَفِي الْأَثَرِ: «مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَقْوَى النَّاسِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَمَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَغْنَى النَّاسِ فَلْيَكُنْ بِمَا فِي يَدِ اللَّهِ أَوْثَقَ مِنْهُ بِمَا فِي يَدِهِ»[3].
text.en: Whoever says this phrase, truly realising what it signifies of reliance, entrusting and sincere refuge-seeking, will be guided, protected and sufficed, and will be among the strongest of people in heart and the best of them in present state and final outcome. In a narration: “Whoever would be pleased to be the strongest of people, let him rely upon Allah; and whoever would be pleased to be the richest of people, let him be more confident in what is in Allah's hand than in what is in his own hand.”[3]
*Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 6384) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 2704).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ (٥/ ١٥٩) وَغَيْرُهُ بِإِسْنَادٍ حَسَنٍ. وَانْظُرْ: «السِّلْسِلَةَ الصَّحِيحَةَ» (٢١٦٦).
text.en: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (5/159) and others with a good (hasan) chain. See also *as-Silsilah as-Sahihah* (2166).

text.ar: ذَكَرَهُ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ فِي «مَجْمُوعِ الْفَتَاوَى» (١٣/ ٣٢٢). وَيُرْوَى حَدِيثاً مَرْفُوعاً وَلَا يَصِحُّ. انْظُرْ: «السِّلْسِلَةَ الضَّعِيفَةَ» (رَقْمُ: ٥٤٢١).
text.en: Ibn Taymiyyah mentioned it in *Majmu‘ al-Fatawa* (13/322). It is also narrated as a hadith traced back to the Prophet, but that is not authentic. See *as-Silsilah ad-Da‘ifah* (no. 5421).

text.ar: أَمَّا «الشَّهِيدُ» فَقَدْ تَكَرَّرَ فِي مَوَاضِعَ عَدِيدَةٍ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ﴾ [الْبُرُوجِ: ٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ٧٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡصِلُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ١٧].
text.en: As for “ash-Shahid” (the Witness), it recurs in many places in the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And Allah is Witness over all things﴿ [al-Buruj 85:9]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴿ [an-Nisa' 4:79]; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Indeed, Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Witness over all things﴿ [al-Hajj 22:17].

text.ar: وَأَمَّا «الرَّقِيبُ» فَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي ثَلَاثَةِ مَوَاطِنَ، قُرِنَ مَعَهُ فِي أَحَدِهَا اسْمُ الشَّهِيدِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ رَقِيبٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ رَّقِيبٗا﴾ [الْأَحْزَابِ: ٥٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكُنتُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدٗا مَّا دُمۡتُ فِيهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيۡتَنِي كُنتَ أَنتَ ٱلرَّقِيبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ وَأَنتَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ﴾ [الْمَائِدَةِ: ١١٧].
text.en: As for “ar-Raqib” (the Ever-Watchful), it has come in three places, and in one of them the name ash-Shahid (the Witness) is joined with it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you﴿ [an-Nisa' 4:1]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴿ [al-Ahzab 33:52]; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them; but when You took me, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things﴿ [al-Ma'idah 5:117].

text.ar: وَمَعْنَى الشَّهِيدِ أَيْ: الْمُطَّلِعُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ الَّذِي لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ، سَمِعَ جَمِيعَ الْأَصْوَاتِ خَفِيَّهَا وَجَلِيَّهَا، وَأَبْصَرَ جَمِيعَ الْمَوْجُودَاتِ دَقِيقَهَا وَجَلِيلَهَا، صَغِيرَهَا وَكَبِيرَهَا، وَأَحَاطَ عِلْمُهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ، الَّذِي شَهِدَ لِعِبَادِهِ وَعَلَى عِبَادِهِ بِمَا عَمِلُوهُ.
text.en: Ash-Shahid (the Witness) means: the One who is aware of everything, from whom nothing is hidden; who hears all sounds, the hidden and the open, and sees all existing things, the minute and the immense, the small and the great; whose knowledge encompasses everything; and who bears witness for His servants and against His servants concerning what they have done.

text.ar: وَمَعْنَى الرَّقِيبِ أَيْ: الْمُطَّلِعُ عَلَى مَا أَكَنَّتْهُ الصُّدُورُ، الْقَائِمُ عَلَى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ، الَّذِي حَفِظَ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ وَأَجْرَاهَا عَلَى أَحْسَنِ نِظَامٍ وَأَكْمَلِ تَدْبِيرٍ، رَقِيبٌ لِلْمُبْصَرَاتِ بِبَصَرِهِ الَّذِي لَا يَغِيبُ عَنْهُ شَيْءٌ، وَرَقِيبٌ لِلْمَسْمُوعَاتِ بِسَمْعِهِ الَّذِي وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ، وَرَقِيبٌ عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ بِعِلْمِهِ الْمُحِيطِ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ.
text.en: Ar-Raqib (the Ever-Watchful) means: the One aware of what the breasts conceal, who stands over every soul with what it has earned; who preserves the created things and runs them according to the finest order and the most perfect management. He is Watchful over all that is seen with His sight, from which nothing is absent; Watchful over all that is heard with His hearing, which encompasses everything; and Watchful over all created things with His knowledge, which encompasses everything.

text.ar: وَمَنْ يَتَأَمَّلْ مَدْلُولَ هَذَيْنِ الِاسْمَيْنِ يَجِدْ بَيْنَهُمَا شَيْئاً مِنَ التَّرَادُفِ؛ وَلِهَذَا قَالَ الشَّيْخُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ سَعْدِيٍّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «الرَّقِيبُ وَالشَّهِيدُ مُتَرَادِفَانِ، وَكِلَاهُمَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى إِحَاطَةِ سَمْعِ اللَّهِ بِالْمَسْمُوعَاتِ وَبَصَرِهِ بِالْمُبْصَرَاتِ وَعِلْمِهِ بِجَمِيعِ الْمَعْلُومَاتِ الْجَلِيَّةِ وَالْخَفِيَّةِ، وَهُوَ الرَّقِيبُ عَلَى مَا دَارَ فِي الْخَوَاطِرِ وَمَا تَحَرَّكَتْ بِهِ اللَّوَاحِظُ، وَمِنْ بَابٍ أَوْلَى الْأَفْعَالُ الظَّاهِرَةُ بِالْأَرْكَانِ قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ رَقِيبٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١]، ﴿وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ﴾ [الْبُرُوجِ: ٩]؛ وَلِهَذَا كَانَتِ الْمُرَاقَبَةُ الَّتِي هِيَ مِنْ أَعْلَى أَعْمَالِ الْقُلُوبِ هِيَ التَّعَبُّدَ لِلَّهِ بِاسْمِهِ الرَّقِيبِ الشَّهِيدِ، فَمَتَى عَلِمَ الْعَبْدُ أَنَّ حَرَكَاتِهِ الظَّاهِرَةَ وَالْبَاطِنَةَ قَدْ أَحَاطَ اللَّهُ بِعِلْمِهَا، وَاسْتَحْضَرَ هَذَا الْعِلْمَ فِي كُلِّ أَحْوَالِهِ أَوْجَبَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ حِرَاسَةَ بَاطِنِهِ عَنْ كُلِّ فِكْرٍ وَهَاجِسٍ يُبْغِضُهُ اللَّهُ وَحِفْظَ ظَاهِرِهِ عَنْ كُلِّ قَوْلٍ أَوْ فِعْلٍ يُسْخِطُ اللَّهَ، وَتَعَبَّدَ بِمَقَامِ الْإِحْسَانِ فَعَبَدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّهُ يَرَاهُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاهُ»[1]. اهـ
text.en: Whoever reflects on what these two names signify will find a degree of synonymy between them. That is why Shaykh ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sa‘di (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Ar-Raqib (the Ever-Watchful) and ash-Shahid (the Witness) are synonymous, and both indicate that Allah's hearing encompasses all that is heard, His sight all that is seen, and His knowledge all that is known, the apparent and the hidden. He is the Watcher over what passes through the mind and what the glances move with, and all the more so over the outward actions done with the limbs. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you﴿ [an-Nisa' 4:1], ﴾And Allah is Witness over all things﴿ [al-Buruj 85:9]. This is why mindfulness of Allah's watching, which is among the loftiest deeds of the heart, is worshipping Allah through His name ar-Raqib ash-Shahid. When the servant knows that Allah's knowledge encompasses his outward and inward movements, and keeps this knowledge present in all his states, it obliges him to guard his inner self from every thought and notion that Allah hates, and to guard his outer self from every word or deed that angers Allah, and he worships at the level of ihsan (excellence), worshipping Allah as though he sees Him, for even if he does not see Him, He sees him.”[1] End quote.

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٞ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٣٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ رَّقِيبٗا﴾ [الْأَحْزَابِ: ٥٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَهُوَ مَعَكُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٞ﴾ [الْحَدِيدِ: ٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَلَمۡ يَعۡلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ﴾ [الْعَلَقِ: ١٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ﴾ [الطُّورِ: ٤٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَعۡلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلۡأَعۡيُنِ وَمَا تُخۡفِي ٱلصُّدُورُ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ١٩]. وَالْآيَاتُ فِي هَذَا الْمَعْنَى كَثِيرَةٌ.
text.en: Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:235]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴿ [al-Ahzab 33:52]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah sees what you do﴿ [al-Hadid 57:4]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾Does he not know that Allah sees?﴿ [al-‘Alaq 96:14]; He, the Exalted, says: ﴾So be patient for the decision of your Lord, for indeed you are in Our sight﴿ [at-Tur 52:48]; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴾He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴿ [Ghafir 40:19]. The verses with this meaning are many.

text.ar: وَفِي حَدِيثِ جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ عَنِ الْإِحْسَانِ فَقَالَ لَهُ: «أَنْ تَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّكَ تَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ تَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاكَ»، رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[2].
text.en: In the hadith of Jibril (peace be upon him), he asked the Prophet ﷺ about ihsan (excellence), and he said to him: “That you worship Allah as though you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He sees you.” Narrated by Muslim.[2]

text.ar: فَتَأَمُّلُ هَذِهِ النُّصُوصِ وَمَا فِي مَعْنَاهَا يُحَرِّكُ فِي الْعَبْدِ مُرَاقَبَةَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي كُلِّ أَعْمَالِهِ وَجَمِيعِ أَحْوَالِهِ، إِذِ الْمُرَاقَبَةُ ثَمَرَةٌ مِنْ ثِمَارِ عِلْمِ الْعَبْدِ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ رَقِيبٌ عَلَيْهِ، نَاظِرٌ إِلَيْهِ، سَامِعٌ لِقَوْلِهِ، مُطَّلِعٌ عَلَى عَمَلِهِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ، وَكُلِّ لَحْظَةٍ، وَكُلِّ نَفَسٍ، وَكُلِّ طَرْفَةِ عَيْنٍ.
text.en: Reflecting on these texts, and on others of similar meaning, stirs in the servant mindfulness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his deeds and in all his states. For this mindfulness is one of the fruits of the servant's knowledge that Allah (Glorified is He) is Watchful over him, looking at him, hearing his words, and aware of his deeds at every moment, every instant, every breath and every blink of an eye.
