So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said: “Allah the Exalted is al-Hakam, and judgement belongs to Him, so why are you called Abu al-Hakam?” He said: “When my people differ over something, they come to me and I judge between them, and both parties are pleased.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How excellent this is! What children do you have?” He said: “I have Shurayh, Muslim and ‘Abdullah.” He said: “Who is the eldest of them?” I said: “Shurayh.” He said: “Then you are Abu Shurayh.” Abu Dawud and an-Nasa'i reported it, as did al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*[1].

text.ar: أَمَّا كَمَالُ الْحِكْمَةِ فَبِثُبُوتِ الْحِكْمَةِ لَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ فِي خَلْقِهِ وَفِي أَمْرِهِ وَشَرْعِهِ، حَيْثُ يَضَعُ الْأَشْيَاءَ مَوَاضِعَهَا وَيُنْزِلُهَا مَنَازِلَهَا، وَلَا يَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْهِ سُؤَالٌ وَلَا يَقْدَحُ فِي حِكْمَتِهِ مَقَالٌ.
text.en: As for perfect wisdom, it lies in affirming wisdom for Him, Glorified is He, in His creation and in His command and law, for He puts things in their proper places and gives them their due positions. No objection can be raised against Him, and no word can call His wisdom into question.

text.ar: أَمَّا الْحِكْمَةُ فِي الْخَلْقِ فَإِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ خَلَقَ الْخَلْقَ بِالْحَقِّ، وَمُشْتَمِلًا عَلَى الْحَقِّ، وَكَانَ نِهَايَتَهُ وَغَايَتَهُ الْحَقُّ، أَوْجَدَهُ بِأَحْسَنِ نِظَامٍ، وَرَتَّبَهُ بِأَكْمَلِ إِتْقَانٍ، وَأَعْطَى كُلَّ مَخْلُوقٍ خَلْقَهُ اللَّائِقَ بِهِ، بَلْ أَعْطَى كُلَّ جُزْءٍ مِنْ أَجْزَاءِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ، وَكُلَّ عُضْوٍ مِنْ أَعْضَاءِ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ خِلْقَتَهُ وَهَيْئَتَهُ اللَّائِقَةَ بِهِ، بِحَيْثُ لَا يُرَى فِيهِ شَيْءٌ مِنَ التَّفَاوُتِ وَالْخَلَلِ ﴿مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتٖۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٖ (٣) ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئٗا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٞ﴾ [الْمُلْك: ٣ ـ ٤]، وَلَوِ اجْتَمَعَتْ عُقُولُ الْخَلْقِ عَلَى أَنْ يَقْتَرِحُوا مِثْلًا أَوْ أَحْسَنَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْمَوْجُودَاتِ لَمْ يَقْدِرُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ ﴿صُنۡعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَتۡقَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍۚ﴾ [النَّمْل: ٨٨].
text.en: As for wisdom in creation, He, Glorified is He, created the creation in truth, containing truth, and its end and goal is truth. He brought it into being in the finest order, arranged it with the most perfect precision, and gave every created thing the form befitting it. Indeed, He gave every part of the created things, and every limb of living creatures, the form and shape befitting it, such that no inconsistency or flaw is seen in it. ﴾You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return your gaze: do you see any breaks? (3) Then return your gaze twice again; your gaze will return to you humbled and weary﴿ [al-Mulk 67:3–4]. If the minds of all creation came together to propose the like of these existing things, or something better, they would not be able to do so. ﴾The work of Allah, who perfected all things﴿ [an-Naml 27:88].

text.ar: وَإِذَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُتَقَرِّرِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ لَهُ الْكَمَالُ الَّذِي لَا يُحِيطُ بِهِ الْعِبَادُ، وَأَنَّهُ مَا مِنْ كَمَالٍ تَفْرِضُهُ الْأَذْهَانُ وَيُقَدِّرُهُ الْمُقَدِّرُونَ إِلَّا وَاللَّهُ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَأَجَلُّ؛ فَإِنَّ أَفْعَالَهُ وَجَمِيعَ مَا أَوْصَلَهُ إِلَى الْخَلْقِ أَكْمَلُ الْأُمُورِ وَأَحْسَنُهَا وَأَنْظَمُهَا وَأَتْقَنُهَا، فَالْفِعْلُ يَتْبَعُ فِي كَمَالِهِ وَحُسْنِهِ فَاعِلَهُ، وَالتَّدْبِيرُ مَنْسُوبٌ إِلَى مُدَبِّرِهِ، وَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى كَمَا لَا يُشْبِهُهُ أَحَدٌ فِي صِفَاتِهِ فِي الْعَظَمَةِ وَالْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ، فَكَذَلِكَ لَا يُشْبِهُهُ أَحَدٌ فِي أَفْعَالِهِ.
text.en: Since it is established that Allah, Glorified is He, has a perfection that the servants cannot comprehend, and that there is no perfection that minds can suppose or estimators can estimate except that Allah is greater and more majestic than that, it follows that His actions, and everything He has conveyed to creation, are the most perfect of things, the finest, the most orderly and the most precise. For an action follows its doer in its perfection and beauty, and management is attributed to the one who manages. And just as no one resembles Allah the Exalted in His attributes of greatness, beauty and splendour, likewise no one resembles Him in His actions.

text.ar: وَأَمَّا الْحِكْمَةُ فِي أَمْرِهِ وَشَرْعِهِ فَإِنَّهُ تَعَالَى شَرَعَ الشَّرَائِعَ، وَأَنْزَلَ الْكُتُبَ، وَأَرْسَلَ الرُّسُلَ لِيَعْرِفَهُ الْعِبَادُ وَيَعْبُدُوهُ، فَلَمْ يَخْلُقْهُمْ هَمَلًا، وَلَمْ يُوجِدْهُمْ سُدًى، بَلْ خَلَقَهُمْ لِأَكْمَلِ مَقْصِدٍ، وَأَوْجَدَهُمْ لِأَجَلِّ غَايَةٍ.
text.en: As for wisdom in His command and law, He the Exalted laid down the laws, sent down the Books and sent the messengers so that the servants would know Him and worship Him. He did not create them to be left neglected, nor bring them into being without purpose; rather, He created them for the most perfect purpose and brought them into being for the most sublime goal.

text.ar: وَمَعْرِفَتُهُ تَعَالَى وَعِبَادَتُهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ الَّتِي هِيَ مَقْصُودُ الْخَلْقِ هِيَ أَفْضَلُ الْعَطَايَا مِنْهُ تَعَالَى لِعِبَادِهِ عَلَى الْإِطْلَاقِ، وَأَجَلُّ الْهِبَاتِ وَأَشْرَفُ الْمِنَنِ لِمَنْ يَمُنُّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بِهَا وَيُكْرِمُهُ بِبُلُوغِهَا وَتَحْقِيقِهَا، وَهِيَ أَكْمَلُ السَّعَادَةِ وَالْفَلَاحِ وَالسُّرُورِ لِلْقُلُوبِ وَالْأَرْوَاحِ، بَلْ هِيَ السَّبَبُ الْوَحِيدُ لِلْوُصُولِ إِلَى السَّعَادَةِ الْأَبَدِيَّةِ، وَالْفَلَاحِ السَّرْمَدِيِّ.
text.en: Knowing Him the Exalted and worshipping Him alone, without partner, which is the purpose of creation, is absolutely the best of His gifts to His servants, the most sublime of endowments and the noblest of favours for whomever Allah favours with it and honours by allowing him to attain and realize it. It is the most complete happiness and success, and the joy of hearts and souls; indeed, it is the only way to reach eternal happiness and everlasting success.

text.ar: إِضَافَةً إِلَى هَذَا فَإِنَّ شَرْعَهُ قَدِ اشْتَمَلَ عَلَى كُلِّ خَيْرٍ، فَأَخْبَارُهُ تَمْلَأُ الْقُلُوبَ عِلْمًا وَعَقَائِدَ صَحِيحَةً، وَتَسْتَقِيمُ بِهَا الْقُلُوبُ وَيَزُولُ انْحِرَافُهَا، وَيَحْصُلُ لَهَا أَفْضَلُ الْمَعَارِفِ وَأَجَلُّ الْعُلُومِ، وَأَوَامِرُهُ كُلُّهَا مَنَافِعُ وَمَصَالِحُ، وَتُثْمِرُ الْأَخْلَاقَ الْجَمِيلَةَ وَالْخِصَالَ الْكَرِيمَةَ وَالْأَعْمَالَ الصَّالِحَةَ وَالطَّاعَاتِ الزَّاكِيَةَ، وَالْهَدْيَ الْكَامِلَ، وَنَوَاهِيهِ كُلُّهَا مُوَافِقَةٌ لِلْعُقُولِ الصَّحِيحَةِ وَالْفِطَرِ السَّلِيمَةِ، فَلَمْ يَنْهَ إِلَّا عَمَّا يَضُرُّ النَّاسَ فِي عُقُولِهِمْ وَأَخْلَاقِهِمْ وَأَعْرَاضِهِمْ وَأَبْدَانِهِمْ وَأَمْوَالِهِمْ.
text.en: In addition to this, His law contains all good. Its reports fill hearts with knowledge and sound beliefs; by them hearts are set straight and their deviation removed, and they attain the best knowledge and the most sublime sciences. His commands are all benefit and welfare, and they yield beautiful character, noble traits, righteous deeds, pure acts of obedience and complete guidance. His prohibitions all agree with sound minds and upright natures; He has forbidden only what harms people in their minds, their character, their honour, their bodies and their wealth.

text.ar: وَمِنْ حُكْمِهِ وَحِكْمَتِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ مُجَازَاةُ الْمُحْسِنِ بِإِحْسَانِهِ، وَالْمُسِيءِ بِإِسَاءَتِهِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى فِي شَأْنِ الْمُحْسِنِ: ﴿هَلۡ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنُ﴾ [الرَّحْمَن: ٦٠]، وَقَالَ فِي شَأْنِ الْمُسِيءِ: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔواْ ٱلسُّوٓأَىٰٓ﴾ [الرُّوم: ١٠]، فَلَا يُسَوِّي سُبْحَانَهُ بَيْنَ مُحْسِنٍ وَمُسِيءٍ، لَا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ ﴿أَمۡ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱجۡتَرَحُواْ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ أَن نَّجۡعَلَهُمۡ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَوَآءٗ مَّحۡيَاهُمۡ وَمَمَاتُهُمۡۚ سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ﴾، وَهَذَا مِنْ كَمَالِ عَدْلِهِ، وَهُوَ مُنَاسِبٌ غَايَةَ الْمُنَاسَبَةِ لِحِكْمَةِ أَحْكَمِ الْحَاكِمِينَ سُبْحَانَهُ.
text.en: Part of His judgement and wisdom, Glorified is He, is that He recompenses the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil. He the Exalted says concerning the doer of good: ﴾Is the reward for good anything but good?﴿ [ar-Rahman 55:60], and He says concerning the doer of evil: ﴾Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴿ [ar-Rum 30:10]. So He, Glorified is He, does not make the doer of good and the doer of evil equal, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. ﴾Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and their death? Evil is what they judge﴿. This is part of the perfection of His justice, and it is in the utmost harmony with the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges, Glorified is He.

text.ar: «سُنَنُ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» (رَقْم: ٤٩٥٥)، وَ«سُنَنُ النَّسَائِيِّ» (رَقْم:٥٣٨٧)، وَ«الْأَدَبُ الْمُفْرَدُ» (رَقْم:٨١١). وَصَحَّحَهُ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ فِي «صَحِيحِ الْأَدَبِ الْمُفْرَدِ» (رَقْم: ٦٢٣).
text.en: *Sunan Abi Dawud* (no. 4955), *Sunan an-Nasa'i* (no. 5387) and *al-Adab al-Mufrad* (no. 811). Al-Albani graded it authentic in *Sahih al-Adab al-Mufrad* (no. 623).

title.en: al-Mu'min, as-Sadiq (the Affirmer of Truth and Giver of Security, the Truthful)

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ «الْمُؤْمِنُ» فِي آيَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، هِيَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ﴾ [الْحَشْر: ٢٣].
text.en: Allah's name “al-Mu'min” (the Affirmer of Truth, the Giver of Security) occurs in a single verse, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴾He is Allah, besides whom none has the right to be worshipped: the King, the Most Holy, the Perfect in Peace, the Affirmer of Truth, the Overseer, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supreme in Greatness. Glorified is Allah above whatever they associate with Him﴿ [al-Hashr 59:23].

text.ar: وَالْإِيمَانُ يَرْجِعُ مَعْنَاهُ إِلَى التَّصْدِيقِ وَالْإِقْرَارِ، وَمَا يَقْتَضِيهِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْإِرْشَادِ وَتَصْدِيقِ الصَّادِقِينَ، وَإِقَامَةِ الْبَرَاهِينِ عَلَى صِدْقِهِمْ، فَهُوَ تَعَالَى الْمُؤْمِنُ الَّذِي هُوَ كَمَا أَثْنَى عَلَى نَفْسِهِ، وَفَوْقَ مَا يُثْنِي عَلَيْهِ عِبَادُهُ، وَلِهَذَا قَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ: الَّذِي وَحَّدَ نَفْسَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ [آلِ عِمْرَانَ: ١٨]».
text.en: The meaning of iman goes back to affirmation and acknowledgement, and what that entails of guidance, affirming the truthful and establishing proofs of their truthfulness. He the Exalted is al-Mu'min (the Affirmer of Truth), who is as He has praised Himself and above whatever His servants praise Him with. For this reason Mujahid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Al-Mu'min: the One who declared His own Oneness by His saying: ﴾Allah bears witness that none has the right to be worshipped but Him﴿ [Al ‘Imran 3:18].”

text.ar: وَهِيَ شَهَادَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ كَرِيمَةٌ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ شَاهِدٍ، وَهُوَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ؛ لِأَعْظَمِ مَشْهُودٍ بِهِ، وَهُوَ تَوْحِيدُ اللَّهِ، وَإِخْلَاصُ الدِّينِ لَهُ.
text.en: This is a tremendous, noble testimony from the greatest of witnesses, Allah, Lord of the worlds, to the greatest thing that can be testified to: the Tawheed of Allah and devoting the religion sincerely to Him.

text.ar: وَمِنْ هَذَا الْمَعْنَى مَا رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ وَابْنُ مَاجَهْ وَغَيْرُهُمَا عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْأَغَرِّ أَبِي مُسْلِمٍ، أَنَّهُ شَهِدَ عَلَى أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ وَأَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، أَنَّهُمَا شَهِدَا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، قَالَ: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: صَدَقَ عَبْدِي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا، وَأَنَا أَكْبَرُ، وَإِذَا قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، قَالَ: صَدَقَ عَبْدِي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا وَحْدِي، وَإِذَا قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، قَالَ: صَدَقَ عَبْدِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا لَا شَرِيكَ لِي، وَإِذَا قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، قَالَ: صَدَقَ عَبْدِي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا لِيَ الْمُلْكُ وَلِيَ الْحَمْدُ، وَإِذَا قَالَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، قَالَ: صَدَقَ عَبْدِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِي»[1].
text.en: Of this meaning is what at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others reported from Abu Ishaq, from al-Agharr Abu Muslim, that he bore witness concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they bore witness concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: “When the servant says, ‘None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest,’ Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: ‘My servant has spoken the truth: none has the right to be worshipped but Me, and I am the Greatest.’ When he says, ‘None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone,’ He says: ‘My servant has spoken the truth: none has the right to be worshipped but Me alone.’ When he says, ‘None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, without partner,’ He says: ‘My servant has spoken the truth: none has the right to be worshipped but Me, and I have no partner.’ When he says, ‘None has the right to be worshipped but Allah; His is the dominion and His is the praise,’ He says: ‘My servant has spoken the truth: none has the right to be worshipped but Me; Mine is the dominion and Mine is the praise.’ And when he says, ‘None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah,’ He says: ‘My servant has spoken the truth: none has the right to be worshipped but Me, and there is no might nor power except with Me.’”[1]

text.ar: قَالَ أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ: ثُمَّ قَالَ الْأَغَرُّ شَيْئًا لَمْ أَفْهَمْهُ، قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: مَا قَالَ؟ قَالَ: «مَنْ رُزِقَهُنَّ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ لَمْ تَمَسَّهُ النَّارُ».
text.en: Abu Ishaq said: Then al-Agharr said something I did not understand, so I said to Abu Ja‘far, “What did he say?” He said: “Whoever is granted them at his death, the Fire will not touch him.”

text.ar: فَهَذِهِ شَهَادَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنَفْسِهِ بِوَحْدَانِيَّتِهِ، وَتَصْدِيقٌ لِلشَّاهِدِينَ بِذَلِكَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ، وَهَذَا التَّصْدِيقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِعِبَادِهِ الشَّاهِدِينَ لَهُ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ، وَكَذَلِكَ تَأْيِيدُهُ لَهُمْ بِالْحُجَّةِ وَالْبُرْهَانِ، كُلُّهُ مِنْ دَلَائِلِ اسْمِهِ «الْمُؤْمِنِ».
text.en: This is a tremendous testimony from Allah to Himself of His Oneness, and an affirmation of those among His servants who bear witness to it. This affirmation from Allah of His servants who bear witness to His Tawheed, as well as His supporting them with proof and evidence, are all among the indications of His name “al-Mu'min” (the Affirmer of Truth).

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «مِنْ أَسْمَائِهِ الْمُؤْمِنُ، وَهُوَ فِي أَحَدِ التَّفْسِيرَيْنِ: الْمُصَدِّقُ، الَّذِي يُصَدِّقُ الصَّادِقِينَ بِمَا يُقِيمُ لَهُمْ مِنْ شَوَاهِدِ صِدْقِهِمْ، فَهُوَ الَّذِي صَدَّقَ رُسُلَهُ وَأَنْبِيَاءَهُ فِيمَا بَلَّغُوا عَنْهُ، وَشَهِدَ لَهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ صَادِقُونَ بِالدَّلَائِلِ الَّتِي دَلَّ بِهَا عَلَى صِدْقِهِمْ قَضَاءً وَخَلْقًا، فَإِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ أَخْبَرَ ـ وَخَبَرُهُ الصِّدْقُ، وَقَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ ـ أَنَّهُ لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يُرِيَ الْعِبَادَ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ الْأُفُقِيَّةِ وَالنَّفْسِيَّةِ مَا يُبَيِّنُ لَهُمْ أَنَّ الْوَحْيَ الَّذِي بَلَّغَتْ رُسُلُهُ حَقٌّ، فَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَنُرِيهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا فِي ٱلۡأٓفَاقِ وَفِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمۡ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّۗ﴾ [فُصِّلَت: ٥٣]، أَيْ: الْقُرْآنُ؛ فَإِنَّهُ هُوَ الْمُتَقَدِّمُ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرۡتُم بِهِۦ﴾ [فُصِّلَت: ٥٢]، ثُمَّ قَالَ: ﴿أَوَلَمۡ يَكۡفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ شَهِيدٌ﴾ [فُصِّلَت: ٥٣]، فَشَهِدَ سُبْحَانَهُ لِرَسُولِهِ بِقَوْلِهِ أَنَّ مَا جَاءَ بِهِ حَقٌّ، وَوَعَدَهُ أَنْ يُرِيَ الْعِبَادَ مِنْ آيَاتِهِ الْفِعْلِيَّةِ الْخَلْقِيَّةِ مَا يَشْهَدُ بِذَلِكَ أَيْضًا، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ مَا هُوَ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَأَجَلُّ وَهُوَ شَهَادَتُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ»[2].
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Among His names is al-Mu'min, which according to one of the two interpretations means the One who confirms as true: He confirms the truthful by the evidences of their truthfulness that He establishes for them. He is the One who confirmed His messengers and prophets in what they conveyed from Him, and bore witness for them that they are truthful by the proofs through which He showed their truthfulness, both by His decree and by His creation. For He, Glorified is He, has told us (and His report is truth and His word is the truth) that He will certainly show the servants signs in the horizons and in themselves that make clear to them that the revelation His messengers conveyed is true. He the Exalted said: ﴾We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴿ [Fussilat 41:53], meaning the Qur'an, for it is what was mentioned before in His saying: ﴾Say: Have you considered: if it is from Allah and then you disbelieve in it﴿ [Fussilat 41:52]. Then He said: ﴾Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is Witness over all things?﴿ [Fussilat 41:53]. So He, Glorified is He, bore witness for His Messenger by His word that what he brought is true, and promised that He would show the servants, from His signs in action and creation, what would also testify to that. Then He mentioned what is greater and more majestic than that: His testimony, Glorified is He, over all things.”[2]

text.ar: وَهَذَا مَعْنَى قَوْلِ قَتَادَةَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ آمَنَ لِقَوْلِهِ أَنَّهُ حَقٌّ»[3].
text.en: This is the meaning of the saying of Qatadah (may Allah have mercy on him): “Al-Mu'min: He affirmed that His own word is true.”[3]

text.ar: كَمَا أَنَّ مِنْ دَلَائِلِ اسْمِهِ «الْمُؤْمِنِ» تَأْمِينَ الْخَائِفِ، وَذَلِكَ بِإِعْطَائِهِ الْأَمَانَ وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْإِخَافَةِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلَّذِيٓ أَطۡعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٖ وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنۡ خَوۡفِۭ﴾ [قُرَيْش: ٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنٗاۚ﴾ [النُّور: ٥٥].
text.en: Also among the indications of His name “al-Mu'min” (the Giver of Security) is His granting security to the fearful by giving them safety, which is the opposite of making afraid. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴿ [Quraysh 106:4], and He the Exalted says: ﴾And He will surely replace their fear with security﴿ [an-Nur 24:55].

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: «الْمُؤْمِنُ: أَيْ: أَمَّنَ خَلْقَهُ مِنْ أَنْ يَظْلِمَهُمْ»[4].
text.en: Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: “Al-Mu'min means: He has made His creation secure from His wronging them.”[4]

text.ar: فَكُلُّ خَائِفٍ يَصْدُقُ فِي لُجُوئِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ يَجِدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ مُؤَمِّنًا لَهُ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ، فَأَمْنُ الْعِبَادِ وَأَمْنُ الْبِلَادِ بِيَدِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ.
text.en: So every fearful person who is sincere in turning to Allah for refuge finds Him, Glorified is He, granting him security from fear. The security of the servants and the security of the lands are in His hand, Glorified is He.

text.ar: وَبِمَا تَقَدَّمَ يُعْلَمُ أَنَّ اسْمَ اللَّهِ «الْمُؤْمِنَ» يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَعَانٍ عَظِيمَةٍ وَأُمُورٍ جَلِيلَةٍ، يُمْكِنُ تَلْخِيصُ أَهَمِّهَا فِي النِّقَاطِ التَّالِيَةِ:
text.en: From what has preceded, it is known that Allah's name “al-Mu'min” (the Affirmer of Truth, the Giver of Security) indicates tremendous meanings and sublime matters, the most important of which can be summarized in the following points:

text.ar: فَمِنْ دَلَائِلِ اسْمِهِ «الْمُؤْمِنِ» شَهَادَتُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ لِنَفْسِهِ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ، وَهِيَ أَعْظَمُ شَهَادَةٍ، مِنْ أَعْظَمِ شَاهِدٍ، لِأَعْظَمِ مَشْهُودٍ بِهِ.
text.en: Among the indications of His name “al-Mu'min” (the Affirmer of Truth, the Giver of Security) is His testimony, Glorified is He, to Himself of Tawheed; it is the greatest testimony, from the greatest witness, to the greatest thing testified to.

text.ar: وَمِنْهَا تَصْدِيقُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ لِلشَّاهِدِينَ لَهُ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ، وَالشَّهَادَةُ لَهُمْ بِأَنَّ مَا قَالُوهُ حَقٌّ وَصِدْقٌ.
text.en: Among them is His affirming, Glorified is He, of those who bear witness to His Tawheed, and His testifying for them that what they said is truth and true.

text.ar: وَمِنْهَا تَصْدِيقُهُ لِأَنْبِيَائِهِ بِالْحُجَجِ وَالْبَيِّنَاتِ بِأَنَّ مَا قَالُوهُ وَبَلَّغُوهُ عَنِ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ، وَصِدْقٌ لَا امْتِرَاءَ فِيهِ.
text.en: Among them is His confirming His prophets with proofs and clear evidences that what they said and conveyed from Allah is truth without any doubt and truthfulness without any dispute.

text.ar: وَمِنْهَا أَنَّهُ يَصْدُقُ عِبَادَهُ مَا وَعَدَهُمْ مِنَ النَّصْرِ وَالتَّمْكِينِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ثُمَّ صَدَقۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡوَعۡدَ فَأَنجَيۡنَٰهُمۡ وَمَن نَّشَآءُ﴾ [الْأَنْبِيَاء: ٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمَا ٱسۡتَخۡلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي ٱرۡتَضَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنٗاۚ يَعۡبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ بِي شَيۡـٔٗاۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ﴾ [النُّور: ٥٥].
text.en: Among them is that He makes good to His servants what He promised them of victory and establishment. He the Exalted says: ﴾Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed﴿ [al-Anbiya' 21:9], and He the Exalted says: ﴾Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the land just as He made those before them successors, that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has chosen for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, it is they who are the defiantly disobedient﴿ [an-Nur 24:55].

text.ar: وَمِنْهَا: أَنَّهُ يُؤَمِّنُ عِبَادَهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَوْلِيَاءَهُ الْمُتَّقِينَ مِنْ عَذَابِهِ وَعِقَابِهِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَمۡ يَلۡبِسُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنَهُم بِظُلۡمٍ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡأَمۡنُ وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ﴾ [الْأَنْعَام: ٨٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَفَمَن يُلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّن يَأۡتِيٓ ءَامِنٗا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ﴾ [فُصِّلَت: ٤٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ فَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ﴾ [الْأَحْقَاف: ١٣].
text.en: Among them: that He grants His believing servants and His God-fearing allies security from His punishment and penalty. He the Exalted says: ﴾Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing, it is they who will have security, and they are rightly guided﴿ [al-An‘am 6:82], and He the Exalted says: ﴾Is one who is cast into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴿ [Fussilat 41:40], and He the Exalted says: ﴾Indeed, those who have said, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remained steadfast, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve﴿ [al-Ahqaf 46:13].

text.ar: وَمِنْهَا أَنَّهُ يُنْجِزُهُمْ مَا وَعَدَهُمْ مِنَ الْفَوْزِ الْعَظِيمِ وَدُخُولِ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعۡدَهُۥ وَأَوۡرَثَنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ حَيۡثُ نَشَآءُۖ فَنِعۡمَ أَجۡرُ ٱلۡعَٰمِلِينَ﴾ [الزُّمَر: ٧٤].
text.en: Among them is that He fulfils for them what He promised them of the great triumph and entry into the Gardens of Bliss. He the Exalted says: ﴾And they will say, “Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, so that we may settle in Paradise wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of those who work!”﴿ [az-Zumar 39:74].

text.ar: وَمِنْهَا تَأْمِينُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ الْخَائِفِينَ بِإِعْطَائِهِمُ الْأَمَانَ وَهُوَ ضِدُّ الْإِخَافَةِ، كَمَا قَالَ سُبْحَانَهُ: ﴿ٱلَّذِيٓ أَطۡعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٖ وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنۡ خَوۡفِۭ﴾ [قُرَيْش: ٤].
text.en: Among them is His granting security, Glorified is He, to the fearful by giving them safety, which is the opposite of making afraid, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴾Who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴿ [Quraysh 106:4].

text.ar: وَأَمَّا اسْمُ اللَّهِ «الصَّادِقُ» فَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي آيَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَهِيَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمۡنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٖۖ وَمِنَ ٱلۡبَقَرِ وَٱلۡغَنَمِ حَرَّمۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ شُحُومَهُمَآ إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتۡ ظُهُورُهُمَآ أَوِ ٱلۡحَوَايَآ أَوۡ مَا ٱخۡتَلَطَ بِعَظۡمٖۚ ذَٰلِكَ جَزَيۡنَٰهُم بِبَغۡيِهِمۡۖ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ﴾ [الْأَنْعَام: ١٤٦].
text.en: As for Allah's name “as-Sadiq” (the Truthful), it occurs in a single verse of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴾And to those who are Jews We forbade every animal with undivided hoof, and of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry, or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That is how We recompensed them for their transgression. And indeed, We are truthful﴿ [al-An‘am 6:146].

text.ar: أَيِ الصَّادِقُ فِي وَعْدِهِ وَوَعِيدِهِ، وَفِي كُلِّ مَا يُخْبِرُ بِهِ، قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ: «فَلَا رَيْبَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى وَعَدَ الْمُطِيعِينَ بِأَنْ يُثِيبَهُمْ، وَوَعَدَ السَّائِلِينَ بِأَنْ يُجِيبَهُمْ، وَهُوَ الصَّادِقُ الَّذِي لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقّٗاۚ وَمَنۡ أَصۡدَقُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ قِيلٗا﴾ [النِّسَاء: ١٢٢]»[5].
text.en: That is, truthful in His promise and His threat, and in everything He informs of. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: “There is no doubt that Allah the Exalted has promised the obedient that He will reward them, and promised those who ask that He will answer them, and He is the Truthful who does not break His promise. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾The promise of Allah, in truth. And who is more truthful than Allah in speech?﴿ [an-Nisa' 4:122].”[5]

text.ar: وَمِنْ آثَارِ الْإِيمَانِ بِهَذَا الِاسْمِ أَنَّ الْمُحْسِنَ لَا يَخَافُ لَدَيْهِ سُبْحَانَهُ ظُلْماً وَلَا هَضْماً، وَلَا يَخَافُ بَخْساً وَلَا رَهَقاً، أَوْ أَنْ يَضِيعَ لَهُ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ؛ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَعَدَ ـ وَهُوَ الصَّادِقُ ـ بِتَوْفِيَتِهِ الْعَامِلِينَ أُجُورَهُمْ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ جَازَاهُ بِهَا وَلَا يُضِيعُهَا عَلَيْهِ بَلْ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُؤْتِي مِنْ لَدُنْهُ أَجْراً عَظِيماً، وَأَمَّا الْمُسِيءُ فَيُجَازِيهِ بِسَيِّئَةٍ مِثْلِهَا، وَيَحُطُّهَا عَنْهُ بِالتَّوْبَةِ وَالنَّدَمِ وَالِاسْتِغْفَارِ وَالْحَسَنَاتِ وَالْمَصَائِبِ. قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنۡهُمۡ أَحۡسَنَ مَا عَمِلُواْ وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَعۡدَ ٱلصِّدۡقِ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ﴾ [الْأَحْقَاف: ١٦].
text.en: Among the effects of believing in this name is that the doer of good does not fear any injustice or curtailment with Him, Glorified is He, nor any loss or burden, nor that even the weight of an atom of his might be lost; for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has promised (and He is the Truthful) to pay those who work their wages in full. Even if it is the weight of an atom, He will reward him for it and not let it go to waste; rather, He multiplies it for whom He wills and gives from Himself a great reward. As for the doer of evil, He recompenses him with an evil like it, and removes it from him through repentance, remorse, seeking forgiveness, good deeds and afflictions. He the Exalted says: ﴾Those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds, among the companions of Paradise: the promise of truth which they had been promised﴿ [al-Ahqaf 46:16].

text.ar: «جَامِعُ التِّرْمِذِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٣٤٣٠)، وَ«سُنَنُ ابْنِ مَاجَهْ» (رَقْمُ: ٣٧٩٤). وَحَسَّنَهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ. وَانْظُرْ: «السِّلْسِلَةَ الصَّحِيحَةَ» (رَقْمُ: ١٣٩١).
text.en: *Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi* (no. 3430) and *Sunan Ibn Majah* (no. 3794). At-Tirmidhi graded it hasan (good). See *as-Silsilah as-Sahihah* (no. 1391).

text.ar: «مَدَارِجُ السَّالِكِينَ» (٣/ ٤٨٥).
text.en: *Madarij as-Salikin* (3/485).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ فِي «تَفْسِيرِهِ» (٢٢/ ٥٥٢).
text.en: Reported by Ibn Jarir at-Tabari in his *Tafsir* (22/552).

text.ar: ذَكَرَهُ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ فِي «تَفْسِيرِهِ» (٨/ ١٠٥).
text.en: Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir* (8/105).

text.ar: «مَجْمُوعُ الْفَتَاوَى» (١/ ٢١٨).
text.en: *Majmu‘ al-Fatawa* (1/218).

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ هَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ مَوْضِعاً مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ذُو ٱلرَّحۡمَةِۚ﴾ [الْأَنْعَامِ: ١٣٣]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ١٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ﴾ [لُقْمَانَ: ٢٦].
text.en: This name occurs in eighteen places in the Qur'an. He the Exalted says: ﴾And your Lord is the Free of need, the Possessor of mercy﴿ [al-An‘am 6:133], and He the Exalted says: ﴾O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴿ [Fatir 35:15], and He the Exalted says: ﴾To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴿ [Luqman 31:26].

text.ar: فَهُوَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى الْغَنِيُّ بِذَاتِهِ، الَّذِي لَهُ الْغِنَى التَّامُّ الْمُطْلَقُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْوُجُوهِ وَالِاعْتِبَارَاتِ، لِكَمَالِهِ وَكَمَالِ صِفَاتِهِ الَّتِي لَا يَتَطَرَّقُ إِلَيْهَا نَقْصٌ بِوَجْهٍ مِنَ الْوُجُوهِ، وَلَا يُمْكِنُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ غَنِيًّا؛ لِأَنَّ غِنَاهُ مِنْ لَوَازِمِ ذَاتِهِ، فَكَمَا لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا خَالِقًا رَازِقًا رَحِيمًا مُحْسِنًا؛ فَلَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا غَنِيًّا عَنْ جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ، لَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِمْ بِوَجْهٍ مِنَ الْوُجُوهِ، وَلَا يُمْكِنُ أَنْ يَكُونُوا كُلُّهُمْ إِلَّا مُفْتَقِرِينَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ كُلِّ وَجْهٍ، لَا يَسْتَغْنُونَ عَنْ إِحْسَانِهِ وَكَرَمِهِ وَتَدْبِيرِهِ وَتَرْبِيَتِهِ الْعَامَّةِ وَالْخَاصَّةِ طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ، وَكُلُّ مَنْ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، مَقْهُورُونَ بِقَهْرِهِ، مُصَرَّفُونَ بِمَشِيئَتِهِ، لَوْ أَهْلَكَهُمْ جَمِيعًا لَمْ يَنْقُصْ مِنْ عِزِّهِ وَسُلْطَانِهِ وَمُلْكِهِ وَرُبُوبِيَّتِهِ وَإِلَهِيَّتِهِ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ.
text.en: He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is al-Ghaniyy (the Free of All Need) in His very Self, who possesses complete and absolute freedom from need in every respect and consideration, because of His perfection and the perfection of His attributes, which no deficiency can touch in any way. He cannot be other than free of need, because His freedom from need is inseparable from His Self. Just as He cannot be other than Creator, Provider, Merciful and Beneficent, He cannot be other than free of need of all creation, not needing them in any way at all; and they, all of them, cannot be other than in need of Him in every respect, unable to do without His kindness, generosity, management and His general and special nurturing for even the blink of an eye. Everyone in the heavens and the earth is His servant, subdued by His dominance and directed by His will. Were He to destroy them all, it would not lessen His might, authority, dominion, Lordship and divinity by the weight of an atom.

text.ar: فَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ أَنَّهُ لَا تَنْفَعُهُ طَاعَةُ الطَّائِعِينَ، وَلَا تَضُرُّهُ مَعْصِيَةُ الْعَاصِينَ، فَلَوْ آمَنَ أَهْلُ الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعًا مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلْكِهِ شَيْئًا، وَلَوْ كَفَرُوا جَمِيعًا لَمْ يَنْقُصْ ذَلِكَ مِنْ مُلْكِهِ شَيْئًا، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيّٞ كَرِيمٞ﴾ [النَّمْلِ: ٤٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن جَٰهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَٰهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [الْعَنْكَبُوتِ: ٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَكَفَرُواْ وَتَوَلَّواْۖ وَّٱسۡتَغۡنَى ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٞ﴾ [التَّغَابُنِ: ٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِن تَكۡفُرُوٓاْ أَنتُمۡ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾ [إِبْرَاهِيمَ: ٨].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His freedom from need is that the obedience of the obedient does not benefit Him and the disobedience of the disobedient does not harm Him. If all the people of the earth believed, that would not add anything to His dominion, and if they all disbelieved, that would not take anything away from His dominion. He the Exalted says: ﴾And whoever is grateful is grateful only for his own good, and whoever is ungrateful, then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous﴿ [an-Naml 27:44], and He the Exalted says: ﴾And whoever strives only strives for his own good. Indeed, Allah is free of need of the worlds﴿ [al-‘Ankabut 29:6], and He the Exalted says: ﴾So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah showed He had no need of them; and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴿ [at-Taghabun 64:6], and He the Exalted says: ﴾If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth all together, then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴿ [Ibrahim 14:8].

text.ar: وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ الْقُدْسِيِّ يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: «يَا عِبَادِي لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَتْقَى قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلْكِي شَيْئًا، وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَفْجَرِ قَلْبِ رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ مُلْكِي شَيْئًا»، وَقَالَ: «يَا عِبَادِي إِنَّكُمْ لَنْ تَبْلُغُوا ضَرِّي فَتَضُرُّونِي، وَلَنْ تَبْلُغُوا نَفْعِي فَتَنْفَعُونِي» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[1].
text.en: In the hadith qudsi, Allah the Exalted says: “O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans among you and the jinn among you, were as pious as the most pious heart of any one man among you, that would not add anything to My dominion. And if the first of you and the last of you, the humans among you and the jinn among you, were as wicked as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would not take anything away from My dominion.” And He said: “O My servants, you will never be able to harm Me so as to harm Me, and you will never be able to benefit Me so as to benefit Me.” Muslim reported it[1].

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ أَنَّ إِنْفَاقَ الْمُنْفِقِينَ وَبَذْلَ الْبَاذِلِينَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ وَابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِهِ لَا يَنْفَعُهُ بِشَيْءٍ، وَكَذَلِكَ شُحُّ الشَّحِيحِينَ وَبُخْلُ الْبُخَلَاءِ لَا يَضُرُّهُ شَيْئًا، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم﴾ [مُحَمَّدٍ: ٣٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنفِقُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا كَسَبۡتُمۡ وَمِمَّآ أَخۡرَجۡنَا لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَلَا تَيَمَّمُواْ ٱلۡخَبِيثَ مِنۡهُ تُنفِقُونَ وَلَسۡتُم بِـَٔاخِذِيهِ إِلَّآ أَن تُغۡمِضُواْ فِيهِۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٦٧].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His freedom from need is that the spending of those who spend and the giving of those who give in His cause and in seeking His pleasure do not benefit Him in anything, and likewise the tight-fistedness of the tight-fisted and the miserliness of misers do not harm Him at all. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴿ [Muhammad 47:38], and He the Exalted says: ﴾O you who believe, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have brought forth for you from the earth. And do not aim for the bad of it to spend from, when you yourselves would not take it except with your eyes closed. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:267].

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ تَنَزُّهُهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْعُيُوبِ، فَمَنْ نَسَبَ إِلَيْهِ تَعَالَى نَقْصًا فَقَدْ نَسَبَ إِلَيْهِ مَا يُنَافِي غِنَاهُ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿قَالُواْ ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ وَلَدٗاۗ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥۖ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّۖ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ﴾ [يُونُسَ: ٦٨].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His freedom from need is that He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is far above all deficiencies and faults. Whoever attributes a deficiency to Him, Exalted is He, has attributed to Him what contradicts His freedom from need. He the Exalted says: ﴾They say, “Allah has taken a son.” Glorified is He! He is the Free of need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴿ [Yunus 10:68].

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ تَنَزُّهُهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى عَنِ الشُّرَكَاءِ وَالْأَنْدَادِ؛ إِذْ كَيْفَ يُسَوَّى التُّرَابُ بِرَبِّ الْأَرْبَابِ، وَكَيْفَ يُسَوَّى الْفَقِيرُ بِالذَّاتِ، الضَّعِيفُ بِالذَّاتِ، الْعَاجِزُ بِالذَّاتِ، الْمُحْتَاجُ بِالذَّاتِ، الَّذِي لَيْسَ لَهُ مِنْ ذَاتِهِ إِلَّا الْعَدَمُ؛ بِالْغَنِيِّ بِالذَّاتِ، الْقَادِرِ بِالذَّاتِ، الَّذِي غِنَاهُ وَقُدْرَتُهُ وَمُلْكُهُ وَجُودُهُ وَإِحْسَانُهُ وَعِلْمُهُ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَكَمَالُهُ الْمُطْلَقُ التَّامُّ مِنْ لَوَازِمِ ذَاتِهِ، وَكَيْفَ يُسَوَّى الْعَبِيدُ بِمَالِكِ الرِّقَابِ، الَّذِي جَمِيعُ رِقَابِ الْعَبِيدِ تَحْتَ قَبْضَتِهِ وَطَوْعَ تَدْبِيرِهِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَّقَدۡ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡمَسِيحُ ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَۚ قُلۡ فَمَن يَمۡلِكُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـًٔا إِنۡ أَرَادَ أَن يُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡمَسِيحَ ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ وَأُمَّهُۥ وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعٗاۗ وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۚ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ﴾ [الْمَائِدَةِ: ١٧].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His freedom from need is that He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is far above having partners and rivals. For how can dust be made equal to the Lord of lords? How can the one who is needy by his very essence, weak by his very essence, incapable by his very essence, dependent by his very essence, who has nothing of himself but nonexistence, be made equal to the One who is free of need by His very Self, All-Powerful by His very Self, whose freedom from need, power, dominion, generosity, kindness, knowledge, mercy and complete, absolute perfection are inseparable from His Self? And how can slaves be made equal to the Owner of all necks, under whose grasp and at the command of whose management are the necks of all the slaves? Allah the Exalted says: ﴾They have certainly disbelieved who say, “Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary.” Say: Then who could do anything against Allah if He intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth all together? And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah has power over all things﴿ [al-Ma'idah 5:17].

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ أَنَّ خَزَائِنَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ بِيَدِهِ، وَأَنَّ جُودَهُ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ مُتَوَاصِلٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَأَنَّ يَدَيْهِ سَحَّاءُ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ ﴿لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ﴾ [لُقْمَانَ: ٢٦].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His richness is that the treasuries of the heavens and the earth are in His hand, that His generosity to His creation continues through the hours of the night and the day, and that His hands pour out abundantly at all times: ﴾To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy﴿ [Luqman 31:26].

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ أَنَّهُ يَدْعُو عِبَادَهُ إِلَى سُؤَالِهِ كُلَّ وَقْتٍ، وَيَعِدُهُمْ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ بِالْإِجَابَةِ مَهْمَا عَظُمَ السُّؤَالُ، وَيَأْمُرُهُمْ بِعِبَادَتِهِ وَيَعِدُهُمُ الْقَبُولَ وَالْإِثَابَةَ، وَهُوَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى وَاسِعُ الْفَضْلِ، جَزِيلُ النَّوَالِ، وَقَدْ آتَاهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ مَا سَأَلُوهُ، وَأَعْطَاهُمْ كُلَّ مَا أَرَادُوهُ وَتَمَنَّوْهُ.
text.en: Part of the perfection of His richness is that He calls His servants to ask of Him at every moment, and promises them an answer when they do, however great the request; and He commands them to worship Him and promises them acceptance and reward. He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is vast in bounty and abundant in giving; He has given them of all that they asked of Him, and granted them all that they wanted and wished for.

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ أَنَّهُ لَوِ اجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَأَوَّلُ الْخَلْقِ وَآخِرُهُمْ فِي صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ فَسَأَلُوهُ كُلَّ مَا تَعَلَّقَتْ بِهِ مَطَالِبُهُمْ فَأَعْطَاهُمْ سُؤْلَهُمْ لَمْ يَنْقُصْ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا عِنْدَهُ، فَفِي الْحَدِيثِ الْقُدْسِيِّ يَقُولُ تَعَالَى: «يَا عِبَادِي لَوْ أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ، قَامُوا فِي صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ، فَسَأَلُونِي، فَأَعْطَيْتُ كُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ مَسْأَلَتَهُ، مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا عِنْدِي، إِلاّ كَمَا يَنْقُصُ الْمِخْيَطُ إِذَا أُدْخِلَ فِي الْبَحْرِ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[2].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His richness is that if the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, the first of creation and the last of them, gathered on one plain and asked Him for everything their wishes were attached to, and He gave them what they asked, that would not decrease anything of what He has. In the hadith qudsi, He the Exalted says: “O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans among you and the jinn among you, were to stand on one plain and ask of Me, and I were to give every person what he asked, that would not decrease what I have except as much as a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped into it.” Narrated by Muslim[2].

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ الْعَظِيمِ الَّذِي لَا يُقَادَرُ قَدْرُهُ وَلَا يُمْكِنُ وَصْفُهُ مَا يَبْسُطُهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى عَلَى أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ مِنْ صُنُوفِ اللَّذَّاتِ وَأَنْوَاعِ النِّعَمِ وَأَطَايِبِ الْمِنَنِ مِمَّا لَا عَيْنٌ رَأَتْ وَلَا أُذُنٌ سَمِعَتْ وَلَا خَطَرَ عَلَى قَلْبِ بَشَرٍ ﴿فَلَا تَعۡلَمُ نَفۡسٞ مَّآ أُخۡفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعۡيُنٖ جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ﴾ [السَّجْدَةِ: ١٧].
text.en: Part of the perfection of His immense richness, whose measure cannot be estimated and which cannot be described, is what He, Blessed and Exalted is He, spreads out for the people of faith in the Gardens of Bliss: kinds of delights, types of blessings and the finest of favours, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of any human being: ﴾No soul knows what has been hidden away for them of the comfort of eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴿ [as-Sajdah 32:17].

text.ar: فَمَنْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ بِهَذَا الْوَصْفِ الْعَظِيمِ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ، مَنْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ بِالْغِنَى الْمُطْلَقِ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ بِالْفَقْرِ الْمُطْلَقِ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ بِالْقُدْرَةِ التَّامَّةِ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ بِالْعَجْزِ التَّامِّ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ بِالْعِزِّ التَّامِّ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ بِالْمَسْكَنَةِ التَّامَّةِ، وَمَنْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ بِالْعِلْمِ التَّامِّ وَالْحِكْمَةِ عَرَفَ نَفْسَهُ بِالْجَهْلِ، وَعِلْمُ الْعَبْدِ بِافْتِقَارِهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ الَّذِي هُوَ ثَمَرَةُ هَذِهِ الْمَعْرِفَةِ هُوَ عُنْوَانُ سَعَادَةِ الْعَبْدِ وَفَلَاحِهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.
text.en: So whoever knows his Lord by this great description knows himself. Whoever knows his Lord by absolute richness knows himself by absolute poverty; whoever knows his Lord by complete power knows himself by complete helplessness; whoever knows his Lord by complete might knows himself by complete lowliness; and whoever knows his Lord by complete knowledge and wisdom knows himself by ignorance. The servant's knowledge of his need for Allah, which is the fruit of this knowledge, is the hallmark of the servant's happiness and success in this world and the Hereafter.

text.ar: (رَقْمُ: ٢٥٧٧) وَهُوَ طَرَفٌ مِنْ حَدِيثٍ طَوِيلٍ عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: (no. 2577). It is part of a long hadith from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him).

text.ar: طَرَفٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ الْمُتَقَدِّمِ.
text.en: Part of the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) mentioned above.

title.en: al-Karim, al-Akram (the Generous, the Most Generous)

text.ar: أَمَّا «الْكَرِيمُ» فَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي ثَلَاثَةِ مَوَاضِعَ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيّٞ كَرِيمٞ﴾ [النَّمْلِ: ٤٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلۡكَرِيمِ﴾ [الِانْفِطَارِ: ٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡحَقُّۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡكَرِيمِ﴾ [الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: ١١٦]، عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ مَنْ قَرَأَ بِرَفْعِ «الْكَرِيمُ» عَلَى أَنَّهُ صِفَةٌ لِلرَّبِّ.
text.en: As for “al-Karim” (the Generous), it occurs in three places. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And whoever is grateful is only grateful for the benefit of himself; and whoever is ungrateful, then indeed my Lord is Rich and Generous﴿ [an-Naml 27:40]; He the Exalted says: ﴾O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous﴿ [al-Infitar 82:6]; and He the Exalted says: ﴾So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth; there is no god but Him, the Lord of the Throne, the Generous﴿ [al-Mu’minun 23:116] — according to the reading of those who recite “al-Karim” in the nominative case, as a description of the Lord.

text.ar: وَأَمَّا «الْأَكْرَمُ» فَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱقۡرَأۡ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡأَكۡرَمُ﴾ [الْعَلَقِ: ٣].
text.en: As for “al-Akram” (the Most Generous), it occurs in one place, namely His saying, the Exalted: ﴾Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴿ [al-‘Alaq 96:3].

text.ar: وَ«الْكَرِيمُ»: هُوَ الْكَثِيرُ الْخَيْرِ الْعَظِيمُ النَّفْعِ، وَهُوَ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَحْسَنُهُ وَأَفْضَلُهُ، وَاللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَصَفَ نَفْسَهُ بِالْكَرَمِ كَمَا فِي الْآيَاتِ الْمُتَقَدِّمَةِ.
text.en: “Al-Karim” (the Generous) is the One abundant in good and immense in benefit; and the karim of anything is its finest and most excellent. Allah, Glorified is He, has described Himself with generosity (karam), as in the verses mentioned above.

text.ar: وَوَصَفَ كَلَامَهُ بِالْكَرَمِ كَمَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّهُۥ لَقُرۡءَانٞ كَرِيمٞ﴾ [الْوَاقِعَةِ: ٧٧]، أَيْ: كَثِيرُ الْخَيْرِ غَزِيرُ الْعِلْمِ، فَكُلُّ خَيْرٍ وَعِلْمٍ إِنَّمَا يُسْتَفَادُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ.
text.en: And He described His Speech as karim (noble), as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴾Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴿ [al-Waqi‘ah 56:77], meaning: abundant in good and rich in knowledge, for all good and knowledge is only gained from the Qur'an.

text.ar: وَوَصَفَ عَرْشَهُ بِذَلِكَ كَمَا فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡحَقُّۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡكَرِيمِ﴾ [الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: ١١٦]، عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ مَنْ قَرَأَ بِالْكَسْرِ عَلَى أَنَّهُ صِفَةٌ لِلْعَرْشِ، أَيْ: حَسَنُ الْمَنْظَرِ بَهِيُّ الشَّكْلِ.
text.en: And He described His Throne in the same way, as in His saying: ﴾So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth; there is no god but Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴿ [al-Mu’minun 23:116] — according to the reading of those who recite it in the genitive case, as a description of the Throne, meaning: beautiful in appearance and splendid in form.

text.ar: وَوَصَفَ بِذَلِكَ ثَوَابَهُ الْعَظِيمَ وَنَعِيمَهُ الْمُقِيمَ الَّذِي أَعَدَّهُ لِعِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَّهُمۡ دَرَجَٰتٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَمَغۡفِرَةٞ وَرِزۡقٞ كَرِيمٞ﴾ [الْأَنْفَالِ: ٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِن تَجۡتَنِبُواْ كَبَآئِرَ مَا تُنۡهَوۡنَ عَنۡهُ نُكَفِّرۡ عَنكُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَنُدۡخِلۡكُم مُّدۡخَلٗا كَرِيمٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ٣١]، وَالْمُدْخَلُ الْكَرِيمُ هُوَ الطَّيِّبُ الْحَسَنُ السَّالِمُ مِنَ الْآفَاتِ وَالْعَاهَاتِ وَمِنَ الْهُمُومِ وَالْأَحْزَانِ وَمِنَ الْمُنَغِّصَاتِ وَالْمُكَدِّرَاتِ.
text.en: And He described with it His immense reward and lasting bliss that He has prepared for His believing servants. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾For them are ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness and noble provision﴿ [al-Anfal 8:4], and He the Exalted says: ﴾If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴿ [an-Nisa’ 4:31]. The noble entrance is the one that is good and fine, free from afflictions and defects, from worries and sorrows, and from everything that spoils and troubles.

text.ar: وَوَصَفَ بِذَلِكَ مَا كَثُرَ خَيْرُهُ وَحَسُنَ مَنْظَرُهُ مِنَ النَّبَاتِ وَغَيْرِهِ كَمَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمۡ أَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجٖ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [الشُّعَرَاءِ: ٧].
text.en: And He described with it plants and other things whose good is abundant and whose appearance is beautiful, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴾Have they not looked at the earth, how much We have caused to grow in it of every noble kind﴿ [ash-Shu‘ara’ 26:7].

text.ar: وَلَفْظُ «الْكَرَمِ» لَفْظٌ جَامِعٌ لِلْمَحَاسِنِ وَالْمَحَامِدِ، لَا يُرَادُ بِهِ مُجَرَّدُ الْإِعْطَاءِ، بَلِ الْإِعْطَاءُ مِنْ تَمَامِ مَعْنَاهُ، وَلِذَا وَرَدَ عَنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ فِي مَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ أَقْوَالٌ عَدِيدَةٌ، فَقِيلَ: مَعْنَاهُ: أَيْ: كَثِيرُ الْخَيْرِ وَالْعَطَاءِ، وَقِيلَ: الدَّائِمُ بِالْخَيْرِ، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي لَهُ قَدْرٌ عَظِيمٌ وَشَأْنٌ كَبِيرٌ، وَقِيلَ: أَيْ: الْمُنَزَّهُ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْآفَاتِ، وَقِيلَ: مَعْنَاهُ: الْمُكْرِمُ الْمُنْعِمُ الْمُتَفَضِّلُ، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي يُعْطِي لَا لِعِوَضٍ، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي يُعْطِي لِغَيْرِ سَبَبٍ، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي يُعْطِي مَنْ يَحْتَاجُ وَمَنْ لَا يَحْتَاجُ، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي إِذَا وَعَدَ وَفَّى، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي تُرْفَعُ إِلَيْهِ كُلُّ حَاجَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ أَوْ كَبِيرَةٍ، وَقِيلَ: الَّذِي لَا يُضِيعُ مَنِ الْتَجَأَ إِلَيْهِ، وَقِيلَ فِي مَعْنَاهُ: الَّذِي يَتَجَاوَزُ عَنِ الذُّنُوبِ وَيَغْفِرُ السَّيِّئَاتِ، إِلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا قِيلَ فِي مَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ حَقٌّ؛ لِأَنَّ هَذَا الِاسْمَ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحُسْنَى الدَّالَّةِ عَلَى مَعَانٍ عَدِيدَةٍ لَا عَلَى مَعْنًى مُفْرَدٍ، وَإِذَا اعْتَبَرْتَ جَمِيعَ مَا قِيلَ فِي مَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ الَّذِي وَجَبَ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ ذَلِكَ لَا يُحْصَى مِنْ جَلَائِلِ الْمَعَانِي وَكَرَائِمِ الْأَوْصَافِ.
text.en: The word “karam” (generosity) is a comprehensive word for all excellent and praiseworthy qualities. It does not mean merely giving; rather, giving is part of the completeness of its meaning. For this reason, many views have been reported from the scholars about the meaning of this name. It has been said that it means: abundant in good and giving. It has been said: the One who is constant in good. It has been said: the One who has immense standing and great importance. It has been said: the One who is free from deficiencies and defects. It has been said that it means: the One who honours, bestows blessings and grants favour. It has been said: the One who gives without seeking anything in return. It has been said: the One who gives without a cause. It has been said: the One who gives both the one in need and the one not in need. It has been said: the One who fulfils His promise when He promises. It has been said: the One to whom every need, small or great, is raised. It has been said: the One who does not abandon whoever seeks refuge with Him. And it has been said about its meaning: the One who overlooks sins and forgives misdeeds — along with other things that have been said about the meaning of this great name. All of this is true, because this name is one of the Most Beautiful Names that indicate many meanings, not a single meaning. If you consider everything that has been said about the meaning of this name, you will know that what is due to Allah the Exalted from it, of sublime meanings and noble attributes, cannot be counted.

text.ar: فَإِذَا قُلْنَا: الْكَرِيمُ: هُوَ الْكَثِيرُ الْخَيْرِ وَالْعَطَاءِ؛ فَمَنْ أَكْثَرُ خَيْرًا مِنَ اللَّهِ؛ لِعُمُومِ قُدْرَتِهِ وَسَعَةِ عَطَائِهِ، بَلِ الْخَيْرُ كُلُّهُ فِي يَدَيْهِ.
text.en: So if we say: al-Karim (the Generous) is the One abundant in good and giving, then who is more abundant in good than Allah, because of the all-encompassing reach of His power and the vastness of His giving? Indeed, all good is in His hands.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: إِنَّهُ الدَّائِمُ بِالْخَيْرِ؛ فَذَلِكَ بِالْحَقِيقَةِ لِلَّهِ وَحْدَهُ، فَإِنَّ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ يَنْقَطِعُ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَإِحْسَانَهُ، فَإِنَّهُ دَائِمٌ مُتَّصِلٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.
text.en: If we say: He is the One constant in good, then in reality that belongs to Allah alone, for everything comes to an end except Allah and His kindness, which is constant and continuous in this world and the Hereafter.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: إِنَّ الْكَرِيمَ هُوَ الَّذِي لَهُ قَدْرٌ عَظِيمٌ وَشَأْنٌ كَبِيرٌ؛ فَاللَّهُ جَلَّ وَعَلَا لَا يُقْدَرُ قَدْرُهُ وَلَا يُدْرِكُ الْعِبَادُ كُنْهَ صِفَاتِهِ وَكَمَالَ نُعُوتِهِ.
text.en: If we say: al-Karim (the Generous) is the One who has immense standing and great importance, then Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, cannot be estimated in His true measure, and the servants cannot grasp the true nature of His attributes or the perfection of His qualities.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: إِنَّ الْكَرِيمَ هُوَ الْمُنَزَّهُ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْآفَاتِ فَهُوَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ بِالْحَقِيقَةِ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ، الَّذِي لَا يَلْحَقُ النَّقْصُ شَيْئًا مِنْ صِفَاتِهِ، الْمُنَزَّهُ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْعُيُوبِ.
text.en: If we say: al-Karim (the Generous) is the One free from deficiencies and defects, then in reality that is Allah alone, al-Quddus (the Most Holy), as-Salam (the Flawless), none of whose attributes is touched by any deficiency, the One free from deficiencies and faults.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: إِنَّ الْكَرِيمَ مَعْنَاهُ الْمُكْرِمُ الْمُنْعِمُ الْمُتَفَضِّلُ؛ فَمَنِ الْمُكْرِمُ الْمُنْعِمُ الْمُتَفَضِّلُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَقَالِيدُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَخَزَائِنُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَالْفَضْلُ كُلُّهُ بِيَدِهِ، يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ، وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَمَنْ لَمْ يُكْرِمْهُ اللَّهُ فَمَنِ الَّذِي يُكْرِمُهُ ﴿وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكۡرِمٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ١٨].
text.en: If we say: al-Karim (the Generous) means the One who honours, bestows blessings and grants favour, then who honours, bestows blessings and grants favour except Allah alone, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth and the treasuries of all things? All bounty is in His hand; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of immense bounty. And whomever Allah does not honour, who is there to honour him? ﴾And whoever Allah humiliates, there is none to honour him. Indeed, Allah does what He wills﴿ [al-Hajj 22:18].

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ: الَّذِي يُعْطِي لَا لِعِوَضٍ؛ فَلَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، فَالْخَلْقُ خَلْقُهُ، وَالْمُلْكُ مُلْكُهُ، وَالْعَطَاءُ عَطَاؤُهُ، وَلَا يَبْلُغُ الْعِبَادُ نَفْعَهُ بِشَيْءٍ، فَهُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ.
text.en: If we say: it means the One who gives without seeking anything in return, then none is like that except Allah alone. The creation is His creation, the dominion is His dominion and the giving is His giving, and the servants can never reach the point of benefiting Him in anything, for He is al-Ghaniyy (the Rich), al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy).

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ: الَّذِي يُعْطِي لِغَيْرِ سَبَبٍ فَهُوَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ الْمُتَفَضِّلُ بِالنَّوَالِ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُؤَالٍ، بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ بِالنِّعَمِ، وَأَوْسَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعَطَاءَ تَفَضُّلًا مِنْهُ وَكَرَمًا.
text.en: If we say: it means the One who gives without a cause, then that is Allah alone, who grants His gifts as a favour without being asked. He began the creation with blessings and gave to them abundantly, out of His favour and generosity.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ الَّذِي يُعْطِي مَنْ يَحْتَاجُ وَمَنْ لَا يَحْتَاجُ؛ فَهُوَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ يُعْطِي الْمُحْتَاجَ حَاجَتَهُ وَيَزِيدُهُ إِنْعَاماً مِنْهُ وَتَفَضُّلاً.
text.en: If we say: it means the One who gives both the one in need and the one not in need, then that is Allah alone. He gives the needy what he needs and gives him more, as a blessing and favour from Him.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ الَّذِي إِذَا وَعَدَ وَفَى؛ فَإِنَّ كُلَّ مَنْ يَعِدُ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ يَفِيَ وَيُمْكِنُ أَنْ يَقْطَعَهُ عُذْرٌ، وَيَحُولَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْوَفَاءِ أَمْرٌ، وَالْبَارِي صَادِقُ الْوَعْدِ لِعُمُومِ قُدْرَتِهِ وَعَظِيمِ مُلْكِهِ، لَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَى، وَلَا مُعْطِيَ لِمَا مَنَعَ.
text.en: If we say: it means the One who fulfils His promise when He promises, then everyone who makes a promise may fulfil it, or he may be cut off from it by some excuse, or something may come between him and fulfilling it. But al-Bari (the Maker) is true to His promise, because of the all-encompassing reach of His power and the greatness of His dominion; none can withhold what He gives, and none can give what He withholds.

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ الَّذِي تُرْفَعُ إِلَيْهِ كُلُّ حَاجَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ وَكَبِيرَةٍ فَهُوَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ ﴿يَسۡـَٔلُهُۥ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ كُلَّ يَوۡمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأۡنٖ﴾ [الرَّحْمَنِ: ٢٩].
text.en: If we say: it means the One to whom every need, small and great, is raised, then that is Allah alone: ﴾Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks of Him; every day He is engaged in some matter﴿ [ar-Rahman 55:29].

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ أَيْ: الَّذِي لَا يُضِيعُ مَنِ الْتَجَأَ إِلَيْهِ؛ فَهُوَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ الْقَائِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ: ﴿إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ مَنۡ أَحۡسَنَ عَمَلًا﴾ [الْكَهْفِ: ٣٠]، وَالْقَائِلُ: ﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدۡعُونِيٓ أَسۡتَجِبۡ لَكُمۡۚ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ٦٠].
text.en: If we say: it means the One who does not abandon whoever seeks refuge with Him, then that is Allah alone, who says of Himself: ﴾Indeed, We do not let the reward of one who does good deeds be lost﴿ [al-Kahf 18:30], and who says: ﴾And your Lord said: Call on Me; I will respond to you﴿ [Ghafir 40:60].

text.ar: وَإِذَا قُلْنَا: مَعْنَاهُ الَّذِي يَتَجَاوَزُ عَنِ الذُّنُوبِ وَيَغْفِرُ السَّيِّئَاتِ؛ فَهُوَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، وَهُوَ مِنْ كَرَمِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ لَا يَتَعَاظَمُهُ ذَنْبٌ أَنْ يَغْفِرَهُ، فَمِنْ كَرَمِهِ أَنَّهُ هُوَ الَّذِي جَادَ وَتَفَضَّلَ بِالتَّوْبَةِ عَلَى التَّائِبِ، وَمِنْ كَرَمِهِ تَفَضُّلُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ بِقَبُولِهَا مَهْمَا عَظُمَ الذَّنْبُ وَكَبُرَ الْجُرْمُ، وَمِنْ كَرَمِهِ أَنَّهُ يُبَدِّلُ سَيِّئَاتِ التَّائِبِينَ حَسَنَاتٍ، وَمِنْ كَرَمِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنَّهُ يَفْرَحُ بِتَوْبَةِ التَّائِبِينَ وَإِنَابَةِ الْمُنِيبِينَ، وَمِنْ كَرَمِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنَّهُ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا مَدَّ يَدَيْهِ إِلَيْهِ سَائِلًا مُتَذَلِّلًا أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْرًا خَائِبَتَيْنِ[1].
text.en: If we say: it means the One who overlooks sins and forgives misdeeds, then that is Allah alone. Out of His generosity, Glorified is He, no sin is too great for Him to forgive. Part of His generosity is that it is He who generously grants repentance to the one who repents as a favour; part of His generosity is that He, Glorified is He, favours him by accepting it, however great the sin and however grave the offence; part of His generosity is that He changes the misdeeds of those who repent into good deeds; part of His generosity, Glorified is He, is that He rejoices at the repentance of those who repent and the return of those who turn back to Him; and part of His generosity, Glorified is He, is that He is too shy before His servant, when the servant raises his hands to Him asking and humbling himself, to turn them back empty and disappointed[1].

text.ar: وَأَعْظَمُ أَسْبَابِ نَيْلِ كَرَامَةِ الْكَرِيمِ سُبْحَانَهُ تَقْوَاهُ جَلَّ وَعَلَا فِي السِّرِّ وَالْعَلَنِ، فَالْأَكْرَمُ عِنْدَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ الْأَتْقَى لَهُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ﴾ [الْحُجُرَاتِ: ١٣].
text.en: The greatest means of attaining the honour bestowed by al-Karim (the Generous), Glorified is He, is having taqwa of Him, Exalted and Majestic is He, in private and in public. The most honoured in His sight, Glorified is He, is the one among His servants who has the most taqwa of Him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴿ [al-Hujurat 49:13].

text.ar: جَعَلَنَا اللَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ، وَمِنْ أَوْلِيَائِهِ الْمُكْرَمِينَ، إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ مُجِيبٌ.
text.en: May Allah make us among His servants who have taqwa, and among His honoured allies; indeed, He is All-Hearing, Ever-Responsive.

text.ar: انْظُرْ: «الْأَسْنَى فِي شَرْحِ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى» لِلْقُرْطُبِيِّ (١/ ٣٣ـ٣٩).
text.en: See: *al-Asna fi Sharh Asma’ Allah al-Husna* by al-Qurtubi (1/33–39).

text.ar: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ وَرَدَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً فِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ﴾ [الْحَشْرِ: ٢٣].
text.en: It is a name that occurs in the Noble Qur'an once, in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴾He is Allah, besides whom there is no god; the King, the Most Holy, the Flawless, the Granter of Security, the Overseer, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glorified is Allah above what they associate with Him﴿ [al-Hashr 59:23].

text.ar: وَمَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ الْكَرِيمِ أَيْ: السَّلَامُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْعُيُوبِ وَالنَّقَائِصِ، لِكَمَالِهِ فِي ذَاتِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ وَأَفْعَالِهِ، فَهُوَ جَلَّ وَعَلَا السَّلَامُ الْحَقُّ بِكُلِّ اعْتِبَارٍ، سَلَامٌ فِي ذَاتِهِ عَنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ وَنَقْصٍ يَتَخَيَّلُهُ وَهْمٌ، وَسَلَامٌ فِي صِفَاتِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ وَنَقْصٍ، وَسَلَامٌ فِي أَفْعَالِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ وَنَقْصٍ وَشَرٍّ وَظُلْمٍ وَفِعْلٍ وَاقِعٍ عَلَى غَيْرِ وَجْهِ الْحِكْمَةِ، وَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ السَّلَامُ مِنَ الصَّاحِبَةِ وَالْوَلَدِ، وَالسَّلَامُ مِنَ النَّظِيرِ وَالْكُفْءِ وَالسَّمِيِّ وَالْمُمَاثِلِ، وَالسَّلَامُ مِنَ النِّدِّ وَالشَّرِيكِ.
text.en: The meaning of this noble name is: the One free from all defects and deficiencies, because of His perfection in His Essence, His attributes and His actions. He, Exalted and Majestic is He, is as-Salam (the Flawless), truly and in every respect: free in His Essence from every defect and deficiency that any imagination might conceive; free in His attributes from every defect and deficiency; and free in His actions from every defect, deficiency, evil and injustice, and from any action that is not in accordance with wisdom. He, Glorified is He, is free from having a wife or a child, free from having any equal, peer, namesake or likeness, and free from having any rival or partner.

text.ar: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ يَتَنَاوَلُ جَمِيعَ صِفَاتِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، فَكُلُّ صِفَةٍ مِنْ صِفَاتِهِ جَلَّ وَعَلَا سَلَامٌ مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ وَنَقْصٍ، وَفِي تَفْصِيلِ هَذَا وَتَقْرِيرِهِ يَقُولُ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: «وَلِذَلِكَ إِذَا نَظَرْتَ إِلَى أَفْرَادِ صِفَاتِ كَمَالِهِ وَجَدْتَ كُلَّ صِفَةٍ سَلَامًا مِمَّا يُضَادُّ كَمَالَهَا، فَحَيَاتُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ وَمِنَ السِّنَةِ وَالنَّوْمِ، وَكَذَلِكَ قَيُّومِيَّتُهُ وَقُدْرَتُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ التَّعَبِ وَاللُّغُوبِ، وَعِلْمُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ عُزُوبِ شَيْءٍ عَنْهُ أَوْ عُرُوضِ نِسْيَانٍ أَوْ حَاجَةٍ إِلَى تَذَكُّرٍ وَتَفَكُّرٍ، وَإِرَادَتُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ خُرُوجِهَا عَنِ الْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَصْلَحَةِ، وَكَلِمَاتُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ الْكَذِبِ وَالظُّلْمِ، بَلْ تَمَّتْ كَلِمَاتُهُ صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا، وَغِنَاهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ الْحَاجَةِ إِلَى غَيْرِهِ بِوَجْهٍ مَا، بَلْ كُلُّ مَا سِوَاهُ مُحْتَاجٌ إِلَيْهِ، وَهُوَ غَنِيٌّ عَنْ كُلِّ مَا سِوَاهُ، وَمُلْكُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ مُنَازِعٍ فِيهِ أَوْ مُشَارِكٍ أَوْ مُعَاوِنٍ مُظَاهِرٍ أَوْ شَافِعٍ عِنْدَهُ بِدُونِ إِذْنِهِ، وَإِلَهِيَّتُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ مُشَارِكٍ لَهُ فِيهَا، بَلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلاّ هُوَ.
text.en: It is a name that encompasses all the attributes of Allah the Exalted, for every one of His attributes, Exalted and Majestic is He, is free from every defect and deficiency. Explaining and establishing this in detail, Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) says: “That is why, if you look at His attributes of perfection one by one, you will find each attribute free from whatever opposes its perfection. His life is free from death, drowsiness and sleep. Likewise, His self-subsistence and His power are free from tiredness and fatigue. His knowledge is free from anything escaping it, from forgetfulness occurring to it, and from any need to recall or reflect. His will is free from departing from wisdom and benefit. His words are free from falsehood and injustice; rather, His words are complete in truthfulness and justice. His richness is free from needing anyone else in any way at all; rather, everything other than Him is in need of Him, and He is free of need of everything other than Him. His dominion is free from anyone contesting it, sharing in it, assisting and supporting Him, or interceding with Him without His permission. His divinity is free from anyone sharing it with Him; rather, He is Allah, besides whom there is no god.

text.ar: وَحِلْمُهُ وَعَفْوُهُ وَصَفْحُهُ وَمَغْفِرَتُهُ وَتَجَاوُزُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ أَنْ تَكُونَ عَنْ حَاجَةٍ مِنْهُ أَوْ ذُلٍّ أَوْ مُصَانَعَةٍ كَمَا يَكُونُ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ، بَلْ هُوَ مَحْضُ جُودِهِ وَإِحْسَانِهِ وَكَرَمِهِ، وَكَذَلِكَ عَذَابُهُ وَانْتِقَامُهُ وَشِدَّةُ بَطْشِهِ وَسُرْعَةُ عِقَابِهِ سَلَامٌ مِنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ ظُلْمًا أَوْ تَشَفِّيًّا أَوْ غِلْظَةً أَوْ قَسْوَةً، بَلْ هُوَ مَحْضُ حِكْمَتِهِ وَعَدْلِهِ وَوَضْعِهِ الْأَشْيَاءَ مَوَاضِعَهَا، وَهُوَ مِمَّا يَسْتَحِقُّ عَلَيْهِ الْحَمْدَ وَالثَّنَاءَ كَمَا يَسْتَحِقُّهُ عَلَى إِحْسَانِهِ وَثَوَابِهِ وَنِعَمِهِ، بَلْ لَوْ وَضَعَ الثَّوَابَ مَوْضِعَ الْعُقُوبَةِ لَكَانَ مُنَاقِضًا لِحِكْمَتِهِ وَلِعِزَّتِهِ، فَوَضْعُهُ الْعُقُوبَةَ مَوْضِعَهَا هُوَ مِنْ حَمْدِهِ وَحِكْمَتِهِ وَعِزَّتِهِ، فَهُوَ سَلَامٌ مِمَّا يَتَوَهَّمُ أَعْدَاؤُهُ وَالْجَاهِلُونَ بِهِ مِنْ خِلَافِ حِكْمَتِهِ.
text.en: His forbearance, His pardon, His overlooking, His forgiveness and His letting faults pass are free from stemming from any need on His part, or any humiliation, or any flattery, as happens with others; rather, they are purely His generosity, kindness and nobility. Likewise, His punishment, His retribution, the severity of His seizing and the swiftness of His penalty are free from being injustice, a quest to vent anger, harshness or cruelty; rather, they are purely His wisdom and justice and His putting things in their proper places. This is something for which He deserves praise and commendation, just as He deserves it for His kindness, His reward and His blessings. Indeed, if He were to put reward in the place of punishment, that would contradict His wisdom and His might. So His putting punishment in its proper place is part of His praiseworthiness, His wisdom and His might. Thus He is free from what His enemies and those ignorant of Him imagine of His acting contrary to His wisdom.

text.ar: وَقَضَاؤُهُ وَقَدَرُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ الْعَبَثِ وَالْجَوْرِ وَالظُّلْمِ وَمِنْ تَوَهُّمِ وُقُوعِهِ عَلَى خِلَافِ الْحِكْمَةِ الْبَالِغَةِ، وَشَرْعُهُ وَدِينُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ التَّنَاقُضِ وَالِاخْتِلَافِ وَالِاضْطِرَابِ وَخِلَافِ مَصْلَحَةِ الْعِبَادِ وَرَحْمَتِهِمْ وَالْإِحْسَانِ إِلَيْهِمْ وَخِلَافِ حِكْمَتِهِ، بَلْ شَرْعُهُ كُلُّهُ حِكْمَةٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَمَصْلَحَةٌ وَعَدْلٌ.
text.en: His decree and predestination are free from futility, oppression and injustice, and from any notion that they occur contrary to perfect wisdom. His law and His religion are free from contradiction, inconsistency and confusion, and from anything contrary to the welfare of the servants, mercy towards them and kindness to them, or contrary to His wisdom; rather, His law is all wisdom, mercy, benefit and justice.

text.ar: وَكَذَلِكَ عَطَاؤُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ كَوْنِهِ مُعَاوَضَةً أَوْ لِحَاجَةٍ إِلَى الْمُعْطَى، وَمَنْعُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنَ الْبُخْلِ وَخَوْفِ الْإِمْلَاقِ، بَلْ عَطَاؤُهُ إِحْسَانٌ مَحْضٌ لَا لِمُعَاوَضَةٍ وَلَا لِحَاجَةٍ، وَمَنْعُهُ عَدْلٌ مَحْضٌ وَحِكْمَةٌ لَا يَشُوبُهُ بُخْلٌ وَلَا عَجْزٌ.
text.en: Likewise, His giving is free from being an exchange or from arising out of need of the one given to, and His withholding is free from stinginess and fear of poverty. Rather, His giving is pure kindness, not for exchange or out of need, and His withholding is pure justice and wisdom, untouched by stinginess or inability.

text.ar: وَاسْتِوَاؤُهُ وَعُلُوُّهُ عَلَى عَرْشِهِ سَلَامٌ مِنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُحْتَاجًا إِلَى مَا يَحْمِلُهُ أَوْ يَسْتَوِي عَلَيْهِ، بَلِ الْعَرْشُ مُحْتَاجٌ إِلَيْهِ، وَحَمَلَتُهُ مُحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ، فَهُوَ الْغَنِيُّ عَنِ الْعَرْشِ وَعَنْ حَمَلَتِهِ وَعَنْ كُلِّ مَا سِوَاهُ، فَهُوَ اسْتِوَاءٌ وَعُلُوٌّ لَا يَشُوبُهُ حَصْرٌ وَلَا حَاجَةٌ إِلَى عَرْشٍ وَلَا غَيْرِهِ وَلَا إِحَاطَةُ شَيْءٍ بِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى، بَلْ كَانَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَلَا عَرْشَ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ بِهِ حَاجَةٌ إِلَيْهِ وَهُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ، بَلِ اسْتِوَاؤُهُ عَلَى عَرْشِهِ وَاسْتِيلَاؤُهُ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ مِنْ مُوجِبَاتِ مُلْكِهِ وَقَهْرِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَاجَةٍ إِلَى عَرْشٍ وَلَا غَيْرِهِ بِوَجْهٍ مَا.
text.en: His rising over (istiwa’) and His elevation above His Throne are free from His being in need of anything that carries Him or that He rises over; rather, the Throne is in need of Him, and its bearers are in need of Him. He is free of need of the Throne, of its bearers and of everything other than Him. It is a rising and an elevation untouched by any confinement, any need for a Throne or anything else, or anything encompassing Him, Glorified and Exalted is He. Indeed, He, Glorified is He, existed when there was no Throne, and He had no need of it, and He is al-Ghaniyy (the Rich), al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy). Rather, His rising over His Throne and His dominance over His creation are among the requirements of His dominion and His overpowering might, without any need for a Throne or anything else in any way at all.

text.ar: وَنُزُولُهُ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى سَمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا سَلَامٌ مِمَّا يُضَادُّ عُلُوَّهُ، وَسَلَامٌ مِمَّا يُضَادُّ غِنَاهُ وَكَمَالَهُ، وَسَلَامٌ مِنْ كُلِّ مَا يَتَوَهَّمُ مُعَطِّلٌ وَمُشَبِّهٌ، وَسَلَامٌ مِنْ أَنْ يَصِيرَ تَحْتَ شَيْءٍ أَوْ مَحْصُورًا فِي شَيْءٍ تَعَالَى اللَّهُ رَبُّنَا عَنْ كُلِّ مَا يُضَادُّ كَمَالَهُ وَغِنَاهُ.
text.en: His descending every night to the lowest heaven is free from whatever opposes His elevation, free from whatever opposes His richness and perfection, free from everything that a denier or a likener imagines, and free from His coming to be beneath anything or confined within anything. Exalted is Allah, our Lord, above everything that opposes His perfection and His richness.

text.ar: وَسَمْعُهُ وَبَصَرُهُ سَلَامٌ مِنْ كُلِّ مَا يَتَخَيَّلُهُ مُشَبِّهٌ أَوْ يَتَقَوَّلُهُ مُعَطِّلٌ، وَمُوَالَاتُهُ لِأَوْلِيَائِهِ سَلَامٌ مِنْ أَنْ تَكُونَ عَنْ ذُلٍّ كَمَا يُوَالِي الْمَخْلُوقُ الْمَخْلُوقَ، بَلْ هِيَ مُوَالَاةُ رَحْمَةٍ وَخَيْرٍ وَإِحْسَانٍ وَبِرٍّ، كَمَا قَالَ: ﴿وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدٗا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٞ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِيّٞ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّۖ﴾ [الْإِسْرَاءِ: ١١١]، فَلَمْ يَنْفِ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ مُطْلَقًا، بَلْ نَفَى أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلِيٌّ مِنَ الذُّلِّ.
text.en: His hearing and His seeing are free from everything that a likener imagines or a denier falsely claims. His taking His allies as friends is free from stemming from humiliation, as one created being takes another as an ally; rather, it is an alliance of mercy, good, kindness and benevolence, as He says: ﴾And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no ally out of humiliation﴿ [al-Isra’ 17:111]. So He did not deny having an ally altogether; rather, He denied having an ally out of humiliation.

text.ar: وَكَذَلِكَ مَحَبَّتُهُ لِمُحِبِّيهِ وَأَوْلِيَائِهِ سَلَامٌ مِنْ عَوَارِضِ مَحَبَّةِ الْمَخْلُوقِ لِلْمَخْلُوقِ مِنْ كَوْنِهَا مَحَبَّةَ حَاجَةٍ إِلَيْهِ أَوْ تَمَلُّقٍ لَهُ أَوِ انْتِفَاعٍ بِقُرْبِهِ، وَسَلَامٌ مِمَّا يَتَقَوَّلُهُ الْمُعَطِّلُونَ فِيهَا، وَكَذَلِكَ مَا أَضَافَهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ مِنَ الْيَدِ وَالْوَجْهِ فَإِنَّهُ سَلَامٌ عَمَّا يَتَخَيَّلُهُ مُشَبِّهٌ أَوْ يَتَقَوَّلُهُ مُعَطِّلٌ».
text.en: Likewise, His love for those who love Him and for His allies is free from the traits of one creature's love for another, such as its being a love born of need for the beloved, or flattery of him, or seeking benefit from being close to him; and it is free from what the deniers falsely say about it. Likewise, what He has attributed to Himself of the Hand and the Face is free from whatever a likener imagines or a denier falsely claims.”

text.ar: ثُمَّ خَتَمَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى هَذَا التَّقْرِيرَ الْوَافِيَ بِقَوْلِهِ: «فَتَأَمَّلْ كَيْفَ تَضَمَّنَ اسْمُهُ «السَّلَامُ» كُلَّ مَا نُزِّهَ عَنْهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى، وَكَمْ مِمَّنْ حَفِظَ هَذَا الِاسْمَ لَا يَدْرِي مَا تَضَمَّنَهُ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأَسْرَارِ وَالْمَعَانِي»[1].
text.en: Then he (may Allah have mercy on him) concluded this thorough exposition by saying: “So reflect on how His name ‘as-Salam’ (the Flawless) encompasses everything that He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is declared free from. And how many there are who have memorised this name without knowing the secrets and meanings it contains!”[1].

text.ar: وَمِنْ دَلَائِلِ هَذَا الِاسْمِ أَنَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى ذُو السَّلَامِ، أَيْ: الْمُسَلِّمُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ، فَهُوَ الْمُسَلِّمُ عَلَى رُسُلِهِ وَأَنْبِيَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَاةُ اللَّهِ وَسَلَامُهُ؛ لِإِيمَانِهِمْ وَكَمَالِ عُبُودِيَّتِهِمْ وَقِيَامِهِمْ بِالْبَلَاغِ الْمُبِينِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ عِبَادِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰٓۗ﴾ [النَّمْلِ: ٥٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٖ فِي ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ٧٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ١٠٩]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ١٢٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَلَٰمٌ عَلَىٰٓ إِلۡ يَاسِينَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ١٣٠]، وَالْمُسَلِّمُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ وَأَوْلِيَائِهِ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿تَحِيَّتُهُمۡ يَوۡمَ يَلۡقَوۡنَهُۥ سَلَٰمٞۚ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرٗا كَرِيمٗا﴾ [الْأَحْزَابِ: ٤٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا بِإِذۡنِ رَبِّهِمۡۖ تَحِيَّتُهُمۡ فِيهَا سَلَٰمٌ﴾ [إِبْرَاهِيمَ: ٢٣]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿سَلَٰمٞ قَوۡلٗا مِّن رَّبّٖ رَّحِيمٖ﴾ [يس: ٥٨].
text.en: Among the indications of this name is that He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is the Possessor of salam (peace), meaning the One who sends peace upon His servants. He sends peace upon His messengers and prophets, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them, because of their faith, the perfection of their servitude and their conveying the message clearly. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Say: Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen﴿ [an-Naml 27:59]; He the Exalted says: ﴾Peace be upon Nuh among all the worlds﴿ [as-Saffat 37:79]; He the Exalted says: ﴾Peace be upon Ibrahim﴿ [as-Saffat 37:109]; He the Exalted says: ﴾Peace be upon Musa and Harun﴿ [as-Saffat 37:120]; and He the Exalted says: ﴾Peace be upon Ilyasin﴿ [as-Saffat 37:130]. And He sends peace upon His servants and allies in the Gardens of Bliss. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be: Peace. And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴿ [al-Ahzab 33:44]; He the Exalted says: ﴾abiding therein eternally by the permission of their Lord; their greeting therein will be: Peace﴿ [Ibrahim 14:23]; and He the Exalted says: ﴾Peace — a word from a Merciful Lord﴿ [Ya-Sin 36:58].

text.ar: وَجَعَلَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى جَنَّتَهُ دَارَ السَّلَامِ لِعِبَادِهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ وَالْأَسْقَامِ وَالْأَحْزَانِ وَالْآلَامِ وَالْهُمُومِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْآفَاتِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَهُمۡ دَارُ ٱلسَّلَٰمِ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡۖ﴾ [الْأَنْعَامِ: ١٢٧]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ دَارِ ٱلسَّلَٰمِ﴾ [يُونُسَ: ٢٥].
text.en: He, Blessed and Exalted is He, has made His Paradise the Abode of Peace for His servants, safe from death, illness, sorrows, pains, worries and other afflictions. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾For them will be the Abode of Peace with their Lord﴿ [al-An‘am 6:127], and He the Exalted says: ﴾And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace﴿ [Yunus 10:25].

text.ar: وَجَعَلَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى إِفْشَاءَ هَذَا الِاسْمِ فِي الدُّنْيَا سَبَبًا لِدُخُولِ دَارِ السَّلَامِ فِي الْآخِرَةِ، قَالَ ﷺ: «لَا تَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا، وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا، أَوَلَا أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ إِذَا فَعَلْتُمُوهُ تَحَابَبْتُمْ؟ أَفْشُوا السَّلَامَ بَيْنَكُمْ»[2].
text.en: And He, Blessed and Exalted is He, has made spreading this name in this world a means of entering the Abode of Peace in the Hereafter. The Prophet ﷺ said: “You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not guide you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread salam (the greeting of peace) among yourselves.”[2]
*Bada’i‘ al-Fawa’id* (2/135–137).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ (رَقْمُ: ٥٤) مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: Narrated by Muslim (no. 54) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

title.en: al-Quddus, as-Subbuh (the Most Holy, the Most Glorified)

text.ar: أَمَّا اسْمُهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى «الْقُدُّوسُ» فَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ مَرَّتَيْنِ: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ﴾ [الْحَشْرِ: ٢٣]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ ٱلۡقُدُّوسِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ﴾ [الْجُمُعَةِ: ١].
text.en: As for His name, Blessed and Exalted is He, “al-Quddus” (the Most Holy), it occurs in the Qur'an twice. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾He is Allah, besides whom there is no god; the King, the Most Holy, the Flawless, the Granter of Security, the Overseer, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glorified is Allah above what they associate with Him﴿ [al-Hashr 59:23], and He the Exalted says: ﴾Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, the King, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴿ [al-Jumu‘ah 62:1].

text.ar: وَأَمَّا «السُّبُّوحُ» فَقَدْ وَرَدَ فِي السُّنَّةِ، وَذَلِكَ فِيمَا رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ فِي «صَحِيحِهِ»[1] عَنْ أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَسُجُودِهِ: «سُبُّوحٌ قُدُّوسٌ رَبُّ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالرُّوحِ».
text.en: As for “as-Subbuh” (the Most Glorified), it occurs in the Sunnah, in what Muslim narrated in his *Sahih*[1] from the Mother of the Believers ‘A’ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in his bowing and his prostration: “Most Glorified, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.”

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ بَيْنَ التَّسْبِيحِ وَالتَّقْدِيسِ كَمَا جُمِعَ بَيْنَهُمَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى فِي ذِكْرِ تَسْبِيحِ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَتَقْدِيسِهِمْ لِلَّهِ: ﴿وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٣٠].
text.en: In this hadith he (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him) combined glorification (tasbih) and sanctification (taqdis), just as the two are combined in the saying of Allah the Exalted, mentioning the angels' glorification and sanctification of Allah: ﴾while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:30].

text.ar: وَ«السُّبُّوحُ الْقُدُّوسُ» اسْمَانِ عَظِيمَانِ دَالَّانِ عَلَى تَنْزِيهِ اللَّهِ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْعُيُوبِ، وَتَبْرِئَتِهِ عَنْ كُلِّ مَا يُضَادُّ كَمَالَهُ وَيُنَافِي عَظَمَتَهُ، كَالسِّنَةِ وَالنَّوْمِ وَاللُّغُوبِ وَالْوَالِدِ وَالْوَلَدِ وَغَيْرِهَا، وَعَنْ أَنْ يُشْبِهَهُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ أَوْ أَنْ يُشْبِهَ هُوَ أَحَدًا مِنْ خَلْقِهِ، تَعَالَى وَتَقَدَّسَ وَتَنَزَّهَ عَنِ الشَّبِيهِ وَالنَّظِيرِ وَالْمِثَالِ ﴿لَيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَيۡءٞۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ﴾ [الشُّورَى: ١١].
