text.en: “As-Subbuh al-Quddus” (the Most Glorified, the Most Holy) are two great names that indicate Allah's being free from deficiencies and faults, and His being clear of everything that opposes His perfection and contradicts His greatness — such as drowsiness, sleep, fatigue, a parent, a child and the like — and free from anyone of His creation resembling Him, or His resembling anyone of His creation. Exalted, Holy and Transcendent is He above any likeness, equal or example: ﴾There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴿ [ash-Shura 42:11].

text.ar: وَمَجْمُوعُ مَا يُنَزَّهُ عَنْهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى شَيْئَانِ:
text.en: What He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is declared free from comes down to two things:

text.ar: أَحَدُهُمَا: أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّهٌ عَنْ كُلِّ مَا يُنَافِي صِفَاتِ كَمَالِهِ، فَإِنَّ لَهُ الْمُنْتَهَى فِي كُلِّ صِفَةِ كَمَالٍ، فَهُوَ الْمَوْصُوفُ بِكَمَالِ الْعِلْمِ وَكَمَالِ الْقُدْرَةِ، مُنَزَّهٌ عَمَّا يُنَافِي ذَلِكَ مِنَ النِّسْيَانِ وَالْغَفْلَةِ، وَأَنْ يَعْزُبَ عَنْهُ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَلَا أَصْغَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْبَرُ، وَمُنَزَّهٌ عَنِ الْعَجْزِ وَالتَّعَبِ وَالْإِعْيَاءِ وَاللُّغُوبِ، وَمَوْصُوفٌ بِكَمَالِ الْحَيَاةِ وَالْقَيُّومِيَّةِ، مُنَزَّهٌ عَنْ ضِدِّهَا مِنَ الْمَوْتِ وَالسِّنَةِ وَالنَّوْمِ، مَوْصُوفٌ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْغِنَى التَّامِّ، مُنَزَّهٌ عَنِ الظُّلْمِ وَالْحَاجَةِ إِلَى أَحَدٍ بِوَجْهٍ مِنَ الْوُجُوهِ، وَمَوْصُوفٌ بِكَمَالِ الْحِكْمَةِ وَالرَّحْمَةِ، مُنَزَّهٌ عَمَّا يُضَادُّ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْعَبَثِ وَالسَّفَهِ، وَأَنْ يَفْعَلَ أَوْ يَشْرَعَ مَا يُنَافِي الْحِكْمَةَ وَالرَّحْمَةَ، وَهَكَذَا جَمِيعُ صِفَاتِهِ مُنَزَّهٌ عَنْ كُلِّ مَا يُنَافِيهَا وَيُضَادُّهَا.
text.en: The first: He is free from everything that contradicts His attributes of perfection, for He has the utmost in every attribute of perfection. He is described with perfect knowledge and perfect power, free from what contradicts that, such as forgetfulness and heedlessness, and from anything the weight of an atom in the heavens and the earth escaping Him, or anything smaller than that or greater; and He is free from inability, tiredness, exhaustion and fatigue. He is described with perfect life and self-subsistence, free from their opposites: death, drowsiness and sleep. He is described with justice and complete richness, free from injustice and from needing anyone in any way at all. He is described with perfect wisdom and mercy, free from what opposes that, such as futility and foolishness, and from doing or legislating anything that contradicts wisdom and mercy. And so it is with all His attributes: He is free from everything that contradicts and opposes them.

text.ar: الثَّانِي: أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّهٌ عَنْ مُمَاثَلَةِ أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ، أَوْ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ نِدٌّ بِوَجْهٍ مِنَ الْوُجُوهِ، فَالْمَخْلُوقَاتُ كُلُّهَا وَإِنْ عَظُمَتْ وَشَرُفَتْ وَبَلَغَتِ الْمُنْتَهَى الَّذِي يَلِيقُ بِهَا مِنَ الْعَظَمَةِ وَالْكَمَالِ اللَّائِقِ بِهَا؛ فَلَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِنْهَا يُقَارِبُ أَوْ يُشَابِهُ الْبَارِيَ، بَلْ جَمِيعُ أَوْصَافِهَا تَضْمَحِلُّ إِذَا نُسِبَتْ إِلَى صِفَاتِ بَارِيهَا وَخَالِقِهَا، بَلْ جَمِيعُ مَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْمَعَانِي وَالنُّعُوتِ وَالْكَمَالِ هُوَ الَّذِي أَعْطَاهَا إِيَّاهُ، فَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ فِيهَا الْعُقُولَ وَالسَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْقُوَى الظَّاهِرَةَ وَالْبَاطِنَةَ، وَهُوَ الَّذِي عَلَّمَهَا وَأَلْهَمَهَا، وَهُوَ الَّذِي نَمَّاهَا ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا وَكَمَّلَهَا.
text.en: The second: He is free from resembling anyone of His creation, or from having a rival in any way at all. All created things, however great and noble they may be, and even if they reach the utmost greatness and perfection befitting them, none of them comes near to or resembles al-Bari (the Maker). Rather, all their qualities fade into nothing when compared to the attributes of their Maker and Creator. Indeed, all the qualities, characteristics and perfection they have were given to them by Him. It is He who created in them minds, hearing, sight, and outward and inward faculties; it is He who taught them and inspired them; and it is He who made them grow, outwardly and inwardly, and brought them to completion.

text.ar: فَهُوَ الْمُنَزَّهُ عَنْ كُلِّ مَا يُنَافِي صِفَاتِ الْمَجْدِ وَالْعَظَمَةِ وَالْكَمَالِ، وَهُوَ الْمُنَزَّهُ عَنِ الضِّدِّ وَالنِّدِّ وَالْكُفُؤِ وَالْأَمْثَالِ.
text.en: So He is the One free from everything that contradicts the attributes of glory, greatness and perfection, and He is the One free from any opposite, rival, equal or likeness.

text.ar: وَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُعْلَمَ هُنَا أَنَّ تَسْبِيحَ اللَّهِ وَتَقْدِيسَهُ إِنَّمَا يَكُونُ بِتَبْرِئَةِ اللَّهِ وَتَنْزِيهِهِ عَنْ كُلِّ سُوءٍ وَعَيْبٍ، مَعَ إِثْبَاتِ الْمَحَامِدِ، وَصِفَاتِ الْكَمَالِ لَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ اللَّائِقِ بِهِ.
text.en: It should be known here that glorifying and sanctifying Allah is only by declaring Allah clear and free of every evil and fault, while affirming for Him, Glorified is He, all praiseworthy qualities and attributes of perfection in the manner befitting Him.

text.ar: قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَالْأَمْرُ بِتَسْبِيحِهِ يَقْتَضِي تَنْزِيهَهُ عَنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ وَسُوءٍ، وَإِثْبَاتَ الْمَحَامِدِ الَّتِي يُحْمَدُ عَلَيْهَا، فَيَقْتَضِي ذَلِكَ تَنْزِيهَهُ وَتَحْمِيدَهُ وَتَكْبِيرَهُ وَتَوْحِيدَهُ»[2].
text.en: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “The command to glorify Him requires declaring Him free from every fault and evil, and affirming the praiseworthy qualities for which He is praised. So this requires declaring Him free of imperfection, praising Him, magnifying Him and affirming His oneness.”[2]

text.ar: وَبِهِ يُعْلَمُ أَنَّ مَا يَفْعَلُهُ الْمُعَطِّلَةُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبِدَعِ مِنْ تَعْطِيلٍ لِلصِّفَاتِ وَعَدَمِ إِثْبَاتٍ لَهَا وَجَحْدٍ لِحَقَائِقِهَا وَمَعَانِيهَا بِحُجَّةِ أَنَّهُمْ يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّهَ وَيُنَزِّهُونَهُ فَهُوَ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ لَيْسَ مِنَ التَّسْبِيحِ وَالتَّقْدِيسِ فِي شَيْءٍ، بَلْ هُوَ إِنْكَارٌ وَجُحُودٌ، وَضَلَالٌ وَبُهْتَانٌ.
text.en: From this it is known that what the deniers among the people of innovation do — denying the attributes, not affirming them, and rejecting their realities and meanings, on the pretext that they are glorifying Allah and declaring Him free of imperfection — is in reality nothing at all of glorification and sanctification. Rather, it is denial and rejection, misguidance and falsehood.

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ رَجَبٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ [الْحِجْرِ: ٩٨]: «أَيْ: سَبِّحْهُ بِمَا حَمِدَ بِهِ نَفْسَهُ، إِذْ لَيْسَ كُلُّ تَسْبِيحٍ بِمَحْمُودٍ، كَمَا أَنَّ تَسْبِيحَ الْمُعْتَزِلَةِ يَقْتَضِي تَعْطِيلَ كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الصِّفَاتِ»[3].
text.en: Ibn Rajab (may Allah have mercy on him) said about the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴾So glorify with the praise of your Lord﴿ [al-Hijr 15:98]: “That is, glorify Him with that with which He has praised Himself, since not every glorification is praiseworthy; for example, the glorification of the Mu‘tazilah entails denying many of the attributes.”[3]

text.ar: فَقَوْلُهُ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «إِذْ لَيْسَ كُلُّ تَسْبِيحٍ بِمَحْمُودٍ» كَلَامٌ فِي غَايَةِ الْأَهَمِّيَّةِ، إِذْ إِنَّ تَسْبِيحَ اللَّهِ بِإِنْكَارِ صِفَاتِهِ وَجَحْدِهَا وَعَدَمِ إِثْبَاتِهَا أَمْرٌ لَا يُحْمَدُ عَلَيْهِ فَاعِلُهُ، بَلْ يُذَمُّ غَايَةَ الذَّمِّ، وَلَا يَكُونُ بِذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ بِحَمْدِ اللَّهِ، بَلْ يَكُونُ مِنَ الْمُعَطِّلِينَ الْمُنْكِرِينَ الْجَاحِدِينَ، مِنَ الَّذِينَ نَزَّهَ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمْ وَتَعْطِيلِهِمْ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ ٱلۡعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ (١٨٠) وَسَلَٰمٌ عَلَى ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ (١٨١) وَٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ١٨٠ ـ ١٨٢]، فَسَبَّحَ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ عَمَّا وَصَفَهُ بِهِ الْمُخَالِفُونَ لِلرُّسُلِ، وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ لِسَلَامَةِ مَا قَالُوهُ فِي حَقِّ اللَّهِ مِنَ النَّقْصِ وَالْعَيْبِ.
text.en: His statement (may Allah have mercy on him), “since not every glorification is praiseworthy”, is extremely important, because glorifying Allah by rejecting and denying His attributes and not affirming them is something for which the one who does it is not praised; rather, he is blamed in the utmost way. By that he is not among those who glorify Allah with His praise; rather, he is among those who deny, reject and repudiate — among those whose saying and denial Allah has declared Himself free of, in His saying: ﴾Glorified is your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe (180) And peace be upon the messengers (181) And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴿ [as-Saffat 37:180–182]. So Allah glorified Himself above what those who oppose the messengers describe Him with, and He sent peace upon the messengers because what they said about Allah is free from deficiency and fault.

text.ar: إِنَّ تَسْبِيحَ اللَّهِ وَتَقْدِيسَهُ وَتَنْزِيهَهُ وَتَعْظِيمَهُ يَجِبُ أَنْ يَكُونَ وَفْقَ دَلَائِلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ وَفِي ضَوْءِ فَهْمِ سَلَفِ الْأُمَّةِ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ بِحَالٍ أَنْ يُبْنَى عَلَى الْأَهْوَاءِ الْمُجَرَّدَةِ أَوِ الظُّنُونِ الْفَاسِدَةِ أَوِ الْأَقْيِسَةِ الْعَقْلِيَّةِ الْكَاسِدَةِ كَمَا هُوَ الشَّأْنُ عِنْدَ أَرْبَابِ الْبِدَعِ الْمُعَطِّلِينَ لِصِفَاتِ الرَّبِّ سُبْحَانَهُ زَعْمًا مِنْهُمْ أَنَّ هَذَا مِنْ بَابِ التَّسْبِيحِ وَالتَّقْدِيسِ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يَعْتَمِدُ فِي بَابِ التَّسْبِيحِ وَالتَّعْظِيمِ عَلَى هَوَاهُ بِغَيْرِ هُدًى مِنَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهُ يَزِلُّ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ وَيَقَعُ فِي أَنْوَاعٍ مِنَ الْبَاطِلِ وَصُنُوفٍ مِنَ الضَّلَالِ، وَمَنْ عَافَاهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ هَذَا السَّبِيلِ فِي تَسْبِيحِهِ فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ.
text.en: The glorification, sanctification, exaltation and magnification of Allah must be in accordance with the proofs of the Book and the Sunnah and in light of the understanding of the Salaf of the Ummah. It is not permissible in any way that it be built upon mere whims, corrupt assumptions or worthless rational analogies, as is the case with the people of innovation who deny the attributes of the Lord, Glorified is He, claiming that this is part of glorification and sanctification. Whoever relies on his own whims in the matter of glorification and magnification, without guidance from Allah, will slip in this matter and fall into kinds of falsehood and types of misguidance. And whoever Allah has kept safe from this path in his glorification has been guided to a straight path.

text.ar: إِذِ التَّسْبِيحُ طَاعَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ وَعِبَادَةٌ جَلِيلَةٌ حَبِيبَةٌ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ، ثَقِيلَةٌ فِي الْمِيزَانِ، كَمَا قَالَ ﷺ: «كَلِمَتَانِ خَفِيفَتَانِ عَلَى اللِّسَانِ، ثَقِيلَتَانِ فِي الْمِيزَانِ، حَبِيبَتَانِ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ». مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ[4].
text.en: For glorification is a great act of obedience and a sublime act of worship, beloved to ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) and heavy in the Scale, as the Prophet ﷺ said: “Two words that are light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale and beloved to ar-Rahman: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent.” Agreed upon[4].

text.ar: وَهُوَ صَلَاةُ جَمِيعِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّۚ وَإِن مِّن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورٗا﴾ [الْإِسْرَاءِ: ٤٤]، وَبِهِ تُرْزَقُ، كَمَا صَحَّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّ نُوحاً عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ لِابْنِهِ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: «آمُرُكَ بِـ «لَا إِلَهَ إِلاّ اللَّهُ»؛ فَإِنَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعَ، وَالْأَرَضِينَ السَّبْعَ لَوْ وُضِعَتْ فِي كِفَّةٍ، وَوُضِعَتْ «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ» فِي كِفَّةٍ رَجَحَتْ بِهِنَّ «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ». وَلَوْ أَنَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعَ، وَالْأَرَضِينَ السَّبْعَ كُنَّ حَلْقَةً مُبْهَمَةً قَصَمَتْهُنَّ «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ»، وَ«سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ»؛ فَإِنَّهَا صَلَاةُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَبِهَا يُرْزَقُ الْخَلْقُ» رَوَاهُ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ، وَالْبُخَارِيُّ فِي «الْأَدَبِ الْمُفْرَدِ»[5].
text.en: It is the prayer of all created things, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴾The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him; and there is nothing except that it glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Ever-Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving﴿ [al-Isra’ 17:44]; and by it they are given provision, as is authentically reported from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet ﷺ, that Nuh (peace be upon him) said to his son at the time of his death: “I command you with ‘La ilaha illallah’ (there is none worthy of worship except Allah), for if the seven heavens and the seven earths were placed in one pan of a scale, and ‘La ilaha illallah’ were placed in the other pan, ‘La ilaha illallah’ would outweigh them. And if the seven heavens and the seven earths were a closed ring, ‘La ilaha illallah’ would break them apart. And with ‘Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih’ (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him), for it is the prayer of everything, and by it the creation is given provision.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and by al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*[5].

text.ar: جَعَلَنَا اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ بِحَمْدِهِ، الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِأَسْمَائِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ، الْمُحَقِّقِينَ لِتَوْحِيدِهِ وَتَعْظِيمِهِ، إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ مُجِيبٌ.
text.en: May Allah make us among those who glorify Him with His praise, who believe in His names and attributes, and who truly realise His Tawheed and His magnification; indeed, He is All-Hearing, Ever-Responsive.

text.ar: «دَقَائِقُ التَّفْسِيرِ» لِابْنِ تَيْمِيَّةَ (٥/ ٥٩).
text.en: *Daqa’iq at-Tafsir* by Ibn Taymiyyah (5/59).

text.ar: «تَفْسِيرُ سُورَةِ النَّصْرِ» (ص/ ٧٣).
text.en: *Tafsir Surat an-Nasr* (p. 73).
Al-Bukhari (no. 6043) and Muslim (no. 2694).

text.ar: «مُسْنَدُ الْإِمَامِ أَحْمَدَ» (٢/ ١٧٠)، وَ«الْأَدَبُ الْمُفْرَدُ» (٥٤٨) وَغَيْرُهُمَا وَإِسْنَادُهُ صَحِيحٌ. وَانْظُرْ: «السِّلْسِلَةَ الصَّحِيحَةَ» (رَقْمُ: ١٣٤).
text.en: *Musnad al-Imam Ahmad* (2/170) and *al-Adab al-Mufrad* (548), among others, and its chain is authentic. See also: *as-Silsilah as-Sahihah* (no. 134).

text.ar: وَقَدْ تَكَرَّرَ وُرُودُ هَذَا الِاسْمِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ١٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَهُدُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيِّبِ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَهُدُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلۡحَمِيدِ﴾ [الْحَجِّ: ٢٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٦٧]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٞ﴾ [لُقْمَانَ: ١٢]، أَيْ: الَّذِي لَهُ الْحَمْدُ كُلُّهُ، الْمَحْمُودُ فِي ذَاتِهِ وَأَسْمَائِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ، فَلَهُ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ أَحْسَنُهَا، وَمِنَ الصِّفَاتِ أَكْمَلُهَا، فَالْحَمْدُ أَوْسَعُ الصِّفَاتِ وَأَعَمُّ الْمَدَائِحِ، وَأَعْظَمُ الثَّنَاءِ؛ لِأَنَّ جَمِيعَ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى حَمْدٌ، وَصِفَاتُهُ حَمْدٌ، وَأَفْعَالُهُ حَمْدٌ، وَأَحْكَامُهُ حَمْدٌ، وَعَدْلُهُ حَمْدٌ، وَانْتِقَامُهُ مِنْ أَعْدَائِهِ حَمْدٌ، وَفَضْلُهُ وَإِحْسَانُهُ إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِ حَمْدٌ، وَالْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ إِنَّمَا قَامَ بِحَمْدِهِ وَوُجِدَ بِحَمْدِهِ وَظَهَرَ بِحَمْدِهِ، وَكَانَ الْغَايَةُ مِنْهُ هِيَ حَمْدُهُ، فَحَمْدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ سَبَبُ ذَلِكَ وَغَايَتُهُ وَمَظْهَرُهُ، فَحَمْدُهُ رُوحُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَقِيَامُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ بِحَمْدِهِ، وَسَرَيَانُ حَمْدِهِ فِي الْمَوْجُودَاتِ وَظُهُورُ آثَارِهِ أَمْرٌ مَشْهُودٌ بِالْبَصَائِرِ وَالْأَبْصَارِ.
text.en: This name occurs repeatedly in the Noble Qur'an, seventeen times. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy﴿ [Fatir 35:15]; He the Exalted says: ﴾And they were guided to good speech, and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴿ [al-Hajj 22:24]; He the Exalted says: ﴾And know that Allah is Rich and Praiseworthy﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:267]; and He the Exalted says: ﴾And whoever is grateful is only grateful for the benefit of himself; and whoever is ungrateful, then indeed Allah is Rich and Praiseworthy﴿ [Luqman 31:12]. That is: the One to whom belongs all praise, who is praised in His Essence, His names and His attributes. His are the most beautiful of names and the most perfect of attributes. Praise is the widest of attributes, the most comprehensive of commendations and the greatest of acclaim, because all the names of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, are praise; His attributes are praise; His actions are praise; His rulings are praise; His justice is praise; His retribution against His enemies is praise; and His favour and kindness to His allies are praise. Creation and command only stand by His praise, came into being by His praise and became manifest by His praise, and their purpose is His praise. So His praise, Glorified is He, is their cause, their purpose and their manifestation. His praise is the spirit of everything, and everything stands by His praise; and the flowing of His praise through all that exists, and the appearance of its effects, are witnessed both by insight and by sight.

text.ar: قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَأَيْضاً فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ أَخْبَرَ أَنَّ لَهُ الْحَمْدَ، وَأَنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، وَأَنَّ لَهُ الْحَمْدَ فِي الْأُولَى وَالْآخِرَةِ وَلَهُ الْحُكْمُ، وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْمَحَامِدِ.
text.en: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Also, Allah, Glorified is He, has informed us that to Him belongs praise, that He is Praiseworthy and Glorious, that to Him belongs praise in the first life and the Hereafter, and to Him belongs judgement, and other such kinds of praise.

text.ar: وَالْحَمْدُ نَوْعَانِ: حَمْدٌ عَلَى إِحْسَانِهِ إِلَى عِبَادِهِ، وَهُوَ مِنَ الشُّكْرِ.
text.en: Praise is of two kinds: praise for His kindness to His servants, and this is a form of thanks.

text.ar: وَحَمْدٌ لِمَا يَسْتَحِقُّهُ هُوَ بِنَفْسِهِ مِنْ نُعُوتِ كَمَالِهِ، وَهَذَا الْحَمْدُ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا عَلَى مَا هُوَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مُسْتَحِقٌّ لِلْحَمْدِ، وَإِنَّمَا يَسْتَحِقُّ ذَلِكَ مَنْ هُوَ مُتَّصِفٌ بِصِفَاتِ الْكَمَالِ»[1].
text.en: And praise for what He Himself deserves on account of His qualities of perfection. This praise is only for that which in itself deserves praise, and only the one who is described with attributes of perfection deserves it.”[1]

text.ar: أَمَّا حَمْدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ عَلَى إِحْسَانِهِ إِلَى عِبَادِهِ فَلِأَنَّ النِّعْمَةَ مُوجِبَةٌ لِحَمْدِ الْمُنْعِمِ، وَالنِّعَمُ كُلُّهَا مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَهَذَا النَّوْعُ مِنَ الْحَمْدِ مَشْهُودٌ لِلْخَلِيقَةِ بَرِّهَا وَفَاجِرِهَا، مُؤْمِنِهَا وَكَافِرِهَا مِنْ جَزِيلِ مَوَاهِبِهِ، وَسَعَةِ عَطَايَاهُ، وَكَرِيمِ أَيَادِيهِ، وَجَمِيلِ صَنَائِعِهِ، وَحُسْنِ إِكْرَامِهِ لِعِبَادِهِ، وَسَعَةِ رَحْمَتِهِ لَهُمْ، وَبِرِّهِ وَلُطْفِهِ، وَإِجَابَتِهِ لِدَعَوَاتِ الْمُضْطَرِّينَ، وَكَشْفِ كُرُبَاتِ الْمَكْرُوبِينَ، وَإِغَاثَةِ الْمَلْهُوفِينَ، وَرَحْمَتِهِ لِلْعَالَمِينَ، وَابْتِدَائِهِ بِالنِّعَمِ قَبْلَ السُّؤَالِ، وَمِنْ غَيْرِ اسْتِحْقَاقٍ، بَلِ ابْتِدَاءً مِنْهُ بِمُجَرَّدِ فَضْلِهِ وَكَرَمِهِ وَإِحْسَانِهِ، وَدَفْعِ الْمِحَنِ وَالْبَلَايَا بَعْدَ انْعِقَادِ أَسْبَابِهَا، وَصَرْفِهَا بَعْدَ وُقُوعِهَا، وَلُطْفِهِ تَعَالَى فِي ذَلِكَ إِلَى مَا لَا تَبْلُغُهُ الْآمَالُ، وَهِدَايَتِهِ خَاصَّتَهُ وَعِبَادَهُ إِلَى سَبِيلِ دَارِ السَّلَامِ، وَمُدَافَعَتِهِ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ الدِّفَاعِ، وَحِمَايَتِهِمْ مِنَ الْوُقُوعِ فِي الْآثَامِ، وَحَبَّبَ إِلَيْهِمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَزَيَّنَهُ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ، وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْهِمُ الْكُفْرَ وَالْفُسُوقَ وَالْعِصْيَانَ، وَجَعَلَهُمْ مِنَ الرَّاشِدِينَ، وَفَتَحَ لَهُمْ أَبْوَابَ الْهِدَايَةِ، وَعَرَّفَهُمُ الْأَسْبَابَ الَّتِي تُدْنِيهِمْ مِنْ رِضَاهُ وَتُبْعِدُهُمْ عَنْ غَضَبِهِ، إِلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ نِعَمِهِ الَّتِي لَا تُحْصَى، وَآلَائِهِ الَّتِي لَا تُسْتَقْصَى، وَمَنْ أَرَادَ مُطَالَعَةَ أُصُولِ النِّعَمِ وَمَا تُوجِبُهُ مِنْ حَمْدِ اللَّهِ وَذِكْرِهِ وَشُكْرِهِ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِهِ فَلْيُدِمْ سَرْحَ الذِّكْرِ فِي رِيَاضِ الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ، وَلْيَتَأَمَّلْ مَا عَدَّدَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ مِنْ نِعَمِهِ وَتَعَرَّفَ بِهَا إِلَى عِبَادِهِ مِنْ أَوَّلِ الْقُرْآنِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ.
text.en: As for praising Him, Glorified is He, for His kindness to His servants, that is because a blessing calls for praise of the One who bestows it, and all blessings are from Allah. This kind of praise is witnessed by all creation, the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever, from His abundant gifts, the vastness of His giving, His generous bounties, His beautiful favours, His fine honouring of His servants, the vastness of His mercy towards them, His benevolence and gentleness, His answering the supplications of those in dire need, His relieving the distress of the distressed, His rescuing those who cry out for help, His mercy to all the worlds, His initiating blessings before being asked and without their being deserved — rather, beginning them out of His sheer favour, generosity and kindness — His warding off trials and calamities after their causes have come together, and turning them away after they have occurred, and His gentleness, the Exalted, in all of that to an extent beyond what hopes can reach; His guiding His elect and His servants to the path of the Abode of Peace, His defending them in the best way, and His protecting them from falling into sins; He made faith beloved to them and beautified it in their hearts, made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to them, made them among the rightly guided, opened for them the doors of guidance, and acquainted them with the means that bring them near to His pleasure and keep them far from His anger — and other such blessings that cannot be counted and favours that cannot be fully enumerated. Whoever wishes to study the foundations of blessings, and the praise, remembrance, gratitude and excellent worship of Allah that they call for, let him keep his reflection roaming continually in the gardens of the Noble Qur'an, and let him contemplate the blessings that Allah has listed in it and by which He has made Himself known to His servants, from the beginning of the Qur'an to its end.

text.ar: فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ شُكْرًا، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فَضْلًا، لَهُ الْحَمْدُ بِالْإِسْلَامِ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ بِالْإِيمَانِ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ بِالْقُرْآنِ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ بِالْأَهْلِ وَالْمَالِ وَالْمُعَافَاةِ، لَهُ الْحَمْدُ بِكُلِّ نِعْمَةٍ أَنْعَمَ بِهَا فِي قَدِيمٍ أَوْ حَدِيثٍ، أَوْ سِرٍّ أَوْ عَلَانِيَةٍ، أَوْ خَاصَّةٍ أَوْ عَامَّةٍ، حَمْداً كَثِيراً طَيِّباً مُبَارَكاً فِيهِ كَمَا يُحِبُّ رَبُّنَا وَيَرْضَى.
text.en: So to Allah belongs praise as thanks, and to Him belongs praise for His favour. To Him belongs praise for Islam, to Him belongs praise for faith, to Him belongs praise for the Qur'an, and to Him belongs praise for family, wealth and well-being. To Him belongs praise for every blessing He has bestowed, in the past or the present, in secret or in the open, specific or general — abundant, good and blessed praise, as our Lord loves and is pleased with.

text.ar: وَأَمَّا حَمْدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ لِمَا لَهُ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ وَالصِّفَاتِ وَلِمَا يَسْتَحِقُّهُ مِنْ كَمَالِ النُّعُوتِ فَأَمْرٌ مُتَوَاتِرٌ؛ فَإِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ قَدْ حَمِدَ نَفْسَهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ عَلَى رُبُوبِيَّتِهِ لِلْعَالَمِينَ، وَحَمِدَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى تَفَرُّدِهِ بِالْإِلَهِيَّةِ، وَحَمِدَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى كَمَالِ أَسْمَائِهِ وَعَظَمَةِ صِفَاتِهِ، وَحَمِدَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى امْتِنَاعِ اتِّصَافِهِ بِمَا لَا يَلِيقُ بِهِ مِنِ اتِّخَاذِ الْوَلَدِ وَالشَّرِيكِ وَمُوَالَاةِ أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ لِحَاجَتِهِ إِلَيْهِ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدٗا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٞ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِيّٞ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّۖ وَكَبِّرۡهُ تَكۡبِيرَۢا﴾ [الْإِسْرَاءِ: ١١١].
text.en: As for praising Him, Glorified is He, for the names and attributes that He has, and for the perfect qualities that He deserves, this is something abundantly established. He, Glorified is He, has praised Himself in His Book for His Lordship over the worlds; He has praised Himself for being alone in divinity; He has praised Himself for the perfection of His names and the greatness of His attributes; and He has praised Himself for the impossibility of His being described with what does not befit Him, such as taking a son or a partner, or taking anyone of His creation as an ally out of need for him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no ally out of humiliation; and magnify Him with great magnification﴿ [al-Isra’ 17:111].

text.ar: وَحَمِدَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى عَظَمَتِهِ وَكِبْرِيَائِهِ، كَمَا قَالَ سُبْحَانَهُ: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَرَبِّ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ (٣٦) وَلَهُ ٱلۡكِبۡرِيَآءُ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ﴾ [الْجَاثِيَةِ: ٣٦ ـ ٣٧]، وَحَمِدَ نَفْسَهُ فِي الْأُولَى وَالْآخِرَةِ، وَأَخْبَرَ عَنْ سَرَيَانِ الْحَمْدِ فِي الْعَالَمِ الْعُلْوِيِّ وَالسُّفْلِيِّ وَنَبَّهَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ فِي كِتَابِهِ فِي آيَاتٍ عَدِيدَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى تَنَوُّعِ حَمْدِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَدُّدِ أَسْبَابِ حَمْدِهِ، وَقَدْ جَمَعَهَا اللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ مِنْ كِتَابِهِ وَفَرَّقَهَا فِي مَوَاطِنَ أُخْرَى لِيَتَعَرَّفَ إِلَيْهِ عِبَادُهُ، وَلِيَعْرِفُوا كَيْفَ يَحْمَدُونَهُ وَكَيْفَ يُثْنُونَ عَلَيْهِ، وَلِيَتَحَبَّبَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِذَلِكَ، وَيُحِبَّهُمْ إِذَا عَرَفُوهُ وَأَحَبُّوهُ وَحَمِدُوهُ.
text.en: And He has praised Himself for His greatness and His supremacy, as He, Glorified is He, says: ﴾So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds (36) And to Him belongs supremacy in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴿ [al-Jathiyah 45:36–37]. He has praised Himself in this life and the Hereafter, and He has informed us of how praise flows through the upper and lower worlds. He has drawn attention to all of this in His Book in many verses that show the variety of His praise, Glorified is He, and the many reasons for His praise. Allah has gathered them together in some places in His Book and spread them out in other places, so that His servants may come to know Him, so that they may know how to praise Him and how to extol Him, and so that He may make Himself beloved to them by this, and love them when they know Him, love Him and praise Him.

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ فِي أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَرْبَعِينَ مَوْضِعًا، جُمِعَ فِي بَعْضِهَا أَسْبَابُ الْحَمْدِ، وَفِي بَعْضِهَا ذُكِرَتْ أَسْبَابُهُ مُفَصَّلَةً.
text.en: Praise is mentioned in the Noble Qur'an in more than forty places; in some of them the reasons for praise are combined, and in others its reasons are mentioned in detail.

text.ar: فَمِنَ الْآيَاتِ الَّتِي جُمِعَ فِيهَا أَسْبَابُ الْحَمْدِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [الْفَاتِحَةِ: ٢]، وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لَهُ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ فِي ٱلۡأُولَىٰ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ﴾ [الْقَصَصِ: ٧٠]، وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ﴾ [سَبَأٍ: ١].
text.en: Among the verses in which the reasons for praise are combined is His saying, the Exalted: ﴾All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴿ [al-Fatihah 1:2], His saying: ﴾To Him belongs all praise in the first and the last﴿ [al-Qasas 28:70], and His saying: ﴾All praise is for Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴿ [Saba’ 34:1].

text.ar: وَمِنَ الْآيَاتِ الَّتِي ذُكِرَ فِيهَا أَسْبَابُ الْحَمْدِ مُفَصَّلَةً قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَىٰنَا لِهَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهۡتَدِيَ لَوۡلَآ أَنۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُۖ﴾ [الْأَعْرَافِ: ٤٣]، فَفِيهَا حَمْدُهُ عَلَى نِعْمَةِ دُخُولِ الْجَنَّةِ، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي نَجَّىٰنَا مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ﴾ [الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: ٢٨]، فَفِيهَا حَمْدُهُ عَلَى النَّصْرِ عَلَى الْأَعْدَاءِ وَالسَّلَامَةِ مِنْ شَرِّهِمْ، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَٱدۡعُوهُ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَۗ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ٦٥]، فَفِيهَا حَمْدُهُ عَلَى نِعْمَةِ التَّوْحِيدِ وَإِخْلَاصِ الْعِبَادَةِ لَهُ وَحْدَهُ، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى ٱلۡكِبَرِ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ﴾ [إِبْرَاهِيمَ: ٣٩]، فَفِيهَا حَمْدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ عَلَى هِبَةِ الْوَلَدِ، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِهِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَلَمۡ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ عِوَجَاۜ﴾ [الْكَهْفِ: ١]، فَفِيهَا حَمْدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ عَلَى نِعْمَةِ إِنْزَالِ الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ قَيِّمًا لَا عِوَجَ فِيهِ، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَقُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَمۡ يَتَّخِذۡ وَلَدٗا وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٞ فِي ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِيّٞ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّۖ وَكَبِّرۡهُ تَكۡبِيرَۢا﴾ [الْإِسْرَاءِ: ١١١]، فَفِيهَا حَمْدُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ لِكَمَالِهِ وَجَلَالِهِ وَتَنَزُّهِهِ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْعُيُوبِ.
text.en: Among the verses in which the reasons for praise are mentioned in detail is His saying, the Exalted: ﴾And they will say: All praise is for Allah, who guided us to this; we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us﴿ [al-A‘raf 7:43] — in it He is praised for the blessing of entering Paradise; His saying, the Exalted: ﴾Then say: All praise is for Allah, who saved us from the wrongdoing people﴿ [al-Mu’minun 23:28] — in it He is praised for victory over enemies and safety from their evil; His saying, the Exalted: ﴾So call on Him, making religion sincerely for Him. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴿ [Ghafir 40:65] — in it He is praised for the blessing of Tawheed and of devoting worship sincerely to Him alone; His saying, the Exalted: ﴾All praise is for Allah, who has granted me in old age Isma‘il and Ishaq. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴿ [Ibrahim 14:39] — in it He, Glorified is He, is praised for granting children; His saying, the Exalted: ﴾All praise is for Allah, who has sent down the Book upon His servant and has not placed in it any crookedness﴿ [al-Kahf 18:1] — in it He, Glorified is He, is praised for the blessing of sending down the Noble Qur'an, upright with no crookedness in it; and His saying, the Exalted: ﴾And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, and has no ally out of humiliation; and magnify Him with great magnification﴿ [al-Isra’ 17:111] — in it He, Glorified is He, is praised for His perfection and majesty and His being free from deficiencies and faults.

text.ar: وَالْآيَاتُ فِي هَذَا الْمَعْنَى كَثِيرَةٌ، وَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَدِ افْتَتَحَ كِتَابَهُ بِالْحَمْدِ، وَافْتَتَحَ بَعْضَ سُوَرِ الْقُرْآنِ بِالْحَمْدِ، وَافْتَتَحَ خَلْقَهُ بِالْحَمْدِ، وَاخْتَتَمَهُ بِالْحَمْدِ، فَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ أَوَّلًا وَآخِرًا، وَلَهُ الشُّكْرُ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا، وَهُوَ الْحَمِيدُ الْمَجِيدُ.
text.en: The verses with this meaning are many. Allah the Exalted opened His Book with praise, opened some of the surahs of the Qur'an with praise, opened His creation with praise and concluded it with praise. So to Him belongs praise first and last, and to Him belongs thanks outwardly and inwardly, and He is al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy), al-Majid (the Glorious).

text.ar: «مَجْمُوعُ الْفَتَاوَى» (٦/ ٨٣ ـ ٨٤).
text.en: *Majmu‘ al-Fatawa* (6/83–84).

text.ar: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ عَظِيمٌ وَرَدَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فِي مَوْضِعَيْنِ: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿رَحۡمَتُ ٱللَّهِ وَبَرَكَٰتُهُۥ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِۚ إِنَّهُۥ حَمِيدٞ مَّجِيدٞ﴾ [هُودٍ: ٧٣]، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلۡوَدُودُ (١٤) ذُو ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡمَجِيدُ﴾ [الْبُرُوجِ: ١٤ ـ ١٥]؛ بِرَفْعِ «الْمَجِيدُ»، وَقَدْ قُرِئَ «الْمَجِيدُ» بِالرَّفْعِ نَعْتًا لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَبِالْجَرِّ نَعْتًا لِلْعَرْشِ.
text.en: It is a great name that occurs in the Book of Allah in two places: His saying, the Exalted: ﴾The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious﴿ [Hud 11:73], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴾And He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Loving (14) Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴿ [al-Buruj 85:14–15], with “al-Majid” (the Glorious) in the nominative case. “Al-Majid” has been recited in the nominative case as a description of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and in the genitive case as a description of the Throne.

text.ar: وَهُوَ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحُسْنَى الدَّالَّةِ عَلَى أَوْصَافٍ عَدِيدَةٍ لَا عَلَى مَعْنًى مُفْرَدٍ.
text.en: It is one of the Most Beautiful Names that indicate many attributes, not a single meaning.

text.ar: وَمَعْنَاهُ: وَاسِعُ الصِّفَاتِ عَظِيمُهَا، كَثِيرُ النُّعُوتِ كَرِيمُهَا، فَالْمَجِيدُ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى عَظَمَةِ أَوْصَافِهِ وَكَثْرَتِهَا وَسَعَتِهَا، وَإِلَى عَظَمَةِ مُلْكِهِ وَسُلْطَانِهِ، وَإِلَى تَفَرُّدِهِ بِالْكَمَالِ الْمُطْلَقِ وَالْجَلَالِ الْمُطْلَقِ وَالْجَمَالِ الْمُطْلَقِ، الَّذِي لَا يُمْكِنُ الْعِبَادَ أَنْ يُحِيطُوا بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، الَّذِي هُوَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَأَعْظَمُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، وَأَجَلُّ وَأَعْلَى، وَلَهُ التَّعْظِيمُ وَالْإِجْلَالُ فِي قُلُوبِ أَوْلِيَائِهِ وَأَصْفِيَائِهِ، قَدْ مُلِئَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِنْ تَعْظِيمِهِ وَإِجْلَالِهِ وَالْخُضُوعِ لَهُ وَالتَّذَلُّلِ لِكِبْرِيَائِهِ، لَا مَجْدَ إِلَّا مَجْدُهُ، وَلَا عَظَمَةَ إِلَّا عَظَمَتُهُ، وَلَا جَلَالَ وَلَا جَمَالَ وَلَا كِبْرِيَاءَ إِلَّا جَلَالُهُ وَجَمَالُهُ وَكِبْرِيَاؤُهُ، أَسْمَاؤُهُ كُلُّهَا مَجْدٌ، وَصِفَاتُهُ مَجْدٌ، وَأَفْعَالُهُ وَأَقْوَالُهُ مَجْدٌ، الْمُمَجَّدُ فِي ذَاتِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ.
text.en: Its meaning is: the One whose attributes are vast and immense, and whose qualities are many and noble. Al-Majid (the Glorious) refers to the greatness, abundance and vastness of His attributes; to the greatness of His dominion and authority; and to His being unique in absolute perfection, absolute majesty and absolute beauty, of which the servants cannot encompass anything — the One who is greater than everything, more immense than everything, more majestic and higher. To Him belong reverence and veneration in the hearts of His allies and His chosen ones; their hearts are filled with reverence and veneration of Him, submission to Him and humility before His supremacy. There is no glory but His glory, no greatness but His greatness, and no majesty, beauty or supremacy but His majesty, beauty and supremacy. His names are all glory, His attributes are glory, His actions and His words are glory; He is the One glorified in His Essence and His attributes.

text.ar: وَاللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مَجَّدَ نَفْسَهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ فِي آيَاتٍ عَدِيدَةٍ، بَلْ إِنَّ الْقُرْآنَ الْكَرِيمَ كُلَّهُ كِتَابُ تَمْجِيدٍ وَتَعْظِيمٍ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، لَا تَخْلُو آيَةٌ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ ذِكْرِ شَيْءٍ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى وَصِفَاتِهِ الْعُلْيَا وَأَفْعَالِهِ الْحَكِيمَةِ، وَأَعْظَمُ آيِ الْقُرْآنِ هِيَ الَّتِي اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ، فَآيَةُ الْكُرْسِيِّ الَّتِي هِيَ أَعْظَمُ آيَةٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى خَمْسَةُ أَسْمَاءٍ، وَفِيهَا مِنْ صِفَاتِ اللَّهِ مَا يَزِيدُ عَلَى الْعِشْرِينَ صِفَةً، وَسُورَةُ الْإِخْلَاصِ الَّتِي تَعْدِلُ ثُلُثَ الْقُرْآنِ أُخْلِصَتْ لِبَيَانِ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى وَصِفَاتِهِ الْعَظِيمَةِ، وَسُورَةُ الْفَاتِحَةِ الَّتِي هِيَ أَعْظَمُ سُورَةٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ نِصْفُهَا ثَنَاءٌ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَتَمْجِيدٌ.
text.en: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has glorified Himself in His Book in many verses. Indeed, the entire Noble Qur'an is a book of glorifying and magnifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; no verse of the Qur'an is free from mention of something of Allah's Most Beautiful Names, His lofty attributes and His wise actions, and the greatest verses of the Qur'an are those that contain this. Ayat al-Kursi, which is the greatest verse in the Noble Qur'an, contains five of Allah's Most Beautiful Names and more than twenty of Allah's attributes. Surat al-Ikhlas, which is equal to a third of the Qur'an, is devoted purely to explaining Allah's Most Beautiful Names and His great attributes. And Surat al-Fatihah, which is the greatest surah in the Noble Qur'an, is half praise and glorification of Allah.

text.ar: رَوَى مُسْلِمٌ فِي «صَحِيحِهِ»[1] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: «قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: قَسَمْتُ الصَّلَاةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي نِصْفَيْنِ، وَلِعَبْدِي مَا سَأَلَ؛ فَإِذَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ؛ قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: حَمِدَنِي عَبْدِي، وَإِذَا قَالَ: الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ؛ قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: أَثْنَى عَلَيَّ عَبْدِي، وَإِذَا قَالَ: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ؛ قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: مَجَّدَنِي عَبْدِي، فَإِذَا قَالَ: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ؛ قَالَ: هَذَا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي، وَلِعَبْدِي مَا سَأَلَ، فَإِذَا قَالَ: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ؛ قَالَ: هَذَا لِعَبْدِي وَلِعَبْدِي مَا سَأَلَ».
text.en: Muslim narrated in his *Sahih*[1] from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah the Exalted said: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves, and My servant shall have what he asks for. When the servant says: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, Allah the Exalted says: My servant has praised Me. When he says: The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Allah the Exalted says: My servant has extolled Me. When he says: Master of the Day of Judgement, Allah the Exalted says: My servant has glorified Me. When he says: You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help, He says: This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for. When he says: Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray, He says: This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.”

text.ar: وَالصَّلَاةُ كُلُّهَا قَائِمَةٌ عَلَى الثَّنَاءِ وَالتَّعْظِيمِ وَالتَّمْجِيدِ لِلْحَمِيدِ الْمَجِيدِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَهْلِ الثَّنَاءِ كُلِّهِ وَالْمَجْدِ، وَقَدْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ قَالَ: «رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ، مِلْءَ السَّمَٰوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَمِلْءَ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ بَعْدُ، أَهْلَ الثَّنَاءِ وَالْمَجْدِ، أَحَقُّ مَا قَالَ الْعَبْدُ، وَكُلُّنَا لَكَ عَبْدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ لَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، وَلَا مُعْطِيَ لِمَا مَنَعْتَ وَلَا يَنْفَعُ ذَا الْجَدِّ مِنْكَ الْجَدُّ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[2]، وَفِي رُكُوعِهِ وَسُجُودِهِ يُعَظِّمُ اللَّهَ وَيُمَجِّدُهُ، وَإِذَا قَعَدَ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ يُثْنِي عَلَى اللَّهِ وَيُمَجِّدُهُ وَيَخْتِمُ ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ: «إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ»، فَأَوَّلُ الصَّلَاةِ حَمْدٌ وَتَمْجِيدٌ، وَآخِرُهَا حَمْدٌ وَتَمْجِيدٌ، بَلْ كُلُّهَا قَائِمَةٌ عَلَى الْحَمْدِ وَالتَّمْجِيدِ.
text.en: The whole prayer is built upon extolling, magnifying and glorifying al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy), al-Majid (the Glorious), Glorified is He, who is worthy of all praise and glory. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head from bowing, he would say: “Our Lord, to You belongs all praise, filling the heavens and the earth, and filling whatever else You will. You are worthy of praise and glory; this is the truest thing a servant has said, and we are all Your servants: O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and the wealth of a wealthy person cannot benefit him before You.” Narrated by Muslim[2]. In his bowing and his prostration he would magnify and glorify Allah, and when he sat for the tashahhud he would extol Allah and glorify Him, concluding it with his words: “Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.” So the beginning of the prayer is praise and glorification, and its end is praise and glorification; indeed, all of it is built upon praise and glorification.

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَأَحْسَنُ مَا قُرِنَ اسْمُ الْمَجِيدِ إِلَى الْحَمِيدِ، كَمَا قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ لِبَيْتِ الْخَلِيلِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: ﴿قَالُوٓاْ أَتَعۡجَبِينَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِۖ رَحۡمَتُ ٱللَّهِ وَبَرَكَٰتُهُۥ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِۚ إِنَّهُۥ حَمِيدٞ مَّجِيدٞ﴾ [هُودٍ: ٧٣]، كَمَا شَرَعَ لَنَا فِي آخِرِ الصَّلَاةِ أَنْ نُثْنِيَ عَلَى الرَّبِّ تَعَالَى أَنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، وَشَرَعَ فِي آخِرِ الرَّكْعَةِ عِنْدَ الِاعْتِدَالِ أَنْ نَقُولَ: «رَبَّنَا وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَهْلَ الثَّنَاءِ وَالْمَجْدِ»، فَالْحَمْدُ وَالْمَجْدُ عَلَى الْإِطْلَاقِ لِلَّهِ الْحَمِيدِ الْمَجِيدِ، فَالْحَمِيدُ: الْحَبِيبُ الْمُسْتَحِقُّ لِجَمِيعِ صِفَاتِ الْكَمَالِ، وَالْمَجِيدُ: الْعَظِيمُ الْوَاسِعُ الْقَادِرُ الْغَنِيُّ ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ»[3].
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “How beautifully the name al-Majid (the Glorious) is paired with al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy), as the angels said to the household of the Khalil (the Intimate Friend of Allah), peace be upon him: ﴾They said: Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy, Glorious﴿ [Hud 11:73]. Likewise, it has been prescribed for us at the end of the prayer to extol the Lord, Exalted is He, as being Praiseworthy and Glorious; and it has been prescribed at the end of the rak‘ah, on rising upright, that we say: ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise, You who are worthy of praise and glory.’ So praise and glory in the absolute sense belong to Allah, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious. Al-Hamid is the Beloved who deserves every attribute of perfection, and al-Majid is the Magnificent, the All-Encompassing, the Able, the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of majesty and honour.”[3]

text.ar: وَفِي خَتْمِ التَّشَهُّدِ بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ الْمَجِيدِ مَعْنًى لَطِيفٌ نَبَّهَ عَلَيْهِ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ قَالَ: «وَتَأَمَّلْ كَيْفَ جَاءَ هَذَا الِاسْمُ مُقْتَرِناً بِطَلَبِ الصَّلَاةِ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ كَمَا عَلَّمَنَاهُ ﷺ؛ لِأَنَّهُ فِي مَقَامِ طَلَبِ الْمَزِيدِ، وَالتَّعَرُّضِ لِسَعَةِ الْعَطَاءِ وَكَثْرَتِهِ وَدَوَامِهِ، فَأَتَى فِي هَذَا الْمَطْلُوبِ بِاسْمٍ يَقْتَضِيهِ»[4].
text.en: In closing the tashahhud with Allah's name al-Majid (the Glorious) there is a subtle meaning, which Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) pointed out. He said: “Reflect on how this name comes paired with asking Allah to send blessings upon His Messenger, as he ﷺ taught us. That is because it is a situation of asking for more, and of seeking the vastness of giving, its abundance and its continuity; so in this request a name was brought that calls for it.”[4]

text.ar: لِأَنَّ الْمَجْدَ يَدُلُّ عَلَى كَثْرَةِ أَوْصَافِ الْكَمَالِ وَكَثْرَةِ أَفْعَالِ الْبِرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ وَتَعَدُّدِ الْعَطَاءِ وَالنَّوَالِ.
text.en: For glory (majd) indicates an abundance of attributes of perfection, an abundance of acts of kindness and goodness, and giving and bestowing again and again.

text.ar: وَأَشْرَفُ أَحْوَالِ الْعَبْدِ وَأَرْفَعُ مَقَامَاتِهِ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُثْنِياً عَلَى رَبِّهِ مُعَظِّمًا لِجَنَابِهِ مُمَجِّداً لَهُ، وَمِنْ أَعْظَمِ ذَلِكَ تِلَاوَةُ كَلَامِهِ الْمَجِيدِ، وَقَدْ وَصَفَهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى بِذَلِكَ فِي مَوْضِعَيْنِ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿بَلۡ هُوَ قُرۡءَانٞ مَّجِيدٞ (٢١) فِي لَوۡحٖ مَّحۡفُوظِۭ﴾ [الْبُرُوجِ: ٢١ ـ ٢٢]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿قٓۚ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ ٱلۡمَجِيدِ﴾ [ق: ١].
text.en: The noblest state of the servant and his loftiest station is to be praising his Lord, exalting His majesty and glorifying Him. Among the greatest forms of this is reciting His Glorious Speech, which He, Blessed and Exalted is He, has described as such in two places in the Qur'an. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Rather, it is a Glorious Qur'an (21) in a Preserved Tablet﴿ [al-Buruj 85:21–22], and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Qaf. By the Glorious Qur'an﴿ [Qaf 50:1].

text.ar: فَالْقُرْآنُ مَجِيدٌ أَيْ: عَلِيٌّ قَدْرُهُ، رَفِيعٌ شَأْنُهُ، عَظِيمَةٌ مَكَانَتُهُ، لَا يَأْتِيهِ الْبَاطِلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدٍ.
text.en: So the Qur'an is glorious, meaning: lofty in worth, high in standing, great in rank. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One who is Wise, Praiseworthy.

text.ar: وَمِمَّا يُمَجَّدُ بِهِ الرَّبُّ سُبْحَانَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّنَاءِ عَلَيْهِ تَحْمِيدًا وَتَكْبِيرًا وَتَسْبِيحًا وَتَهْلِيلاً، وَمَنْ لَازَمَ ذَلِكَ سَعِدَ سَعَادَةً لَا شَقَاءَ مَعَهَا، وَفَازَ بِخَيْرَيِ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.
text.en: Among the ways the Lord, Glorified is He, is glorified is to praise Him beautifully: with words of praise (tahmid), of His greatness (takbir), of His perfection (tasbih) and of His oneness (tahlil). Whoever holds fast to this attains a happiness with no misery after it, and wins the good of both this world and the Hereafter.

text.ar: رَوَى الْبُخَارِيُّ فِي «صَحِيحِهِ»[5] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً يَطُوفُونَ فِي الطُّرُقِ يَلْتَمِّسُونَ أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ، فَإِذَا وَجَدُوا قَوْمًا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ تَنَادَوْا: هَلُمُّوا إِلَى حَاجَتِكُمْ، قَالَ: فَيَحُفُّونَهُمْ بِأَجْنِحَتِهِمْ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا، قَالَ: فَيَسْأَلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ـ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ مِنْهُمْ ـ: مَا يَقُولُ عِبَادِي؟ قَالَ: تَقُولُ: يُسَبِّحُونَكَ، وَيُكَبِّرُونَكَ، وَيَحْمَدُونَكَ، وَيُمَجِّدُونَكَ، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: هَلْ رَأَوْنِي؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ مَا رَأَوْكَ، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: كَيْفَ لَوْ رَأَوْنِي؟ قَالَ: يَقُولُونَ: لَوْ رَأَوْكَ كَانُوا أَشَدَّ لَكَ عِبَادَةً وَأَشَدَّ لَكَ تَمْجِيداً، وَأَكْثَرَ لَكَ تَسْبِيحاً، قَالَ: يَقُولُ: فَمَا يَسْأَلُونِي؟ قَالَ: يَسْأَلُونَكَ الْجَنَّةَ، قَالَ: يَقُولُ: وَهَلْ رَأَوْهَا؟ قَالَ: يَقُولُونَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَبِّ مَا رَأَوْهَا، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: فَيَكُفُ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ رَأَوْهَا؟ قَالَ: يَقُولُونَ: لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ رَأَوْهَا كَانُوا أَشَدَّ عَلَيْهَا حِرْصاً، وَأَشَدَّ لَهَا طَلَباً، وَأَعْظَمَ فِيهَا رَغْبَةً، قَالَ: فَمِمَّ يَتَعَوَّذُونَ؟ قَالَ:يَقُولُونَ: مِنَ النَّارِ، قَالَ: يَقُولُ: وَهَلْ رَأَوْهَا؟ قَالَ: فَيَقُولُونَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ يَا رَبِّ مَا رَأَوْهَا، قَالَ: يَقُولُ: فَكَيْفَ لَوْ رَأَوْهَا؟ قَالَ: يَقُولُونَ: لَوْ رَأَوْهَا كَانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهَا فِرَاراً، وَأَشَدَّ مِنْهَا مَخَافَةً، قَالَ: فَيَقُولُ: فَأُشْهِدُكُمْ أَنِّي قَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَهُمْ، قَالَ: يَقُولُ مَلَكٌ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: فِيهِمْ فُلَانٌ لَيْسَ مِنْهُمْ إِنَّمَا جَاءَ لِحَاجَةٍ، قَالَ: هُمُ الْجُلَسَاءُ لَا يَشْقَى جَلِيسُهُمْ».
text.en: Al-Bukhari reported in his *Sahih*[5] from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has angels who go about the roads seeking out the people of remembrance. When they find a people remembering Allah, they call out to one another: ‘Come to what you are looking for!’ He said: Then they surround them with their wings, up to the lowest heaven. He said: Then their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, asks them — though He knows better than them —: ‘What are My servants saying?’ He said: They say: ‘They are glorifying You, proclaiming Your greatness, praising You and extolling Your glory.’ He said: He says: ‘Have they seen Me?’ They say: ‘No, by Allah, they have not seen You.’ He said: He says: ‘And how would it be if they saw Me?’ He said: They say: ‘If they saw You, they would be even more intense in worshipping You, more intense in extolling Your glory, and more abundant in glorifying You.’ He said: He says: ‘Then what do they ask Me for?’ He said: They ask You for Paradise. He said: He says: ‘And have they seen it?’ He said: They say: ‘No, by Allah, O Lord, they have not seen it.’ He said: He says: ‘And how would it be if they saw it?’ He said: They say: ‘If they saw it, they would be even more eager for it, more intense in seeking it, and greater in their longing for it.’ He said: ‘Then from what do they seek refuge?’ He said: They say: ‘From the Fire.’ He said: He says: ‘And have they seen it?’ He said: They say: ‘No, by Allah, O Lord, they have not seen it.’ He said: He says: ‘And how would it be if they saw it?’ He said: They say: ‘If they saw it, they would flee from it even more and fear it even more.’ He said: Then He says: ‘I call you to witness that I have forgiven them.’ He said: One of the angels says: ‘Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he only came for some need of his.’ He said: ‘They are the people of the gathering; the one who sits with them is not left wretched.’”

text.ar: وَإِذَا كَانَ جَلِيسُهُمْ لَا يَشْقَى فَكَيْفَ الشَّأْنُ بِهِمْ، نَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ الْكَرِيمَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ.
text.en: And if the one who sits with them is not left wretched, then what of them themselves! We ask Allah, the Most Generous, of His bounty.

text.ar: (رَقْم: ٤٧٧) مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: (no. 477), from the hadith of Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him).

text.ar: «التِّبْيَانُ فِي أَقْسَامِ الْقُرْآنِ» (ص/ ١٢٥).
text.en: *at-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Qur'an* (p. 125).
*Bada’i‘ al-Fawa’id* (1/144).

title.en: ash-Shakur, ash-Shakir (the Most Appreciative, the Appreciative)

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ اسْمُ «الشَّكُورِ» فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ:
text.en: The name “ash-Shakur” (the Most Appreciative) occurs in four places in the Qur'an:

text.ar: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿لِيُوَفِّيَهُمۡ أُجُورَهُمۡ وَيَزِيدَهُم مِّن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ غَفُورٞ شَكُورٞ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٣٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَذۡهَبَ عَنَّا ٱلۡحَزَنَۖ إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٞ شَكُورٌ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٣٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن يَقۡتَرِفۡ حَسَنَةٗ نَّزِدۡ لَهُۥ فِيهَا حُسۡنًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ شَكُورٌ﴾ [الشُّورَى: ٢٣]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِن تُقۡرِضُواْ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنٗا يُضَٰعِفۡهُ لَكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾ [التَّغَابُنِ: ١٧].
text.en: Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴾That He may pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative﴿ [Fatir 35:30]; He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾And they will say: Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us all sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative﴿ [Fatir 35:34]; He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative﴿ [ash-Shura 42:23]; and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾If you lend Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing﴿ [at-Taghabun 64:17].

text.ar: وَوَرَدَ «الشَّاكِرُ» فِي مَوْضِعَيْنِ:
text.en: And “ash-Shakir” (the Appreciative) occurs in two places:

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ١٥٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿مَّا يَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمۡ إِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ وَءَامَنتُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ شَاكِرًا عَلِيمٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١٤٧].
text.en: He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾And whoever does good voluntarily, then indeed Allah is Appreciative, All-Knowing﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:158]; and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing﴿ [an-Nisa’ 4:147].

text.ar: وَجَمِيعُ هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ السِّتَّةِ الَّتِي وَرَدَ فِيهَا هَذَانِ الِاسْمَانِ مَوَاضِعُ امْتِنَانٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ بِإِثَابَةِ الْمُطِيعِينَ، وَتَوْفِيَةِ الْأُجُورِ، وَالزِّيَادَةِ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ، وَالْمُضَاعَفَةِ لِلثَّوَابِ، وَهَذَا مِمَّا يُبَيِّنُ لَنَا مَعْنَى هَذَيْنِ الِاسْمَيْنِ، وَأَنَّ الشَّكُورَ الشَّاكِرَ: هُوَ الَّذِي لَا يَضِيعُ عِنْدَهُ عَمَلُ عَامِلٍ، بَلْ يُضَاعِفُ الْأَجْرَ بِلَا حُسْبَانٍ، الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ الْيَسِيرَ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ، وَيُثِيبُ عَلَيْهِ الثَّوَابَ الْكَثِيرَ وَالْعَطَاءَ الْجَزِيلَ، وَالنَّوَالَ الْوَاسِعَ، الَّذِي يُضَاعِفُ لِلْمُخْلِصِينَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ، وَيَشْكُرُ الشَّاكِرِينَ، وَيَذْكُرُ الذَّاكِرِينَ، وَمَنْ تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيْهِ شِبْرًا تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيْهِ ذِرَاعًا، وَمَنْ تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيْهِ ذِرَاعًا تَقَرَّبَ إِلَيْهِ بَاعًا، وَمَنْ جَاءَهُ بِالْحَسَنَةِ زَادَ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْنًا، وَآتَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا.
text.en: All six of the places in which these two names occur are contexts in which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminds of His favour: rewarding the obedient, paying wages in full, giving more from His bounty and multiplying the reward. This shows us the meaning of these two names: ash-Shakur, ash-Shakir (the Most Appreciative, the Appreciative) is the One with whom the deed of no doer is ever lost; rather, He multiplies the reward beyond reckoning. He accepts a small deed and rewards it with abundant reward, generous giving and vast bestowal. He multiplies for the sincere their deeds without measure, appreciates those who are grateful, and remembers those who remember Him. Whoever draws near to Him by a hand-span, He draws near to him by a forearm's length; and whoever draws near to Him by a forearm's length, He draws near to him by the length of two outstretched arms. Whoever comes to Him with a good deed, He increases its goodness for him, and gives him from Himself a mighty reward.

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي بَسْطِ الْقَوْلِ فِي مَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ وَذِكْرِ مَعَانِيهِ الْعَظِيمَةِ وَدَلَائِلِهِ الْجَلِيلَةِ: «وَأَمَّا شُكْرُ الرَّبِّ تَعَالَى فَلَهُ شَأْنٌ آخَرُ، فَهُوَ أَوْلَى بِصِفَةِ الشُّكْرِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَكُورٍ، بَلْ هُوَ الشَّكُورُ عَلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ، فَإِنَّهُ يُعْطِي الْعَبْدَ وَيُوَفِّقُهُ لِمَا يَشْكُرُهُ عَلَيْهِ، وَيَشْكُرُ الْقَلِيلَ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ وَالْعَطَاءِ فَلَا يَسْتَقِلُّهُ أَنْ يَشْكُرَهُ، وَيَشْكُرُ الْحَسَنَةَ بِعَشْرِ أَمْثَالِهَا إِلَى أَضْعَافٍ مُضَاعَفَةٍ، وَيَشْكُرُ عَبْدَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ بِأَنْ يُثْنِيَ عَلَيْهِ بَيْنَ مَلَائِكَتِهِ وَفِي مَلَئِهِ الْأَعْلَى، وَيُلْقِي لَهُ الشُّكْرَ بَيْنَ عِبَادِهِ، وَيَشْكُرُ بِفِعْلِهِ، فَإِذَا تَرَكَ لَهُ شَيْئًا أَعْطَاهُ أَفْضَلَ مِنْهُ، وَإِذَا بَذَلَ لَهُ شَيْئًا رَدَّهُ عَلَيْهِ أَضْعَافًا مُضَاعَفَةً، وَهُوَ الَّذِي وَفَّقَهُ لِلتَّرْكِ وَالْبَذْلِ، وَشَكَرَهُ عَلَى هَذَا وَذَاكَ، وَلَمَّا تَرَكَ الصَّحَابَةُ دِيَارَهُمْ وَخَرَجُوا مِنْهَا فِي مَرْضَاتِهِ أَعَاضَهُمْ عَنْهَا أَنْ مَلَّكَهُمُ الدُّنْيَا وَفَتَحَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ، وَلَمَّا احْتَمَلَ يُوسُفُ الصِّدِّيقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ ضِيقَ السِّجْنِ شَكَرَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ بِأَنْ مَكَّنَ لَهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنْهَا حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ، وَلَمَّا بَذَلَ الشُّهَدَاءُ أَبْدَانَهُمْ لَهُ حَتَّى مَزَّقَتْهَا أَعْدَاؤُهُ شَكَرَ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ بِأَنْ أَعَاضَهُمْ مِنْهَا طَيْرًا خُضْرًا أَقَرَّ أَرْوَاحَهُمْ فِيهَا تَرِدُ أَنْهَارَ الْجَنَّةِ وَتَأْكُلُ مِنْ ثِمَارِهَا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْبَعْثِ، فَيَرُدُّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَكْمَلَ مَا تَكُونُ وَأَجْمَلَهُ وَأَبْهَاهُ، وَلَمَّا بَذَلَ رُسُلُهُ أَعْرَاضَهُمْ فِيهِ لِأَعْدَائِهِمْ فَنَالُوا مِنْهُمْ وَسَبُّوهُمْ أَعَاضَهُمْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ بِأَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيْهِمْ هُوَ وَمَلَائِكَتُهُ، وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَطْيَبَ الثَّنَاءِ فِي سَمَٰوَاتِهِ وَبَيْنَ خَلْقِهِ، فَأَخْلَصَهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ.
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him), expounding the meaning of this name and mentioning its tremendous meanings and sublime indications, said: “As for the appreciation (shukr) of the Lord, Exalted is He, it is of another order altogether. He is more worthy of the attribute of appreciation than anyone who is appreciative; indeed, He is the truly Appreciative. For He gives the servant, and grants him success in that for which He then thanks him. He appreciates the little of deeds and giving, and does not consider it too little to appreciate. He rewards a good deed with ten like it, up to many times multiplied. He thanks His servant by His word, by praising him among His angels and in His Highest Assembly and by spreading thanks for him among His servants; and He thanks him by His action: when the servant leaves something for His sake, He gives him something better than it, and when he spends something for Him, He returns it to him many times over — and it was He who granted him success to leave and to spend, and then thanked him for both this and that. When the Companions left their homes and departed from them seeking His pleasure, He compensated them by giving them dominion over the world and opening it to them. When Yusuf, the truthful one, peace be upon him, bore the narrowness of prison, He thanked him for that by establishing him in the land, to settle therein wherever he wished. When the martyrs gave their bodies for Him until His enemies tore them apart, He thanked them for that by giving them in their place green birds in which He settled their souls, which come to the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits until the Day of Resurrection, when He will return the bodies to them in the most complete, most beautiful and most splendid form. When His messengers gave up their honour for His sake to their enemies, who attacked them and reviled them, He compensated them for that by sending blessings upon them, He and His angels, and gave them the finest praise in His heavens and among His creation; so He singled them out with an exclusive quality: remembrance of the Home.

text.ar: وَمِنْ شُكْرِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ: أَنَّهُ يُجَازِي عَدُوَّهُ بِمَا يَفْعَلُهُ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ وَالْمَعْرُوفِ فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَيُخَفِّفُ عَنْهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلَا يُضِيعُ عَلَيْهِ مَا يَعْمَلُهُ مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ، وَهُوَ مِنْ أَبْغَضِ خَلْقِهِ إِلَيْهِ.
text.en: Part of His appreciation, Glorified is He, is that He repays His enemy for whatever good and kindness he does in this world, and lightens things for him on the Day of Resurrection, so that the good he does is not lost to him — even though he is among the most hated of His creation to Him.

text.ar: وَمِنْ شُكْرِهِ: أَنَّهُ غَفَرَ لِلْمَرْأَةِ الْبَغِيِّ بِسَقْيِهَا كَلْبًا قَدْ جَهَدَهُ الْعَطَشُ حَتَّى أَكَلَ الثَّرَى، وَغَفَرَ لِآخَرَ بِتَنْحِيَتِهِ غُصْنَ شَوْكٍ عَنْ طَرِيقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ.
text.en: Part of His appreciation is that He forgave the prostitute for giving water to a dog that thirst had so exhausted that it was eating the moist earth, and He forgave another man for moving a thorny branch out of the Muslims' path.

text.ar: فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ يَشْكُرُ الْعَبْدَ عَلَى إِحْسَانِهِ لِنَفْسِهِ، وَالْمَخْلُوقُ إِنَّمَا [يَشْكُرُ] مَنْ أَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِ، وَأَبْلَغُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ الَّذِي أَعْطَى الْعَبْدَ مَا يُحْسِنُ بِهِ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ، وَشَكَرَهُ عَلَى قَلِيلِهِ بِالْأَضْعَافِ الْمُضَاعَفَةِ الَّتِي لَا نِسْبَةَ لِإِحْسَانِ الْعَبْدِ إِلَيْهَا، فَهُوَ الْمُحْسِنُ بِإِعْطَاءِ الْإِحْسَانِ وَإِعْطَاءِ الشُّكْرِ، فَمَنْ أَحَقُّ بِاسْمِ «الشَّكُورِ» مِنْهُ سُبْحَانَهُ؟!.
text.en: So He, Glorified is He, thanks the servant for doing good to himself, whereas a created being thanks only the one who has done good to him. More profound still: it is He, Glorified is He, who gave the servant the means by which he does good to himself, and then thanked him for his little with manifold multiples to which the servant's good bears no comparison. So He is the Benefactor both in granting the good deed and in granting the thanks. Who, then, is more deserving of the name “ash-Shakur” (the Most Appreciative) than He, Glorified is He?!

text.ar: وَتَأَمَّلْ قَوْلَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ: ﴿مَّا يَفۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمۡ إِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ وَءَامَنتُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ شَاكِرًا عَلِيمٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١٤٧]؛ كَيْفَ تَجِدُ فِي ضِمْنِ هَذَا الْخِطَابِ أَنَّ شُكْرَهُ تَعَالَى يَأْبَى تَعْذِيبَ عِبَادِهِ بِغَيْرِ جُرْمٍ، كَمَا يَأْبَى إِضَاعَةَ سَعْيِهِمْ بَاطِلًا، فَالشَّكُورُ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مُحْسِنٍ، وَلَا يُعَذِّبُ غَيْرَ مُسِيءٍ.
text.en: Reflect on His words, Glorified is He: ﴾What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing﴿ [an-Nisa’ 4:147]. See how you find within this address that His appreciation, Exalted is He, refuses to punish His servants without a crime, just as it refuses to let their striving go to waste. For the Most Appreciative does not let the reward of one who does good go to waste, and does not punish one who has done no wrong.

text.ar: وَمِنْ شُكْرِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ: أَنَّهُ يُخْرِجُ الْعَبْدَ مِنَ النَّارِ بِأَدْنَى مِثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ خَيْرٍ وَلَا يُضِيعُ عَلَيْهِ هَذَا الْقَدْرَ.
text.en: Part of His appreciation, Glorified is He, is that He brings the servant out of the Fire for the smallest weight of an atom of good, and does not let even that amount be lost to him.

text.ar: وَمِنْ شُكْرِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ: أَنَّ الْعَبْدَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ يَقُومُ لَهُ مَقَامًا يُرْضِيهِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فَيَشْكُرُهُ لَهُ، وَيُنَوِّهُ بِذِكْرِهِ، وَيُخْبِرُ بِهِ مَلَائِكَتَهُ وَعِبَادَهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كَمَا شَكَرَ لِمُؤْمِنِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ ذَلِكَ الْمَقَامَ، وَأَثْنَى بِهِ عَلَيْهِ، وَنَوَّهَ بِذِكْرِهِ بَيْنَ عِبَادِهِ، وَكَذَلِكَ شُكْرُهُ لِصَاحِبِ يس مَقَامَهُ وَدَعْوَتَهُ إِلَيْهِ، فَلَا يَهْلِكُ عَلَيْهِ بَيْنَ شُكْرِهِ وَمَغْفِرَتِهِ إِلَّا هَالِكٌ، فَإِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ، يَغْفِرُ الْكَثِيرَ مِنَ الزَّلَلِ، وَيَشْكُرُ الْقَلِيلَ مِنَ الْعَمَلِ.
text.en: Part of His appreciation, Glorified is He, is that when one of His servants takes a stand for Him among people that pleases Him, He appreciates it from him, raises mention of him, and tells His angels and His believing servants about him — just as He appreciated that stand from the believer of Pharaoh's family, praised him for it and raised mention of him among His servants; and likewise His appreciation of the man in Ya Sin for his stand and his call to Him. So none perishes, between His appreciation and His forgiveness, except one who is truly doomed. For He, Glorified is He, is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative: He forgives many slips and appreciates little deeds.

text.ar: وَلَمَّا كَانَ سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ الشَّكُورَ عَلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ كَانَ أَحَبَّ خَلْقِهِ إِلَيْهِ مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِصِفَةِ الشُّكْرِ، كَمَا أَنَّ أَبْغَضَ خَلْقِهِ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ عَطَّلَهَا وَاتَّصَفَ بِضِدِّهَا، وَهَذَا شَأْنُ أَسْمَائِهِ الْحُسْنَى، أَحَبُّ خَلْقِهِ إِلَيْهِ مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِمُوجَبِهَا، وَأَبْغَضُهُمْ إِلَيْهِ مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِأَضْدَادِهَا، وَلِهَذَا يُبْغِضُ الْكَفُورَ وَالظَّالِمَ وَالْجَاهِلَ وَالْقَاسِيَ الْقَلْبِ وَالْبَخِيلَ وَالْجَبَانَ وَالْمَهِينَ وَاللَّئِيمَ، وَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ، عَلِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْعُلَمَاءَ، رَحِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الرَّاحِمِينَ، مُحْسِنٌ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ، شَكُورٌ يُحِبُّ الشَّاكِرِينَ، صَبُورٌ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ، جَوَادٌ يُحِبُّ أَهْلَ الْجُودِ، سَتَّارٌ يُحِبُّ أَهْلَ السَّتْرِ، قَادِرٌ يَلُومُ عَلَى الْعَجْزِ، وَالْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، عَفُوٌّ يُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ، وِتْرٌ يُحِبُّ الْوِتْرَ، وَكُلُّ مَا يُحِبُّهُ فَهُوَ مِنْ آثَارِ أَسْمَائِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ وَمُوجَبِهَا، وَكُلُّ مَا يُبْغِضُهُ فَهُوَ مِمَّا يُضَادُّهَا وَيُنَافِيهَا» اهـ[1].
text.en: Since He, Glorified is He, is the truly Appreciative, the most beloved of His creation to Him is the one who has the quality of gratitude, just as the most hated of His creation to Him is the one who negates it and has its opposite. This is the way of His Beautiful Names: the most beloved of His creation to Him is the one who has the qualities they call for, and the most hated of them to Him is the one who has their opposites. That is why He hates the ungrateful, the wrongdoer, the ignorant, the hard-hearted, the miser, the coward, the contemptible and the base. He, Glorified is He, is Beautiful and loves beauty; All-Knowing and loves the people of knowledge; Merciful and loves the merciful; a Doer of good and loves those who do good; Appreciative and loves the grateful; Patient and loves the patient; Generous and loves the people of generosity; a Concealer of faults and loves those who conceal; Able and blames incapacity — and the strong believer is more beloved to Him than the weak believer; Pardoning and loves pardon; Single (Witr) and loves what is odd. Everything He loves is among the effects of His names and attributes and what they call for, and everything He hates is among what opposes and contradicts them.” End quote.[1]

text.ar: وَفِي الْآيَاتِ الْمُتَقَدِّمَةِ جَمْعٌ بَيْنَ الْغَفُورِ وَالشَّكُورِ، فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ غَفُورٌ لِلذُّنُوبِ كُلِّهَا مَهْمَا عَظُمَتْ فَلَا يَتَعَاظَمُهُ ذَنْبٌ أَنْ يَغْفِرَهُ، الشَّكُورُ لِكُلِّ عَمَلٍ وَإِنْ قَلَّ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ، وَلِهَذَا لَا يَجُوزُ لِلْمُسْلِمِ أَنْ يَقْنَطَ مِنْ غُفْرَانِ اللَّهِ لِلذُّنُوبِ مَهْمَا عَظُمَتْ، كَمَا لَا يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَحْقِرَ مِنْ أَعْمَالِ الْبِرِّ شَيْئًا مَهْمَا قَلَّتْ؛ فَإِنَّ الرَّبَّ سُبْحَانَهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ.
text.en: In the verses cited above, al-Ghafur (the Oft-Forgiving) and ash-Shakur (the Most Appreciative) are joined together. He, Glorified is He, forgives all sins, however great they may be — no sin is too great for Him to forgive — and He appreciates every deed, however small, even if it is the weight of an atom. That is why it is not permissible for a Muslim to despair of Allah's forgiveness of sins, however great they are, just as it is not permissible for him to belittle any righteous deed, however small; for the Lord, Glorified is He, is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.

text.ar: وَإِنَّا لَنَسْأَلُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ مُتَوَسِّلِينَ إِلَيْهِ بِهَذَيْنِ الِاسْمَيْنِ الْعَظِيمَيْنِ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِي أَمْرِنَا، وَأَنْ يَتَقَبَّلَ مِنَّا صَالِحَ أَعْمَالِنَا، إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ.
text.en: We ask Him, Glorified is He, seeking nearness to Him through these two tremendous names, to forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, and to accept from us our righteous deeds. Indeed, He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Appreciative.

text.ar: «عُدَّةُ الصَّابِرِينَ» (ص/ ٣٣٥ ـ ٣٣٧) بِاخْتِصَارٍ.
text.en: *‘Uddat as-Sabirin* (pp. 335–337), abridged.

text.ar: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ تَكَرَّرَ وُرُودُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ فِي عِدَّةِ مَوَاضِعَ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمۡسِكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَن تَزُولَاۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَهُمَا مِنۡ أَحَدٖ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورٗا﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٤١]، وَقَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٞ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٣٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَلِيمٗا﴾ [الْأَحْزَابِ: ٥١].
text.en: This is a name that occurs repeatedly in the Noble Qur'an, in several places. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving﴿ [Fatir 35:41]; Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴾And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Forbearing﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:235]; and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾And Allah knows what is in your hearts. And Allah is ever All-Knowing, Forbearing﴿ [al-Ahzab 33:51].

text.ar: وَمَعْنَاهُ: أَيْ: الَّذِي لَا يَعْجَلُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ بِعُقُوبَتِهِمْ عَلَى ذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَعَاصِيهِمْ، يَرَى عِبَادَهُ وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِهِ وَيَعْصُونَهُ، وَهُوَ يَحْلُمُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيُؤَخِّرُ وَيُنْظِرُ وَيُؤَجِّلُ وَلَا يَعْجَلُ، وَيُوَالِي النِّعَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ مَعَ مَعَاصِيهِمْ وَكَثْرَةِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ وَزَلَّاتِهِمْ، فَيَحْلُمُ عَنْ مُقَابَلَةِ الْعَاصِينَ بِعِصْيَانِهِمْ، وَيُمْهِلُهُمْ كَيْ يَتُوبُوا، وَلَا يُعَاجِلُهُمْ بِالْعُقُوبَةِ كَيْ يُنِيبُوا وَيَرْجِعُوا.
text.en: Its meaning is: the One who does not hasten to punish His servants for their sins and acts of disobedience. He sees His servants disbelieving in Him and disobeying Him, yet He is forbearing with them: He delays, gives respite and postpones, and does not hasten. He continues His favours upon them one after another despite their disobedience and their many sins and slips. He forbears from repaying the disobedient for their disobedience, and gives them respite so that they may repent; He does not hasten punishment upon them, so that they may turn back and return.

text.ar: وَحِلْمُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ عَمَّنْ كَفَرَ بِهِ وَعَصَاهُ عَنْ عِلْمٍ وَقُوَّةٍ وَقُدْرَةٍ لَا عَنْ عَجْزٍ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَوَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَكَانُوٓاْ أَشَدَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةٗۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعۡجِزَهُۥ مِن شَيۡءٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَلِيمٗا قَدِيرٗا﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٤٤].
text.en: His forbearance, Glorified is He, towards those who disbelieve in Him and disobey Him comes from knowledge, strength and power, not from incapacity. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? And they were greater than them in strength. And Allah is not such that anything in the heavens or on the earth could escape Him. Indeed, He is ever All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴿ [Fatir 35:44].

text.ar: وَقَدْ أَخْبَرَ سُبْحَانَهُ عَنْ حِلْمِهِ بِأَهْلِ الْمَعَاصِي وَالذُّنُوبِ وَأَنْوَاعِ الظُّلْمِ بِأَنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ يُؤَاخِذُهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ أَوَّلًا بِأَوَّلٍ لَمَا أَبْقَى عَلَى ظَهْرِ الْأَرْضِ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ، كَمَا قَالَ سُبْحَانَهُ: ﴿وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلۡمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيۡهَا مِن دَآبَّةٖ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٖ مُّسَمّٗىۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَـٔۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةٗ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ٦١]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ذُو ٱلرَّحۡمَةِۖ لَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُهُم بِمَا كَسَبُواْ لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ بَل لَّهُم مَّوۡعِدٞ لَّن يَجِدُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦ مَوۡئِلٗا﴾ [الْكَهْفِ: ٥٨].
text.en: He, Glorified is He, has told of His forbearance with the people of disobedience, sins and all kinds of wrongdoing: that if He were to take them to task for their sins one by one, He would not leave a single creature on the face of the earth. As He, Glorified is He, said: ﴾And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature; but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they go ahead of it﴿ [an-Nahl 16:61]; and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾And your Lord is the Oft-Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. If He were to seize them for what they earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. Rather, for them is an appointed time from which they will never find an escape﴿ [al-Kahf 18:58].

text.ar: فَمَعَ مَا يَكُونُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ شِرْكٍ بِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ، وَوُقُوعٍ فِي مَسَاخِطِهِ وَاجْتِهَادٍ فِي مُخَالَفَتِهِ وَمُحَارَبَةِ دِينِهِ، وَمُعَادَاةٍ لِأَوْلِيَائِهِ يَحْلُمُ عَلَيْهِمْ، وَيَسُوقُ إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْوَاعَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ، وَيَرْزُقُهُمْ وَيُعَافِيهِمْ، كَمَا فِي «الصَّحِيحِ»[1] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِيمَا يَرْوِيهِ عَنْ رَبِّهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «يَشْتِمُنِي ابْنُ آدَمَ، وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَشْتِمَنِي، وَيُكَذِّبُنِي، وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ، أَمَّا شَتْمُهُ فَقَوْلُهُ: إِنَّ لِي وَلَداً، وَأَمَّا تَكْذِيبُهُ فَقَوْلُهُ: لَيْسَ يُعِيدُنِي كَمَا بَدَأَنِي».
text.en: So despite their associating partners with Him, Glorified is He, their falling into what angers Him, their striving to oppose Him and to fight His religion, and their enmity towards His allies, He is forbearing with them, sends them all kinds of good things, provides for them and grants them well-being. As in the *Sahih*[1], from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ in what he narrates from his Lord, that He said: “The son of Adam reviles Me, and it is not fitting for him to revile Me; and he belies Me, and it is not fitting for him. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: ‘I have a child.’ And as for his belying Me, it is his saying: ‘He will not bring me back as He began me.’”

text.ar: وَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[2] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: «لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ أَوْ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ أَصْبَرَ عَلَى أَذًى سَمِعَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّهُمْ لَيَدْعُونَ لَهُ وَلَداً، وَإِنَّهُ لَيُعَافِيهِمْ وَيَرْزُقُهُمْ».
text.en: And in the two *Sahih*s[2], from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “There is no one — or: nothing — more patient over harm that he hears than Allah. They claim that He has a child, yet He grants them well-being and provides for them.”

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَهُوَ مَعَ هَذَا الشَّتْمِ لَهُ وَالتَّكْذِيبِ يَرْزُقُ الشَّاتِمَ الْمُكَذِّبَ، وَيُعَافِيهِ، وَيَدْفَعُ عَنْهُ، وَيَدْعُوهُ إِلَى جَنَّتِهِ، وَيَقْبَلُ تَوْبَتَهُ إِذَا تَابَ إِلَيْهِ، وَيُبَدِّلُهُ بِسَيِّئَاتِهِ حَسَنَاتٍ، وَيَلْطُفُ بِهِ فِي جَمِيعِ أَحْوَالِهِ، وَيُؤَهِّلُهُ لِإِرْسَالِ رُسُلِهِ، وَيَأْمُرُهُمْ بِأَنْ يُلِينُوا لَهُ الْقَوْلَ وَيَرْفُقُوا بِهِ»[3].
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Yet despite this reviling and belying of Him, He provides for the one who reviles and belies Him, grants him well-being, defends him, invites him to His Paradise, accepts his repentance if he repents to Him, replaces his evil deeds with good deeds, is gentle with him in all his states, makes him fit for the sending of His messengers, and commands them to speak to him gently and to be kind to him.”[3]

text.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكُمْ حِلْمُهُ بِفِرْعَوْنَ مَعَ شِدَّةِ طُغْيَانِهِ وَعُلُوِّهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِفْسَادِهِ لِلْخَلْقِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱذۡهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ (٤٣) فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوۡلٗا لَّيِّنٗا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ﴾ [طَهَ: ٤٣ ـ ٤٤].
text.en: Among this is His forbearance with Pharaoh, despite the severity of his tyranny, his arrogance in the land and his corruption of people. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed. (43) And speak to him with gentle speech, that perhaps he may take heed or fear﴿ [Ta Ha 20:43–44].

text.ar: وَحِلْمُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ بِالَّذِينَ نَسَبُوا لَهُ الْوَلَدَ حَيْثُ دَعَاهُمْ لِلتَّوْبَةِ، وَفَتَحَ لَهُمْ أَبْوَابَهَا، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَّقَدۡ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَٰثَةٖۘ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّآ إِلَٰهٞ وَٰحِدٞۚ وَإِن لَّمۡ يَنتَهُواْ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٧٣) أَفَلَا يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَيَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَهُۥۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ﴾ [الْمَائِدَةِ: ٧٣ ـ ٧٤].
text.en: And His forbearance, Glorified is He, with those who ascribed a child to Him, in that He invited them to repentance and opened its doors to them. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾They have certainly disbelieved who say: Allah is the third of three. And there is no deity except one Deity. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, a painful punishment will surely afflict those of them who disbelieve. (73) Will they not then turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴿ [al-Ma’idah 5:73–74].

text.ar: وَحِلْمُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ بِأَصْحَابِ الْأُخْدُودِ وَهُمْ قَوْمٌ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ، كَانَ عِنْدَهُمْ قَوْمٌ مُؤْمِنُونَ، فَرَاوَدُوهُمْ لِلدُّخُولِ فِي دِينِهِمْ، فَامْتَنَعُوا، فَشَقَّ الْكُفَّارُ أُخْدُودًا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَجَّجُوا فِيهِ نَارًا، ثُمَّ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَعَرَضُوهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ، فَمَنِ اسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ أَطْلَقُوهُ، وَمَنِ امْتَنَعَ قَذَفُوهُ فِي النَّارِ، وَهَذَا فِي غَايَةِ الْمُحَارَبَةِ لِلَّهِ وَلِأَوْلِيَائِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَمَعَ هَذَا كُلِّهِ دَعَاهُمْ سُبْحَانَهُ لِلتَّوْبَةِ.
text.en: And His forbearance, Glorified is He, with the People of the Trench. They were a people of disbelievers among whom lived some believers. They tried to entice them into entering their religion, but they refused. So the disbelievers dug a trench in the ground and kindled a fire in it, then put the believers to trial and brought them before the fire: whoever gave in to them they released, and whoever refused they hurled into the fire. This is the utmost in waging war against Allah and His believing allies — and despite all this, He, Glorified is He, invited them to repentance.

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَتَنُواْ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَتُوبُواْ فَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابُ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ﴾ [الْبُرُوجِ: ١٠].
text.en: He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the burning fire﴿ [al-Buruj 85:10].

text.ar: قَالَ الْحَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيُّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «انْظُرُوا إِلَى هَذَا الْكَرَمِ وَالْجُودِ، قَتَلُوا أَوْلِيَاءَهُ وَهُوَ يَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى التَّوْبَةِ وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ»[4].
text.en: Al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Look at this generosity and kindness! They killed His allies, and He invites them to repentance and forgiveness.”[4]

text.ar: وَمِنْ حِلْمِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ إِمْسَاكُهُ لِلسَّمَاءِ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ، وَإِمْسَاكُهُ لَهُمَا أَنْ تَزُولَا مَعَ كَثْرَةِ ذُنُوبِ بَنِي آدَمَ وَمَعَاصِيهِمْ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمۡسِكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَن تَزُولَاۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَهُمَا مِنۡ أَحَدٖ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورٗا﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٤١].
text.en: Part of His forbearance, Glorified is He, is that He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, and holds them both back from ceasing, despite the many sins and acts of disobedience of the children of Adam. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴾Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving﴿ [Fatir 35:41].

text.ar: قَالَ الْعَلَّامَةُ ابْنُ سَعْدِيٍّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي تَفْسِيرِهِ لِهَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: «يُخْبِرُ تَعَالَى عَنْ كَمَالِ قُدْرَتِهِ، وَتَمَامِ رَحْمَتِهِ، وَسَعَةِ حِلْمِهِ وَمَغْفِرَتِهِ، وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى يُمْسِكُ السَّمَٰوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ عَنِ الزَّوَالِ، فَإِنَّهُمَا لَوْ زَالَتَا مَا أَمْسَكَهُمَا أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْخَلْقِ، وَلَعَجَزَتْ قُدْرَتُهُمْ وَقُوَاهُمْ عَنْهُمَا، وَلَكِنَّهُ تَعَالَى قَضَى أَنْ يَكُونَا كَمَا وُجِدَا، لِيَحْصُلَ لِلْخَلْقِ الْقَرَارُ وَالنَّفْعُ وَالِاعْتِبَارُ، وَلِيَعْلَمُوا مِنْ عَظِيمِ سُلْطَانِهِ، وَقُوَّةِ قُدْرَتِهِ مَا بِهِ تَمْتَلِئُ قُلُوبُهُمْ لَهُ إِجْلَالًا وَتَعْظِيمًا، وَمَحَبَّةً وَتَكْرِيمًا، وَلِيَعْلَمُوا كَمَالَ حِلْمِهِ وَمَغْفِرَتِهِ بِإِمْهَالِ الْمُذْنِبِينَ، وَعَدَمِ مُعَاجَلَتِهِ لِلْعَاصِينَ، مَعَ أَنَّهُ لَوْ أَمَرَ السَّمَاءَ لَحَصَبَتْهُمْ، وَلَوْ أَذِنَ لِلْأَرْضِ لَابْتَلَعَتْهُمْ، وَلَكِنْ وَسِعَتْهُمْ مَغْفِرَتُهُ وَحِلْمُهُ وَكَرَمُهُ ﴿إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورٗا﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٤١]»[5].
text.en: The great scholar Ibn Sa‘di (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his tafsir of this verse: “Allah, Exalted is He, tells of the perfection of His power, the completeness of His mercy and the vastness of His forbearance and forgiveness; and that He, Exalted is He, holds the heavens and the earth back from ceasing. For if they were to cease, no one from among creation could hold them; their power and strength would fall short of them. But He, Exalted is He, decreed that they remain as they were brought into being, so that creation may have stability, benefit and lessons to reflect on; and so that they may come to know, of His mighty dominion and the strength of His power, that which fills their hearts with reverence and veneration for Him, and love and honour; and so that they may know the perfection of His forbearance and forgiveness in giving respite to sinners and not hastening against the disobedient — even though, were He to command the sky, it would pelt them with stones, and were He to permit the earth, it would swallow them up. But His forgiveness, forbearance and generosity encompass them. ﴾Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Oft-Forgiving﴿ [Fatir 35:41].”[5]
