text.ar: وَعَجَبًا ثُمَّ عَجَبًا مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ الطَّغَامِ سُفَهَاءِ الْعُقُولِ وَالْأَحْلَامِ كَيْفَ رَضُوا لِأَنْفُسِهِمُ الِاسْتِكْبَارَ عَنْ عِبَادَةِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ، وَالِاسْتِنْكَافَ عَنِ الْإِخْلَاصِ لِلْعَزِيزِ الْغَفَّارِ، ثُمَّ صَرَفُوا عِبَادَتَهُمْ وَذُلَّهُمْ وَخُضُوعَهُمْ لِحَجَرٍ مِنَ الْأَحْجَارِ، أَوْ شَجَرَةٍ مِنَ الْأَشْجَارِ، أَوْ لِأَيِّ مَخْلُوقٍ لَيْسَ لَهُ إِلَّا الذُّلُّ وَالِافْتِقَارُ، فَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ كَيْفَ ذَهَبَتْ عُقُولُهُمْ عَنِ الْحَقِّ وَالْهُدَى، وَعَمِيَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ عَنِ النُّورِ وَالضِّيَاءِ، وَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ مَا أَشْنَعَهَا مِنْ حَالٍ.
text.en: How astonishing, truly astonishing, are these rabble, foolish in mind and understanding! How could they accept for themselves to be too arrogant to worship al-Wahid al-Qahhar (the One, the All-Subduing), and too proud to be sincere to al-‘Aziz al-Ghaffar (the Almighty, the Ever-Forgiving), and then direct their worship, their humility and their submission to a stone among stones, or a tree among trees, or to any created being that has nothing but lowliness and neediness? There is none worthy of worship but Allah! How their minds have strayed from the truth and guidance, and how their eyes have been blinded to the light and radiance! Glory be to Allah, how hideous a state it is!

text.ar: يَقُولُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَحۡدَهُ ٱشۡمَأَزَّتۡ قُلُوبُ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِذَا هُمۡ يَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ٤٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُوٓاْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ (٣٥) وَيَقُولُونَ أَئِنَّا لَتَارِكُوٓاْ ءَالِهَتِنَا لِشَاعِرٖ مَّجۡنُونِۭ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ٣٥ ـ ٣٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذَا ذَكَرۡتَ رَبَّكَ فِي ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَحۡدَهُۥ وَلَّوۡاْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَٰرِهِمۡ نُفُورٗا﴾ [الْإِسْرَاءِ: ٤٦].
text.en: Allah the Exalted says: ﴾And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those besides Him are mentioned, at once they rejoice﴿ [az-Zumar 39:45]. The Exalted said: ﴾Indeed, when it was said to them, “There is no god but Allah,” they were arrogant, (35) and they said: Are we to abandon our gods for a mad poet?﴿ [as-Saffat 37:35–36]. And the Exalted said: ﴾And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion﴿ [al-Isra’ 17:46].

text.ar: أَلَا مَا أَسْفَهَهَا مِنْ عُقُولٍ، نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الضَّلَالِ، وَنَسْأَلُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنْ يَرْزُقَنَا الذُّلَّ لِجَنَابِهِ، وَأَنْ يُعِيذَنَا مِنْ سَبِيلِ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ، فَهُوَ وَحْدَهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى الْمَانُّ وَالْمُعِينُ.
text.en: Indeed, how foolish such minds are! We seek refuge with Allah from misguidance, and we ask Him, Glorified is He, to grant us humility before His majesty and to protect us from the path of the arrogant. He alone, Blessed and Exalted is He, is the Bestower of favours and the Helper.

text.ar: تَقَدَّمَ تَخْرِيجُهُ.
text.en: Its sources have already been given.

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ هَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشۡكَوٰةٖ فِيهَا مِصۡبَاحٌۖ ٱلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوۡكَبٞ دُرِّيّٞ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٖ مُّبَٰرَكَةٖ زَيۡتُونَةٖ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةٖ وَلَا غَرۡبِيَّةٖ يَكَادُ زَيۡتُهَا يُضِيٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارٞۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٖۚ يَهۡدِي ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَيَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلَ لِلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٞ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٣٥].
text.en: This name occurs in the Noble Qur'an in the saying of the Exalted: ﴾Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is as a niche within which is a lamp; the lamp is in a glass; the glass is as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah strikes parables for people, and Allah is All-Knowing of all things﴿ [an-Nur 24:35].

text.ar: وَقَدْ أَفَادَ هَذَا النَّصُّ وَغَيْرُهُ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ الْوَارِدَةِ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ تَسْمِيَةَ الرَّبِّ سُبْحَانَهُ نُورًا، وَبِأَنَّ لَهُ نُورًا مُضَافًا إِلَيْهِ، وَبِأَنَّهُ نُورُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَبِأَنَّ حِجَابَهُ نُورٌ، فَهَذِهِ أَرْبَعَةُ أَنْوَاعٍ:
text.en: This text, and other texts that have come on this subject, establish that the Lord, Glorified is He, is named Light; that He has a light attributed to Him; that He is the Light of the heavens and the earth; and that His veil is light. So these are four kinds:

text.ar: الْأَوَّلُ: إِطْلَاقُهُ عَلَيْهِ سُبْحَانَهُ اسْماً.
text.en: The first: applying it to Him, Glorified is He, as a name.

text.ar: الثَّانِي: إِضَافَتُهُ إِلَيْهِ وَصْفاً، كَمَا يُضَافُ إِلَيْهِ حَيَاتُهُ وَسَمْعُهُ وَبَصَرُهُ وَسَائِرُ صِفَاتِهِ، وَتَارَةً يُضَافُ إِلَى وَجْهِهِ كَقَوْلِهِ فِي الْحَدِيثِ: «أَعُوذُ بِنُورِ وَجْهِكَ»، وَتَارَةً يُضَافُ إِلَى ذَاتِهِ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَشۡرَقَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ٦٩].
text.en: The second: attributing it to Him as an attribute, just as His life, His hearing, His sight and the rest of His attributes are attributed to Him. Sometimes it is attributed to His Face, as in his saying in the hadith: “I seek refuge in the light of Your Face,” and sometimes it is attributed to His Self, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴾And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴿ [az-Zumar 39:69].

text.ar: الثَّالِثُ: إِضَافَةُ نُورِهِ إِلَى السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ﴾.
text.en: The third: attributing His light to the heavens and the earth, as in His saying: ﴾Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴿.

text.ar: الرَّابِعُ: ذِكْرُ أَنَّ حِجَابَهُ النُّورُ، كَمَا فِي الْحَدِيثِ الصَّحِيحِ: «حِجَابُهُ النُّورُ، لَوْ كَشَفَهُ لَأَحْرَقَتْ سُبُحَاتُ وَجْهِهِ مَا انْتَهَى إِلَيْهِ بَصَرُهُ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ».
text.en: The fourth: mentioning that His veil is light, as in the authentic hadith: “His veil is light; were He to remove it, the glories of His Face would burn up everything of His creation that His sight reaches.”

text.ar: قَالَ الشَّيْخُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ سَعْدِيٍّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي كَلَامٍ جَامِعٍ لَهُ فِي بَيَانِ مَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ، وَتَوْضِيحِ مَدْلُولِهِ:
text.en: Shaykh ‘Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sa‘di (may Allah have mercy on him) said, in comprehensive words of his explaining the meaning of this name and clarifying what it indicates:

text.ar: «النُّورُ مِنْ أَوْصَافِهِ تَعَالَى عَلَى نَوْعَيْنِ:
text.en: “Light, as one of the attributes of the Exalted, is of two kinds:

text.ar: نُورٌ حِسِّيٌّ: وَهُوَ مَا اتَّصَفَ بِهِ مِنَ النُّورِ الْعَظِيمِ، الَّذِي لَوْ كَشَفَ الْحِجَابَ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ لَأَحْرَقَتْ سُبُحَاتُ وَجْهِهِ وَنُورُ جَلَالِهِ مَا انْتَهَى إِلَيْهِ بَصَرُهُ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ، وَهَذَا النُّورُ لَا يُمْكِنُ التَّعْبِيرُ عَنْهُ إِلَّا بِمِثْلِ هَذِهِ الْعِبَارَةِ النَّبَوِيَّةِ الْمُؤَدِّيَةِ لِلْمَعْنَى الْعَظِيمِ، وَأَنَّهُ لَا تُطِيقُ الْمَخْلُوقَاتُ كُلُّهَا الثُّبُوتَ لِنُورِ وَجْهِهِ لَوْ تَبَدَّى لَهَا، وَلَوْلَا أَنَّ أَهْلَ دَارِ الْقَرَارِ يُعْطِيهِمُ الرَّبُّ حَيَاةً كَامِلَةً، وَيُعِينُهُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ لَمَا تَمَكَّنُوا مِنْ رُؤْيَةِ الرَّبِّ الْعَظِيمِ، وَجَمِيعُ الْأَنْوَارِ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ الْعُلْوِيَّةِ كُلُّهَا مِنْ نُورِهِ، بَلْ نُورُ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ الَّتِي عَرْضُهَا السَّمَوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ ـ وَسَعَتُهَا لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا اللَّهُ ـ مِنْ نُورِهِ، فَنُورُ الْعَرْشِ وَالْكُرْسِيِّ وَالْجَنَّاتِ مِنْ نُورِهِ، فَضْلًا عَنْ نُورِ الشَّمْسِ وَالْقَمَرِ وَالْكَوَاكِبِ.
text.en: Sensory light: this is the immense light with which He is described, such that if He removed the veil from His Face, the glories of His Face and the light of His majesty would burn up everything of His creation that His sight reaches. This light cannot be expressed except with the like of this prophetic expression, which conveys the immense meaning that all of creation could not withstand the light of His Face if it were to appear to them. Were it not that the Lord gives the people of the Abode of Permanence a perfect life and helps them to that, they would not be able to see the Lord, the Magnificent. All the lights in the upper heavens are from His light; indeed, the light of the Gardens of Bliss, whose width is the heavens and the earth, and whose vastness none knows but Allah, is from His light. So the light of the Throne, the Footstool and the Gardens is from His light, let alone the light of the sun, the moon and the stars.

text.ar: وَالنَّوْعُ الثَّانِي: نُورُهُ الْمَعْنَوِيُّ، وَهُوَ النُّورُ الَّذِي نَوَّرَ قُلُوبَ أَنْبِيَائِهِ وَأَصْفِيَائِهِ وَأَوْلِيَائِهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ، مِنْ أَنْوَارِ مَعْرِفَتِهِ وَأَنْوَارِ مَحَبَّتِهِ، فَإِنَّ لِمَعْرِفَتِهِ فِي قُلُوبِ أَوْلِيَائِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْوَارًا بِحَسَبِ مَا عَرَفُوهُ مِنْ نُعُوتِ جَلَالِهِ، وَمَا اعْتَقَدُوهُ مِنْ صِفَاتِ جَمَالِهِ، فَكُلُّ وَصْفٍ مِنْ أَوْصَافِهِ لَهُ تَأْثِيرٌ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ، فَإِنَّ مَعْرِفَةَ الْمَوْلَى أَعْظَمُ الْمَعَارِفِ كُلِّهَا، وَالْعِلْمُ بِهِ أَجَلُّ الْعُلُومِ، وَالْعِلْمُ النَّافِعُ كُلُّهُ أَنْوَارٌ فِي الْقُلُوبِ، فَكَيْفَ بِهَذَا الْعِلْمِ الَّذِي هُوَ أَفْضَلُ الْعُلُومِ وَأَجَلُّهَا وَأَصْلُهَا وَأَسَاسُهَا.
text.en: The second kind: His spiritual light, which is the light with which He has illuminated the hearts of His prophets, His chosen ones, His allies and His angels, from the lights of knowing Him and the lights of loving Him. For knowing Him has lights in the hearts of His believing allies, according to what they know of His qualities of majesty and what they believe of His attributes of beauty. Every one of His attributes has an effect in their hearts, for knowing the Master is the greatest of all knowledge, and knowledge of Him is the most sublime of sciences. All beneficial knowledge is lights in the hearts, so how much more this knowledge, which is the best of sciences, the most sublime of them, their root and their foundation.

text.ar: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا انْضَمَّ إِلَى هَذَا نُورُ مَحَبَّتِهِ وَالْإِنَابَةِ إِلَيْهِ، فَهُنَالِكَ تَمْتَلِئُ أَقْطَارُ الْقَلْبِ وَجِهَاتُهُ مِنَ الْأَنْوَارِ الْمُتَنَوِّعَةِ وَفُنُونِ اللَّذَّاتِ الْمُتَشَابِهَةِ فِي الْحُسْنِ وَالنَّعِيمِ.
text.en: So how about when to this is joined the light of loving Him and turning to Him? Then all the regions and sides of the heart are filled with varied lights and kinds of delights, alike in beauty and bliss.

text.ar: فَمَعَانِي الْعَظَمَةِ وَالْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَالْجَلَالِ وَالْمَجْدِ تَمْلَأُ قُلُوبَهُمْ مِنْ أَنْوَارِ الْهَيْبَةِ وَالتَّعْظِيمِ وَالْإِجْلَالِ وَالتَّكْبِيرِ.
text.en: The meanings of grandeur, supreme majesty, majesty and glory fill their hearts with the lights of awe, reverence, veneration and magnification.

text.ar: وَمَعَانِي الْجَمَالِ وَالْبِرِّ وَالْإِكْرَامِ: تَمْلَأُهَا مِنْ أَنْوَارِ الْمَحَبَّةِ وَالْوُدِّ وَالشَّوْقِ.
text.en: The meanings of beauty, kindness and honouring fill them with the lights of love, affection and longing.

text.ar: وَمَعَانِي الرَّحْمَةِ وَالرَّأْفَةِ وَالْجُودِ وَاللُّطْفِ: تَمْلَأُ قُلُوبَهُمْ مِنْ أَنْوَارِ الْحُبِّ النَّامِي عَلَى الْإِحْسَانِ، وَأَنْوَارِ الشُّكْرِ وَالْحَمْدِ بِأَنْوَاعِهِ وَالثَّنَاءِ.
text.en: The meanings of mercy, compassion, munificence and gentleness fill their hearts with the lights of a love that grows from His goodness, and the lights of gratitude, praise of every kind, and extolling Him.

text.ar: وَمَعَانِي الْأُلُوهِيَّةِ: تَمْلَأُهَا مِنْ أَنْوَارِ التَّعَبُّدِ، وَضِيَاءِ التَّقَرُّبِ، وَسَنَاءِ التَّحَبُّبِ، وَأَسْرَارِ التَّوَدُّدِ، وَحُرِّيَّةِ التَّعَلُّقِ التَّامِّ بِاللَّهِ رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً، وَطَلَبًا وَإِنَابَةً، وَانْصِرَافِ الْقَلْبِ عَنْ تَعَلُّقِهِ بِالْأَغْيَارِ كُلِّهَا.
text.en: The meanings of divinity (the right to be worshipped) fill them with the lights of devotion, the radiance of drawing near, the splendour of seeking His love, the secrets of affection, the freedom of being completely attached to Allah in longing and fear, in seeking and turning to Him, and the heart's turning away from attachment to all others.

text.ar: وَمَعَانِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْإِحَاطَةِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ وَالْقُرْبِ الْخَاصِّ: تَمْلَأُ قُلُوبَهُمْ مِنْ أَنْوَارِ مُرَاقَبَتِهِ، وَتُوصِلُهُمْ إِلَى مَقَامِ الْإِحْسَانِ الَّذِي هُوَ أَعْلَى الْمَقَامَاتِ كُلِّهَا، أَنْ تَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّكَ تَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ تَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاكَ.
text.en: The meanings of knowledge, encompassing, witnessing and special nearness fill their hearts with the lights of being mindful that He watches them, and bring them to the station of excellence (ihsan), which is the highest of all stations: that you worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you.

text.ar: فَكُلُّ مَعْنًى وَنَعْتٍ مِنْ نُعُوتِ الرَّبِّ يَكْفِي فِي امْتِلَاءِ الْقَلْبِ مِنْ نُورِهِ، فَكَيْفَ إِذَا تَنَوَّعَتْ وَتَوَارَدَتْ عَلَى الْقُلُوبِ الطَّاهِرَةِ الزَّكِيَّةِ الذَّكِيَّةِ، وَهُنَا يَصْدُقُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْقُلُوبِ الْقُدْسِيَّةِ انْطِبَاقُ هَذَا الْمَثَلِ عَلَيْهَا، وَهُوَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشۡكَوٰةٖ فِيهَا مِصۡبَاحٌۖ ٱلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوۡكَبٞ دُرِّيّٞ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٖ مُّبَٰرَكَةٖ زَيۡتُونَةٖ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةٖ وَلَا غَرۡبِيَّةٖ يَكَادُ زَيۡتُهَا يُضِيٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارٞۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٖۚ يَهۡدِي ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ ...﴾ الْآيَةَ [النُّورِ: ٣٥].
text.en: Each single meaning and quality among the qualities of the Lord is enough to fill the heart with His light; so how about when they are varied and come one after another upon pure, purified and perceptive hearts? Here this parable truly applies to these holy hearts, namely His saying: ﴾The likeness of His light is as a niche within which is a lamp; the lamp is in a glass; the glass is as if it were a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills ...﴿ to the end of the verse [an-Nur 24:35].

text.ar: وَهَذَا النُّورُ الْمَضْرُوبُ هُوَ نُورُ الْإِيمَانِ بِاللَّهِ، وَبِصِفَاتِهِ وَآيَاتِهِ مَثَلُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَثَلُ هَذَا النُّورِ الَّذِي جَمَعَ جَمِيعَ الْأَوْصَافِ الَّتِي فِيهَا زِيَادَةُ النُّورِ، وَهُوَ أَعْظَمُ مَثَلٍ يَعْرِفُهُ الْعِبَادُ، وَقَدْ دَعَا ﷺ لِحُصُولِ هَذَا النُّورِ فَقَالَ: «اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ فِي قَلْبِي نُورًا، وَفِي سَمْعِي نُورًا، وَفِي بَصَرِي نُورًا، وَعَنْ يَمِينِي نُورًا، وَعَنْ شِمَالِي نُورًا، وَمِنْ فَوْقِي نُورًا، وَمِنْ تَحْتِي نُورًا، اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي نُورًا» مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ[1].
text.en: This light which is struck as a parable is the light of faith in Allah, His attributes and His signs. Its likeness in the hearts of the believers is the likeness of this light, which combines all the qualities that increase light, and it is the greatest parable known to the servants. He ﷺ supplicated for attaining this light, saying: “O Allah, place light in my heart, light in my hearing, light in my sight, light on my right, light on my left, light above me and light below me. O Allah, make me light.” Agreed upon[1].

text.ar: وَمَتَى امْتَلَأَ الْقَلْبُ مِنْ هَذَا النُّورِ فَاضَ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ، فَاسْتَنَارَ الْوَجْهُ، وَانْقَادَتِ الْجَوَارِحُ بِالطَّاعَةِ رَاغِبَةً، وَهَذَا النُّورُ الَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي الْقَلْبِ هُوَ الَّذِي يَمْنَعُ الْعَبْدَ مِنِ ارْتِكَابِ الْفَوَاحِشِ، كَمَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: «لَا يَزْنِي الزَّانِي حِينَ يَزْنِي وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ، وَلَا يَسْرِقُ السَّارِقُ حِينَ يَسْرِقُ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ، وَلَا يَشْرَبُ الْخَمْرَ حِينَ يَشْرَبُهَا وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ» مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ[2].
text.en: When the heart is filled with this light, it overflows onto the face, so the face becomes radiant, and the limbs yield in obedience, willingly. This light which is in the heart is what prevents the servant from committing indecencies, as the Prophet ﷺ said: “The fornicator does not fornicate, at the time he fornicates, while he is a believer; the thief does not steal, at the time he steals, while he is a believer; and one does not drink wine, at the time he drinks it, while he is a believer.” Agreed upon[2].

text.ar: فَأَخْبَرَ أَنَّ وُقُوعَ هَذِهِ الْكَبَائِرِ لَا يَكُونُ وَلَا يَقَعُ مَعَ وُجُودِ الْإِيمَانِ وَنُورِهِ»[3] اهـ.
text.en: So he informed us that these major sins do not take place and do not occur while faith and its light are present.”[3] End quote.

text.ar: وَبِهَذَا التَّقْرِيرِ الْوَافِي، وَالْبَيَانِ الْبَيِّنِ يَظْهَرُ مَعْنَى هَذَا الِاسْمِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَيَتَّضِحُ مَدْلُولُهُ.
text.en: With this full explanation and clear exposition, the meaning of this great name appears and what it indicates becomes clear.

text.ar: هَذَا؛ وَلَمَّا كَانَ النُّورُ مِنْ أَسْمَائِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَصِفَاتِهِ كَانَ دِينُهُ نُورًا، وَرَسُولُهُ نُورًا، وَكَلَامُهُ نُورًا، وَدَارُ كَرَامَتِهِ لِعِبَادِهِ نُورًا يَتَلَأْلَأُ، وَالنُّورُ يَتَوَقَّدُ فِي قُلُوبِ عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَيَجْرِي عَلَى أَلْسِنَتِهِمْ، وَيَظْهَرُ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ، وَيُتِمُّ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى عَلَيْهِمْ هَذَا النُّورَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، كَمَا قَالَ سُبْحَانَهُ: ﴿نُورُهُمۡ يَسۡعَىٰ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتۡمِمۡ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ﴾ [التَّحْرِيمِ: ٨].
text.en: Furthermore, since an-Nur (the Light) is among His names and attributes, Glorified is He, His religion is light, His Messenger is light, His speech is light, and the abode of His honour for His servants is light that glitters. Light is kindled in the hearts of His believing servants, runs on their tongues and appears on their faces, and He, Blessed and Exalted is He, will complete this light for them on the Day of Resurrection, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴾Their light will run ahead of them and on their right; they will say: Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are Able to do all things﴿ [at-Tahrim 66:8].

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ (٦٣١٦)، وَمُسْلِمٌ (٧٦٣) عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا فِي حَدِيثِ قِيَامِ اللَّيْلِ.
text.en: Reported by al-Bukhari (6316) and Muslim (763) from Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), in the hadith about the night prayer.

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ (٦٨١٠)، وَمُسْلِمٌ (٥٧) عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: Reported by al-Bukhari (6810) and Muslim (57) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

text.ar: «فَتْحُ الرَّحِيمِ الْمَلِكِ الْعَلاّمِ» (ص/ ٦٢ ـ ٦٥).
text.en: *Fath ar-Rahim al-Malik al-‘Allam* (pp. 62–65).

text.ar: وَلَمْ يَرِدْ هَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ اسْماً وَإِنَّمَا وَرَدَ فِعْلًا كَمَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ﴾ [الْقَصَصِ: ٧٧]، وَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَقَدۡ أَحۡسَنَ بِيٓ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَنِي مِنَ ٱلسِّجۡنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡبَدۡوِ﴾ [يُوسُفَ: ١٠٠]، وَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿قَدۡ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ رِزۡقًا﴾ [الطَّلَاقِ: ١١]، وَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقَهُۥۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينٖ﴾ [السَّجْدَةِ: ٧]، وَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحۡسَنُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقِينَ﴾ [الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: ١٤].
text.en: This name does not occur in the Qur'an as a name; rather, it occurs as a verb, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴾And do good as Allah has done good to you﴿ [al-Qasas 28:77]; His saying: ﴾And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the desert﴿ [Yusuf 12:100]; the saying of the Exalted: ﴾Allah has indeed made good provision for him﴿ [at-Talaq 65:11]; the saying of the Exalted: ﴾Who made excellent everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay﴿ [as-Sajdah 32:7]; and the saying of the Exalted: ﴾So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴿ [al-Mu’minun 23:14].

text.ar: وَجَاءَتِ السُّنَّةُ بِإِثْبَاتِ هَذَا الِاسْمِ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي ثَلَاثَةِ أَحَادِيثَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ.
text.en: The Sunnah has come affirming this name for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in three hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

text.ar: الْأَوَّلُ: حَدِيثُ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «إِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ فَاعْدِلُوا، وَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مُحْسِنٌ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ» رَوَاهُ الطَّبَرَانِيُّ، وَأَبُو نُعَيْمٍ[1].
text.en: The first: the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you judge, be just, and when you kill, do it well, for Allah is Muhsin (the Doer of Good) and loves those who do good.” Reported by at-Tabarani and Abu Nu‘aym[1].

text.ar: الثَّانِي: حَدِيثُ شَدَّادِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: حَفِظْتُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ اثْنَتَيْنِ: قَالَ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُحْسِنٌ يُحِبُّ الْإِحْسَانَ إِلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الْقِتْلَةَ، وَإِذَا ذَبَحْتُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا الذَّبْحَ، وَلْيُحِدَّ أَحَدُكُمْ شَفْرَتَهُ وَلْيُرِحْ ذَبِيحَتَهُ». رَوَاهُ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ وَغَيْرُهُ[2].
text.en: The second: the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I memorised two things from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: “Indeed, Allah is Muhsin (the Doer of Good) and loves excellent treatment toward everything. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well; let each of you sharpen his blade and give ease to the animal he slaughters.” Reported by ‘Abd ar-Razzaq and others[2].

text.ar: الثَّالِثُ: حَدِيثُ سَمُرَةَ بْنِ جُنْدُبٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مُحْسِنٌ فَأَحْسِنُوا، فَإِذَا قَتَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيُحْسِنْ مَقْتُولَهُ، وَإِذَا ذَبَحَ فَلْيُحِدَّ شَفْرَتَهُ وَلْيُرِحْ ذَبِيحَتَهُ» رَوَاهُ ابْنُ عَدِيٍّ[3].
text.en: The third: the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Muhsin (the Doer of Good), so do good. When one of you kills, let him do it well to the one he kills, and when he slaughters, let him sharpen his blade and give ease to the animal he slaughters.” Reported by Ibn ‘Adi[3].

text.ar: وَهَذِهِ الرِّوَايَاتُ تَدُلُّ بِمَجْمُوعِهَا عَلَى ثُبُوتِ هَذَا الِاسْمِ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ.
text.en: Taken together, these narrations indicate that this name is established for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَاءَ ذِكْرُ هَذَا الِاسْمِ فِي ثَنَايَا كَلَامِ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ، وَكَثُرَ التَّعْبِيدُ لِلَّهِ بِهِ[4].
text.en: This name has been mentioned in the course of the words of the people of knowledge, and naming people as servants of Allah by it has been common[4].

text.ar: قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَكَانَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ الْهَرَوِيُّ قَدْ سَمَّى أَهْلَ بَلَدِهِ بِعَامَّةِ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى، وَكَذَلِكَ أَهْلُ بَيْتِنَا غَلَبَ عَلَى أَسْمَائِهِمُ التَّعْبِيدُ لِلَّهِ: كَعَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَعَبْدِ الْغَنِيِّ وَالسَّلَامِ وَالْقَاهِرِ وَاللَّطِيفِ وَالْحَكِيمِ وَالْعَزِيزِ وَالرَّحِيمِ وَالْمُحْسِنِ...»[5]، وَذَكَرَ بَعْضَ أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى.
text.en: Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Shaykh al-Islam al-Harawi named the people of his town after most of Allah's beautiful names. Likewise in our household, names expressing servitude to Allah predominated, such as ‘Abdullah and ‘Abd ar-Rahman, ‘Abd al-Ghani, ‘Abd as-Salam, ‘Abd al-Qahir, ‘Abd al-Latif, ‘Abd al-Hakim, ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, ‘Abd ar-Rahim and ‘Abd al-Muhsin...”[5] And he mentioned some of Allah's beautiful names.

text.ar: وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَإِقْرَارُ قُلُوبِنَا بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ... وَأَنَّهُ حَكِيمٌ كَرِيمٌ مُحْسِنٌ... وَلَا أَحَدَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْهِ الْإِحْسَانُ مِنْهُ، فَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ»[6].
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “And our hearts' affirmation that Allah, other than whom there is none worthy of worship... and that He is Wise, Generous, Muhsin (the Doer of Good)... and there is none to whom doing good is more beloved than to Him; so He is Muhsin and loves those who do good.”[6]

text.ar: وَمَعْنَى اسْمِ اللَّهِ «الْمُحْسِنِ» يَرْجِعُ إِلَى الْفَضْلِ وَالْإِنْعَامِ وَالْجُودِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ وَالْمَنِّ وَالْعَطَاءِ، وَالْإِحْسَانُ وَصْفٌ لَازِمٌ لَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ، لَا يَخْلُو مَوْجُودٌ عَنْ إِحْسَانِهِ طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ بِالْإِيجَادِ وَالْإِنْعَامِ وَالْإِمْدَادِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقَهُۥۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينٖ﴾ [السَّجْدَةِ: ٧]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَصَوَّرَكُمۡ فَأَحۡسَنَ صُوَرَكُمۡۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ﴾ [التَّغَابُنِ: ٣].
text.en: The meaning of Allah's name “al-Muhsin” (the Doer of Good) goes back to bounty, bestowing favours, munificence, generosity, kindness and giving. Doing good is an attribute inseparable from Him, Glorified is He; no existing thing is ever without His goodness for the blink of an eye, through bringing it into existence, bestowing favours upon it and sustaining it. The Exalted said: ﴾Who made excellent everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay﴿ [as-Sajdah 32:7]. And the Exalted said: ﴾And He formed you and made your forms excellent, and to Him is the final destination﴿ [at-Taghabun 64:3].

text.ar: وَأَعْظَمُ الْإِحْسَانِ التَّوْفِيقُ لِهَذَا الدِّينِ وَشَرْحُ الصَّدْرِ لِلُزُومِ طَاعَةِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَالتَّثْبِيتُ عَلَى الْحَقِّ وَالْهُدَى إِلَى الْمَمَاتِ، إِلَى أَنْ يُتَوَّجَ ذَلِكَ بِأَعْظَمِ الْكَرَامَةِ وَأَجَلِّ الْإِحْسَانِ بِدُخُولِ الْجِنَانِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَرُؤْيَةِ الْكَرِيمِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْمُحْسِنِ الْمَنَّانِ، نَسْأَلُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ الْعَظِيمِ وَإِحْسَانِهِ الْجَزِيلِ.
text.en: The greatest goodness is being granted success to this religion, having one's chest opened to holding fast to obedience to the Lord of the worlds, and being kept firm upon truth and guidance until death, until all of that is crowned with the greatest honour and the most sublime goodness: entering the Gardens on the Day of Resurrection and seeing al-Karim (the Most Generous), ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful), al-Muhsin (the Doer of Good), al-Mannan (the Bestower of favours). We ask Him, Glorified is He, from His immense bounty and abundant goodness.

text.ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ يُحِبُّ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ أَنْ يَتَقَرَّبُوا إِلَيْهِ بِمُقْتَضَى مَعَانِي أَسْمَائِهِ، فَهُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ يُحِبُّ الرُّحَمَاءَ، وَهُوَ الْكَرِيمُ يُحِبُّ الْكُرَمَاءَ، مُحْسِنٌ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ، قَالَ تَعَالَى:
text.en: Moreover, Allah, Glorified is He, loves His servants to draw near to Him by acting upon what the meanings of His names require. He is ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) and loves the merciful; He is al-Karim (the Generous) and loves the generous; He is Muhsin (the Doer of Good) and loves those who do good. The Exalted said:

text.ar: ﴿وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ١٩٥]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ﴾ [الْقَصَصِ: ٧٧]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿هَلۡ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنُ﴾ [الرَّحْمَنِ: ٦٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَواْ وَّٱلَّذِينَ هُم مُّحۡسِنُونَ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ١٢٨].
text.en: ﴾And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:195], and He the Exalted said: ﴾And do good as Allah has done good to you﴿ [al-Qasas 28:77], and He the Exalted said: ﴾Is the reward for good anything but good?﴿ [ar-Rahman 55:60], and He the Exalted said: ﴾Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴿ [an-Nahl 16:128].

text.ar: وَالْإِحْسَانُ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ هُوَ أَعْلَى مَقَامَاتِ الدِّينِ وَأَرْفَعُهَا كَمَا جَاءَ ذَلِكَ فِي حَدِيثِ جِبْرِيلَ الْمَشْهُورِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَفُسِّرَ الْإِحْسَانُ فِي الْحَدِيثِ بِأَنْ يَعْبُدَ رَبَّهُ كَأَنَّهُ يَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَرَاهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ جَلَّ وَعَلَا يَرَاهُ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ، وَهَذَا إِحْسَانٌ فِي عِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ، وَهُوَ أَشْرَفُ الدِّينِ وَأَرْفَعُ مَقَامَاتِهِ كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ، وَمِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ أَيْضًا الْإِحْسَانُ إِلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ بِرًّا بِالْوَالِدَيْنِ، وَصِلَةً لِلْأَرْحَامِ، وَوَفَاءً بِالْحُقُوقِ، وَإِعَانَةً لِذَوِي الْحَاجَاتِ، وَكَفَّ الْأَذَى عَنِ النَّاسِ، وَالِاجْتِهَادَ فِي إِيصَالِ الْخَيْرِ لَهُمْ، إِلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ لِعِبَادِ اللَّهِ.
text.en: Ihsan (excellence and doing good) on the part of the servant is the highest and loftiest station of the religion, as came in the well-known hadith of Jibreel (peace be upon him). In that hadith, ihsan is explained as worshipping one's Lord as though one sees Him, and if one does not see Him, then Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, sees him, and nothing of him is hidden from Him. This is ihsan in the worship of Allah, and it is the noblest part of the religion and its highest station, as mentioned above. Also part of ihsan is doing good to Allah's servants: being dutiful to parents, keeping the ties of kinship, fulfilling rights, helping those in need, holding back harm from people, and striving to bring good to them, along with other ways of doing good to Allah's servants.

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَعَدَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ بِالثَّوَابِ الْعَظِيمِ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿هَلۡ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنُ﴾، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٞۖ﴾ [يُونُسَ: ٢٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ١٢٠].
text.en: Allah has promised a great reward for this. He the Exalted said: ﴾Is the reward for good anything but good?﴿, and He the Exalted said: ﴾For those who have done good is the best reward, and more﴿ [Yunus 10:26], and He the Exalted said: ﴾Indeed, Allah does not let the reward of the doers of good be lost﴿ [at-Tawbah 9:120].

text.ar: وَمِنْ ثِمَارِ الْإِحْسَانِ الْعَظِيمَةِ فِي الدُّنْيَا انْشِرَاحُ صَدْرِ الْمُحْسِنِ وَطِيبُ نَفْسِهِ وَطُمَأْنِينَةُ قَلْبِهِ، وَلِذَا يَقُولُ الْعَلَّامَةُ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ فِي كَلَامٍ عَظِيمٍ لَهُ عَنْ أَسْبَابِ شَرْحِ الصَّدْرِ، قَالَ: «وَمِنْهَا: الْإِحْسَانُ إِلَى الْخَلْقِ، وَنَفْعُهُمْ بِمَا يُمْكِنُهُ مِنَ الْمَالِ وَالْجَاهِ، وَالنَّفْعُ بِالْبَدَنِ وَأَنْوَاعِ الْإِحْسَانِ، فَإِنَّ الْكَرِيمَ الْمُحْسِنَ أَشْرَحُ النَّاسِ صَدْرًا، وَأَطْيَبُهُمْ نَفْسًا، وَأَنْعَمُهُمْ قَلْبًا، وَالْبَخِيلُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ فِيهِ إِحْسَانٌ أَضْيَقُ النَّاسِ صَدْرًا، وَأَنْكَدُهُمْ عَيْشًا، وَأَعْظَمُهُمْ هَمًّا وَغَمًّا.
text.en: Among the great fruits of ihsan in this world are the openness of the chest of the one who does good, the goodness of his soul and the tranquillity of his heart. That is why the great scholar Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him), in a magnificent passage of his on the causes of the chest's expansion, said: “Among them is doing good to the creation and benefiting them with whatever one can of wealth and standing, benefiting them with one's body, and all kinds of good. For the generous one who does good is the most open-chested of people, the most at ease in soul and the most blissful in heart, while the miser who has no goodness in him is the most constricted of people in chest, the most wretched in life, and the greatest in worry and grief.

text.ar: وَقَدْ ضَرَبَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي «الصَّحِيحِ»[7] مَثَلًا لِلْبَخِيلِ وَالْمُتَصَدِّقِ كَمَثَلِ رَجُلَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا جُنَّتَانِ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ، كُلَّمَا هَمَّ الْمُتَصَدِّقُ بِصَدَقَةٍ اتَّسَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَانْبَسَطَتْ، حَتَّى يَجُرَّ ثِيَابَهُ وَيُعْفِيَ أَثَرَهُ، وَكُلَّمَا هَمَّ الْبَخِيلُ بِالصَّدَقَةِ لَزِمَتْ كُلُّ حَلْقَةٍ مَكَانَهَا، وَلَمْ تَتَّسِعْ عَلَيْهِ، فَهَذَا مَثَلُ انْشِرَاحِ صَدْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ الْمُتَصَدِّقِ وَانْفِسَاحِ قَلْبِهِ، وَمَثَلُ ضِيقِ صَدْرِ الْبَخِيلِ وَانْحِصَارِ قَلْبِهِ»[8].
text.en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in *as-Sahih*[7], gave a parable of the miser and the one who gives charity: they are like two men wearing two coats of iron armour. Whenever the one who gives charity intends to give, it widens and spreads out over him until it trails over his garments and wipes away his footprints; and whenever the miser intends to give charity, every ring clings to its place and it does not widen for him. This is the likeness of the expansion of the chest of the believer who gives charity and the spaciousness of his heart, and the likeness of the constriction of the miser's chest and the confinement of his heart.”[8]

text.ar: وَأَمَّا ثَوَابُ الْإِحْسَانِ فِي الْآخِرَةِ فَكُلُّ مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ الْأَنْفُسُ وَتَلَذُّهُ الْأَعْيُنُ يَنَالُهُ الْمُحْسِنُونَ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ﴾ [الزُّمَرِ: ٣٤].
text.en: As for the reward of ihsan in the Hereafter, everything that souls desire and eyes delight in will be attained by the doers of good. He the Exalted said: ﴾They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good﴿ [az-Zumar 39:34].

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَمَعَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ بَيْنَ الثَّوَابَيْنِ الْمُعَجَّلِ وَالْمُؤَجَّلِ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَـَٔاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَحُسۡنَ ثَوَابِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ﴾ [آلِ عِمْرَانَ: ١٤٨].
text.en: Allah has combined for them both rewards, the immediate and the deferred, in His saying: ﴾So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the doers of good﴿ [Al ‘Imran 3:148].

text.ar: جَعَلَنَا اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ بِمَنِّهِ وَكَرَمِهِ.
text.en: May Allah make us among them, by His favour and generosity.

text.ar:
«الْأَوْسَطُ» (٥٧٣٥)، وَ«أَخْبَارُ أَصْبَهَانَ» (٢/ ١١٣) مِنْ طُرُقٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ بِلَالٍ، ثَنَا عِمْرَانُ الْقَطَّانُ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
قَالَ الْحَافِظُ الْهَيْثَمِيُّ فِي «مَجْمَعِ الزَّوَائِدِ»: «رِجَالُهُ ثِقَاتٌ».
وَقَالَ الْعَلاّمَةُ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ فِي «السِّلْسِلَةِ الصَّحِيحَةِ» (١/ ٧٦١): «إِسْنَادُهُ جَيِّدٌ».
text.en:
*al-Awsat* (5735) and *Akhbar Asbahan* (2/113), via several routes from Muhammad ibn Bilal: ‘Imran al-Qattan narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him).
Al-Hafiz al-Haythami said in *Majma‘ az-Zawa’id*: “Its narrators are trustworthy.”
And the great scholar al-Albani said in *as-Silsilah as-Sahihah* (1/761): “Its chain is good.”

text.ar:
«مُصَنَّفُ عَبْدِ الرَّزَّاقِ» (٤/ ٤٩٢) ـ وَمِنْ طَرِيقِهِ الطَّبَرَانِيُّ فِي «الْكَبِيرِ» (٧/ ٢٧٥) ـ، عَنْ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَشْعَثِ الصَّنْعَانِيِّ، عَنْ شَدَّادِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ، قَالَ (فَذَكَرَهُ).
وَرِجَالُ إِسْنَادِهِ ثِقَاتٌ رِجَالُ مُسْلِمٍ. أَبُو الْأَشْعَثِ اسْمُهُ شَرَاحِيلُ بْنُ آدَةَ، وَأَبُو قِلَابَةَ هُوَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ زَيْدٍ الْجَرْمِيُّ.
وَرَوَاهُ إِسْمَاعِيلُ الْقَاضِي فِي «حَدِيثِ أَيُّوبَ السَّخْتِيَانِيِّ» (٣٦) عَنْ يَحْيَى الْحِمَّانِيِّ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، بِهِ، مِثْلَهُ.
وَالْحِمَّانِيُّ مُخْتَلَفٌ فِيهِ، وَقَدِ اتُّهِمَ بِسَرِقَةِ الْحَدِيثِ.
وَالْحَدِيثُ رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ (رَقْمُ: ١٩٥٥) مِنْ طَرِيقِ خَالِدٍ الْحَذَّاءِ، عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، بِإِسْنَادِهِ، بِلَفْظِ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الْإِحْسَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ، فَإِذَا قَتَلْتُمْ...» الْحَدِيثَ.
text.en:
*Musannaf ‘Abd ar-Razzaq* (4/492) – and via him at-Tabarani in *al-Kabir* (7/275) – from Ma‘mar, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu al-Ash‘ath as-San‘ani, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said (and he mentioned it).
The narrators of its chain are trustworthy, narrators used by Muslim. Abu al-Ash‘ath's name is Shurahbil ibn Adah, and Abu Qilabah is ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Jarmi.
Isma‘il al-Qadi narrated it in *Hadith Ayyub as-Sakhtiyani* (36) from Yahya al-Himmani: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, with this chain, in the same way.
Al-Himmani is disputed, and he was accused of stealing hadith.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim (no. 1955) via Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from Abu Qilabah, with his chain, in the wording: “Allah has prescribed excellence in everything, so when you kill...” to the end of the hadith.

text.ar:
فِي «الْكَامِلِ» (٦/ ٢٤١٩) مِنْ طَرِيقِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ رُشَيْدٍ، ثَنَا مُجَّاعَةُ بْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنْ سَمُرَةَ، فَذَكَرَهُ.
وَإِسْنَادُهُ ضَعِيفٌ مُسَلْسَلٌ بِالْعِلَلِ؛ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ رُشَيْدٍ لَيْسَ بِالْقَوِيِّ وَفِيهِ جَهَالَةٌ، وَمُجَّاعَةُ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ مُخْتَلَفٌ فِيهِ وَضَعَّفَهُ الدَّارَقُطْنِيُّ وَغَيْرُهُ، وَالْحَسَنُ مُخْتَلَفٌ فِي سَمَاعِهِ مِنْ سَمُرَةَ.
وَقَالَ الْمُنَاوِيُّ فِي «التَّيْسِيرِ» (١/ ٩٠): «إِسْنَادُهُ ضَعِيفٌ».
لَكِنَّ الْحَدِيثَ صَحِيحٌ يَشْهَدُ لَهُ الْحَدِيثَانِ قَبْلَهُ.
text.en:
In *al-Kamil* (6/2419) via ‘Abdullah ibn Rashid: Mujja‘ah ibn az-Zubayr Abu ‘Ubaydah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, and he mentioned it.
Its chain is weak and riddled with defects: ‘Abdullah ibn Rashid is not strong and there is some obscurity about him; Mujja‘ah ibn az-Zubayr is disputed, and ad-Daraqutni and others declared him weak; and whether al-Hasan heard from Samurah is disputed.
Al-Munawi said in *at-Taysir* (1/90): “Its chain is weak.”
But the hadith is authentic, supported by the two hadiths before it.

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَمَعْتُ فِي رِسَالَةٍ لِي مُفْرَدَةٍ حَوْلَ إِثْبَاتِ هَذَا الِاسْمِ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ مَنْ سُمِّيَ مُعَبَّدًا لِلْمُحْسِنِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ إِلَى نِهَايَةِ الْقَرْنِ التَّاسِعِ، فَبَلَغَ عَدَدُهُمْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ خَمْسِينَ شَخْصاً.
text.en: In a separate treatise of mine on affirming this name for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, I have gathered those, scholars and others, who were named as servants of al-Muhsin (‘Abd al-Muhsin) up to the end of the ninth century, and they numbered more than fifty people.

text.ar: «مَجْمُوعُ الْفَتَاوَى» (١/ ٣٧٩).
text.en: *Majmu‘ al-Fatawa* (1/379).

text.ar: «طَرِيقُ الْهِجْرَتَيْنِ» (ص/ ١٢٠).
text.en: *Tariq al-Hijratayn* (p. 120).

text.ar: «صَحِيحُ الْبُخَارِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ١٤٤٣)، وَ«صَحِيحُ مُسْلِمٍ» (رَقْمُ: ١٠٢١) مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: *Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 1443) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 1021), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

text.ar: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ ثَابِتٌ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي سُنَّةِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، رَوَى الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ فِي «الْمُسْنَدِ» وَالْبُخَارِيُّ فِي «الْأَدَبِ الْمُفْرَدِ» وَابْنُ أَبِي عَاصِمٍ فِي «السُّنَّةِ» وَالْحَاكِمُ فِي «الْمُسْتَدْرَكِ» وَغَيْرُهُمْ عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: «بَلَغَنِي حَدِيثٌ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَمِعَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَاشْتَرَيْتُ بَعِيرًا، ثُمَّ شَدَدْتُ عَلَيْهِ رَحْلِي، فَسِرْتُ إِلَيْهِ شَهْرًا حَتَّى قَدِمْتُ عَلَيْهِ الشَّامَ، فَإِذَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُنَيْسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَقَالَ لِلْبَوَّابِ: قُلْ لَهُ: جَابِرٌ عَلَى الْبَابِ، فَقَالَ: ابْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ؟ قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، فَخَرَجَ يَطَأُ ثَوْبَهُ، فَاعْتَنَقَنِي وَاعْتَنَقْتُهُ، فَقُلْتُ: حَدِيثًا بَلَغَنِي عَنْكَ أَنَّكَ سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْقِصَاصِ، فَخَشِيتُ أَنْ تَمُوتَ أَوْ أَمُوتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ أَسْمَعَهُ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: يُحْشَرُ النَّاسُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ـ أَوْ قَالَ: الْعِبَادُ ـ عُرَاةً غُرْلًا بُهْمًا، قَالَ: قُلْنَا: وَمَا بُهْمًا؟ قَالَ: لَيْسَ مَعَهُمْ شَيْءٌ، ثُمَّ يُنَادِيهِمْ بِصَوْتٍ يَسْمَعُهُ مَنْ بَعُدَ كَمَا يَسْمَعُهُ مَنْ قَرُبَ: أَنَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَا الدَّيَّانُ، وَلَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ النَّارَ وَلَهُ عِنْدَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَقٌّ حَتَّى أُقِصَّهُ مِنْهُ، وَلَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلِأَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ عِنْدَهُ حَقٌّ حَتَّى أُقِصَّهُ مِنْهُ، حَتَّى اللَّطْمَةُ، قَالَ: قُلْنَا: كَيْفَ وَإِنَّمَا نَأْتِي اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عُرَاةً غُرْلًا بُهْمًا؟ قَالَ: بِالْحَسَنَاتِ وَالسَّيِّئَاتِ»، زَادَ الْحَاكِمُ: «وَتَلَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: ﴿ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡۚ لَا ظُلۡمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۚ﴾»[1].
text.en: It is a name established for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ. Imam Ahmad narrated in *al-Musnad*, al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad*, Ibn Abi ‘Asim in *as-Sunnah*, al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak* and others, from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “A hadith reached me from a man who had heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I bought a camel, fastened my saddle on it, and travelled to him for a month until I reached him in Sham. There was ‘Abdullah ibn Unays (may Allah be pleased with him). I said to the doorkeeper: Tell him: Jabir is at the door. He said: The son of ‘Abdullah? I said: Yes. So he came out, treading on his garment, and he embraced me and I embraced him. I said: A hadith has reached me from you, that you heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about retribution, and I feared that you would die, or I would die, before I heard it. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection – or he said: the servants – naked, uncircumcised and buhm. We said: And what is buhm? He said: They have nothing with them. Then He will call out to them with a voice heard by those far away just as it is heard by those nearby: I am the King, I am ad-Dayyan (the Requiter). It is not fitting for anyone of the people of the Fire to enter the Fire while one of the people of Paradise has a right against him, until I settle it for him from him; and it is not fitting for anyone of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise while one of the people of the Fire has a right against him, until I settle it from him, even a slap. We said: How, when we will come to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, naked, uncircumcised and buhm? He said: With good deeds and bad deeds.” Al-Hakim added: “And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴾This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today﴿.”[1]

text.ar: وَالدَّيَّانُ: مَعْنَاهُ الْمُجَازِي الْمُحَاسِبُ، وَاللَّهُ جَلَّ وَعَلَا يَجْمَعُ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عُرَاةً لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ ثِيَابٌ، حُفَاةً بِلَا نِعَالٍ، غُرْلًا أَيْ: غَيْرَ مُخْتَتَنِينَ، بُهْمًا لَيْسَ مَعَهُمْ شَيْءٌ مِنْ مَتَاعِ الدُّنْيَا، ثُمَّ يُجَازِيهِمْ وَيُحَاسِبُهُمْ عَلَى مَا قَدَّمُوا فِي حَيَاتِهِمُ الدُّنْيَا مِنْ أَعْمَالٍ، إِنْ خَيْرًا فَخَيْرٌ، وَإِنْ شَرًّا فَشَرٌّ.
text.en: ad-Dayyan (the Requiter) means the One who recompenses and holds to account. Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, will gather the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection naked, with no clothes on them, barefoot without sandals, ghurl, that is, uncircumcised, and buhm, having nothing of the goods of this world with them. Then He will recompense them and hold them to account for the deeds they sent ahead in their worldly life: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

text.ar: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡۚ لَا ظُلۡمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ١٧].
text.en: Allah the Exalted said: ﴾This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today! Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴿ [Ghafir 40:17].

text.ar: وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَنَضَعُ ٱلۡمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلۡقِسۡطَ لِيَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسٞ شَيۡـٔٗاۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةٖ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلٍ أَتَيۡنَا بِهَاۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ﴾ [الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: ٤٧].
text.en: And He the Exalted said: ﴾And We will set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴿ [al-Anbiya’ 21:47].

text.ar: وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيۡرٗا يَرَهُۥ (٧) وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٖ شَرّٗا يَرَهُۥ﴾ [الزَّلْزَلَةِ: ٧ ـ ٨].
text.en: And He the Exalted said: ﴾So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴿ [az-Zalzalah 99:7–8].

text.ar: وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٖۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةٗ يُضَٰعِفۡهَا وَيُؤۡتِ مِن لَّدُنۡهُ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ٤٠].
text.en: And He the Exalted said: ﴾Indeed, Allah does not wrong even an atom's weight; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴿ [an-Nisa’ 4:40].

text.ar: وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَوۡمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ مِنۡ خَيۡرٖ مُّحۡضَرٗا وَمَا عَمِلَتۡ مِن سُوٓءٖ تَوَدُّ لَوۡ أَنَّ بَيۡنَهَا وَبَيۡنَهُۥٓ أَمَدَۢا بَعِيدٗاۗ وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسَهُۥۗ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ﴾ [آلِ عِمْرَانَ: ٣٠].
text.en: And He the Exalted said: ﴾On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good brought forward, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that there were a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to His servants﴿ [Al ‘Imran 3:30].

text.ar: وَيَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ يُسَمَّى يَوْمَ الدِّينِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَوْمُ الْجَزَاءِ وَالْحِسَابِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿مَٰلِكِ يَوۡمِ ٱلدِّينِ﴾، أَيْ: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الْجَزَاءِ عَلَى الْأَعْمَالِ وَالْحِسَابِ بِهَا، يَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿يَوۡمَئِذٖ يُوَفِّيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ ٱلۡحَقَّ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٢٥]، أَيْ: حِسَابَهُمْ، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡۚ﴾ [غَافِرٍ: ١٧]، وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ﴾ [الْجَاثِيَةِ: ٢٨]، وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿أَءِنَّا لَمَدِينُونَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ٥٣]، أَيْ: مَجْزِيُّونَ مُحَاسَبُونَ.
text.en: The Day of Resurrection is called Yawm ad-Din (the Day of Recompense), because it is the day of recompense and reckoning. Allah the Exalted said: ﴾Master of the Day of Recompense﴿, that is, the Owner of the Day of recompense for deeds and reckoning for them. This is shown by His saying: ﴾On that Day Allah will pay them in full their true recompense﴿ [an-Nur 24:25], that is, their reckoning; His saying: ﴾This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned﴿ [Ghafir 40:17]; His saying: ﴾Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴿ [al-Jathiyah 45:28]; and His saying: ﴾Will we indeed be recompensed?﴿ [as-Saffat 37:53], that is, recompensed and held to account.

text.ar: وَإِذَا عَرَفَ الْعَاقِلُ أَنَّ الرَّبَّ سُبْحَانَهُ دَيَّانٌ، وَأَنَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَوْمُ جَزَاءٍ وَحِسَابٍ، وَأَنَّهُ سَيَلْقَى اللَّهَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ لَا مَحَالَةَ، وَأَنَّهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ سَيَجِدُ أَعْمَالَهُ كُلَّهَا مُحْضَرَةً خَيْرَهَا وَشَرَّهَا، حَسَنَهَا وَسَيِّئَهَا؛ فَإِنَّهُ سَيَحْسُبُ لِذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ حِسَابَهُ وَيُعِدُّ لَهُ عُدَّتَهُ.
text.en: When a person of sound mind knows that the Lord, Glorified is He, is ad-Dayyan (the Requiter), that the Day of Resurrection is a day of recompense and reckoning, that he will meet Allah on that Day without a doubt, and that on that Day he will find all his deeds brought forward, their good and their evil, their fair and their foul, then he will take that Day into account and make ready for it.

text.ar: رَوَى الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ فِي «الزُّهْدِ»[2] عَنْ أَبِي قِلَابَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: «الْبِرُّ لَا يَبْلَى، وَالْإِثْمُ لَا يُنْسَى، وَالدَّيَّانُ لَا يَنَامُ، فَكُنْ كَمَا شِئْتَ، كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ».
text.en: Imam Ahmad narrated in *az-Zuhd*[2] from Abu Qilabah, who said: Abu ad-Darda’ (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Righteousness does not wear out, sin is not forgotten, and ad-Dayyan (the Requiter) does not sleep. So be as you wish: as you deal, so you will be repaid.”

text.ar: فَالْكَيِّسُ مَنْ دَانَ نَفْسَهُ وَحَاسَبَهَا مَا دَامَ فِي دَارِ الْمُهْلَةِ وَالْعَمَلِ، وَالْعَاجِزُ مَنْ أَهْمَلَهَا سَادِرَةً فِي غَيِّهَا وَأَتْبَعَهَا هَوَاهَا إِلَى أَنْ يَفْجَأَهُ النَّدَمُ.
text.en: The wise one is he who brings himself to account and reckons with it while he is still in the abode of respite and action, and the helpless one is he who neglects it, leaving it to persist heedlessly in its error, and lets it follow its desires until regret takes him by surprise.

text.ar: رَوَى ابْنُ أَبِي الدُّنْيَا فِي كِتَابِهِ «مُحَاسَبَةِ النَّفْسِ»[3] عَنِ الْخَلِيفَةِ الرَّاشِدِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «حَاسِبُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُحَاسَبُوا، وَزِنُوا أَعْمَالَكُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُوزَنُوا، فَإِنَّهُ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْحِسَابِ غَدًا أَنْ تُحَاسِبُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ، وَتَزَيَّنُوا لِلْعَرْضِ الْأَكْبَرِ، يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ».
text.en: Ibn Abi ad-Dunya narrated in his book *Muhasabat an-Nafs*[3] from the Rightly-Guided Caliph ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: “Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, and weigh your deeds before you are weighed; for it will be easier for you in the reckoning tomorrow that you take account of yourselves today. And adorn yourselves for the Greatest Presentation: on that Day you will be presented, and nothing hidden of you will remain hidden.”

text.ar: أَوَلَا يَذْكُرُ الظَّالِمُ الْغَشُومُ هَوْلَ الْمُطَّلَعِ وَشِدَّةَ الْحِسَابِ وَقَوْلَ الدَّيَّانِ سُبْحَانَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ: «لَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ النَّارَ وَلَهُ عِنْدَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَقٌّ حَتَّى أُقِصَّهُ مِنْهُ، وَلَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلِأَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ عِنْدَهُ حَقٌّ حَتَّى أُقِصَّهُ مِنْهُ حَتَّى اللَّطْمَةُ».
text.en: Does the tyrannical oppressor not remember the terror of what lies ahead, the severity of the reckoning, and the words of ad-Dayyan (the Requiter), Glorified is He, on that Day: “It is not fitting for anyone of the people of the Fire to enter the Fire while one of the people of Paradise has a right against him, until I settle it from him; and it is not fitting for anyone of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise while one of the people of the Fire has a right against him, until I settle it from him, even a slap”?

text.ar: وَلَمَّا سَأَلَ الصَّحَابَةُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ كَيْفَ يَكُونُ الْحِسَابُ حِينَئِذٍ وَالنَّاسُ إِنَّمَا يَقْدَمُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عُرَاةً غُرْلًا بُهْمًا قَالَ: «بِالْحَسَنَاتِ وَالسَّيِّئَاتِ»، أَيْ: أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ يَأْخُذُ لِلْمَظْلُومِ مِنْ حَسَنَاتِ ظَالِمِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهُ حَسَنَاتٌ أُخِذَ مِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ الْمَظْلُومِ فَطُرِحَتْ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ طُرِحَ فِي النَّارِ، كَمَا فِي حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: «أَتَدْرُونَ مَا الْمُفْلِسُ؟ قَالُوا: الْمُفْلِسُ فِينَا مَنْ لَا دِرْهَمَ لَهُ وَلَا مَتَاعَ، فَقَالَ: إِنَّ الْمُفْلِسَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ بِصَلَاةٍ وَصِيَامٍ وَزَكَاةٍ، وَيَأْتِي قَدْ شَتَمَ هَذَا، وَقَذَفَ هَذَا، وَأَكَلَ مَالَ هَذَا، وَسَفَكَ دَمَ هَذَا، وَضَرَبَ هَذَا، فَيُعْطَى هَذَا مِنْ حَسَنَاتِهِ، وَهَذَا مِنْ حَسَنَاتِهِ، فَإِنْ فَنِيَتْ حَسَنَاتُهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْضَى مَا عَلَيْهِ، أُخِذَ مِنْ خَطَايَاهُمْ فَطُرِحَتْ عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ طُرِحَ فِي النَّارِ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[4].
text.en: When the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) asked how the reckoning would be then, when people will come to Allah on the Day of Resurrection naked, uncircumcised and buhm, he said: “With good deeds and bad deeds”. That is, He, Glorified is He, will take for the wronged person from the good deeds of the one who wronged him, and if he has no good deeds, He will take from the bad deeds of the wronged person and they will be thrown upon him, and then he will be thrown into the Fire. This is as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do you know who the bankrupt one is? They said: The bankrupt among us is the one who has neither dirham nor goods. He said: The bankrupt one of my Ummah is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and zakah, but he comes having insulted this one, slandered that one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of that one and struck this one. So this one is given some of his good deeds, and that one some of his good deeds, and if his good deeds run out before what he owes is settled, some of their sins are taken and thrown upon him, then he is thrown into the Fire.” Narrated by Muslim[4].

text.ar: وَرَوَى أَيْضًا مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: «لَتُؤَدُّنَّ الْحُقُوقَ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، حَتَّى يُقَادَ لِلشَّاةِ الْجَلْحَاءِ مِنَ الشَّاةِ الْقَرْنَاءِ»[5].
text.en: He also narrated, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Rights will surely be paid to those entitled to them on the Day of Resurrection, so much so that the hornless sheep will be avenged against the horned sheep.”[5]

text.ar: وَفِي هَذَا الْمَعْنَى يَقُولُ الشَّاعِرُ:
text.en: On this meaning the poet says:

text.ar: أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ الظُّلْمَ لُؤْمٌ ... وَمَا زَالَ الْمُسِيءُ هُوَ الظَّلُومُ
text.en: By Allah, injustice is indeed a vile thing ... and the evildoer is ever the true oppressor

text.ar: إِلَى دَيَّانِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ نَمْضِي ... وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ تَجْتَمِعُ الْخُصُومُ
text.en: To the Requiter of the Day of Recompense we are heading ... and with Allah all disputants will gather

text.ar: وَمِنْ كَمَالِ مُجَازَاةِ الرَّبِّ سُبْحَانَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ أَنَّهُ يَجِيءُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ لِلْفَصْلِ بَيْنَ الْعِبَادِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلۡمَلَكُ صَفّٗا صَفّٗا (٢٢) وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذٖ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ (٢٣) يَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي قَدَّمۡتُ لِحَيَاتِي﴾ [الْفَجْرِ: ٢٢ ـ ٢٤].
text.en: Part of the perfection of the Lord's recompense, Glorified is He, on that Day is that He Himself will come on that Day to judge between the servants. Allah the Exalted said: ﴾And your Lord comes, with the angels, rank upon rank (22) and Hell is brought near that Day. On that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance avail him? (23) He will say: If only I had sent ahead something for my life﴿ [al-Fajr 89:22–24].

text.ar: فَتَفَكَّرْ أَيُّهَا الْعَبْدُ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَتَذَكَّرْ أَنَّ الرَّبَّ سُبْحَانَهُ دَيَّانٌ، وَأَنَّ الْحُقُوقَ سَتُؤَدَّى فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا، وَأَنْ مَا ثَمَّ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ إِلَّا الْحَسَنَاتُ وَالسَّيِّئَاتُ.
text.en: So reflect, O servant, on this tremendous Day, and remember that the Lord, Glorified is He, is ad-Dayyan (the Requiter), that rights will be paid on that Day to those entitled to them, and that on that Day there will be nothing there but good deeds and bad deeds.

text.ar: تَذَكَّرْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي اللَّهَ فَرْدًا ... وَقَدْ نُصِبَتْ مَوَازِينُ الْقَضَاءِ
text.en: Remember the Day you will come to Allah alone ... when the scales of judgement have been set up

text.ar: وَهُتِكَتِ السُّتُورُ عَنِ الْمَعَاصِي ... وَجَاءَ الذَّنْبُ مُنْكَشِفَ الْغِطَاءِ
text.en: And the veils over sins have been torn away ... and each sin comes with its cover laid bare

text.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَجِرْنَا مِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِ النَّدَامَةِ، وَمِنَ الْفَضِيحَةِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ.
text.en: O Allah, protect us from the disgrace of the Day of Regret and from exposure on the Day of Resurrection, the Day when neither wealth nor sons will benefit, except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart.

text.ar:
رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ (٣/ ٤٩٥)، وَالْبُخَارِيُّ فِي «الْأَدَبِ الْمُفْرَدِ» (٩٧٠)، وَابْنُ أَبِي عَاصِمٍ فِي «السُّنَّةِ» (٥١٤)، وَالْحَاكِمُ (٢/ ٤٣٧) وَغَيْرُهُمْ مِنْ طَرِيقِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْوَاحِدِ الْمَكِّيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ابْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَقِيلٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ (فَذَكَرَهُ).
وَإِسْنَادُهُ حَسَنٌ؛ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَقِيلٍ مُخْتَلَفٌ فِيهِ لَكِنَّهُ حَسَنُ الْحَدِيثِ، وَالْقَاسِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْوَاحِدِ الْمَكِّيُّ رَوَى عَنْهُ جَمْعٌ، وَذَكَرَهُ ابْنُ حِبَّانَ فِي «الثِّقَاتِ» (٧/ ٣٣٧) وَلَمْ يُجْرَحْ.
وَعَزَاهُ الْحَافِظُ الْمُنْذِرِيُّ فِي «التَّرْغِيبِ وَالتَّرْهِيبِ» إِلَى أَحْمَدَ وَحَسَّنَ إِسْنَادَهُ، وَكَذَا حَسَّنَهُ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ فِي «صَحِيحِ التَّرْغِيبِ وَالتَّرْهِيبِ» (٣٦٠٨)، وَفِي «ظِلَالِ الْجَنَّةِ فِي تَخْرِيجِ السُّنَّةِ لِابْنِ أَبِي عَاصِمٍ».
وَلَهُ إِسْنَادٌ آخَرُ أَخْرَجَهُ الطَّبَرَانِيُّ فِي «مُسْنَدِ الشَّامِيِّينَ» (١٥٦) مِنْ طَرِيقِ الْحَجَّاجِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ ابْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، بِهِ، مُطَوَّلاً.
قَالَ الْحَافِظُ فِي «الْفَتْحِ» (١/ ١٧٤): «وَإِسْنَادُهُ صَالِحٌ».
text.en:
Narrated by Ahmad (3/495), al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad* (970), Ibn Abi ‘Asim in *as-Sunnah* (514), al-Hakim (2/437) and others, via al-Qasim ibn ‘Abd al-Wahid al-Makki, from ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Aqil, that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah say (and he mentioned it).
Its chain is hasan (good): ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Aqil is disputed, but his hadith is hasan; and al-Qasim ibn ‘Abd al-Wahid al-Makki had a number of people narrate from him, Ibn Hibban mentioned him in *ath-Thiqat* (7/337), and he was not criticised.
Al-Hafiz al-Mundhiri attributed it in *at-Targhib wat-Tarhib* to Ahmad and declared its chain hasan, and al-Albani likewise declared it hasan in *Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib* (3608) and in *Zilal al-Jannah fi Takhrij as-Sunnah li-Ibn Abi ‘Asim*.
It has another chain, which at-Tabarani recorded in *Musnad ash-Shamiyyin* (156) via al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, with it, at length.
Al-Hafiz said in *al-Fath* (1/174): “Its chain is acceptable.”

text.ar: (رَقْمُ: ٧٦٤) وَرِجَالُهُ ثِقَاتٌ، وَفِيهِ انْقِطَاعٌ.
text.en: (no. 764). Its narrators are trustworthy, but there is a break in its chain.
*Sahih Muslim* (no. 2582).

title.en: al-Muqaddim, al-Mu’akhkhir (the One who Brings Forward, the One who Puts Back)

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ هَذَانِ الِاسْمَانِ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَحَادِيثِ الثَّابِتَةِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ مِنْهَا:
text.en: These two names have come in a number of authentic hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ, among them:

text.ar: حَدِيثُ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَدْعُو بِهَذَا الدُّعَاءِ: «اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي خَطِيئَتِي وَجَهْلِي، وَإِسْرَافِي فِي أَمْرِي، وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي، اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي جِدِّي وَهَزْلِي، وَخَطَئِي وَعَمْدِي، وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ عِنْدِي، اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ، وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ، وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي، أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ» مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ[1].
text.en: The hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, that he used to supplicate with this supplication: “O Allah, forgive me my sin and my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and what You know better than I. O Allah, forgive me my seriousness and my jest, my mistakes and my deliberate acts, and all of that is in me. O Allah, forgive me what I have sent before and what I have left behind, what I have done in secret and what I have done openly, and what You know better than I. You are al-Muqaddim (the One who brings forward) and You are al-Mu’akhkhir (the One who puts back), and You have power over all things.” Agreed upon[1].

text.ar: وَحَدِيثُ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فِي وَصْفِهِ لِصَلَاةِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَفِيهِ يَقُولُ: «ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مِنْ آخِرِ مَا يَقُولُ بَيْنَ التَّشَهُّدِ وَالتَّسْلِيمِ: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ، وَمَا أَسْرَفْتُ وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي، أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[2].
text.en: And the hadith of ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) describing the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, in which he says: “Then among the last things he would say between the tashahhud and the taslim was: O Allah, forgive me what I have sent before and what I have left behind, what I have done in secret and what I have done openly, what I have done in excess, and what You know better than I. You are al-Muqaddim (the One who brings forward) and You are al-Mu’akhkhir (the One who puts back); there is no god worthy of worship but You.” Narrated by Muslim[2].

text.ar: وَحَدِيثُ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِذَا قَامَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ يَتَهَجَّدُ قَالَ: «اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ قَيِّمُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ لَكَ مُلْكُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ نُورُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ مَلِكُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ الْحَقُّ، وَوَعْدُكَ الْحَقُّ، وَلِقَاؤُكَ حَقٌّ، وَقَوْلُكَ حَقٌّ، وَالْجَنَّةُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّبِيُّونَ حَقٌّ، وَمُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ حَقٌّ، وَالسَّاعَةُ حَقٌّ، اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ، وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ، وَعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْتُ، وَبِكَ خَاصَمْتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ حَاكَمْتُ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ، وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ، أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ» مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ[3].
text.en: And the hadith of Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: When the Prophet ﷺ rose at night to pray tahajjud, he would say: “O Allah, to You belongs all praise; You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. To You belongs all praise; to You belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. To You belongs all praise; You are the Light of the heavens and the earth. To You belongs all praise; You are the King of the heavens and the earth. To You belongs all praise; You are the Truth, Your promise is true, the meeting with You is true, Your word is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the prophets are true, Muhammad ﷺ is true, and the Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned, by You I have contended, and to You I have brought my case for judgement. So forgive me what I have sent before and what I have left behind, what I have done in secret and what I have done openly. You are al-Muqaddim (the One who brings forward) and You are al-Mu’akhkhir (the One who puts back); there is no god worthy of worship but You.” Agreed upon[3].

text.ar: وَهَذَانِ الِاسْمَانِ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْمُزْدَوِجَةِ الْمُتَقَابِلَةِ الَّتِي لَا يُطْلَقُ وَاحِدٌ بِمُفْرَدِهِ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا مَقْرُونًا بِالْآخَرِ، فَإِنَّ الْكَمَالَ مِنِ اجْتِمَاعِهِمَا، وَالتَّقْدِيمُ وَالتَّأْخِيرُ وَصْفَانِ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ دَالاّنِ عَلَى كَمَالِ قُدْرَتِهِ وَنُفُوذِ مَشِيئَتِهِ، وَكَمَالِ حِكْمَتِهِ، وَهُمَا مِنَ الصِّفَاتِ الذَّاتِيَّةِ لِكَوْنِهِمَا قَائِمَيْنِ بِاللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ مُتَّصِفٌ بِهِمَا، وَمِنْ صِفَاتِ الْأَفْعَالِ؛ لِأَنَّ التَّقْدِيمَ وَالتَّأْخِيرَ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِالْمَخْلُوقَاتِ ذَوَاتِهَا وَأَفْعَالِهَا وَأَوْصَافِهَا.
text.en: These two names are among the paired, contrasting names, neither of which is applied to Allah on its own but only together with the other, for the perfection lies in their being joined. Bringing forward and putting back are two attributes of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which indicate the perfection of His power, the effectiveness of His will and the perfection of His wisdom. They are among the attributes of the essence, since they subsist in Allah and Allah is described by them; and among the attributes of action, because bringing forward and putting back relate to created things: their beings, their actions and their qualities.

text.ar: وَهَذَا التَّقْدِيمُ وَالتَّأْخِيرُ يَكُونُ كَوْنِيًّا كَتَقْدِيمِ بَعْضِ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَتَأْخِيرِ بَعْضِهَا عَنْ بَعْضٍ، وَكَتَقْدِيمِ الْأَسْبَابِ عَلَى مُسَبَّبَاتِهَا، وَالشُّرُوطِ عَلَى مَشْرُوطَاتِهَا، إِلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ التَّقْدِيمِ وَالتَّأْخِيرِ فِي الْخَلْقِ وَالتَّقْدِيرِ، وَيَكُونُ شَرْعِيًّا كَمَا فَضَّلَ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ عَلَى الْخَلْقِ وَفَضَّلَ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ، وَفَضَّلَ بَعْضَ عِبَادِهِ عَلَى بَعْضٍ، وَقَدَّمَهُمْ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْإِيمَانِ وَالْعَمَلِ وَالْأَخْلَاقِ وَسَائِرِ الْأَوْصَافِ، وَأَخَّرَ مَنْ أَخَّرَ مِنْهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَكُلُّ هَذَا تَبَعٌ لِحِكْمَتِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ، يُقَدِّمُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ إِلَى رَحْمَتِهِ بِتَوْفِيقِهِ وَفَضْلِهِ، وَيُؤَخِّرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ بِعَدْلِهِ.
text.en: This bringing forward and putting back may be in the order of creation (kawni), such as putting some created things before others and some after others, putting causes before their effects and conditions before what depends on them, and other kinds of bringing forward and putting back in creation and decree. And it may be in the order of the Law (shar‘i), as when He favoured the prophets over the rest of creation and favoured some of them over others, favoured some of His servants over others, advanced them in knowledge, faith, deeds, character and all other qualities, and put back whomever He put back among them in any of that. All of this follows His wisdom, Glorified is He: He brings forward whom He wills of His creation to His mercy by His granting of success and His favour, and He holds back whom He wills from that by His justice.

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ هَذَانِ الِاسْمَانِ فِي الثَّلَاثَةِ أَحَادِيثَ الْمُتَقَدِّمَةِ فِي سِيَاقِ طَلَبِ الْغُفْرَانِ لِلذُّنُوبِ جَمِيعِهَا الْمُتَقَدِّمِ وَالْمُتَأَخِّرِ، وَالسِّرِّ وَالْعَلَانِيَةِ، وَالْخَطَأِ وَالْعَمْدِ، وَفِي هَذَا أَنَّ الذُّنُوبَ تُوبِقُ الْعَبْدَ وَتُؤَخِّرُهُ، وَصَفْحُ اللَّهِ عَنْ عَبْدِهِ وَغُفْرَانُهُ لَهُ يُقَدِّمُهُ وَيَرْفَعُهُ، وَالْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ وَبِيَدِهِ يَخْفِضُ وَيَرْفَعُ، وَيُعِزُّ وَيُذِلُّ، وَيُعْطِي وَيَمْنَعُ، مَنْ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ عِزًّا وَرِفْعَةً وَتَقَدُّمًا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَحَدٌ حِرْمَانَهُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَمَنْ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ ذُلًّا وَخَفْضًا وَتَأَخُّرًا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَحَدٌ عَوْنَهُ لِلْخَلَاصِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: «مَا مِنْ قَلْبٍ إِلاّ وَهُوَ بَيْنَ أُصْبُعَيْنِ مِنْ أَصَابِعِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُقِيمَهُ أَقَامَهُ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُزِيغَهُ أَزَاغَهُ. وَكَانَ يَقُولُ: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قُلُوبَنَا عَلَى دِينِكَ، وَالْمِيزَانُ بِيَدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَخْفِضُهُ وَيَرْفَعُهُ» رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ[4].
text.en: These two names came in the three hadiths mentioned above in the context of seeking forgiveness for all sins, earlier and later, secret and open, mistaken and deliberate. This shows that sins destroy the servant and set him back, while Allah's pardoning His servant and forgiving him bring him forward and raise him. The whole matter belongs to Allah and is in His hand: He lowers and raises, honours and humbles, gives and withholds. Whomever Allah has decreed honour, elevation and advancement for, no one can deprive him of that; and whomever Allah has decreed humiliation, lowering and falling behind for, no one can help him escape from that. In the hadith: “There is no heart except that it is between two of the fingers of the Lord of the worlds: if He wills to keep it upright, He keeps it upright, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate. And he used to say: O Turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion. And the Scale is in the hand of ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful), the Mighty and Majestic; He lowers it and raises it.” Narrated by Ahmad[4].

text.ar: وَفِي هَذَا بَيَانُ أَنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيْسَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ أَمْرِ سَعَادَتِهِ أَوْ شَقَاوَتِهِ أَوْ خَفْضِهِ أَوْ رَفْعِهِ، أَوْ تَقَدُّمِهِ أَوْ تَأَخُّرِهِ، إِنِ اهْتَدَى فَبِهِدَايَةِ اللَّهِ إِيَّاهُ، وَإِنْ ثَبَتَ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ فَبِتَثْبِيتِهِ، وَإِنْ ضَلَّ فَبِصَرْفِهِ عَنِ الْهُدَى، وَأَنَّ الَّذِي يَتَوَلَّى قُلُوبَ الْعِبَادِ هُوَ اللَّهُ يَتَصَرَّفُ فِيهَا بِمَا شَاءَ، لَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْهَا، يُقَلِّبُهَا كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ.
text.en: This makes clear that nothing of the servant's happiness or misery, his lowering or raising, or his advancing or falling behind is in his own hands. If he is guided, it is by Allah's guiding him; if he stays firm on faith, it is by His making him firm; and if he goes astray, it is by His turning him away from guidance. It is Allah who has charge of the hearts of the servants, disposing of them as He wills; nothing of them is beyond Him, and He turns them however He wills.

text.ar: وَالْعَبْدُ مَعَ هَذَا مُحْتَاجٌ إِلَى بَذْلِ الْمَسَاعِي النَّافِعَةِ، وَسُلُوكِ الْمَسَالِكِ الصَّالِحَةِ الَّتِي يَكُونُ بِهَا تَقَدُّمُهُ وَنَيْلُهُ رِضَا اللَّهِ، وَالْبُعْدِ عَنِ الْمَسَالِكِ السَّيِّئَةِ الَّتِي يَكُونُ بِهَا تَأَخُّرُهُ وَوُقُوعُهُ فِي سَخَطِ اللَّهِ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمۡ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوۡ يَتَأَخَّرَ﴾ [الْمُدَّثِّرِ: ٣٧]، أَيْ: يَتَقَدَّمُ بِفِعْلِ مَا يُقَرِّبُهُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَيُدْنِيهِ مِنْ رِضَاهُ وَدَارِ كَرَامَتِهِ، أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرُ بِفِعْلِ الْمَعَاصِي وَاقْتِرَافِ الْآثَامِ الَّتِي تُبَاعِدُهُ عَنْ رِضَى اللَّهِ وَتُدْنِيهِ مِنْ سَخَطِهِ وَمِنَ النَّارِ، وَلَا غِنَى لِلْعَبْدِ فِي فِعْلِ مَا فِيهِ تَقَدُّمُهُ وَالْبُعْدِ عَمَّا فِيهِ تَأَخُّرُهُ عَنِ الرَّبِّ الْمُقَدِّمِ وَالْمُؤَخِّرِ سُبْحَانَهُ، فَهُوَ مُحْتَاجٌ إِلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ شُؤُونِهِ، مُفْتَقِرٌ إِلَيْهِ فِي جَمِيعِ حَاجَاتِهِ، لَا يَسْتَغْنِي عَنْ رَبِّهِ وَمَوْلَاهُ طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ.
text.en: Yet along with this, the servant needs to make beneficial efforts and follow the righteous paths through which he advances and attains Allah's pleasure, and to keep away from the evil paths through which he falls behind and incurs Allah's displeasure, as He the Exalted said: ﴾To whoever among you wills to advance or to fall behind﴿ [al-Muddaththir 74:37], that is, to advance by doing what brings him closer to his Lord and nearer to His pleasure and the abode of His honour, or to fall behind by committing sins and perpetrating wrongs that take him far from Allah's pleasure and bring him near to His displeasure and to the Fire. In doing what brings him forward and avoiding what sets him back, the servant can never do without the Lord, al-Muqaddim and al-Mu’akhkhir (the One who brings forward and the One who puts back), Glorified is He. He needs Him in all his affairs and is in want of Him in all his needs; he cannot do without his Lord and Master for the blink of an eye.

text.ar: وَقَدْ فَتَحَ سُبْحَانَهُ أَبْوَابَهُ لِلرَّاغِبِينَ السَّائِلِينَ، وَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ لَا يَرُدُّ مَنْ دَعَاهُ، وَلَا يُخَيِّبُ مَنْ نَادَاهُ، الْقَائِلُ فِي الْحَدِيثِ الْقُدْسِيِّ: «يَا عِبَادِي كُلُّكُمْ ضَالٌّ إِلَّا مَنْ هَدَيْتُهُ، فَاسْتَهْدُونِي أَهْدِكُمْ، يَا عِبَادِي كُلُّكُمْ جَائِعٌ إِلَّا مَنْ أَطْعَمْتُهُ، فَاسْتَطْعِمُونِي أُطْعِمْكُمْ، يَا عِبَادِي كُلُّكُمْ عَارٍ إِلَّا مَنْ كَسَوْتُهُ، فَاسْتَكْسُونِي أَكْسُكُمْ، يَا عِبَادِي إِنَّكُمْ تُخْطِئُونَ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَأَنَا أَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا، فَاسْتَغْفِرُونِي أَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[5].
text.en: He, Glorified is He, has opened His doors to those who long for Him and ask of Him. He, Glorified is He, does not turn away whoever calls on Him, nor disappoint whoever calls out to Him. It is He who says in the hadith qudsi: “O My servants, all of you are astray except whom I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except whom I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except whom I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you.” Narrated by Muslim[5].

text.ar: إِنَّ إِيمَانَ الْعَبْدِ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَالْمُؤَخِّرُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ يُثْمِرُ كَمَالَ الذُّلِّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، وَقُوَّةَ الطَّمَعِ فِيمَا عِنْدَهُ، وَالْخَوْفَ مِنْهُ سُبْحَانَهُ، وَعَدَمَ الْيَأْسِ مِنْ رَوْحِهِ، وَعَدَمَ الْأَمْنِ مِنْ مَكْرِهِ، وَحُسْنَ الِالْتِجَاءِ إِلَيْهِ رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَخَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا، وَحِرْصًا وَمُسَابَقَةً إِلَى الْخَيْرَاتِ وَالْأَعْمَالِ الصَّالِحَاتِ ﴿سَابِقُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةٖ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ﴾ [الْحَدِيدِ: ٢١].
text.en: The servant's faith that Allah alone is al-Muqaddim and al-Mu’akhkhir (the One who brings forward and the One who puts back), without any partner, bears fruit: complete humility before Him, strong hope for what is with Him, fear of Him, Glorified is He, not despairing of His relief, not feeling safe from His plan, turning to Him wholeheartedly in longing and in awe, in fear and in hope, and eagerness and racing towards good things and righteous deeds: ﴾Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴿ [al-Hadid 57:21].

text.ar: عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَأَى فِي أَصْحَابِهِ تَأَخُّراً فَقَالَ لَهُمْ: «تَقَدَّمُوا فَائْتَمُّوا بِي، وَلْيَأْتَمَّ بِكُمْ مَنْ بَعْدَكُمْ، لَا يَزَالُ قَوْمٌ يَتَأَخَّرُونَ حَتَّى يُؤَخِّرَهُمُ اللَّهُ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[6].
text.en: From Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him): the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw his Companions hanging back, so he said to them: “Come forward and follow me, and let those after you follow you. A people will keep hanging back until Allah puts them back.” Narrated by Muslim[6].

text.ar: وَمِنْ ثِمَارِ الْإِيمَانِ بِهَذَا الِاسْمِ الْحِرْصُ عَلَى تَقْدِيمِ مَا قَدَّمَ اللَّهُ وَتَأْخِيرِ مَا أَخَّرَ «وَالنَّبِيُّ ﷺ كَانَ شَدِيدَ التَّحَرِّي لِتَقْدِيمِ مَا قَدَّمَهُ اللَّهُ وَالْبَدَاءَةِ بِمَا بَدَأَ بِهِ، فَلِهَذَا بَدَأَ بِالصَّفَا فِي السَّعْيِ، وَقَالَ: نَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ، وَبَدَأَ بِالْوَجْهِ ثُمَّ الْيَدَيْنِ ثُمَّ الرَّأْسِ فِي الْوُضُوءِ، وَلَمْ يُخِلَّ بِذَلِكَ مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً»[7].
text.en: Among the fruits of believing in this name is being keen to put first what Allah has put first and to put last what He has put last. “The Prophet ﷺ was very careful to put first what Allah had put first and to begin with what He began with. That is why he began with as-Safa in the sa‘y and said: We begin with what Allah began with. And he began with the face, then the hands, then the head in wudu’, and he did not depart from that even once.”[7]

text.ar: وَهَكَذَا فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِ الدِّينِ، وَالْوَاجِبُ كَذَلِكَ تَقْدِيمُ مَنْ قَدَّمَهُ اللَّهُ وَتَأْخِيرُ مَنْ أَخَّرَهُ، وَمَحَبَّةُ مَنْ أَحَبَّهُ اللَّهُ وَبُغْضُ مَنْ أَبْغَضَ، فَإِنَّ هَذَا أَوْثَقُ عُرَى الْإِيمَانِ.
text.en: And so it is in all matters of the religion. It is likewise obligatory to put forward whom Allah has put forward and to put back whom He has put back, and to love whom Allah loves and hate whom He hates, for this is the firmest handhold of faith.
al-Bukhari (no. 6398) and Muslim (no. 2719).

text.ar: الْبُخَارِيُّ (رَقْمُ: ١١٢٠) ـ وَاللَّفْظُ لَهُ ـ، وَمُسْلِمٌ (رَقْمُ: ٧٦٩). وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ: «أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ».
text.en: al-Bukhari (no. 1120) – the wording is his – and Muslim (no. 769). Muslim's version does not include: “You are al-Muqaddim and You are al-Mu’akhkhir.”

text.ar: (٤/ ١٨٢) مِنْ حَدِيثِ النَّوَّاسِ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ، وَإِسْنَادُهُ صَحِيحٌ.
text.en: (4/182), from the hadith of an-Nawwas ibn Sam‘an, and its chain is authentic.

text.ar: (رَقْمُ: ٢٥٧٧) مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: (no. 2577), from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him).
*Bada’i‘ al-Fawa’id* (2/189).

text.ar: وَرَدَ هَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ أَمَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِمَا أَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ فَقَالَ: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلرُّسُلُ كُلُواْ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَٱعۡمَلُواْ صَٰلِحًاۖ إِنِّي بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ عَلِيمٞ﴾ [الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: ٥١]، وَقَالَ: ﴿يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ١٧٢]، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ الرَّجُلَ يُطِيلُ السَّفَرَ، أَشْعَثَ أَغْبَرَ، يَمُدُّ يَدَيْهِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ: يَا رَبِّ يَا رَبِّ، وَمَطْعَمُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَشْرَبُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَمَلْبَسُهُ حَرَامٌ، وَغُذِّيَ بِالْحَرَامِ، فَأَنَّى يُسْتَجَابُ لِذَلِكَ» رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ[1].
text.en: This name came in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O people, Allah is Tayyib (good and pure) and accepts only what is good and pure. And Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, for He said: ﴾O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed, I know well what you do﴿ [al-Mu’minun 23:51], and He said: ﴾O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:172]. Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dishevelled and dusty, stretching his hands towards the sky: O Lord, O Lord! while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with the unlawful; so how can he be answered?” Narrated by Muslim[1].

text.ar: وَالْمَعْنَى: أَنَّهُ تَعَالَى مُقَدَّسٌ وَمُنَزَّهٌ عَنِ النَّقَائِصِ وَالْعُيُوبِ كُلِّهَا؛ لِأَنَّ أَصْلَ الطِّيبِ الطَّهَارَةُ وَالسَّلَامَةُ مِنَ الْخُبْثِ، وَاللَّهُ جَلَّ وَعَلَا لَمْ يَزَلْ وَلَا يَزَالُ كَامِلًا بِذَاتِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ، وَأَفْعَالُهُ وَأَقْوَالُهُ صَادِرَةٌ عَنْ كَمَالِهِ، كَمُلَ سُبْحَانَهُ فَفَعَلَ الْفِعْلَ اللَّائِقَ بِكَمَالِهِ، وَمِنْ هُنَا فَأَسْمَاءُ اللَّهِ الْحُسْنَى وَصِفَاتُهُ الْعُلَا دَالَّةٌ عَلَى مَا يَفْعَلُهُ وَيَقُولُهُ، وَمَا لَا يَفْعَلُهُ وَلَا يَقُولُهُ، فَإِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ يَفْعَلُ وَيَقُولُ مَا هُوَ مُوجَبُ كَمَالِهِ وَعَظَمَتِهِ وَلَا يَفْعَلُ وَلَا يَقُولُ مَا يُنَاقِضُ ذَلِكَ.
text.en: The meaning is that He the Exalted is holy and free of all deficiencies and faults, because the root meaning of tayyib is purity and freedom from anything foul. Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, has always been and will always be perfect in His essence and His attributes, and His actions and words issue from His perfection. He, Glorified is He, is perfect, and so He does the action that befits His perfection. Hence Allah's beautiful names and lofty attributes indicate what He does and says, and what He does not do or say; for He, Glorified is He, does and says what His perfection and greatness require, and does not do or say what contradicts that.

text.ar: وَيَنْتَظِمُ تَقْرِيرَ هَذَا الْمَعْنَى وَالدَّلَالَةَ عَلَيْهِ مِنِ اسْمِهِ الطَّيِّبِ قَوْلُ الْمُصَلِّي فِي التَّشَهُّدِ «وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ» أَيْ: لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ.
text.en: The establishing of this meaning, and its being indicated by His name at-Tayyib (the Good and Pure), is contained in the words of the one praying in the tashahhud: “and at-tayyibat (the good things)”, that is, belong to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: «الطَّيِّبَاتُ» فَهِيَ صِفَةُ الْمَوْصُوفِ الْمَحْذُوفِ، أَيْ: الطَّيِّبَاتُ مِنَ الْكَلِمَاتِ وَالْأَفْعَالِ وَالصِّفَاتِ وَالْأَسْمَاءِ؛ لِلَّهِ وَحْدَهُ، فَهُوَ طَيِّبٌ، وَأَفْعَالُهُ طَيِّبَةٌ، وَصِفَاتُهُ أَطْيَبُ شَيْءٍ، وَأَسْمَاؤُهُ أَطْيَبُ الْأَسْمَاءِ، وَاسْمُهُ الطَّيِّبُ، لَا يَصْدُرُ عَنْهُ إِلَّا طَيِّبٌ، وَلَا يَصْعَدُ إِلَيْهِ إِلَّا طَيِّبٌ، وَلَا يَقْرُبُ مِنْهُ إِلَّا طَيِّبٌ، فَكَلِمُهُ طَيِّبٌ، وَإِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ، وَفِعْلُهُ طَيِّبٌ، وَالْعَمَلُ الطَّيِّبُ يَعْرُجُ إِلَيْهِ، فَالطَّيِّبَاتُ كُلُّهَا لَهُ، وَمُضَافَةٌ إِلَيْهِ، صَادِرَةٌ عَنْهُ، وَمُنْتَهِيَةٌ إِلَيْهِ، قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا».
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Likewise his saying ‘at-tayyibat (the good things)’: it describes an omitted noun, that is, the good things among words, actions, attributes and names belong to Allah alone. For He is Tayyib (Good and Pure), His actions are good, His attributes are the best of things, His names are the best of names, and His name is at-Tayyib. Nothing issues from Him but what is good, nothing ascends to Him but what is good, and nothing draws near to Him but what is good.
