text.ar: وَذَكَّرَ سُبْحَانَهُ بِمِنَّةِ بَعْثِ الرُّسُلِ عَلَيْهِمُ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ، وَإِكْرَامِهِ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةَ بِبَعْثِ صَفْوَةِ رُسُلِهِ وَخَيْرِ أَنْبِيَائِهِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ: ﴿وَلَقَدۡ بَعَثۡنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٖ رَّسُولًا أَنِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱجۡتَنِبُواْ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَۖ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ٣٦]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِن مِّنۡ أُمَّةٍ إِلَّا خَلَا فِيهَا نَذِيرٞ﴾ [فَاطِرٍ: ٢٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَقَدۡ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذۡ بَعَثَ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولٗا مِّنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٍ﴾ [آلِ عِمْرَانَ: ١٢٤].
text.en: He, Glorified is He, has reminded of the favour of sending the messengers (peace and blessings be upon them), and of His honouring this Ummah by sending the choicest of His messengers and the best of His prophets, Muhammad ﷺ: ﴾And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, saying: Worship Allah and avoid the taghut (false objects of worship)﴿ [an-Nahl 16:36]. And the Exalted said: ﴾And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴿ [Fatir 35:24]. And the Exalted said: ﴾Certainly Allah conferred a great favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although before that they had been in manifest error﴿ [Al ‘Imran 3:124].

text.ar: وَذَكَّرَ سُبْحَانَهُ بِمِنَّةِ التَّمْكِينِ لِأَنْبِيَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ وَلِعِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَقَدۡ مَنَنَّا عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ (١١٤) وَنَجَّيۡنَٰهُمَا وَقَوۡمَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلۡكَرۡبِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ (١١٥) وَنَصَرۡنَٰهُمۡ فَكَانُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰلِبِينَ (١١٦) وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَبِينَ (١١٧) وَهَدَيۡنَٰهُمَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلۡمُسۡتَقِيمَ﴾ [الصَّافَّاتِ: ١١٤ ـ ١١٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَنَجۡعَلَهُمۡ أَئِمَّةٗ وَنَجۡعَلَهُمُ ٱلۡوَٰرِثِينَ (٥) وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَنُرِيَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَحۡذَرُونَ﴾ [الْقَصَصِ: ٥ ـ ٦].
text.en: He, Glorified is He, has reminded of the favour of granting establishment to His prophets (peace be upon them) and to His believing servants. Allah the Exalted said: ﴾And We had certainly conferred favour upon Musa and Harun (114) and We saved them and their people from the great distress (115) and We supported them, so it was they who were the victors (116) and We gave them the clarifying Scripture (117) and We guided them on the straight path﴿ [as-Saffat 37:114–118]. And the Exalted said: ﴾And We wished to confer favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors (5) and to establish them in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers through them that which they had feared﴿ [al-Qasas 28:5–6].

text.ar: وَذَكَّرَ بِمِنَّتِهِ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِدُخُولِ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّجَاةِ مِنَ النَّارِ، وَاسْتِشْعَارِهِمْ لِهَذِهِ الْمِنَّةِ الْعَظِيمَةِ وَالْفَضْلِ الْكَبِيرِ ﴿قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبۡلُ فِيٓ أَهۡلِنَا مُشۡفِقِينَ (٢٦) فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ (٢٧) إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلُ نَدۡعُوهُۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾ [الطُّورِ: ٢٦ ـ ٢٨]، ﴿وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَىٰنَا لِهَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهۡتَدِيَ لَوۡلَآ أَنۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُۖ لَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ وَنُودُوٓاْ أَن تِلۡكُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةُ أُورِثۡتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ﴾ [الْأَعْرَافِ: ٤٣].
text.en: And He has reminded His believing servants of His favour upon them in their entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire, and of their awareness of this immense favour and great bounty: ﴾They will say: Indeed, we were previously, among our people, fearful (26) so Allah conferred favour upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching fire (27) indeed, we used to call upon Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful﴿ [at-Tur 52:26–28]; ﴾And they will say: Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this; and we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us. Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. And they will be called: This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴿ [al-A‘raf 7:43].

text.ar: وَمَنْ عَرَفَ رَبَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ بِهَذَا الِاسْمِ الْعَظِيمِ وَأَنَّهُ وَحْدَهُ وَلِيُّ الْمَنِّ وَالْعَطَاءِ، صَاحِبُ الْهِبَةِ وَالنَّعْمَاءِ؛ أَوْجَبَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ أَنْ يَحْمَدَ رَبَّهُ عَلَى نَعْمَائِهِ، وَأَنْ يَشْكُرَهُ عَلَى فَضْلِهِ وَعَطَائِهِ ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ﴾ [الْأَحْقَافِ: ١٥].
text.en: Whoever knows his Lord, Glorified is He, by this great name, and knows that He alone is the Master of favour and giving, the Possessor of gifts and blessings, this knowledge requires him to praise his Lord for His blessings and thank Him for His bounty and His giving: ﴾He said: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents﴿ [al-Ahqaf 46:15].

text.ar: وَقَدْ أَمَرَ اللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ بِالشُّكْرِ وَنَهَاهُمْ عَنْ ضِدِّهِ، وَأَثْنَى عَلَى عِبَادِهِ الشَّاكِرِينَ، وَوَعَدَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ الْجَزَاءِ، وَجَعَلَ الشُّكْرَ سَبَبًا لِمَزِيدِ الْفَضْلِ وَالْعَطَاءِ، وَحَارِسًا وَحَافِظًا لِلْهِبَةِ وَالنَّعْمَاءِ ﴿وَإِذۡ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمۡ لَئِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمۡۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرۡتُمۡ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدٞ﴾ [إِبْرَاهِيمَ: ٧]، وَأَوْجَبَ لَهُ كَذَلِكَ أَلَّا يَسْتَعْمِلَ نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ وَمِنَّتَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ فِي مَعْصِيَتِهِ، وَأَلَّا يُضِيفَ النِّعْمَةَ إِلَّا إِلَى الْمُنْعِمِ وَحْدَهُ، وَهُوَ اللَّهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، خِلَافَ مَنْ قَالَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: ﴿يَعۡرِفُونَ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنكِرُونَهَا وَأَكۡثَرُهُمُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ٨٣]، أَيْ: بِإِضَافَتِهِمُ النِّعْمَةَ إِلَى غَيْرِ الْمُنْعِمِ.
text.en: Allah has commanded His servants to give thanks and forbidden them its opposite. He has praised His grateful servants, promised them the best reward, and made gratitude a cause of increased bounty and giving, and a guard and protector of gifts and blessings: ﴾And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you are ungrateful, indeed, My punishment is severe﴿ [Ibrahim 14:7]. This knowledge likewise requires him not to use the blessing and favour of Allah, Glorified is He, in disobeying Him, and not to attribute the blessing to anyone but the Bestower alone, who is Allah, without partner — unlike those of whom Allah said: ﴾They recognise the blessing of Allah, then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers﴿ [an-Nahl 16:83], that is, by attributing the blessing to someone other than the Bestower.

text.ar: فَاللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ شُكْرًا، وَلَكَ الْمَنُّ فَضْلًا، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ بِالْإِسْلَامِ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ بِالْإِيمَانِ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ بِالْقُرْآنِ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ بِالْأَهْلِ وَالْمَالِ وَالْمُعَافَاةِ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ بِكُلِّ نِعْمَةٍ أَنْعَمْتَ بِهَا عَلَيْنَا فِي قَدِيمٍ أَوْ حَدِيثٍ، أَوْ سِرٍّ أَوْ عَلَانِيَةٍ، أَوْ خَاصَّةٍ أَوْ عَامَّةٍ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا طَيِّبًا مُبَارَكًا فِيهِ، اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ حَتَّى تَرْضَى، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ رَبَّنَا إِذَا رَضِيتَ.
text.en: So, O Allah, to You belongs praise in gratitude, and to You belongs the favour in grace. To You belongs praise for Islam, to You belongs praise for faith, to You belongs praise for the Qur’an, to You belongs praise for family, wealth and well-being. To You belongs praise for every blessing You have bestowed upon us, old or new, secret or open, particular or general. To You belongs praise for that, abundant, good and blessed praise. O Allah, to You belongs praise until You are pleased, and to You belongs praise, our Lord, when You are pleased.

text.ar: سَبَقَ تَخْرِيجُهُ.
text.en: Its source has already been given.

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ هَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي حَدِيثَيْنِ:
text.en: This name has come in two hadiths:

text.ar: الْأَوَّلُ: حَدِيثُ يَعْلَى بْنِ أُمَيَّةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَأَى رَجُلًا يَغْتَسِلُ بِالْبَرَازِ بِلَا إِزَارٍ، فَصَعِدَ الْمِنْبَرَ، فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ ﷺ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَيِيٌّ سِتِّيرٌ يُحِبُّ الْحَيَاءَ وَالسِّتْرَ، فَإِذَا اغْتَسَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَسْتَتِرْ»، رَوَاهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ وَالنَّسَائِيُّ[1].
text.en: The first: the hadith of Ya‘la ibn Umayyah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man bathing in an open place without a lower garment. So he ascended the minbar, praised Allah and extolled Him, then he ﷺ said: “Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Hayiyy (Modest) and Sittir (the One who conceals), and He loves modesty and concealment. So when one of you bathes, let him cover himself.” Reported by Abu Dawud and an-Nasa’i[1].

text.ar: الثَّانِي: حَدِيثُ سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ، يَسْتَحِي مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْرًا»، رَوَاهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ وَابْنُ مَاجَهْ[2].
text.en: The second: the hadith of Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, your Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, is Hayiyy (Modest) and Karim (Generous). When His servant raises his hands to Him, He is too modest to turn them back empty.” Reported by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah[2].

text.ar: وَفِي هَذَا الِاسْمِ الْكَرِيمِ دَلَالَةٌ عَلَى ثُبُوتِ الْحَيَاءِ صِفَةً لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَى مَا يَلِيقُ بِجَلَالِهِ وَكَمَالِهِ، وَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ فِي صِفَاتِهِ كُلِّهَا لَا يُمَاثِلُ أَحَدًا مِنْ خَلْقِهِ، وَلَا يُمَاثِلُهُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿لَيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَيۡءٞۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ﴾ [الشُّورَى: ١١]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿هَلۡ تَعۡلَمُ لَهُۥ سَمِيّٗا﴾ [مَرْيَمَ: ٦٥]، فَحَيَاؤُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَصْفٌ يَلِيقُ بِهِ، لَيْسَ كَحَيَاءِ الْمَخْلُوقِينَ.
text.en: This noble name indicates that modesty is established as an attribute of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the way that befits His majesty and perfection. In all His attributes, Glorified is He, He is not like any of His creation, and none of His creation is like Him, as the Exalted said: ﴾There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴿ [ash-Shura 42:11], and the Exalted said: ﴾Do you know of any equal to Him?﴿ [Maryam 19:65]. So His modesty, Glorified is He, is an attribute befitting Him, not like the modesty of created beings.

text.ar: وَقَدْ وَرَدَ ذِكْرُ الْحَيَاءِ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَالسُّنَّةِ بِصِيغَةِ الْفِعْلِ مُضَافًا إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلٗا مَّا بَعُوضَةٗ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ﴾ [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٢٦].
text.en: Modesty is mentioned in the Qur’an and the Sunnah in verbal form, attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: ﴾Indeed, Allah is not too shy to strike a parable — a mosquito or what is above it﴿ [al-Baqarah 2:26].

text.ar: وَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[3] عَنْ أَبِي وَاقِدٍ اللَّيْثِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ بَيْنَمَا هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَالنَّاسُ مَعَهُ إِذْ أَقْبَلَ ثَلَاثَةُ نَفَرٍ، فَأَقْبَلَ اثْنَانِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَذَهَبَ وَاحِدٌ، قَالَ: فَوَقَفَا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَأَمَّا أَحَدُهُمَا فَرَأَى فُرْجَةً فِي الْحَلْقَةِ فَجَلَسَ فِيهَا، وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ فَجَلَسَ خَلْفَهُمْ، وَأَمَّا الثَّالِثُ فَأَدْبَرَ ذَاهِبًا، فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: «أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ عَنِ النَّفَرِ الثَّلَاثَةِ؟ أَمَّا أَحَدُهُمْ فَأَوَى إِلَى اللَّهِ فَآوَاهُ إِلَيْهِ، وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ فَاسْتَحْيَا مِنَ اللَّهِ فَاسْتَحْيَا اللَّهُ مِنْهُ، وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ فَأَعْرَضَ فَأَعْرَضَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ».
text.en: In *as-Sahihayn*[3], from Abu Waqid al-Laythi: while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the mosque with people around him, three men approached. Two of them came towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and one went away. He said: The two stood by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them saw a gap in the circle and sat in it, the other sat behind them, and the third turned his back and went away. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished, he said: “Shall I not tell you about the three men? As for one of them, he sought refuge with Allah, so Allah gave him refuge. As for the other, he was shy before Allah, so Allah was shy of him. And as for the other, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him.”

text.ar: وَالْقَوْلُ فِي هَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ كَالْقَوْلِ فِي سَائِرِ صِفَاتِ الرَّبِّ سُبْحَانَهُ، فَكَمَا أَنَّا نُثْبِتُ لِلَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ عِلْمًا لَا كَعِلْمِنَا، وَبَصَرًا لَا كَبَصَرِنَا، وَسَمْعًا لَا كَسَمْعِنَا، وَإِرَادَةً لَا كَإِرَادَتِنَا فَكَذَلِكَ نُثْبِتُ لَهُ حَيَاءً لَا كَحَيَائِنَا؛ إِذْ كُلُّ مَا أَثْبَتَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَأَثْبَتَهُ لَهُ رَسُولُهُ ﷺ حَقٌّ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ.
text.en: What is said about this attribute is the same as what is said about all the other attributes of the Lord, Glorified is He. Just as we affirm for Allah, Glorified is He, knowledge unlike our knowledge, sight unlike our sight, hearing unlike our hearing and will unlike our will, so too we affirm for Him modesty unlike our modesty; for everything that He, Glorified is He, has affirmed for Himself, and that His Messenger ﷺ has affirmed for Him, is true beyond any doubt.

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَقَدْ وَصَفَ نَفْسَهُ بِالْحَيَاءِ، وَوَصَفَهُ رَسُولُهُ ﷺ، فَهُوَ الْحَيِيُّ الْكَرِيمُ، كَمَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَ إِلَيْهِ يَدَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْرًا»، وَقَالَتْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ: «يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ»[4]، وَأَقَرَّهَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ، وَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ، لَا تَأْتُوا النِّسَاءَ فِي أَعْجَازِهِنَّ»[5]»[6].
text.en: Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “He has described Himself with modesty, and His Messenger ﷺ has described Him with it. He is al-Hayiyy (the Modest), al-Karim (the Generous), as the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Indeed, Allah is Modest and Generous; when His servant raises his hands to Him, He is too modest to turn them back empty.’ Umm Sulaym said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, Allah is not shy of the truth,’[4] and he approved her in that. And the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Indeed, Allah is not shy of the truth: do not approach women in their rear passages.’[5]”[6]

text.ar: وَقَالَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَأَمَّا حَيَاءُ الرَّبِّ تَعَالَى مِنْ عَبْدِهِ فَذَاكَ نَوْعٌ آخَرُ لَا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَفْهَامُ، وَلَا تُكَيِّفُهُ الْعُقُولُ؛ فَإِنَّهُ حَيَاءُ كَرَمٍ وَبِرٍّ وَجُودٍ وَجَلَالٍ، فَإِنَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا رَفَعَ إِلَيْهِ يَدَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُمَا صِفْرًا، وَيَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يُعَذِّبَ ذَا شَيْبَةٍ شَابَتْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، وَكَانَ يَحْيَى بْنُ مُعَاذٍ يَقُولُ: سُبْحَانَ مَنْ يُذْنِبُ عَبْدُهُ وَيَسْتَحْيِي هُوَ، وَفِي أَثَرٍ: مَنِ اسْتَحَى مِنَ اللَّهِ اسْتَحَى اللَّهُ مِنْهُ»[7].
text.en: He (may Allah have mercy on him) also said: “As for the Lord’s modesty, Exalted is He, towards His servant, that is another kind altogether, which understanding cannot grasp and minds cannot picture how it is. It is a modesty of generosity, goodness, munificence and majesty. For He, Blessed and Exalted is He, is Modest and Generous: when His servant raises his hands to Him, He is too modest to turn them back empty, and He is too modest to punish someone with grey hair that turned grey in Islam. Yahya ibn Mu‘adh used to say: ‘Glory be to the One whose servant sins, yet it is He who feels shy.’ And in a narration: ‘Whoever is shy before Allah, Allah is shy of him.’”[7]

text.ar: وَاللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى يُحِبُّ أَسْمَاءَهُ وَصِفَاتِهِ، وَيُحِبُّ ظُهُورَ آثَارِهَا فِي خَلْقِهِ؛ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ لَوَازِمِ كَمَالِهِ، فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ حَيِيٌّ يُحِبُّ أَهْلَ الْحَيَاءِ، كَرِيمٌ يُحِبُّ الْكُرَمَاءَ، شَكُورٌ يُحِبُّ الشَّاكِرِينَ، مُحْسِنٌ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ، عَفُوٌّ يُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ وَأَهْلَهُ، حَلِيمٌ يُحِبُّ أَهْلَ الْحِلْمِ، وَلِمَحَبَّتِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ لِأَسْمَائِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ أَمَرَ عِبَادَهُ بِمُوجَبِهَا وَمُقْتَضَاهَا، فَأَمَرَهُمْ بِالْحَيَاءِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ وَالرَّحْمَةِ وَالْكَرَمِ وَالْعَفْوِ، وَأَحَبُّ عِبَادِهِ إِلَيْهِ مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِالصِّفَاتِ الَّتِي يُحِبُّهَا، وَأَبْغَضُهُمْ إِلَيْهِ مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِالصِّفَاتِ الَّتِي يَكْرَهُهَا، وَيُسْتَثْنَى مِنْ ذَلِكَ مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِالْكِبْرِ وَالْعَظَمَةِ وَالْجَبَرُوتِ؛ لِأَنَّ اتِّصَافَ الْعَبْدِ بِهَا ظُلْمٌ إِذْ لَا تَلِيقُ بِهِ هَذِهِ الصِّفَاتُ وَلَا تَحْسُنُ مِنْهُ لِمُنَافَاتِهَا لِصِفَاتِ الْعَبْدِ، وَلِتَعَدِّي مَنِ اتَّصَفَ بِهَا طَوْرَهُ وَحَدَّهُ، وَلِمُفَارَقَتِهِ مَقَامَهُ وَرُتْبَتَهُ، رُتْبَةَ الْعُبُودِيَّةِ وَالذُّلِّ.
text.en: Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, loves His names and attributes, and loves for their effects to appear in His creation, for that is a necessary consequence of His perfection. He, Glorified is He, is Hayiyy (Modest) and loves people of modesty; Karim (Generous) and loves the generous; Shakur (Appreciative) and loves the grateful; Muhsin (the Doer of good) and loves those who do good; ‘Afuww (Pardoning) and loves pardon and those who pardon; Halim (Forbearing) and loves people of forbearance. Because He, Glorified is He, loves His names and attributes, He commanded His servants to act according to what they require and entail: He commanded them to have modesty, to do good, and to show mercy, generosity and pardon. The most beloved of His servants to Him is the one who has the qualities He loves, and the most hated of them to Him is the one who has the qualities He dislikes. Excluded from this is the one who takes on the attributes of pride, grandeur and overpowering might, because the servant’s taking them on is wrongdoing: these attributes do not befit him and are not good coming from him, since they contradict the qualities of a servant; and because the one who takes them on oversteps his station and his limit, and departs from his place and his rank — the rank of servitude and humility.

text.ar: وَقَدْ تَكَاثَرَتِ النُّصُوصُ فِي الْأَمْرِ بِالْحَيَاءِ وَالْحَثِّ عَلَيْهِ وَالتَّرْغِيبِ فِيهِ، وَعَدِّهِ مِنْ شُعَبِ الْإِيمَانِ، وَبَيَانِ ثِمَارِهِ الْعَظِيمَةِ وَآثَارِهِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ، وَأَنَّهُ خَيْرٌ كُلُّهُ.
text.en: The texts commanding modesty, urging it and encouraging it are many. They count it among the branches of faith, explain its great fruits and blessed effects, and state that it is entirely good.

text.ar: فَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[8] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: «الْإِيمَانُ بِضْعٌ وَسَبْعُونَ شُعْبَةً، أَعْلَاهَا: قَوْلُ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَدْنَاهَا: إِمَاطَةُ الْأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ، وَالْحَيَاءُ شُعْبَةٌ مِنْ شُعَبِ الْإِيمَانِ».
text.en: In *as-Sahihayn*[8], from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet ﷺ said: “Faith has seventy-some branches. The highest of them is saying: ‘There is no god but Allah,’ and the lowest of them is removing something harmful from the road. And modesty is a branch of faith.”

text.ar: وَفِيهِمَا[9] عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ مَرَّ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُ أَخَاهُ فِي الْحَيَاءِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «دَعْهُ فَإِنَّ الْحَيَاءَ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ».
text.en: And in both of them[9], from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man of the Ansar who was admonishing his brother about modesty, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Leave him, for modesty is part of faith.”

text.ar: وَفِيهِمَا[10] عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ حُصَيْنٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: «الْحَيَاءُ لَا يَأْتِي إِلَّا بِخَيْرٍ»، وَفِي لَفْظٍ: «الْحَيَاءُ كُلُّهُ خَيْرٌ».
text.en: And in both of them[10], from ‘Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Modesty brings nothing but good.” And in another wording: “Modesty is all good.”

text.ar: وَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ حَيَاءً، فَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[11] عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَشَدَّ حَيَاءً مِنَ الْعَذْرَاءِ فِي خِدْرِهَا».
text.en: He (peace and blessings be upon him) was the most modest of people. In *as-Sahihayn*[11], from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more modest than a virgin in her private quarters.”

text.ar: وَالْحَيَاءُ فِي الْعَبْدِ خُلُقٌ جَمِيلٌ يَبْعَثُ عَلَى اجْتِنَابِ الْقَبِيحِ، وَيَمْنَعُ مِنَ التَّقْصِيرِ فِي حَقِّ ذِي الْحَقِّ، وَلِهَذَا قَالَ ﷺ: «إِنَّ مِمَّا أَدْرَكَ النَّاسُ مِنْ كَلَامِ النُّبُوَّةِ الْأُولَى: إِذَا لَمْ تَسْتَحْيِ فَاصْنَعْ مَا شِئْتَ» رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ[12]، أَيْ: مَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَحْيِ صَنَعَ مَا شَاءَ مِنَ الْفَوَاحِشِ وَالْمُنْكَرَاتِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْحَيَاءَ هُوَ الْمَانِعُ مِنْ فِعْلِهَا.
text.en: Modesty in the servant is a beautiful trait that moves him to avoid what is ugly and keeps him from falling short in the right of the one to whom it is due. That is why he ﷺ said: “Among what people have obtained from the words of the earlier prophethood is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish.” Reported by al-Bukhari[12]. That is, whoever has no modesty will do whatever he wishes of immoralities and evils, because modesty is what keeps one from doing them.

text.ar: وَأَعْظَمُ الْحَيَاءِ وَأَوْجَبُهُ الْحَيَاءُ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، فَفِي التِّرْمِذِيِّ وَغَيْرِهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: «اسْتَحْيُوا مِنَ اللَّهِ حَقَّ الْحَيَاءِ، قَالَ:قُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّا نَسْتَحِي وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، قَالَ: لَيْسَ ذَاكَ، وَلَكِنَّ الِاسْتِحْيَاءَ مِنَ اللَّهِ حَقَّ الْحَيَاءِ أَنْ تَحْفَظَ الرَّأْسَ وَمَا وَعَى، وَالْبَطْنَ وَمَا حَوَى، وَتَذْكُرَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْبِلَى، وَمَنْ أَرَادَ الْآخِرَةَ تَرَكَ زِينَةَ الدُّنْيَا، فَمَنْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ فَقَدِ اسْتَحْيَا مِنَ اللَّهِ حَقَّ الْحَيَاءِ» رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ وَالتِّرْمِذِيُّ[13].
text.en: The greatest and most obligatory modesty is modesty before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. In at-Tirmidhi and elsewhere, from ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be shy before Allah with the shyness that is truly His due. He said: We said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, we do feel shy, praise be to Allah.’ He said: ‘Not that. Rather, being shy before Allah with the shyness that is truly His due is that you guard the head and what it holds, and the belly and what it contains, and that you remember death and decay. Whoever desires the Hereafter leaves the adornment of this world. Whoever does that has been shy before Allah with the shyness that is truly His due.’” Reported by Ahmad and at-Tirmidhi[13].

text.ar: وَحِفْظُ الرَّأْسِ وَمَا وَعَى يَدْخُلُ فِيهِ حِفْظُ السَّمْعِ وَالْبَصَرِ وَاللِّسَانِ مِنَ الْمُحَرَّمَاتِ، وَحِفْظُ الْبَطْنِ وَمَا حَوَى يَتَضَمَّنُ حِفْظَ الْقَلْبِ عَنِ الْإِصْرَارِ عَلَى مُحَرَّمٍ، وَحِفْظَ الْبَطْنِ مِنْ إِدْخَالِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَآكِلِ وَالْمَشَارِبِ، وَحِفْظَ الْفَرْجِ عَنِ الْفَوَاحِشِ، قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: اسْتَحْيِي مِنَ اللَّهِ عَلَى قَدْرِ قُرْبِهِ مِنْكَ، وَخَفِ اللَّهَ عَلَى قَدْرِ قُدْرَتِهِ عَلَيْكَ»[14].
text.en: Guarding the head and what it holds includes guarding the hearing, the sight and the tongue from what is forbidden. Guarding the belly and what it contains includes guarding the heart from persisting in anything forbidden, guarding the belly from taking in forbidden food and drink, and guarding the private parts from immoral acts. One of them said: “Be shy before Allah in proportion to His nearness to you, and fear Allah in proportion to His power over you.”[14]

text.ar: رَزَقَنَا اللَّهُ الْحَيَاءَ مِنْهُ، وَوَفَّقَنَا لِتَحْقِيقِ خَشْيَتِهِ فِي الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ وَالسِّرِّ وَالْعَلَانِيَةِ.
text.en: May Allah grant us modesty before Him, and enable us to truly fear Him in the unseen and the seen, in private and in public.

text.ar: «سُنَنُ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» (رَقْمُ: ٤٠١٢)، وَ«سُنَنُ النَّسَائِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٤٠٦) مِنْ طَرِيقِ زُهَيْرٍ (هُوَ ابْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ أَبُو خَيْثَمَةَ)، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلَيْمَانَ الْعَرْزَمِيِّ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ يَعْلَى بْنِ أُمَيَّةَ، فَذَكَرَهُ. وَرِجَالُهُ ثِقَاتٌ. وَصَحَّحَ إِسْنَادَهُ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ فِي «إِرْوَاءِ الْغَلِيلِ» (٧/ ٣٦٧).
text.en: *Sunan Abi Dawud* (no. 4012) and *Sunan an-Nasa’i* (no. 406), via Zuhayr (that is, Ibn Mu‘awiyah, Abu Khaythamah), from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman al-‘Arzami, from ‘Ata’, from Ya‘la ibn Umayyah, who mentioned it. Its narrators are trustworthy. Al-Albani graded its chain authentic in *Irwa’ al-Ghalil* (7/367).

text.ar: «سُنَنُ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» (رَقْمُ: ١٤٨٨)، وَ«جَامِعُ التِّرْمِذِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٣٥٥٦)، وَ«سُنَنُ ابْنِ مَاجَهْ» (رَقْمُ:٣٨٦٥)، وَغَيْرُهُمْ مِنْ طَرِيقِ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ ـ صَاحِبِ الْأَنْمَاطِ ـ، عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ النَّهْدِيِّ، عَنْ سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيِّ، مَرْفُوعاً. وَقَالَ التِّرْمِذِيُّ: حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ. وَيُنْظَرُ: «صَحِيحُ الْجَامِعِ» (٢٦٣٨).
text.en: *Sunan Abi Dawud* (no. 1488), *Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi* (no. 3556), *Sunan Ibn Majah* (no. 3865) and others, via Ja‘far ibn Maymun — the carpet seller — from Abu ‘Uthman an-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi, attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. At-Tirmidhi said: “Hasan gharib.” See: *Sahih al-Jami‘* (2638).
*Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 66) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 2176).
Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (no. 130) and Muslim (no. 313).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ (٥/ ٢١٣)، وَابْنُ مَاجَهْ (رَقْمُ: ١٩٢٤) مِنْ حَدِيثِ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ الْعَبْسِيِّ. وَصَحَّحَهُ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ فِي «إِرْوَاءِ الْغَلِيلِ» (رَقْمُ: ٢٠٠٥).
text.en: Reported by Imam Ahmad (5/213) and Ibn Majah (no. 1924) from the hadith of Khuzaymah ibn Thabit al-‘Absi. Al-Albani graded it authentic in *Irwa' al-Ghalil* (no. 2005).
*as-Sawa‘iq al-Mursalah* (4/1499).

text.ar: «مَدَارِجُ السَّالِكِينَ» (٢/ ٢٦١).
text.en: *Madarij as-Salikin* (2/261).

text.ar: «صَحِيحُ الْبُخَارِيِّ» (رَقْمُ: ٩)، وَ«صَحِيحُ مُسْلِمٍ» (رَقْمُ: ٣٥).
text.en: *Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 9) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 35).
Al-Bukhari (no. 24) and Muslim (no. 36).
Al-Bukhari (no. 5766) and Muslim (no. 37).
Al-Bukhari (no. 3369) and Muslim (no. 2320).

text.ar: «الْمُسْنَدُ» (١/ ٣٨٧)، وَ«جَامِعُ التِّرْمِذِيِّ» (٢٤٥٨) وَغَيْرُهُمَا. وَقَالَ التِّرْمِذِيُّ: «حَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ إِنَّمَا نَعْرِفُهُ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبَانَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنِ الصَّبَّاحِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ». قَالَ الْحَافِظُ الْمُنْذِرِيُّ: «أَبَانُ وَالصَّبَّاحُ مُخْتَلَفٌ فِيهِمَا، وَقَدْ قِيلَ: إِنَّ الصَّبَّاحَ إِنَّمَا رَفَعَ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ وَهْماً مِنْهُ، وَضُعِّفَ بِرَفْعِهِ، وَصَوَابُهُ مَوْقُوفٌ». وَحَسَّنَهُ لِغَيْرِهِ الْأَلْبَانِيُّ فِي «صَحِيحِ التَّرْغِيبِ وَالتَّرْهِيبِ» (٣٣٣٧).
text.en: *al-Musnad* (1/387), *Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi* (2458) and others. At-Tirmidhi said: “A gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Aban ibn Ishaq from as-Sabbah ibn Muhammad.” Al-Hafiz al-Mundhiri said: “Aban and as-Sabbah are disputed. It has been said that as-Sabbah attributed this hadith to the Prophet only by mistake, and he was declared weak for attributing it; the correct view is that it stops at the Companion (mawquf).” Al-Albani graded it hasan li-ghayrihi in *Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib* (3337).

text.ar: انْظُرْ: «جَامِعُ الْعُلُومِ وَالْحِكَمِ» (ص/ ٣٦).
text.en: See *Jami‘ al-‘Ulum wal-Hikam* (p. 36).

text.ar: وَرَدَ هَذَا الِاسْمُ فِي حَدِيثِ يَعْلَى بْنِ أُمَيَّةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَأَى رَجُلاً يَغْتَسِلُ بِالْبَرَازِ بِلَا إِزَارٍ، فَصَعِدَ الْمِنْبَرَ، فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ ﷺ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَيِيٌّ سِتِّيرٌ، يُحِبُّ الْحَيَاءَ وَالسِّتْرَ، فَإِذَا اغْتَسَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَسْتَتِرْ»[1].
text.en: This name is mentioned in the hadith of Ya‘la ibn Umayyah (may Allah be pleased with him): Allah's Messenger ﷺ saw a man bathing in an open place without a waist-wrap. So he ascended the minbar, praised Allah and extolled Him, and then he ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Hayiyy (Ever-Modest) and Sittir (the One Who Conceals); He loves modesty and concealment. So when one of you bathes, let him cover himself.”[1]

text.ar: وَرَوَى ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ فِي «تَفْسِيرِهِ»، وَالْبَيْهَقِيُّ فِي «السُّنَنِ الْكُبْرَى» عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ سَأَلَاهُ عَنِ الِاسْتِئْذَانِ فِي الثَّلَاثِ عَوْرَاتٍ الَّتِي أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا فِي الْقُرْآنِ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ سِتِّيرٌ يُحِبُّ السِّتْرَ، كَانَ النَّاسُ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ سُتُورٌ عَلَى أَبْوَابِهِمْ وَلَا حِجَالٌ فِي بُيُوتِهِمْ، فَرُبَّمَا فَاجَأَ الرَّجُلَ خَادِمُهُ أَوْ وَلَدُهُ أَوْ يَتِيمُهُ فِي حَجْرِهِ وَهُوَ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ، فَأَمَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَسْتَأْذِنُوا فِي تِلْكَ الْعَوْرَاتِ الَّتِي سَمَّى اللَّهُ، ثُمَّ جَاءَ اللَّهُ بَعْدُ بِالسُّتُورِ، فَبَسَطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّزْقَ فَاتَّخَذُوا السُّتُورَ وَاتَّخَذُوا الْحِجَالَ، فَرَأَى النَّاسُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ كَفَاهُمْ مِنَ الِاسْتِئْذَانِ الَّذِي أُمِرُوا بِهِ». صَحَّحَ إِسْنَادَهُ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ فِي «تَفْسِيرِهِ»، وَالسُّيُوطِيُّ فِي «الدُّرِّ الْمَنْثُورِ»[2].
text.en: Ibn Abi Hatim reported in his *Tafsir*, and al-Bayhaqi in *as-Sunan al-Kubra*, from ‘Ikrimah from Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that two men asked him about seeking permission at the three times of privacy which Allah commanded in the Qur'an. Ibn ‘Abbas said: “Allah is Sittir (the One Who Conceals) and loves concealment. The people had no curtains on their doors and no screened alcoves in their houses, so a man's servant, or his child, or an orphan in his care might come upon him unexpectedly while he was with his wife. So Allah commanded them to seek permission at those times of privacy that Allah named. Then Allah later brought curtains: Allah expanded their provision, so they took curtains and screened alcoves, and the people saw that this sufficed them in place of the seeking of permission they had been commanded.” Ibn Kathir graded its chain authentic in his *Tafsir*, as did as-Suyuti in *ad-Durr al-Manthur*.[2]

text.ar: وَ«السِّتِّيرُ» أَيْ: السَّاتِرُ الَّذِي يَسْتُرُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ كَثِيرًا، وَلَا يَفْضَحُهُمْ فِي الْمَشَاهِدِ، الَّذِي يُحِبُّ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ السَّتْرَ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا يَفْضَحُهُمْ وَيُخْزِيهِمْ وَيَشِينُهُمْ، وَهَذَا فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَةٌ، وَحِلْمٌ مِنْهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَكَرَمٌ، فَالْعَبْدُ قَدْ يُقَارِفُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْمَعَاصِي وَالْآثَامِ، مَعَ فَقْرِهِ الشَّدِيدِ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ، حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَا يُمْكِنُهُ أَنْ يَعْصِيَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَتَقَوَّى عَلَيْهَا بِنِعَمِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالْبَصَرِ وَالْيَدِ وَالْقَدَمِ وَالصِّحَّةِ وَالْمَالِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ.
text.en: “As-Sittir” (the One Who Conceals) means: the Concealer who conceals His servants abundantly and does not expose them in public gatherings; who loves for His servants to conceal, for their own sake, whatever would expose, disgrace or shame them. This is a favour and mercy from Allah, and forbearance and generosity from Him, Glorified is He. For the servant may commit some sins and wrongdoings despite his intense need for his Lord, Glorified is He — so much so that he cannot even disobey except by drawing strength for it from Allah's blessings upon him: hearing, sight, hands, feet, health, wealth and the like.

text.ar: وَالرَّبُّ سُبْحَانَهُ ـ مَعَ كَمَالِ غِنَاهُ عَنِ الْخَلْقِ كُلِّهِمْ وَعَنْ طَاعَتِهِمْ وَعِبَادَتِهِمْ ـ يُكْرِمُ عَبْدَهُ وَيَسْتُرُهُ وَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ هَتْكِهِ وَفَضِيحَتِهِ وَإِحْلَالِ الْعُقُوبَةِ بِهِ، وَيُقَيِّضُ لَهُ مِنْ أَسْبَابِ السَّتْرِ، وَيُوَفِّقُهُ لِلنَّدَمِ وَالتَّوْبَةِ، وَيَعْفُو عَنْهُ وَيَغْفِرُ لَهُ، وَهَذَا مِنْ لُطْفِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ بِخَلْقِهِ وَرَحْمَتِهِ بِعَبِيدِهِ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَأۡخُذُ ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ١٠٤]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ سُوٓءًا أَوۡ يَظۡلِمۡ نَفۡسَهُۥ ثُمَّ يَسۡتَغۡفِرِ ٱللَّهَ يَجِدِ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١١٠]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ﴾ [الشُّورَى: ٢٥].
text.en: And the Lord, Glorified is He — despite His perfect independence of all creation, and of their obedience and worship — honours His servant, conceals him, and is too modest to tear away his cover, expose him and bring punishment down upon him. He provides him with means of concealment, guides him to remorse and repentance, and pardons and forgives him. This is from His gentle kindness, Glorified is He, toward His creation and His mercy toward His servants. Allah the Exalted says: ﴾Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and receives charities, and that it is Allah who is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful?﴿ [at-Tawbah 9:104]. And the Exalted says: ﴾Whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks Allah's forgiveness will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴿ [an-Nisa' 4:110]. And the Exalted says: ﴾And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do﴿ [ash-Shura 42:25].

text.ar: وَلِهَذَا فَإِنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ يَكْرَهُ مِنْ عَبْدِهِ إِذَا وَقَعَ فِي مَعْصِيَةٍ أَنْ يُذِيعَهَا وَيَشْهَرَهَا، بَلْ يَدْعُوهُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتُوبَ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ، وَسِتْرُ اللَّهِ مَسْبُولٌ عَلَيْهِ، لَا أَنْ يُظْهِرَهَا لِأَحَدٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ، وَمِنْ أَبْغَضِ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ بَاتَ عَاصِيًا وَاللَّهُ يَسْتُرُهُ، ثُمَّ يُصْبِحُ يَكْشِفُ سِتْرَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ.
text.en: For this reason He, Glorified is He, dislikes that His servant, when he falls into a sin, should broadcast and publicise it. Rather, He calls him to repent to Allah from it privately, between himself and his Lord, while Allah's cover is drawn over him — not to reveal it to anyone among people. And among the most hateful of people to Him is one who spends the night in sin while Allah conceals him, and then in the morning tears away Allah's cover from himself.

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَاءَتِ السُّنَّةُ بِالنَّهْيِ عَنْ هَتْكِ الْإِنْسَانِ سِتْرَ نَفْسِهِ، فَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[3] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: «كُلُّ أُمَّتِي مُعَافًى إِلَّا الْمُجَاهِرِينَ، وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْمُجَاهَرَةِ أَنْ يَعْمَلَ الرَّجُلُ بِاللَّيْلِ عَمَلًا وَقَدْ سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ، فَيَقُولُ: يَا فُلَانُ عَمِلْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ كَذَا وَكَذَا، وَقَدْ بَاتَ يَسْتُرُهُ رَبُّهُ، وَيُصْبِحُ يَكْشِفُ سِتْرَ اللَّهِ عَنْهُ».
text.en: The Sunnah has come forbidding a person from tearing away his own cover. In the two *Sahih*s[3], Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard Allah's Messenger ﷺ say: “All of my Ummah will be pardoned except those who sin openly. And part of sinning openly is that a man does a deed at night, and Allah has concealed it, then he says: ‘O so-and-so, last night I did such-and-such,’ when his Lord had spent the night concealing him, and in the morning he tears away Allah's cover from himself.”

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ بَطَّالٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «فِي الْجَهْرِ بِالْمَعْصِيَةِ اسْتِخْفَافٌ بِحَقِّ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَبِصَالِحِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَفِيهِ ضَرْبٌ مِنَ الْعِنَادِ لَهُمْ، وَفِي السَّتْرِ بِهَا السَّلَامَةُ مِنَ الِاسْتِخْفَافِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْمَعَاصِيَ تُذِلُّ أَهْلَهَا، وَمِنْ إِقَامَةِ الْحَدِّ عَلَيْهِ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ حَدٌّ، وَمِنَ التَّعْزِيرِ إِنْ لَمْ يُوجِبْ حَدًّا، وَإِذَا تَمَحَّضَ حَقُّ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ أَكْرَمُ الْأَكْرَمِينَ، وَرَحْمَتُهُ سَبَقَتْ غَضَبَهُ، فَلِذَلِكَ إِذَا سَتَرَهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا لَمْ يَفْضَحْهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ، وَالَّذِي يُجَاهِرُ يَفُوتُهُ جَمِيعُ ذَلِكَ»[4] اهـ.
text.en: Ibn Battal (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “Committing sin openly involves treating lightly the right of Allah and His Messenger and of the righteous believers, and it contains a kind of defiance toward them. Concealing it brings safety from treating it lightly — because sins humiliate those who commit them — and safety from having the prescribed punishment carried out on him if it carries one, and from discretionary punishment if it does not require a prescribed punishment. And when it is purely the right of Allah, then He is the Most Generous of the generous, and His mercy has outstripped His anger; so if He conceals him in this world, He will not expose him in the Hereafter. The one who sins openly misses all of that.”[4] End quote.

text.ar: وَلِذَا جَاءَ فِي «صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ»[5] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَا يَسْتُرُ اللَّهُ عَلَى عَبْدٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا، إِلَاّ سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ».
text.en: Hence it has come in *Sahih Muslim*[5], in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah does not conceal a servant in this world except that Allah will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection.”

text.ar: وَرَوَى الْبُخَارِيُّ وَمُسْلِمٌ[6] عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا؛ أَنَّ رَجُلاً سَأَلَهُ كَيْفَ سَمِعْتَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ فِي النَّجْوَى؟ قَالَ: «يَدْنُو أَحَدُكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِ حَتَّى يَضَعَ كَنَفَهُ عَلَيْهِ، فَيَقُولُ: عَمِلْتَ كَذَا وَكَذَا؟ فَيَقُولُ: نَعَمْ. وَيَقُولُ: عَمِلْتَ كَذَا وَكَذَا؟ فَيَقُولُ: نَعَمْ. فَيُقَرِّرُهُ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: إِنِّي سَتَرْتُ عَلَيْكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا، فَأَنَا أَغْفِرُهَا لَكَ الْيَوْمَ».
text.en: Al-Bukhari and Muslim[6] reported from Ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that a man asked him: How did you hear Allah's Messenger ﷺ speak about the private conversation (an-najwa)? He said: “One of you will draw near to his Lord until He places His cover over him, and He will say: ‘Did you do such-and-such?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ And He will say: ‘Did you do such-and-such?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ So He will make him confess, then He will say: ‘I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today.’”

text.ar: وَفِي هَذَا أَنَّ الْوَاجِبَ عَلَى الْعَبْدِ أَنْ يُجَاهِدَ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى الْبُعْدِ عَنِ الذُّنُوبِ وَمُقَارَفَتِهَا، وَإِذَا أَلَمَّ بِشَيْءٍ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَسْتُرَ نَفْسَهُ وَيُبَادِرَ إِلَى التَّوْبَةِ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَالْإِنَابَةِ إِلَيْهِ، وَلْيُكْثِرْ مِنَ الْأَعْمَالِ الصَّالِحَاتِ، كَمَا فِي «صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ»[7] عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: «جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي عَالَجْتُ امْرَأَةً فِي أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ، وَإِنِّي أَصَبْتُ مِنْهَا مَا دُونَ أَنْ أَمَسَّهَا، فَأَنَا هَذَا فَاقْضِ فِيَّ مَا شِئْتَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ: لَقَدْ سَتَرَكَ اللَّهُ لَوْ سَتَرْتَ نَفْسَكَ، قَالَ: فَلَمْ يَرُدَّ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ شَيْئًا، فَقَامَ الرَّجُلُ فَانْطَلَقَ، فَأَتْبَعَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ رَجُلاً وَتَلَا عَلَيْهِ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ: ﴿وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَيِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡحَسَنَٰتِ يُذۡهِبۡنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلذَّٰكِرِينَ﴾ [هُودٍ: ١١٤]، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ هَذَا لَهُ خَاصَّةً؟ قَالَ: بَلْ لِلنَّاسِ كَافَّةً».
text.en: This shows that the servant must strive against himself to stay far from sins and from committing them; and if he slips into something, he should conceal himself and hasten to repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and turn back to Him, and do many righteous deeds. As in *Sahih Muslim*[7], ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, I dallied with a woman on the far side of Madinah, and I did with her everything short of intercourse. Here I am, so judge me as you wish.’ ‘Umar said to him: ‘Allah had concealed you; if only you had concealed yourself.’ The Prophet ﷺ gave no reply. The man got up and left, and the Prophet ﷺ sent a man after him who recited to him this verse: ﴾And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds wipe away bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴿ [Hud 11:114]. A man among the people said: ‘O Prophet of Allah, is this for him specifically?’ He said: ‘Rather, for all people.’”

text.ar: وَمِنْ هَذَا الْمَعْنَى السَّتْرُ عَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ وَتَجَنُّبُ هَتْكِ أَسْتَارِهِمْ وَتَتَبُّعِ عَوْرَاتِهِمْ، فَفِي «الْمُسْنَدِ» وَ«سُنَنِ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» عَنْ أَبِي بَرْزَةَ الْأَسْلَمِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: «يَا مَعْشَرَ مَنْ آمَنَ بِلِسَانِهِ وَلَمْ يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ قَلْبَهُ، لَا تَغْتَابُوا الْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا عَوْرَاتِهِمْ؛ فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ يَتَّبِعْ عَوْرَاتِهِمْ يَتَّبِعِ اللَّهُ عَوْرَتَهُ، وَمَنْ يَتَّبِعِ اللَّهُ عَوْرَتَهُ يَفْضَحْهُ فِي بَيْتِهِ»[8].
text.en: Also part of this meaning is concealing the faults of Allah's servants, and avoiding tearing away their covers and searching out their private faults. In *al-Musnad* and *Sunan Abi Dawud*, Abu Barzah al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “O you who have believed with your tongues while faith has not entered your hearts! Do not backbite the Muslims and do not search out their faults, for whoever searches out their faults, Allah will search out his fault, and whoever Allah searches out his fault, He will expose him even in his own home.”[8]

text.ar: وَفِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[9] مِنْ حَدِيثِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: «مَنْ سَتَرَ مُسْلِمًا سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ».
text.en: In the two *Sahih*s[9], in the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever conceals a Muslim, Allah will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection.”

text.ar: هَذَا؛ وَإِنَّ الْوَاجِبَ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَسْتَتِرَ بِسِتْرِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَأَنْ يَتَجَنَّبَ الذُّنُوبَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ، وَأَنْ يَحْفَظَ عَوْرَتَهُ، وَأَنْ يَصُونَ عِرْضَهُ، وَأَنْ يَتَجَنَّبَ أَبْوَابَ الرَّذَائِلِ وَدُرُوبَ الْفَسَادِ، وَأَنْ يُقْبِلَ عَلَى رَبِّهِ تَائِبًا مُنِيبًا، وَأَنْ يَرْجُوَهُ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنْ يَحْفَظَهُ بِمَا يَحْفَظُ بِهِ عِبَادَهُ الصَّالِحِينَ، وَأَنْ يَسْتُرَ عُيُوبَهُ وَعَوْرَتَهُ، وَأَنْ يَمُنَّ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَفْوِ وَالْعَافِيَةِ، يَدْعُو بِذَلِكَ لِنَفْسِهِ وَلِمَنْ أَحَبَّ.
text.en: That said, it is obligatory upon every Muslim to keep himself covered with the cover of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; to avoid sins, both open and hidden; to guard his private parts; to protect his honour; to avoid the doors of vice and the paths of corruption; to turn to his Lord repentant and returning; to hope that He, Glorified is He, will protect him with that by which He protects His righteous servants, conceal his faults and his private matters, and bestow on him pardon and well-being — supplicating for this for himself and for those he loves.

text.ar: رَوَى الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: «لَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَدَعُ هَؤُلَاءِ الدَّعَوَاتِ حِينَ يُمْسِي وَحِينَ يُصْبِحُ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي، اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي، وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي، اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ وَمِنْ خَلْفِي، وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي، وَمِنْ فَوْقِي، وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي»[10].
text.en: Imam Ahmad reported that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: “Allah's Messenger ﷺ never left these supplications in the evening and in the morning: ‘O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family and my wealth. O Allah, conceal my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from in front of me and from behind me, from my right and from my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being taken unawares from beneath me.’”[10]

text.ar: وَقَوْلُهُ فِي هَذَا الدُّعَاءِ: «اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي» فِيهِ طَلَبُ السَّتْرِ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، وَالْعَوْرَاتُ الْمُرَادُ بِهَا: عُيُوبُ الْإِنْسَانِ وَتَقْصِيرُهُ وَكُلُّ مَا يَسُوؤُهُ انْكِشَافُهُ، وَيَدْخُلُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْحِفْظُ مِنِ انْكِشَافِ الْعَوْرَةِ، وَهِيَ فِي الرَّجُلِ مَا بَيْنَ السُّرَّةِ إِلَى الرُّكْبَةِ، وَفِي الْمَرْأَةِ جَمِيعُ بَدَنِهَا، وَحَرِيٌّ بِالْمَرْأَةِ الْمُسْلِمَةِ أَنْ تُوَاظِبَ عَلَى هَذَا الدُّعَاءِ، وَأَنْ تَصُونَ نَفْسَهَا بِالسِّتْرِ، وَأَنْ تُضْفِيَ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا جِلْبَابَ الْحِشْمَةِ، وَلَا سِيَّمَا فِي هَذَا الزَّمَنِ الَّذِي كَثُرَ فِيهِ التَّهَتُّكُ، وَضَعُفَ فِيهِ السَّتْرُ وَالْحَيَاءُ.
text.en: His saying in this supplication, “O Allah, conceal my faults (‘awrat)”, contains a request for concealment from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. What is meant by ‘awrat is a person's faults and shortcomings and everything whose exposure would grieve him. Included in this is being protected from the exposure of one's ‘awrah, which for a man is what lies between the navel and the knee, and for a woman is her entire body. The Muslim woman is most worthy of keeping up this supplication, of protecting herself with covering, and of wrapping herself in the garment of modesty, especially in this age in which immodesty has spread and covering and modesty have weakened.

text.ar: اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عُيُوبَنَا وَعَوْرَاتِنَا، وَاغْفِرْ ذُنُوبَنَا وَزَلَّاتِنَا، وَاخْتِمْ بِالصَّالِحَاتِ أَعْمَالَنَا وَأَعْمَارَنَا.
text.en: O Allah, conceal our faults and our private shortcomings, forgive our sins and our slips, and seal our deeds and our lives with righteous deeds.

text.ar: سَبَقَ تَخْرِيجُهُ.
text.en: Its source has already been given.

text.ar: يُنْظَرُ: «تَفْسِيرُ ابْنِ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ» (٨/ ٢٦٣٢)، وَ«السُّنَنُ الْكُبْرَى» لِلْبَيْهَقِيِّ (٧/ ٩٧)، وَ«تَفْسِيرُ ابْنِ كَثِيرٍ» (٦/ ٨٩ ـ ٩٠ ـ ط. الشَّعْبِ)، وَ«الدُّرُّ الْمَنْثُورُ» (١١/ ١٠٤). وَالْحَدِيثُ فِي «سُنَنِ أَبِي دَاوُدَ» أَيْضًا (٥١٩٢) بِلَفْظِ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَلِيمٌ رَحِيمٌ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ يُحِبُّ السَّتْرَ..».
text.en: See *Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim* (8/2632), *as-Sunan al-Kubra* by al-Bayhaqi (7/97), *Tafsir Ibn Kathir* (6/89–90, ash-Sha‘b edition) and *ad-Durr al-Manthur* (11/104). The hadith is also in *Sunan Abi Dawud* (5192) with the wording: “Indeed Allah is Forbearing, Merciful to the believers, and loves concealment...”
Al-Bukhari (no. 6069) and Muslim (no. 2990).
See *Fath al-Bari* (10/487).
*Sahih al-Bukhari* (no. 6070) and *Sahih Muslim* (no. 2768).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ (٤/ ٤٢٠)، وَأَبُو دَاوُدَ (رَقْمُ: ٤٨٨٠) وَغَيْرُهُمَا مِنْ طَرِيقِ أَبِي بَكْرِ ابْنِ عَيَّاشٍ، عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بَرْزَةَ، بِهِ. وَإِسْنَادُهُ حَسَنٌ. وَانْظُرْ: «صَحِيحُ التَّرْغِيبِ وَالتَّرْهِيبِ» (رَقْمُ: ٢٣٤٠).
text.en: Reported by Imam Ahmad (4/420), Abu Dawud (no. 4880) and others via Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash, from al-A‘mash, from Sa‘id ibn ‘Abdillah ibn Jurayj, from Abu Barzah, with it. Its chain is sound (hasan). See also *Sahih at-Targhib wat-Tarhib* (no. 2340).
Al-Bukhari (no. 2442) and Muslim (no. 2580).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ (٢/ ٢٥)، وَأَبُو دَاوُدَ (رَقْمُ: ٥٠٧٤)، وَابْنُ مَاجَهْ (رَقْمُ: ٣٨٧١) وَغَيْرُهُمْ بِإِسْنَادٍ صَحِيحٍ.
text.en: Reported by Imam Ahmad (2/25), Abu Dawud (no. 5074), Ibn Majah (no. 3871) and others with an authentic chain.

text.ar: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ مَأْثُورٌ فِي الْحَدِيثِ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، رَوَى أَبُو دَاوُدَ بِسَنَدٍ جَيِّدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الشِّخِّيرِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: «انْطَلَقْتُ فِي وَفْدِ بَنِي عَامِرٍ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَقُلْنَا: أَنْتَ سَيِّدُنَا، فَقَالَ: السَّيِّدُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى، قُلْنَا: وَأَفْضَلُنَا فَضْلًا، وَأَعْظَمُنَا طَوْلًا، فَقَالَ: قُولُوا بِقَوْلِكُمْ أَوْ بَعْضِ قَوْلِكُمْ، وَلَا يَسْتَجْرِيَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ»[1].
text.en: It is a name transmitted in the hadith from Allah's Messenger ﷺ. Abu Dawud reported with a good chain that ‘Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “I went with the delegation of Banu ‘Amir to Allah's Messenger ﷺ, and we said: ‘You are our master (sayyid).’ He said: ‘The Master (as-Sayyid) is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He.’ We said: ‘And the most excellent of us in virtue and the greatest of us in bounty.’ He said: ‘Say what you say, or part of what you say, and do not let Satan draw you along.’”[1]

text.ar: وَجَاءَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي مَعْنَى قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلۡ أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡغِي رَبّٗا﴾ [الْأَنْعَامِ: ١٦٤]: «إِلَهًا سَيِّدًا»، وَقَالَ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ﴾: «إِنَّهُ السَّيِّدُ الَّذِي قَدْ كَمُلَ فِي سُؤْدَدِهِ»[2].
text.en: It is reported that Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, regarding the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted ﴾Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah?﴿ [al-An‘am 6:164]: “A god and master.” And he said regarding His words ﴾Allah, as-Samad﴿: “He is the Master (as-Sayyid) who is perfect in His mastery.”[2]

text.ar: وَمُرَادُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ بِقَوْلِهِ: «السَّيِّدُ اللَّهُ» أَيْ: أَنَّ السُّؤْدَدَ حَقِيقَةً لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، فَهُوَ الْمَالِكُ الْمَوْلَى الرَّبُّ، وَالْخَلْقُ كُلُّهُمْ عَبِيدٌ لَهُ، مَمْلُوكُونَ مَقْهُورُونَ لَيْسَ بِهِمْ غُنْيَةٌ عَنْهُ فِي بَدْءِ أَمْرِهِمْ وَهُوَ الْوُجُودُ، إِذْ لَوْ لَمْ يُوجِدْهُمْ لَمْ يُوجَدُوا، وَلَا فِي الْبَقَاءِ بَعْدَ الْإِيجَادِ، وَلَا فِي الْعَوَارِضِ الْعَارِضَةِ أَثْنَاءَ الْبَقَاءِ، مُحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ شُؤُونِهِمْ، مُفْتَقِرُونَ إِلَيْهِ فِي جَمِيعِ حَاجَاتِهِمْ، لَا غِنَى لَهُمْ عَنْهُ طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ، وَالْأَمْرُ كُلُّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَحْدَهُ، وَالْخَلْقُ كُلُّهُمْ طَوْعُ تَدْبِيرِهِ وَتَحْتَ تَصَرُّفِهِ، يُعْطِي وَيَمْنَعُ، وَيَخْفِضُ وَيَرْفَعُ، وَيُعِزُّ وَيُذِلُّ، وَيُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَيَأْمُرُ وَيَنْهَى، وَيَقْبِضُ وَيَبْسُطُ، وَيُكْرِمُ وَيُهِينُ، وَيَهْدِي وَيُضِلُّ، وَيُضْحِكُ وَيُبْكِي، وَيُغْنِي وَيُفْقِرُ، الْأَمْرُ أَمْرُهُ، وَالْمُلْكُ مُلْكُهُ، وَالْعَبِيدُ عَبِيدُهُ، فَهُوَ وَحْدَهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى الَّذِي تَحِقُّ لَهُ السِّيَادَةُ مُلْكاً وَخَلْقاً وَتَدْبِيراً، وَذُلّاً وَخُضُوعاً وَانْكِسَارًا.
text.en: What the Prophet ﷺ meant by his words “The Master is Allah” is that mastery in reality belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He is the Owner, the Patron, the Lord, and all creation are His slaves: owned and subdued, with no independence from Him in the beginning of their affair — that is, their existence, for had He not brought them into existence they would not exist — nor in continuing after being brought into existence, nor in whatever circumstances arise while they continue. They need Him in all their affairs and are dependent on Him in all their needs; they cannot do without Him for the blink of an eye. The whole affair belongs to Him alone, and all creation is subject to His management and under His control. He gives and withholds, lowers and raises, honours and humiliates, gives life and causes death, commands and forbids, constricts and expands, ennobles and abases, guides and lets go astray, causes laughter and causes weeping, enriches and impoverishes. The command is His command, the dominion is His dominion, and the slaves are His slaves. So He alone, Blessed and Exalted is He, is the One truly entitled to mastery — in dominion, creation and management, and in the humility, submission and brokenness owed to Him.

text.ar: فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ السَّيِّدُ الَّذِي لَهُ التَّصَرُّفُ وَالتَّدْبِيرُ فِي هَذَا الْكَوْنِ لَا نِدَّ لَهُ، وَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ السَّيِّدُ الَّذِي يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُصْرَفَ لَهُ وَحْدَهُ الطَّاعَةُ وَالذُّلُّ وَالْخُضُوعُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، فَكَمَا أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ السَّيِّدُ الْمُتَصَرِّفُ فِي الْخَلْقِ لَا نِدَّ لَهُ، فَكَذَلِكَ يَجِبُ أَنْ يَكُونَ السَّيِّدَ الْمَعْبُودَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، كَمَا قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلۡ أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡغِي رَبّٗا وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖۚ﴾ [الْأَنْعَامِ: ١٦٤]، وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: «إِلَهًا سَيِّدًا».
text.en: So He, Glorified is He, is as-Sayyid (the Master) to whom belongs control and management of this universe, with no rival; and He, Glorified is He, is the Master to whom alone obedience, humility and submission should be directed, with no partner. Just as He, Glorified is He, is the Master who controls creation with no rival, likewise He must be the Master who is worshipped with no partner, as the Exalted says: ﴾Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?﴿ [al-An‘am 6:164]. The statement of Ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) has already been mentioned: “A god and master.”

text.ar: قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ فِي تَفْسِيرِ[3] هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: «يَقُولُ تَعَالَى ذِكْرُهُ لِنَبِيِّهِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ: ﴿قُلۡ﴾ يَا مُحَمَّدُ لِهَؤُلَاءِ الْعَادِلِينَ بِرَبِّهِمُ الْأَوْثَانَ، الدَّاعِيكَ إِلَى عِبَادَةِ الْأَصْنَامِ وَاتِّبَاعِ خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ: ﴿أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡغِي رَبّٗا﴾، يَقُولُ: أَسِوَى اللَّهِ أَطْلُبُ سَيِّدًا يَسُودُنِي ﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖۚ﴾ يَقُولُ: وَهُوَ سَيِّدُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ دُونَهُ وَمُدَبِّرُهُ وَمُصْلِحُهُ».
text.en: Ibn Jarir at-Tabari said in his explanation[3] of this verse: “Allah, exalted be His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴾Say﴿, O Muhammad, to these who set up idols as equals to their Lord, who call you to worship the idols and follow the footsteps of Satan: ﴾Shall I seek a lord other than Allah﴿ — He says: Shall I seek, besides Allah, a master to be master over me? ﴾while He is the Lord of all things﴿ — He says: while He is the Master of everything besides Him, its Manager and the One who sets it right.”

text.ar: وَقَالَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ فِي تَفْسِيرِهَا: «يَقُولُ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلۡ﴾ يَا مُحَمَّدُ لِهَؤُلَاءِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ بِاللَّهِ فِي إِخْلَاصِ الْعِبَادَةِ لَهُ وَالتَّوَكُّلِ عَلَيْهِ: ﴿أَغَيۡرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبۡغِي رَبّٗا﴾ أَيْ: أَطْلُبُ رَبًّا سِوَاهُ، ﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖۚ﴾ يَرُبُّنِي وَيَحْفَظُنِي وَيَكْلَؤُنِي، وَيُدَبِّرُ أَمْرِي، أَيْ: لَا أَتَوَكَّلُ إِلَّا عَلَيْهِ، وَلَا أُنِيبُ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكُهُ، وَلَهُ الْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ»[4].
text.en: Ibn Kathir said in his explanation of it: “The Exalted says: ﴾Say﴿, O Muhammad, to these who associate others with Allah, regarding making worship sincerely for Him and relying on Him: ﴾Shall I seek a lord other than Allah﴿, meaning: shall I seek a lord besides Him, ﴾while He is the Lord of all things﴿ — who nurtures me, protects me, guards me and manages my affairs? That is: I rely on none but Him and turn to none but Him, because He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything, and His are the creation and the command.”[4]

text.ar: وَهَذَا أَدَلُّ الدَّلِيلِ وَأَبْيَنُ الْبُرْهَانِ عَلَى بُطْلَانِ الشِّرْكِ وَاتِّخَاذِ الْأَنْدَادِ، إِذْ كَيْفَ يُتَّخَذُ الْمَخْلُوقُ الضَّعِيفُ نِدًّا لِلسَّيِّدِ الْعَظِيمِ وَالْخَالِقِ الْجَلِيلِ وَالرَّبِّ الْقَدِيرِ، تَعَالَى اللَّهُ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ.
text.en: This is the clearest proof and the plainest evidence of the falsehood of shirk and of taking rivals. For how can a weak created being be taken as a rival to the Mighty Master, the Majestic Creator and the All-Powerful Lord? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.

text.ar: ﴿أَيُشۡرِكُونَ مَا لَا يَخۡلُقُ شَيۡـٔٗا وَهُمۡ يُخۡلَقُونَ (١٩١) وَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ لَهُمۡ نَصۡرٗا وَلَآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَنصُرُونَ (١٩٢) وَإِن تَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡهُدَىٰ لَا يَتَّبِعُوكُمۡۚ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَدَعَوۡتُمُوهُمۡ أَمۡ أَنتُمۡ صَٰمِتُونَ (١٩٣) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمۡثَالُكُمۡۖ فَٱدۡعُوهُمۡ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ (١٩٤) أَلَهُمۡ أَرۡجُلٞ يَمۡشُونَ بِهَآۖ أَمۡ لَهُمۡ أَيۡدٖ يَبۡطِشُونَ بِهَآۖ أَمۡ لَهُمۡ أَعۡيُنٞ يُبۡصِرُونَ بِهَآۖ أَمۡ لَهُمۡ ءَاذَانٞ يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَاۗ قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ شُرَكَآءَكُمۡ ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنظِرُونِ (١٩٥) إِنَّ وَلِـِّۧيَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَۖ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ (١٩٦) وَٱلَّذِينَ تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ نَصۡرَكُمۡ وَلَآ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَنصُرُونَ﴾ [الْأَعْرَافِ: ١٩١ ـ ١٩٧].
text.en: ﴾Do they associate with Him those who create nothing while they themselves are created? (191) They are unable to help them, nor can they help themselves. (192) And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same for you whether you invite them or remain silent. (193) Indeed, those you call upon besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them and let them answer you, if you are truthful. (194) Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear? Say: Call your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite. (195) Indeed, my Protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He takes care of the righteous. (196) And those you call upon besides Him are unable to help you, nor can they help themselves﴿ [al-A‘raf 7:191–197].

text.ar: وَبِهَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ وَنَظَائِرِهَا يُعْلَمُ أَنَّ اتِّخَاذَ النَّاسِ سَيِّدًا غَيْرَ اللَّهِ سَوَاءٌ مِنَ الْمَقْبُورِينَ أَوِ الْأَحْيَاءِ، يَعْتَقِدُونَ فِيهِ جَلْبَ النَّفْعِ أَوْ دَفْعَ الضُّرِّ، أَوْ يُعَلِّقُونَ بِهِ حَاجَاتِهِمْ، أَوْ يُنْزِلُونَ بِهِ طَلَبَاتِهِمْ وَرَغَبَاتِهِمْ، أَوْ يَصْرِفُونَ لَهُ لُجُوءَهُمْ وَدَعَوَاتِهِمْ، أَوْ يَطْلُبُونَ مِنْهُ كَشْفَ غُمُومِهِمْ وَكُرُبَاتِهِمْ؛ يُعَدُّ شِرْكًا بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَاتِّبَاعًا لِلسَّبِيلِ الْمُفْضِيَةِ إِلَى الْجَحِيمِ، وَهَذَا غَايَةُ الْجَهْلِ وَالظُّلْمِ، إِذْ كَيْفَ يُسَوَّى التُّرَابُ بِرَبِّ الْأَرْبَابِ، وَكَيْفَ يُسَوَّى الْعَبِيدُ بِمَالِكِ الرِّقَابِ، وَكَيْفَ يُسَوَّى مَنْ لَا يَمْلِكُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَلَا لِغَيْرِهِ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا يَمْلِكُ نَصْرًا وَلَا مَوْتًا وَلَا حَيَاةً وَلَا نُشُورًا بِالسَّيِّدِ الْعَظِيمِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَقَالِيدُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ، وَبِيَدِهِ أَزِمَّةُ الْأُمُورِ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ.
text.en: Through these verses and others like them, it is known that people's taking a master other than Allah — whether among the buried dead or the living — believing that he brings benefit or wards off harm, or attaching their needs to him, or laying their requests and desires before him, or directing their refuge-seeking and supplications to him, or asking him to remove their griefs and distress, is counted as shirk with Allah the Mighty, and following the path that leads to Hellfire. This is the utmost of ignorance and wrongdoing. For how can dust be made equal to the Lord of lords? How can slaves be made equal to the Owner of all necks? And how can one who does not possess, for himself or for anyone else, an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and who has no power over help, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection, be made equal to the Mighty Master to whom belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, and in whose Hand are the reins of all affairs, with no partner?

text.ar: وَلَمَّا بُلِيَ أَقْوَامٌ بِمِثْلِ هَذَا التَّعَلُّقِ بِالْمَقْبُورِينَ أَضْفَوْا عَلَيْهِمْ هَذَا اللَّقَبَ، مُعْتَقِدِينَ فِيهِمْ، مُلْتَجِئِينَ إِلَيْهِمْ، خَاضِعِينَ ذَلِيلِينَ، نَاكِثِينَ بِذَلِكَ تَوْحِيدَهُمْ، مُتَلَوِّثِينَ بِمَا يُنَاقِضُهُ وَيُضَادُّهُ.
text.en: When some peoples were afflicted with this kind of attachment to the buried dead, they conferred this title upon them, holding beliefs about them, seeking refuge with them, submissive and humbled — thereby breaking their Tawheed and becoming stained with what contradicts and opposes it.

text.ar: وَتَأَمَّلْ فِي الْحَدِيثِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِ حِمَايَةَ الْمُصْطَفَى ﷺ حِمَى التَّوْحِيدِ، وَصِيَانَتَهُ لِجَنَابِهِ، وَسَدَّهُ طُرُقَ الشِّرْكِ، فَلَمَّا قَالُوا لَهُ: «أَنْتَ سَيِّدُنَا» قَالَ: «السَّيِّدُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى»، ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُمْ: «لَا يَسْتَجْرِيَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ»، مَعَ أَنَّهُمْ لَمْ يَقُولُوا إِلَّا حَقًّا.
text.en: Reflect, in the hadith mentioned earlier, on how the Chosen One ﷺ guarded the sanctuary of Tawheed, protected its domain and blocked the paths to shirk: when they said to him, “You are our master,” he said, “The Master is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He,” and then said to them, “Do not let Satan draw you along,” even though they had said nothing but the truth.

text.ar: وَنَظِيرُهُ مَا رَوَى الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ، وَالنَّسَائِيُّ فِي «الْكُبْرَى»[5] بِسَنَدٍ جَيِّدٍ عَنْ أَنَسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: «أَنَّ نَاساً قَالُوا لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ: يَا خَيْرَنَا وَابْنَ خَيْرِنَا، وَيَا سَيِّدَنَا وَابْنَ سَيِّدِنَا. فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِقَوْلِكُمْ وَلَا يَسْتَهْوِيَنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ؛ إِنِّي لَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَرْفَعُونِي فَوْقَ مَنْزِلَتِي الَّتِي أَنْزَلَنِيهَا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى، أَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».
text.en: Similar to it is what Imam Ahmad, and an-Nasa'i in *al-Kubra*[5], reported with a good chain from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): “Some people said to Allah's Messenger ﷺ: ‘O best of us and son of the best of us, O our master and son of our master.’ Allah's Messenger ﷺ said: ‘O people, keep to your ordinary words, and do not let Satan lead you astray. I do not want you to raise me above the rank in which Allah the Exalted has placed me. I am Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah, His slave and His Messenger.’”

text.ar: فَهُوَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ سَيِّدُ وَلَدِ آدَمَ وَأَفْضَلُ عِبَادِ اللَّهِ وَإِمَامُ الْمُتَّقِينَ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ كَرِهَ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ وَسِيلَةً إِلَى الْغُلُوِّ فِيهِ وَالْإِطْرَاءِ، كَمَا قَالَ ﷺ: «لَا تُطْرُونِي كَمَا أَطْرَتِ النَّصَارَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ، فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا عَبْدُهُ، فَقُولُوا: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ» رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ[6].
text.en: He, upon him be prayers and peace, is the master of the children of Adam, the best of Allah's servants and the leader of the God-fearing; yet he disliked this from them lest it become a means to exaggeration and excessive praise of him, as he ﷺ said: “Do not overpraise me as the Christians overpraised the son of Maryam. I am only His slave, so say: the slave of Allah and His Messenger.” Reported by al-Bukhari.[6]

text.ar: وَنَهَى عَنِ الْمَدْحِ وَشَدَّدَ الْقَوْلَ فِيهِ، كَمَا فِي «الصَّحِيحَيْنِ»[7] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي بَكْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: «أَنَّ رَجُلاً أَثْنَى عَلَى رَجُلٍ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: وَيْحَكَ قَطَعْتَ عُنُقَ صَاحِبِكَ، يَقُولُهُ مِرَارًا»، وَفِي «صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ»[8] عَنِ الْمِقْدَادِ بْنِ الْأَسْوَدِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: «إِذَا رَأَيْتُمُ الْمَدَّاحِينَ فَاحْثُوا فِي وُجُوهِهِمُ التُّرَابَ».
text.en: He also forbade praising people and spoke severely about it, as in the two *Sahih*s[7], in the hadith of Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him): “A man praised another man in the presence of Allah's Messenger ﷺ, and he said to him: ‘Woe to you! You have cut your companion's neck,’ saying it repeatedly.” And in *Sahih Muslim*[8], al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When you see those who heap praise, throw dust in their faces.”

text.ar: فَمُوَاجَهَةُ الْمَمْدُوحِ بِمَدْحِهِ وَلَوْ بِمَا فِيهِ لَا يَنْبَغِي، لِمَا قَدْ تُفْضِي إِلَيْهِ مَحَبَّةُ الْمَدْحِ مِنْ تَعَاظُمِ الْمَمْدُوحِ فِي نَفْسِهِ، وَذَلِكَ يُنَافِي كَمَالَ التَّوْحِيدِ، وَيُوقِعُهُ فِي أَمْرٍ عَظِيمٍ يُنَافِي الْعُبُودِيَّةَ الْخَاصَّةَ، فَالنَّبِيُّ ﷺ لَمَّا أَكْمَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ مَقَامَ الْعُبُودِيَّةِ صَارَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يُقَابَلَ بِالْمَدْحِ صِيَانَةً لِهَذَا الْمَقَامِ، وَإِرْشَادًا لِلْأُمَّةِ إِلَى تَرْكِ ذَلِكَ نُصْحًا لَهُمْ، وَحِمَايَةً لِمَقَامِ التَّوْحِيدِ عَنْ أَنْ يَدْخُلَهُ مَا يُفْسِدُهُ أَوْ يُضْعِفُهُ مِنَ الشِّرْكِ وَوَسَائِلِهِ، بِانْصِرَافِ الْقَلْبِ إِلَى نَوْعٍ مِنَ التَّعَلُّقِ بِالْمَخْلُوقِينَ وَالذُّلِّ لَهُمْ وَالِانْكِسَارِ الَّذِي لَا يَحِلُّ وَلَا يَجُوزُ صَرْفُهُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ.
text.en: So praising a person to his face, even with what is true of him, is not appropriate, because the love of praise may lead the one praised to grow great in his own eyes. That contradicts the perfection of Tawheed and drops him into a grave matter that contradicts special servitude. When Allah perfected for the Prophet ﷺ the station of servitude, he came to dislike being met with praise — to safeguard this station; to guide the Ummah, out of sincere care for them, to abandon it; and to protect the station of Tawheed from being entered by what corrupts or weakens it of shirk and its means, through the heart turning toward a kind of attachment to created beings, and a humility and brokenness before them that is not permissible and may not be directed to anyone but Allah, the One, the Subduer.

text.ar: رَوَاهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ (٤٨٠٦)، وَالْبُخَارِيُّ فِي «الْأَدَبِ الْمُفْرَدِ» (٢١١) وَغَيْرُهُمَا.
text.en: Reported by Abu Dawud (4806), al-Bukhari in *al-Adab al-Mufrad* (211) and others.
See *Tafsir at-Tabari* (24/736).
(10/48, at-Turki edition).
*Tafsir Ibn Kathir* (3/378).
*Musnad al-Imam Ahmad* (3/249) and *as-Sunan al-Kubra* (10078).

text.ar: رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ (رَقْمُ: ٣٤٤٥) مِنْ حَدِيثِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
text.en: Reported by al-Bukhari (no. 3445) from the hadith of ‘Umar (may Allah be pleased with him).
Al-Bukhari (no. 6061) and Muslim (no. 3000).

text.ar: وَهُوَ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحُسْنَى الثَّابِتَةِ فِي السُّنَّةِ، رَوَى الْبُخَارِيُّ فِي «صَحِيحِهِ»[1] عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا قَالَتْ: «اسْتَأْذَنَ رَهْطٌ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فَقَالُوا: السَّامُ عَلَيْكَ، فَقُلْتُ: بَلْ عَلَيْكُمُ السَّامُ وَاللَّعْنَةُ، فَقَالَ: يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الْأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ، قُلْتُ: أَوَلَمْ تَسْمَعْ مَا قَالُوا؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ: وَعَلَيْكُمْ».
text.en: It is one of the beautiful names established in the Sunnah. Al-Bukhari reported in his *Sahih*[1] from ‘Urwah from ‘A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: “A group of Jews asked permission to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ and said: ‘As-samu ‘alayk (death be upon you).’ I said: ‘Rather, upon you be death and the curse.’ He said: ‘O ‘A'ishah, Allah is Rafiq (Gentle) and loves gentleness in every matter.’ I said: ‘Did you not hear what they said?’ He said: ‘I said: And upon you.’”

text.ar: وَرَوَى مُسْلِمٌ فِي «صَحِيحِهِ»[2] عَنْ عَمْرَةَ بِنْتِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: «يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ، وَيُعْطِي عَلَى الرِّفْقِ مَا لَا يُعْطِي عَلَى الْعُنْفِ، وَمَا لَا يُعْطِي عَلَى مَا سِوَاهُ».
text.en: Muslim reported in his *Sahih*[2] from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd ar-Rahman from ‘A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that Allah's Messenger ﷺ said: “O ‘A'ishah, Allah is Rafiq (Gentle) and loves gentleness, and He gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness, and what He does not give for anything else.”

text.ar: فَفِي الْحَدِيثِ التَّصْرِيحُ بِتَسْمِيَةِ اللَّهِ بِالرَّفِيقِ وَوَصْفِهِ بِالرِّفْقِ، وَأَنَّ لَهُ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَصْفِ أَعْلَاهُ وَأَكْمَلَهُ وَمَا يَلِيقُ بِجَلَالِهِ وَكَمَالِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ.
text.en: In the hadith Allah is explicitly named ar-Rafiq (the Gentle) and described with gentleness, and it shows that He has the highest and most perfect share of this attribute, in the way that befits His majesty and perfection, Glorified is He.

text.ar: وَالرِّفْقُ: اللِّينُ وَالسُّهُولَةُ وَالتَّأَنِّي فِي الْأُمُورِ وَالتَّمَهُّلُ فِيهَا، وَضِدُّهُ الْعُنْفُ وَالتَّشْدِيدُ، فَهُوَ مَأْخُوذٌ مِنَ الرِّفْقِ الَّذِي هُوَ التَّأَنِّي فِي الْأُمُورِ وَالتَّدَرُّجُ فِيهَا، وَاللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ رَفِيقٌ فِي قَدَرِهِ وَقَضَائِهِ وَأَفْعَالِهِ، رَفِيقٌ فِي أَوَامِرِهِ وَأَحْكَامِهِ وَدِينِهِ وَشَرْعِهِ.
text.en: Rifq (gentleness) is softness, ease, and taking matters calmly and unhurriedly; its opposite is harshness and severity. The name is taken from rifq, which is taking matters calmly and proceeding in them step by step. Allah, Glorified is He, is Gentle in His decree and judgement and in His actions, and Gentle in His commands, rulings, religion and law.

text.ar: وَمِنْ رِفْقِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ فِي أَفْعَالِهِ أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ خَلَقَ الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ كُلَّهَا بِالتَّدَرُّجِ شَيْئًا فَشَيْئًا، بِحَسَبِ حِكْمَتِهِ وَرِفْقِهِ، مَعَ أَنَّهُ قَادِرٌ عَلَى خَلْقِهَا دَفْعَةً وَاحِدَةً وَفِي لَحْظَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، وَهُوَ دَلِيلٌ عَلَى حِلْمِ اللَّهِ وَحِكْمَتِهِ وَعِلْمِهِ وَلُطْفِهِ، وَقَدْ وَرَدَ عَنِ الصَّحَابَةِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ حَمْدُهُمْ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَى رِفْقِهِ فِي الْخَلْقِ وَتَصْرِيفِهِ الدَّائِمِ لِلْمَخْلُوقَاتِ، وَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَجْعَلِ الْخَلْقَ ثَابِتًا عَلَى هَيْئَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ.
text.en: Part of His gentleness, Glorified is He, in His actions is that He created all created things gradually, little by little, according to His wisdom and gentleness, though He is able to create them all at once, in a single moment. This is a proof of Allah's forbearance, wisdom, knowledge and kindness. It has been reported from the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) that they praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His gentleness in creation and His constant turning of created things from state to state, and that He did not make creation fixed in a single form.

text.ar: رَوَى ابْنُ أَبِي الدُّنْيَا بِسَنَدٍ جَيِّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «كَانُوا يَقُولُونَ ـ يَعْنِي أَصْحَابَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ـ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الرَّفِيقِ الَّذِي لَوْ جَعَلَ هَذَا الْخَلْقَ خَلْقًا دَائِمًا لَا يَتَصَرَّفُ لَقَالَ الشَّاكُّ فِي اللَّهِ: لَوْ كَانَ لِهَذَا الْخَلْقِ رَبًّا لَحَادَثَهُ، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ قَدْ حَادَثَ بِمَا تَرَوْنَ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ: إِنَّهُ جَاءَ بِضَوْءٍ طَبَّقَ مَا بَيْنَ الْخَافِقَيْنِ، وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا مَعَاشًا، وَسِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا، ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ ذَهَبَ بِذَلِكَ الْخَلْقِ، وَجَاءَ بِظُلْمَةٍ طَبَّقَتْ مَا بَيْنَ الْخَافِقَيْنِ، وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سَكَنًا وَنُجُومًا وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا، وَإِذَا شَاءَ بَنَى بِنَاءً جَعَلَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْمَطَرِ وَالْبَرْقِ وَالرَّعْدِ وَالصَّوَاعِقِ مَا شَاءَ، وَإِذَا شَاءَ صَرَفَ ذَلِكَ، وَإِذَا شَاءَ جَاءَ بِبَرْدٍ يُقَرْقِفُ النَّاسَ، وَإِذَا شَاءَ ذَهَبَ بِذَلِكَ، وَجَاءَ بِحَرٍّ يَأْخُذُ بِأَنْفَاسِ النَّاسِ لِيَعْلَمَ النَّاسُ أَنَّ لِهَذَا الْخَلْقِ رَبًّا هُوَ يُحَادِثُهُ بِمَا يَرَوْنَ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ، كَذَلِكَ إِذَا شَاءَ ذَهَبَ بِالدُّنْيَا وَجَاءَ بِالْآخِرَةِ»[3].
text.en: Ibn Abi ad-Dunya reported with a good chain that al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “They — meaning the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ — used to say: Praise be to Allah, the Gentle (ar-Rafiq), who, had He made this creation permanent and unchanging, the one who doubts about Allah would have said: If this creation had a Lord, He would bring about new things in it. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has brought about new things through the signs that you see: He brought light that fills what is between east and west, and made in it a means of livelihood and a blazing lamp; then, when He wills, He takes that creation away and brings darkness that fills what is between east and west, and makes in it rest, stars and a shining moon. When He wills, He builds a structure in which He places whatever rain, lightning, thunder and thunderbolts He wills, and when He wills, He turns that away. When He wills, He brings cold that makes people shiver, and when He wills, He takes that away and brings heat that takes people's breath away — so that people may know that this creation has a Lord who brings about new things in it through the signs they see. Likewise, when He wills, He will take away this world and bring the Hereafter.”[3]

text.ar: قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّةَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: «وَأَصْحَابُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَرَفُوا ذَلِكَ وَبَيَّنُوهُ لِلنَّاسِ، وَعَرَفُوا أَنَّ حُدُوثَ الْحَوَادِثِ الْيَوْمِيَّةِ الْمَشْهُودَةِ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْعَالَمَ مَخْلُوقٌ، وَأَنَّ لَهُ رَبًّا خَلَقَهُ وَيُحْدِثُ فِيهِ الْحَوَادِثَ»[4].
text.en: Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) said: “The Companions of Allah's Messenger ﷺ knew this and explained it to people. They knew that the occurrence of the daily events that are witnessed proves that the world is created, and that it has a Lord who created it and brings about events in it.”[4]

text.ar: ثُمَّ أَوْرَدَ أَثَرَ الْحَسَنِ الْمُتَقَدِّمَ وَعَلَّقَ عَلَيْهِ تَعْلِيقاً مُخْتَصَراً.
text.en: Then he cited the narration of al-Hasan mentioned above and commented on it briefly.

text.ar: وَمِنْ رِفْقِ اللَّهِ بِعِبَادِهِ رِفْقُهُ سُبْحَانَهُ بِهِمْ فِي أَحْكَامِهِ وَأَمْرِهِ وَنَهْيِهِ، فَلَا يُكَلِّفُ عِبَادَهُ مَا لَا يُطِيقُونَ، وَجَعَلَ فِعْلَ الْأَوَامِرِ قَدْرَ الِاسْتِطَاعَةِ، وَأَسْقَطَ عَنْهُمْ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْأَعْمَالِ بِمُجَرَّدِ الْمَشَقَّةِ رُخْصَةً لَهُمْ وَرِفْقًا بِهِمْ وَرَحْمَةً، وَلَمْ يَأْخُذْ عِبَادَهُ بِالتَّكَالِيفِ دَفْعَةً وَاحِدَةً، بَلْ تَدَرَّجَ بِهِمْ مِنْ حَالٍ إِلَى حَالٍ حَتَّى تَأْلَفَ النُّفُوسُ وَتَلِينَ الطِّبَاعُ وَيَتِمَّ الِانْقِيَادُ.
text.en: Part of Allah's gentleness with His servants is His gentleness, Glorified is He, with them in His rulings, commands and prohibitions. He does not burden His servants with what they cannot bear; He made the carrying out of commands according to ability; He lifted many deeds from them on account of hardship alone, as a concession to them, out of gentleness and mercy toward them; and He did not impose obligations on His servants all at once, but rather moved them gradually from one stage to another, until souls grew accustomed, natures softened and submission became complete.

text.ar: وَمِنْ رِفْقِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ إِمْهَالُهُ رَاكِبَ الْخَطِيئَةِ وَمُقْتَرِفَ الذَّنْبِ وَعَدَمُ مُعَاجَلَتِهِ بِالْعُقُوبَةِ لِيُنِيبَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ وَلِيَتُوبَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَلِيَعُودَ إِلَى رُشْدِهِ.
text.en: Part of His gentleness, Glorified is He, is His granting respite to the one who commits wrongdoing and perpetrates sin, and not hastening punishment upon him, so that he may turn back to his Lord, repent from his sin and return to right guidance.

text.ar: قَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ذُو ٱلرَّحۡمَةِۖ لَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُهُم بِمَا كَسَبُواْ لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ بَل لَّهُم مَّوۡعِدٞ لَّن يَجِدُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦ مَوۡئِلٗا﴾ [الْكَهْفِ: ٥٨]، وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَوۡ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلۡمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيۡهَا مِن دَآبَّةٖ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٖ مُّسَمّٗىۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَـٔۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةٗ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ﴾ [النَّحْلِ: ٦١].
text.en: The Exalted says: ﴾And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. Were He to seize them for what they have earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. Rather, they have an appointed time from which they will find no refuge﴿ [al-Kahf 18:58]. And the Exalted says: ﴾And if Allah were to seize people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it a single creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term comes, they cannot delay it for an hour, nor can they bring it forward﴿ [an-Nahl 16:61].

text.ar: فَبَيَّنَ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنَّهُ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ النَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُوا مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ كَالْكُفْرِ وَالْمَعَاصِي لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ الْعَذَابَ لِشَنَاعَةِ مَا يَرْتَكِبُونَهُ، وَلَكِنَّهُ حَلِيمٌ رَفِيقٌ لَا يَعْجَلُ بِالْعُقُوبَةِ بَلْ يُمْهِلُ وَلَا يُهْمِلُ.
text.en: So He, Glorified is He, made clear that if He were to seize people for the sins they earn, such as disbelief and disobedience, He would hasten the punishment for them because of the enormity of what they commit; but He is Forbearing and Gentle, He does not hasten the punishment — rather, He grants respite but does not neglect.

text.ar: وَمِنْ رِفْقِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنَّ دِينَهُ كُلَّهُ رِفْقٌ وَيُسْرٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ، وَأَمَرَ عِبَادَهُ بِالرِّفْقِ، وَيُعْطِيهِمْ عَلَى الرِّفْقِ مَا لَا يُعْطِي عَلَى الشِّدَّةِ، وَلَا يَكُونُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْأُمُورِ إِلَّا زَانَهُ، وَمَنْ حُرِمَهُ حُرِمَ الْخَيْرَ، وَلِذَا يَنْبَغِي عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَكُونَ رَفِيقًا فِي أُمُورِهِ كُلِّهَا، وَأَحْوَالِهِ جَمِيعِهَا، بَعِيداً عَنِ الْعَجَلَةِ وَالتَّسَرُّعِ وَالتَّهَوُّرِ وَالِانْدِفَاعِ، فَإِنَّ الْعَجَلَةَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ، وَلَا يَبُوءُ صَاحِبُهَا إِلَّا بِالْخَيْبَةِ وَالْخُسْرَانِ، وَكَفَى بِالرِّفْقِ نُبْلًا وَفَضْلًا أَنَّهُ حَبِيبٌ لِلرَّحْمَنِ، فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ.
text.en: Part of His gentleness, Glorified is He, is that His religion is entirely gentleness, ease and mercy. He commanded His servants to be gentle, and He gives for gentleness what He does not give for severity. It is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and whoever is deprived of it is deprived of good. Therefore every Muslim ought to be gentle in all his affairs and in all his circumstances, far from haste, rashness, recklessness and impulsiveness; for haste is from Satan, and the one given to it ends up with nothing but failure and loss. It is enough nobility and virtue for gentleness that it is beloved to the Most Merciful, for He, Glorified is He, is Gentle and loves gentleness.

text.ar: وَقَدْ جَاءَتِ السُّنَّةُ النَّبَوِيَّةُ بِالْحَثِّ عَلَى الرِّفْقِ فِي الْأُمُورِ كُلِّهَا، فَفِي «صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ»[5] عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: «إِنَّ الرِّفْقَ لَا يَكُونُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا زَانَهُ، وَلَا يُنْزَعُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا شَانَهُ».
text.en: The Prophetic Sunnah has come urging gentleness in all matters. In *Sahih Muslim*[5], ‘A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Gentleness is not found in anything except that it beautifies it, and it is not removed from anything except that it disfigures it.”

text.ar: وَفِيهِ[6] عَنْ جَرِيرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: «مَنْ يُحْرَمِ الرِّفْقَ يُحْرَمِ الْخَيْرَ»، وَفِي «الْمُسْنَدِ»[7] عَنْ عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: «إِنَّهُ مَنْ أُعْطِيَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ الرِّفْقِ فَقَدْ أُعْطِيَ حَظَّهُ مِنْ خَيْرِ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، وَحُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ وَحُسْنُ الْجِوَارِ يَعْمُرَانِ الدِّيَارَ، وَيَزِيدَانِ فِي الْأَعْمَارِ».
text.en: Also in it[6], Jarir (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of good.” And in *al-Musnad*[7], ‘A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever is given his share of gentleness has been given his share of the good of this world and the Hereafter. Good character and good neighbourliness make homes flourish and increase lifespans.”

text.ar: وَكَانَ نَبِيُّنَا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ أَرْفَقَ النَّاسِ، وَشَوَاهِدُ رِفْقِهِ فِي سُنَّتِهِ ظَاهِرَةٌ، وَدَلَائِلُ حِلْمِهِ وَأَنَاتِهِ فِي سِيرَتِهِ وَاضِحَةٌ، بَلْ إِنَّهُ ضَرَبَ أَرْوَعَ الْأَمْثِلَةِ فِي تَحْقِيقِ الرِّفْقِ وَالْأَنَاةِ فِي تَعَامُلِهِ مَعَ النَّاسِ وَدَعْوَتِهِ إِلَى دِينِ اللَّهِ، وَمُعَالَجَتِهِ لِمَا قَدْ يَقَعُ مِنْ أَخْطَاءٍ أَوْ مُخَالَفَاتٍ، وَمِنْ ذَلِكُمْ مَا رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ وَمُسْلِمٌ عَنْ أَنَسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: «بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذْ جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ فَقَامَ يَبُولُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، فَقَالَ أَصْحَابُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ: مَهْ مَهْ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: لَا تُزْرِمُوهُ دَعُوهُ، فَتَرَكُوهُ حَتَّى بَالَ، ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ دَعَاهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ: إِنَّ هَذِهِ الْمَسَاجِدَ لَا تَصْلُحُ لِشَيْءٍ مِنْ هَذَا الْبَوْلِ وَلَا الْقَذَرِ، إِنَّمَا هِيَ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَالصَّلَاةِ وَقِرَاءَةِ الْقُرْآنِ»[8]، وَرَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ[9] مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، وَفِيهِ: «أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ لَهُمْ: دَعُوهُ وَهَرِيقُوا عَلَى بَوْلِهِ سَجْلًا مِنْ مَاءٍ ـ أَوْ ذَنُوبًا مِنْ مَاءٍ ـ، فَإِنَّمَا بُعِثْتُمْ مُيَسِّرِينَ وَلَمْ تُبْعَثُوا مُعَسِّرِينَ».
text.en: Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was the gentlest of people. The evidence of his gentleness in his Sunnah is plain, and the signs of his forbearance and patience in his biography are clear.
